title: Bengals star DJ Turner is turning it up a notch
summary: If DJ Turner II’s 2025 season was his breakout, Joe Burrow has some bad news for the rest of the NFL: Turner might be even better now. The Cincinnati Bengals cornerback emerged as one of the bright spots of the defense last season, but his performance in training camp has caught the attention of the […]
full_text: If DJ Turner II’s 2025 season was his breakout, Joe Burrow has some bad news for the rest of the NFL: Turner might be even better now. The Cincinnati Bengals cornerback emerged as one of the bright spots of the defense last season, but his performance in training camp has caught the attention of the two players who are in perhaps the best position to judge just how difficult Turner has become to play against: Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase. And Burrow sees a different player. “Obviously, he was really good last year, but he’s taken it to a new level,” Burrow said. “He’s motivated. To see the steps he’s taken, just to see the dedication to his craft, the levels that he’s grown over the last several years, it’s fun to be a part of.” Need any further proof of a DJ Turner breakout? Here’s the stamp of approval from Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase 👍 @Bengals | @Real10jayy__ | @JoeyB | @djturner_5 | @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/0ChsgJLqFY — Up & Adams (@UpAndAdamsShow) August 12, 2026 The former Michigan standout played in all 17 games last year, starting 16, and finished with 40 total tackles, two interceptions, and two forced fumbles. His 18 passes defensed tied for third in the NFL and were the most by a Bengals defender since 2009. But maybe the most encouraging part of Turner’s development isn’t showing up on a stat sheet. Chase sees it in his confidence. “DJ’s been playing pretty good in camp,” Chase said. “He’s been playing a little different. His style of play has changed a little bit, and so has his confidence. He’s embracing more of his style.” There has never been a question about Turner’s physical ability. Cincinnati selected him in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft after he turned heads at the NFL Combine with a blazing 4.26-second 40-yard dash. Speed alone, however, doesn’t make an elite NFL cornerback. Turner’s first two seasons included the growing pains that come with playing one of football’s most unforgiving positions. His second season also ended prematurely when a fractured collarbone cost him the final six games. Then came 2025. Turner didn’t simply return from the injury. He established himself as Cincinnati’s top cover corner and routinely drew assignments against opposing teams’ best receivers. Every day in practice, Turner gets the opportunity to test himself against one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks and arguably its best wide receiver. If Burrow believes Turner has taken his game “to a new level,” and Chase sees a more confident cornerback embracing his own style, those are endorsements worth paying attention to.
author: John Acree

title: 10 winners and 4 losers in Cincinnati Bengals’ preseason win vs. Detroit Lions
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals opened their 2026 preseason with a 16-14 victory over the Detroit Lions on Thursday night at Paycor Stadium, but the final score was hardly the most important part of the evening. For a team with legitimate expectations entering the season, the preseason opener was the first opportunity to see some of the […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Kris Jenkins Jr. (90) celebrates a sack in the second quarter of the NFL Preseason game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Detroit Lions at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Thursday, Aug. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals opened their 2026 preseason with a 16-14 victory over the Detroit Lions on Thursday night at Paycor Stadium, but the final score was hardly the most important part of the evening. For a team with legitimate expectations entering the season, the preseason opener was the first opportunity to see some of the offseason changes in a real-game environment. Joe Burrow and the first-team offense played two series, while the revamped defense got a brief look at the new-look front featuring Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. The results were encouraging in some areas and concerning in others. Cincinnati’s defense immediately made its presence felt, forcing turnovers and generally making life difficult for Detroit’s young quarterbacks. Meanwhile, several players competing for roster spots or larger roles gave the coaching staff plenty to think about heading into the second preseason game. Here are the biggest winners and losers from the Bengals’ preseason opener. Winners Al Golden It wasn’t a perfect performance by Golden’s unit, and not even the type we saw in the early parts of training camp, but there were things to smile about on Thursday night. Whether it was in their two first-half turnovers (interception and fumble recovery), the unit being a half-minute away from a first-half shutout, or their tenacity in going after the football, it was a promising 2026 debut, overall. Evan McPherson The Bengals’ kicker looked to be in midseason form in the preseason opener. He drilled a 56-yarder in the rain in the first half and continued putting up points against Detroit all evening. Cashius Howell The rookie edge defender was active in limited time, picking up a fumble recovery and teaming up for a half-sack with Kris Jenkins Jr. in the first half. He looks to be the spark plug the Bengals hoped for when they selected him in the second round. Colbie Young Young’s preseason debut provided another reason for optimism surrounding one of the Bengals’ most intriguing young offensive players. The fourth-round rookie has been one of the biggest stories of Cincinnati’s training camp, repeatedly making difficult catches and showing off the size that makes him such an intriguing option in the passing game. The preseason opener wasn’t necessarily about putting up huge numbers. It was about showing that the impressive work at practice can translate to game action. Bengals’ interior defensive line (Kris Jenkins Jr., Dexter Lawrence, and Landon Robinson) While Lawrence’s impact was limited due to few snaps, his general presence was felt by the defensive unit. Jenkins shared a sack with Howell, and Robinson had a would-be sack, if not for a hold called on the offensive lineman. Depth up front is going to be key for the Bengals’ defense, and it was effective against the Lions. Jack Endries The Bengals’ other seventh-round pick this year had a great preseason debut for the team. Whether it was hauling in a touchdown grab from Joe Flacco or making three Lions defenders miss on a 17-yard gain in the second half, he looks to be a boost to an already-solid tight end room. Jack Endries’ follow-up to his first half touchdown: pic.twitter.com/Js5QpQt67b — Anthony Cosenza (@CJAnthonyCUI) August 14, 2026 Jordan Battle Battle made arguably the biggest defensive play of the night when he intercepted Lions rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer. The interception came after the ball deflected off the hands of Detroit receiver Isaac TeSlaa, but Battle still had to be in position to make the play. That is exactly the type of production Battle needs during what could be an important season for his future in Cincinnati. Dohnte Meyers The youngster is grinding for a roster spot in a crowded receiver room, and he was a joy to watch in second-half action. He made a few nice catches, showing a little bit of everything, and had a nice 13-yard sprint as a rusher. Russ Yeast The son of former Bengals player Craig Yeast made the game-sealing interception with about 20 seconds to play. He also had two tackles, but from a bigger-picture perspective, it was great to see the defense close it out after the game became tight. Losers Andrew Coker and Orlando Brown Jr. It was a rough night for the Bengals’ left tackles. The opening unit of starters allowed two sacks on Joe Burrow (No. 9 ran into one of those), but Brown was beat off the edge by a quick rush. In the third quarter, Coker had a sequence of plays in which he committed a false start and allowed a sack that derailed a drive. He did recover a fumble for the offense to keep possession, though. Kendall Milton The Bengals’ second-half back had a rough night with a fumble and just 2.8 yards per carry. It was a rough night for both teams handling the football because of the earlier immense rain, but he will need to show more in the next couple of games. The Bigger Picture The Bengals didn’t need to win Thursday night. They needed to get some meaningful game reps, evaluate their young players, and come away healthy. They accomplished most of that. The defense once again looked like a completely different unit from the group that struggled so badly at times last season. Lawrence and Allen barely needed to play before the young defenders started making plays, while Battle and Howell each found ways to impact the game. On offense, there were flashes from Burrow, Chase, Chase Brown, and the rest of the first-team group, but there is still work to do along the offensive line. And then there were the young players. Endries scored a touchdown. Young continued to build his case. Howell made another splash play. Those are exactly the types of developments Cincinnati wanted to see from its first preseason game. The Bengals will now turn their attention to the next stage of camp and preseason action, where the competition for roster spots will only intensify.

title: Instant recap of the Bengals starters vs. Lions
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals kicked off their NFL preseason Thursday as they hosted the Detroit Lions at a rainy Paycor Stadium. Ted Karras and Dexter Lawrence came out as captains to start the game. This is another sign of just how bought in Lawrence has been since the Bengals traded for the massive defensive tackle. It […]
full_text: Joe Burrow is questionable to return with a wrist injury. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals kicked off their NFL preseason Thursday as they hosted the Detroit Lions at a rainy Paycor Stadium. Ted Karras and Dexter Lawrence came out as captains to start the game. This is another sign of just how bought in Lawrence has been since the Bengals traded for the massive defensive tackle. It seemed like he barely left the building after the trade went through. The majority of the Bengals’ starting defense was going against the Lions’ backup offense. The Lions were driving right down the field until a deflection off the facemask of Lions receiver Isaac TeSlaa led to a Jordan Battle interception. On the first drive for Joe Burrow, the Bengals got one first down on a nice pass to Ja’Marr Chase, but a sack on second down basically shut the drive down. The sack seemed like the result of good coverage by the Lions, with Burrow having to hold on to the ball a bit long. On the second defensive series, the Bengals quickly got off the field, returning the ball to Joe Burrow and the first-team offense. Veterans Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen did not play on that second drive, giving the established veterans the rest of the night off. Burrow was getting the ball out quickly on short passes for the majority of the second drive. As expected, Chase Brown and Samaje Perine were splitting a lot of reps with the first-team offense. Unfortunately, pressure off the edge led to a stop on third down after Orlando Brown Jr. gave up a sack. There is real concern with his ability to handle speed off of the edge at this stage of his career. Thankfully, Evan McPherson hit a 56-yard field goal, one that would likely have been good from about 65 yards out. It wasn’t a large sample size, but what were your thoughts on what you saw from the Bengals’ offensive and defensive starters tonight?

summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will host the Detroit Lions tonight, marking the first return to actual live reps of the season for both teams. full_text: Dec 28, 2025; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. (44) and Cincinnati Bengals linebacker Barrett Carter (49) react after a play during the second half against the Arizona Cardinals at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals will host the Detroit Lions tonight, marking the first return to actual live reps of the season for both teams. Head coach Zac Taylor has already said we should see starters playing (obviously no one with any injuries). That does mean we get to see Joe Burrow and company try to put some offense together. We also should see the new names on the defensive side of the ball for the first time. The big thing will be watching those linebackers in the middle, Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter. Both have heard tons of criticism this entire Offseason. This is an early chance to show Cincinnati was right not to bring in any competition for them. Bengals News What to Watch For | Lions vs Bengals Preseason Week 1 While Zac Taylor confirmed that offseason free agent acquisition Bryan Cook will be among the players who will not see action in Thursday’s preseason opener, fans will get a look at several other Bengals who joined the team over the past five months. Notably, defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II, who Cincinnati acquired in a trade less than a week before the NFL Draft, has garnered high praise from his new teammates and coaches throughout the early stages of training camp. The big thing to watch for tonight is which younger player, or players, on the roster bubble actually pop. We may see the starters for a series or two, but the vast majority of reps should go to backups looking to show what they can do by taking live reps. The wide receiver and defensive tackle rooms look particularly deep. It will be interesting to see who stays and who goes when it is all said and done. Ja’Marr Chase names two Bengals breakout candidates The rookie Young, a fourth-round pick this year, keeps making huge plays in camp, so it’s deserved praise. He’s looking like a threat to steal some snaps, perhaps even over Andrei Iosivas. Colbie Young has been the worst-kept secret to anyone even barely paying attention to Cincinnati’s training camp. He has looked the part of a dynamic third wide receiver that this offense has desperately needed. Andrei Iosivas has, unfortunately, had some struggles with drops recently, and if that isn’t corrected, he has credible competition right behind him. Bengals’ estimated NFL franchise value rank doesn’t tell whole story Maybe the Bengals don’t climb out of 32nd place for the seventh year running, but getting a $453ish million check for television revenue and otherwise in a league whose teams total nearly $300 billion won’t cause the Bengals any concerns. We need to be honest. The Bengals’ ownership could not care less about this whole “franchise value” thing that comes out every year. We have seen them take baby steps towards modernizing, but that seems more like they are being dragged, kicking and screaming, into doing so. It also seems like this year they wanted to actually turn the team back into a contender. None of these things have been done or will be done, so they can be viewed as a valuable franchise. Trevor Sikkema: ‘I think Ja’Marr Chase is the best WR’ in fantasy | ‘NFL Fantasy Football Show’ This may seem obvious to Bengals fans, but we also have an inherent bias because we believe Chase is the best wide receiver in the NFL. To be the top wide receiver in fantasy is something different entirely, though. If Burrow stays healthy, Chase gets the volume and valuable goal-line targets to easily reach that mark. NFL News NFL Power Rankings: Rams enter preseason on top; Seahawks at No. 3, Patriots outside top 10 The Bengals finally invested in their defense and proved to the rest of the NFL that they’re serious about contending again. That’s a good start, and so far, early returns are very promising — so much so that Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ increasingly complex offense has been frustrated at times during camp. This is being sold as a real “iron sharpens iron” situation, which is either the product of typical camp optimism or a sign of good things to come. If Burrow can (finally) stay healthy, I expect this to be the best Bengals team we’ve seen since Cincy reached Super Bowl LVI. Pretty shocking to see the Bengals at number eight overall on a national list. Then again, it seems there is an expectation that several teams will bounce back, as the Baltimore Ravens came in sixth. It is for all the reasons we fans have been saying. The offense is returning, which has been great. The defense has been completely overhauled with several key veterans (linebackers still needing to show their worth). Deshaun Watson to start Browns’ first preseason game vs. Bears; Shedeur Sanders slated for next week New head coach Todd Monken has conducted a battle for the starting job throughout the offseason and hasn’t provided many hints on who is leading at this stage, leaving the race to be interpreted by those covering the team. Early in camp, Sanders appeared to be ahead of Watson, but Watson’s improvement over the weekend seemed to narrow the competition. Sometimes it is important to appreciate that this team hasn’t been in the pits of despair at quarterback in quite some time. Ever since Carson Palmer was drafted in 2003, Cincinnati has had one of the most steady quarterback rooms in the NFL. Palmer looked like an MVP-level player before his injury in the 2005-06 Playoffs. After he forced his way out, the team entered the Andy Dalton era, which led to trips to the Playoffs for five straight years. Now we are in the middle of the Burrow era that saw the Bengals return to the Super Bowl. 2026 NFL fantasy football: Six late-round sleepers to target I’ve narrowed this list down to six players, but I have discussed other candidates elsewhere, including some breakouts and value picks such as running backs Jordan Mason and Jonathon Brooks, wide receiver Josh Downs and tight ends Isaiah Likely and Chigoziem Okonkwo. Now it’s time to read on and take your shots. May you strike gold! It is never too late to see some players you might want to take a flyer on at the end of your fantasy draft. Tell us which sleepers you are excited to take this year in fantasy; drop them in the comments!

title: Ja’Marr Chase likes the new ‘Mean Joe’ Burrow
summary: Joe Burrow has always been competitive. Apparently, we haven’t seen anything yet. The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback has made it clear throughout the offseason that he intends to take a more vocal, and sometimes less forgiving, approach to leadership in 2026. Now, Ja’Marr Chase says he is seeing that version of Burrow firsthand. And Chase loves it. Chase […]
full_text: Joe Burrow has always been competitive. Apparently, we haven’t seen anything yet. The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback has made it clear throughout the offseason that he intends to take a more vocal, and sometimes less forgiving, approach to leadership in 2026. Now, Ja’Marr Chase says he is seeing that version of Burrow firsthand. And Chase loves it. Chase was recently asked about the emergence of what has come to be known as “Mean Joe” Burrow. “I like it when Joe’s like that,” Chase said. “I like it when he’s pissed. I like the fire that he has. He don’t always bring it out.” The year of "mean" Joe Burrow is upon us and @Real10jayy__ is loving it 😡 @CameronWolfe | @MarcRoss | @Bengals pic.twitter.com/O470DElFjh — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) August 9, 2026 Chase said the difference isn’t difficult to spot. Burrow talked about changing his leadership style during the offseason, saying he wanted to create a greater sense of urgency throughout the organization. He acknowledged that part of that meant being willing to immediately call out things that weren’t meeting the Bengals’ standard, sometimes a little louder than he had in the past. “I want to say his demeanor is just more aggressive,” Chase said. “His face is more aggressive; the way he talks is more aggressive. He got like a little mean mug on his face. I kinda like when he’s like that.” There is an obvious reason for the change. Cincinnati has missed the playoffs three consecutive seasons. The Bengals have had a quarterback capable of playing at an elite level and one of the NFL’s most dangerous offensive weapons in Chase, yet those pieces haven’t translated into postseason football recently. That has helped create a different atmosphere around the team heading into 2026. Burrow seems determined to make sure everyone feels that urgency. There have already been signs of a more intense training camp. Competition between Cincinnati’s offense and revamped defense has occasionally become heated, including an early-camp practice scuffle. The players involved dismissed any suggestion of lingering hostility and instead pointed to the competitiveness of the practices. For Chase, apparently, that’s exactly the version of Burrow he wants to see. The chemistry between the two has never been much of a question. Their relationship goes back to LSU, and Chase knows Burrow about as well as anyone in the Bengals locker room. So, when Chase notices something different about his quarterback, it carries some weight. The Bengals have spent much of the offseason talking about expectations, urgency, and the need to turn a talented roster into actual results. Burrow appears to have decided that one way he can help make that happen is by demanding more from both himself and everyone around him. If that means Cincinnati gets a slightly angrier Joe Burrow in 2026, Chase is all for it. And if “Mean Joe” helps get the Bengals back into the postseason, chances are Chase won’t be the only one who likes him.

title: Myles Murphy says Boye Mafe’s impact on Bengals goes well beyond the pass rush
summary: When the Cincinnati Bengals added Boye Mafe this offseason, the obvious expectation was that he would help the pass rush. According to Myles Murphy, Mafe is bringing considerably more than that. The knowledge Mafe has brought to Cincinnati’s defensive front is one of the biggest things that has impressed Murphy so far through camp. “That’s […]
full_text: When the Cincinnati Bengals added Boye Mafe this offseason, the obvious expectation was that he would help the pass rush. According to Myles Murphy, Mafe is bringing considerably more than that. The knowledge Mafe has brought to Cincinnati’s defensive front is one of the biggest things that has impressed Murphy so far through camp. “That’s one of the big reasons why we got him here,” Murphy said recently. “Of course he can rush; he’s a big, twitchy player, but his IQ is very high as well.” “His football IQ is second to none. He knows ball.” Myles Murphy on Boye Mafe and the impact he’s had on him and Bengals D. pic.twitter.com/EcvvEeuSNo — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) August 9, 2026 Mafe arrived in Cincinnati after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seattle Seahawks and helping them to a Super Bowl championship last year. The former second-round pick has 20 career sacks and gives the Bengals an experienced edge presence as they reshape their defensive front. Murphy is entering a pivotal season of his own. The Bengals’ 2023 first-round pick has shown flashes during his first three years in Cincinnati, with last year being his best to date with 52 total tackles, 5.5 sacks, a fumble recovery and three passes defensed. The addition of an experienced player such as Mafe gives Murphy someone alongside him who can help with the finer points of playing the position. That veteran influence has become a theme throughout Cincinnati’s defense. Mafe is among a group of experienced newcomers who have taken on vocal roles, and Murphy has specifically talked about learning from the veterans Cincinnati brought into the building. The results are beginning to show on the practice field as well. Mafe and Murphy were among the standouts during Cincinnati’s first padded practice, repeatedly creating pressure and disrupting the offense in the backfield. Murphy also offered some insight into what defensive coordinator Al Golden is trying to accomplish schematically. “He never wants to give the quarterback a concrete look,” Murphy said. “It’s the NFL, and we’re going against the best quarterback in the league every single day, so the last thing we want to do is to sit still and give him a concrete read.” For Murphy, though, perhaps the biggest change entering this season isn’t another player or even Golden’s scheme. It’s confidence. “More so just knowing who I am and seeing who I can be,” Murphy said. “Having that confidence and sureness in the defense and knowing that we’re going to get on the ball and balling out.” That’s an encouraging statement from a player the Bengals have been waiting to see take the next step. Murphy has recorded just 8.5 sacks through his first three seasons in the league. But at 24 years old, there is still plenty of reason to believe his best football could be ahead of him. And perhaps Mafe can help bring some of that out.

title: Browns still searching for DE help, work out another familiar face
summary: The Cleveland Browns knew life would be different along the defensive line after trading Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. Jared Verse was a nice return, as were the future draft picks, but the Browns also needed the remaining members of the defensive end group, most notably Alex Smith and Isaiah McGuire, to step […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 27: Za'Darius Smith #99 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates after a sack in the fourth quarter of a game against the Baltimore Ravens at Huntington Bank Field on October 27, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns knew life would be different along the defensive line after trading Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. Jared Verse was a nice return, as were the future draft picks, but the Browns also needed the remaining members of the defensive end group, most notably Alex Smith and Isaiah McGuire, to step up in support of Verse. With the first preseason game on Saturday against the Chicago Bears, and the opening game of the 2026 regular season looming in a little more than four weeks, it is fair to wonder if those plans have gone awry. On Wednesday, the Browns hosted 10 players for a tryout , with defensive end Genard Avery, who has not played since a one-game appearance with the Indianapolis Colts in 2024, on the list. Free agent pass-rusher Za’Darius Smith, who recently un-retired with the possibility of playing, worked out for the #Browns today. pic.twitter.com/l3A4lcFAp8 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 13, 2026 Today, it was time for another blast from the past as the Browns reportedly hosted free agent defensive end Za’Darius Smith for a workout, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. An 11-year veteran, Smith appeared in 25 games for the Browns, starting in 2023, before he was traded to the Detroit Lions midway through the 2024 season. Smith finished out that season with the Lions before signing with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025, only to retire after just five games with Philadelphia. Smith is a surprising name to see pop back up in Berea, but continues a trend of the Browns looking for more help at defensive end. They originally agreed to a one-year deal with free agent A.J. Epenesa before the deal fell through after Epenesa failed his physical . Cleveland also had free agent defensive end Jadeveon Clowney in for a visit and was interested in signing him, but Clowney chose to sign with the Houston Texans . Now they are eyeing Smith, who had 10.5 sacks during his time with the Browns, and 70.5 sacks for his career. He would be a veteran presence on what is mostly a young defensive line, which is nice. But after the way he walked away from the Eagles – a team with legitimate playoff aspirations – last season, the Browns have to weigh how much production he may still bring to the field vs. how much his heart is really still in the game.

full_text: When the Cleveland Browns traded DE Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams , GM Andrew Berry made it clear that acquiring DE Jared Verse was the key to the whole deal . Analyzing the deal overall was difficult, as Verse’s trade value was hard to calculate as a player at a premium position, going into his third season, with his impressive NFL resume already in hand (DROY, 2 Pro Bowls), just doesn’t change hands in a trade. While we asked whether you thought Verse could compete with Garrett’s sack totals in 2026 , there is obviously a big difference between the two pass rushers. As the Rams showed in what they were willing to trade away, Garrett’s value is much higher in 2026 than Verse’s. Long-term, if Cleveland can turn those extra picks into productive players, the trade could more than even out. Especially if Verse has a “monster year,” as NFL Network’s Brian Baldinger predicts: "Just watch out for the year Jared Verse has." @BaldyNFL has eyes on Jared Verse 👀 pic.twitter.com/URzXHMUryu — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) August 12, 2026 In two seasons, Verse has had 12 sacks, 124 tackles, 22 tackles for loss, 45 QB hits, five forced fumbles, three passes defended, and two fumble recoveries. A “monster year” could see him match some of those totals in one season alone. What do you think are realistic expectations for Verse in 2026? What would a “monster year” look like then? full_text: Browns coach Todd Monken addresses his players after Browns training camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus of the Cleveland Browns in Berea, Ohio on June 9, 2026. on July, 31, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Fans of the Cleveland Browns are oh so close to getting to see what the team will look like on the field under HC Todd Monken after six seasons with HC Kevin Stefanski. DBN readers are mostly positive about Monken so far , despite him “dithering” over the quarterback decision , but everything changes when preseason games are played. Then everything changes when it comes time for the regular season. Browns GM Andrew Berry has once again been proven to provide the team with quality young guys , with his last two NFL draft classes shining. The lack of certainty at the quarterback position continues to “suck up all the oxygen,” but Cleveland’s roster has a lot of exciting pieces on it heading into the 2026 season. Besides making the oxygen-related comment, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer also came away impressed with the Browns coaching staff and new players during his day with the team: • One thing that was really noticeable to me was the pace and vibe of this place. There’s a lot of energy in how Monken and coordinators Travis Switzer, Mike Rutenberg and Byron Storer, all first-timers in their roles, are leading. The makeup of the past two draft classes—players such as Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson, Harold Fannin Jr., Spencer Fano, KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston—is undeniably part of it. So, too, are the new guys coming in. Jared Verse, acquired in June in the trade for Myles Garrett , has wasted no time taking a major leadership role in the locker room and has quickly emerged as a tone-setter. And linebacker Quincy Williams, who was with Rutenberg for four years with the Jets, has done the same. What will that add up to? I think a team that buys in and plays hard. We’ll see how it translates to wins and losses. As Breer notes, playing hard and being bought in doesn’t guarantee anything in the win-loss column. It is, however, always notable when national media come around for their once-a-year visit to Berea. Unlike the media and fans that are present and checking in regularly, Breer’s visit gives him a snapshot from year to year to see the changes and growth. His statement echoes some of what I heard and noticed in my visit to Browns training camp this year. The speed and amount of reps that the team is going through under Monken is more, by a significant amount, compared to Stefanski. title: Dallas Cowboys named most valuable professional sports franchise again
summary: Death, taxes, and the Dallas Cowboys being worth a ton of money. Technically speaking here “a ton” simply means more than literally everyone else. Wednesday saw Sportico release their annual rankings and you will be shocked to learn that the Cowboys are once again kings. According to Sportico, the Cowboys are valued at $15.5B. That […]
full_text: OXNARD, CA - JULY 28: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones (right) and chief operating officer Stephen Jones take their seats for an opening press conference at training camp on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, in Oxnard, Calif. (Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images) Death, taxes, and the Dallas Cowboys being worth a ton of money. Technically speaking here “a ton” simply means more than literally everyone else. Wednesday saw Sportico release their annual rankings and you will be shocked to learn that the Cowboys are once again kings. According to Sportico, the Cowboys are valued at $15.5B. That B stands for billion, by the way. The ranking in question focuses mostly on the NFL and it should come as no surprise that most teams are ridiculously loaded. The Cowboys have a lead of almost $3 billion against the closest NFL team as the Los Angeles Rams sit valued at $12.7B. Perhaps the most interesting set of data in this analysis is the operating profits of each team. The Cowboys literally doubled up their nearest challenger, once again the Rams, as they had $510M in profit last year compared to L.A.’s $255M. The Cowboys are in a league of their own with $1.3 billion in revenue—Real Madrid is the only sports franchise to post more. America’s Team owns the NFC’s longest active drought without a conference championship game appearance, but its local revenue is still nearly 70% higher than the Rams in second. Dallas’ estimated $510 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization is twice the Rams’ runner-up total and nearly 4x the league average EBITDA of $139 million. Real Madrid had $279 million in EBITDA before player trading. The Cowboys are the only team that operates outside of the league’s shared merchandise system. It is a business that generates nearly $200 million in annual revenue. Dallas has re-upped several of its biggest sponsors over the past year, and the club’s $300 million in annual sponsorship revenue is nearly twice that of any other team. Dallas is also among the top clubs for generating revenue outside of NFL events, alongside the Rams, Dolphins, Raiders and Atlanta Falcons. Top teams generate more than $100 million in gross revenue, and profits run into the tens of millions of dollars from concerts and other events, money that’s captured in Sportico ‘s revenue reporting. Again, none of this is shocking to anyone who has been paying attention. The Cowboys are worth an enormous amount of money and if they were ever sold they would go for a figure that is difficult to conceive. Consider that the Los Angeles Lakers were sold about an hour after the Sportico report went live and that they went for $12.5B. The Cowboys would go for a much, much higher amount.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 31
summary: It is Day 31 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES - OCTOBER 14: Running back Calvin Hill #35 of the Dallas Cowboys runs upfield against the Los Angeles Rams at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles, California. The Rams defeated the Cowboys 37-31. (Photo by James Flores/Getty Images) It is Day 31 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Here we go for Day 31 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the beginning of one of the defining NFC playoff rivalries of the 1970s. Dallas watched a 17-point lead shrink against the Los Angeles Rams, but a rookie Drew Pearson delivered the decisive play in a divisional-round victory. Sunday, December 23, 1973 — 4:00 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Los Angeles Rams 16 The Cowboys entered at 10-4 after winning six of their final seven regular-season games in 1973 to capture the NFC East. Los Angeles had finished 12-2 and had already beaten Dallas 37-31 in October, when Harold Jackson torched the Cowboys for 238 receiving yards and four first-half touchdowns. The playoff rematch gave Tom Landry’s defense an opportunity to correct one of its worst performances of the season. Dallas created immediate separation through its defense. Lee Roy Jordan intercepted John Hadl on the first play of the game, setting up Calvin Hill’s three-yard touchdown run. Mel Renfro then recovered a Lawrence McCutcheon fumble, and Roger Staubach converted the second takeaway into a four-yard touchdown pass to Pearson. Before the Rams could settle into the game, the Cowboys led 14-0. Toni Fritsch extended the advantage with a 39-yard field goal, but Los Angeles slowly began working its way back. David Ray made field goals from 33 and 37 yards before halftime, cutting the score to 17-6. Dallas had controlled the beginning of the game, yet the Rams’ defensive front was beginning to make every possession difficult. The third quarter passed without either team scoring, and Ray’s 40-yard field goal reduced the margin to eight early in the fourth. Hill then lost a fumble, giving Los Angeles the short field it needed. Tony Baker scored on a five-yard run, leaving Dallas ahead only 17-16 with approximately 10 minutes remaining. Momentum had completely shifted. Staubach was sacked seven times, including twice by Merlin Olsen and two-and-a-half times by Jack Youngblood, and Dallas had managed only four first downs since building its 17-0 lead. Another Olsen sack placed the Cowboys in a long-yardage situation with the Rams threatening to take control. Staubach responded with a short throw over the middle to Pearson. Rams defensive backs Dave Elmendorf and Steve Preece collided while closing on the rookie receiver, clearing the field in front of him. Pearson raced untouched for an 83-yard touchdown, turning what appeared likely to be a modest gain into the play that saved Dallas’ season. The touchdown restored an eight-point lead, and Fritsch later added a short field goal to complete the scoring. Dallas’ defense prevented another response, finishing with five sacks while holding Harold Jackson to one reception for 40 yards. The Rams were limited to 192 total yards after gaining 383 against Dallas earlier that season. This game belongs on the countdown because it began the postseason rivalry between Dallas and Los Angeles while producing the first iconic playoff moment of Pearson’s career. The Cowboys survived seven sacks, a fourth-quarter collapse and a Rams team that had already beaten them once. #Cowboys vs #Rams 1973 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Los Angeles Rams 16 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/qzIiZWbwug — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 13, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game This was the first postseason meeting between the Cowboys and Rams. The franchises would meet eight more times in the playoffs, making it one of the most frequently contested postseason matchups in NFL history. Just the fact that he’ll be back in pads soon is a win for Dallas.

title: Cowboys players who might be losing their roster battles
summary: The Cowboys recently visited the Los Angeles Rams for an intra-squad scrimmage. The Rams are loaded with talent and among the favorites to contend for the Super Bowl, making them a very good measuring stick for Dallas. Although the scrimmage wasn’t open to the public, news has emerged about who stood out and who didn’t […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 25: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys hands the ball off to Malik Davis #43 during the second half of the NFL game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cowboys recently visited the Los Angeles Rams for an intra-squad scrimmage. The Rams are loaded with talent and among the favorites to contend for the Super Bowl, making them a very good measuring stick for Dallas. Although the scrimmage wasn’t open to the public, news has emerged about who stood out and who didn’t fare as well. For example, reserve linebacker Justin Barron recorded three interceptions, and Shavon Revel had a strong day in coverage. For the team, it’s a moment to feel great about where they are and also a chance to recalibrate before Saturday’s preseason opener. For some players, it unfortunately illustrated the need to pick it up before it’s too late. Before Dallas travels to Seattle, let’s examine who is on the hot seat. Here are four players already in danger of missing the cut. Sam Howell Offhand, can you think of one Sam Howell highlight at training camp? Sam Howell is in open competition for the backup quarterback job with Joe Milton. Milton, who has had trouble with accuracy since joining the Cowboys, has made some good throws thus far. His athleticism has allowed him to extend plays and make big-time throws outside of the framework of the offense. For Howell, he hasn’t flashed as much and has taken a backseat to Milton. Howell has much more regular season experience than Milton does, but right now Howell is on the outside looking in. Don’t expect Dallas to carry three quarterbacks on the active roster. There still would be an avenue for Howell to remain with the team on the practice squad, but as of now, it’s hard to imagine Howell making the 53-man roster. Malik Davis While at first some might have thought Phil Mafah is the running back in the most trouble to make the team, it’s actually Malik Davis who is in hot water. From what we’ve seen, Javonte Williams is the top runner, followed by Jaydon Blue, and then Phil Mafah according to the team’s depth chart. While Davis has more value on special teams than Mafah does, Mafah is the more powerful, downhill mauler like Javonte Williams, and Blue has that second gear of speed that Davis almost has, making Davis’ role somewhat redundant when you factor Blue’s explosiveness. Mafah does need to stack together a few really good games in the preseason to hold his spot ahead of Davis, but it looks like he’s very much ahead. Also, don’t forget about Israel Abanikanda. He’s got a physical running style and very good speed who could showcase his talents in the later stages of these upcoming preseason games. He may also get some opportunities on kickoffs as well. Things are looking murky for Davis right now. Anthony Smith The Dallas Cowboys boast a very good wide receiver group where it would be hard to get targets outside of the top three receivers, let alone earn a spot on the team. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens spearhead the pecking order. Meanwhile, Ryan Flournoy looks primed to be an essential third receiver to further elevate the group. KaVontae Turpin is still recognized in the NFL as one of the best return specialists in the league. You can practically pencil him in as the fourth receiver. This leaves Anthony Smith battling for one roster spot with the remainder of the field. Can Smith outshine Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Jonathan Mingo, Traeshon Holden, Camden Brown or Denzel Mims for a spot? From what we’ve seen, it doesn’t look likely. He’s going to have to step up tremendously to even have a remote chance. His status as a seventh-round draft pick isn’t enough investment from the team to feel uncomfortable parting with him, and without some splash moments during the preseason, it’s not looking good for the rookie receiver. Markquese Bell The Cowboys have completely reconstructed the safety position, and that’s somewhat due in part to Christian Parker’s influence. Not only did the Cowboys land Caleb Downs, who can play the slot or either safety position, they also signed veteran Jalen Thompson before the draft. Malik Hooker redid his contract to remain with the team, so his place is cemented for this season. Where it gets dicey for Bell is being able to separate himself from others for down-roster spots on the depth chart. P.J. Locke was signed because of his connection to Parker. Julius Wood and Alijah Clark are also in the mix. Bell arguably might be the most limited safety in terms of range in pass coverage on the team. He’s the safest player on this, but nowhere near where he should feel comfortable.

title: Undrafted free agents on offense that could make roster
summary: Being an undrafted free agent means you have a steep hill to climb, not just to make the roster, but even getting regular reps in camp can be hard. UDFAs have to work harder, have fewer mistakes, and ultimately stand out with the few reps they get, making their journey to the 53-man roster excruciatingly […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys receiver Camden Brown (6) catches the ball at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Being an undrafted free agent means you have a steep hill to climb, not just to make the roster, but even getting regular reps in camp can be hard. UDFAs have to work harder, have fewer mistakes, and ultimately stand out with the few reps they get, making their journey to the 53-man roster excruciatingly difficult. However, some have made it; Dallas fans need to look no further than their own Tony Romo. This year, we’ll look at a group of players who have hope to make the 53-man roster going into the preseason. TE Michael Trigg The tight end room is crowded in Big D, and it’s safe to say the training camp battles are just beginning, but we know that Jake Ferguson and Brevyn Spann-Ford are locks to make the roster. Spann-Ford is a plus blocker with elite size, and he has put that on display thus far, and Ferg is, well, Ferg. But looking beyond those two spots, Luke Schoonmaker has suddenly been thrust into “could be cut” conversations, and it’s because Michael Trigg has made an impression. Trigg’s work ethic stands out, but more than that, his ability to catch the ball is at a level that is making the coaching staff take notice. Michael Trigg with a tough catch in traffic pic.twitter.com/Gr5GtFA1qY — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 4, 2026 With that said, Dallas values blocking TEs very highly, much like they value blocking running backs. Unless Trigg makes a huge leap in blocking, an area he still needs to improve, Schoonmaker could very well make the grade once again. UDFA RB It would appear that the Cowboys are still looking for something else at the running back position behind Javonte Williams. On Monday, August 9, Dallas held three tryouts in one day for the RB position. Jashaun Corbin, Hassan Haskins and Zamir White. They signed Corbin and then waived ex-Tulsa RB Dominic Richardson. These moves don’t sound like solely a search for a camp body. It seems that the search is on for somebody to step up and raise the competition. Jaydon Blue has had some nice plays in camp, and Phil Mafah has had his moments, but the search was still on at the position. The Cowboys seemed poised to have answers at every level of that position, and so far, they haven’t found exactly what they want. There is going to be a path for Corbin to make this roster, albeit a very difficult one; he has to show he can do a little more than Phil Mafah and Malik Davis. In what seems like a signing of no consequence, Jashaun Corbin brings a nice one-cut ability, good vision, and all-purpose flexibility that fits well with the Cowboys. While his chances to make the roster are low, he's on the right team to give himself a fighting chance. pic.twitter.com/qCyZw8gKGq — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) August 8, 2026 WR Camden Brown Camden Brown is quickly emerging as someone who might snatch the last receiver spot in camp, much to the chagrin of Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Jonathan Mingo. The former Georgia Southern wide receiver has rapidly played his way into the roster conversation with a string of highly impressive practices and some amazing catches that have caught people’s attention. This includes hauling back-to-back touchdown catches from backup quarterback Sam Howell in consecutive practices. Camden Brown with an impressive TD grab pic.twitter.com/jDx160UitH — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 8, 2026 Yet another athletic Camden Brown grab, but just one foot in. Alijah Clark: “That’s a great college catch.” Brown scores a TD one play later pic.twitter.com/Pl7BrtdI2w — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 9, 2026 At 6’2″ and 205 pounds, Brown is using his catch radius to his advantage in practice. So far, he has showcased incredible body control and boundary awareness, something that Mingo or Valdes-Scantling have not done since the start of camp, and with both of their stocks trending down, it looks like Brown may have a real shot at that final receiver spot in Dallas.

title: 3 surprise cuts the Cowboys could make
summary: When you examine the Dallas roster in contrast to the end of last season, things certainly have improved in some troublesome areas. Entering the year, the Cowboys needed to enhance the safety and linebacker positions. The Cowboys had their prayers answered when Caleb Downs fell to them in the draft, and he has been good […]
full_text: OXNARD, CA - AUGUST 05: Dallas Cowboys offensive tackle Nate Thomas (71) during the Los Angeles Rams - Dallas Cowboys joint Training Camp on August 05, 2025, at the River Ridge Playing Fields in Oxnard, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When you examine the Dallas roster in contrast to the end of last season, things certainly have improved in some troublesome areas. Entering the year, the Cowboys needed to enhance the safety and linebacker positions. The Cowboys had their prayers answered when Caleb Downs fell to them in the draft, and he has been good as advertised. The linebacker position also appears better with a healthy DeMarvion Overshown, Dee Winters, and surprise rookie Jaishawn Barham. Furthermore, the Cowboys have good depth in other areas, making roster cuts at the end of the summer difficult. Yearly, the Cowboys make their trim to 53 players, and it raises a stir as some pet cats are thrown out to waivers and cuts raise an eyebrow. Fast forward to this season, and the question sparks anew. Who might the Cowboys cut that would surprise us? Luke Schoonmaker Cutting a second-round pick for nothing in return should cause a stir. So maybe the Cowboys trade him. But if they can’t cut a deal, they may have to cut the player. The Cowboys just lost a tight end to injury for the season after Princeton Fant was placed on injured reserve. Yet, Brevyn Spann-Ford has seemingly made enough progress for the Cowboys to rid themselves of Schoonmaker. Spann-Ford has made plays during training camp and also caught a touchdown during the scrimmage against the Los Angeles Rams. He is clearly the best blocker out of the tight end group on the team, with just enough athleticism to provide an option as a pass catcher in spurts. With both in the final year of their contracts, Spann-Ford seems like the the likelier choice to hold a spot on the roster as of now. Beyond that, Michael Trigg is starting to demonstrate his skills as a mismatch for smaller defenders. Cutting (or trading) Schoonmaker would give Dallas a tight end group that has Jake Ferguson and Spann-Ford locked, plus one of the trio of Trigg, D.J. Rogers or the newly-arrived Zack Kuntz. Nate Thomas My, how things have changed. At one point during the offseason, Nate Thomas was competing with Tyler Guyton for starting left tackle spot. Now that Guyton has won the job, Thomas could very well be on the outs with the team. Thomas is now more likely competing with Drew Shelton in a battle where, politically, the battle may already be over. It would be unlikely that the Cowboys part with a player they just selected in the fourth round. Shortly after the draft, coach Schottenheimer spoke very highly of Shelton, and even though he has started on a rough patch, that was to be expected. However, that can’t explain why Nate Thomas hasn’t looked markedly better than the rookie. Although, Thomas has occupied the swing tackle spot in the past, Ajani Cornelius looks to be on track to make the team. Dallas could look to another veteran on the free agent market since outside of the starting five, the Cowboys don’t have much proven depth. Thomas also wasn’t very good in his outings last season. He ranked dead last among qualified tackles in pass protection per PFF.com, allowing 23 quarterback pressures. James Houston James Houston has provided the Cowboys with a solid option for depth as a reserve edge rusher, and the transition to standup linebacker suits his talents well. The Cowboys struggled with the pass rush last season, but Houston’s 5.5 sacks were more than a welcome addition. So why? Why would the Cowboys elect to drop Houston after the preseason? In short, it’s a numbers game. Newcomer Rashan Gary will occupy a starting spot as will second-year player Donovan Ezeiruaku, and Dallas took Malachi Lawrence in the first round. Plus, Sam Williams returned to the team and has had a very good training camp. Ultimately, the Houston decision comes down to potential and versatility. LT Overton has done well as a run defender in Oxnard, and Marist Liufau has shown the willingness to do whatever is asked of him, whether he is playing as an outside linebacker and occasionally roaming to an off-ball linebacker. Pluse, he can help on special teams. While it would raise an eyebrow, Dallas cutting Houston to keep Liufau and Overton could make sense.

title: Cowboys news: Dallas showed improvements in key areas vs Rams
summary: The Dallas Cowboys came into the offseason needing to show vast improvement in the red zone offense from a year ago. In their joint practice with the Rams, it was clear that an elevation in that regard has taken place. The team will have to open up the bank if they want to keep wide […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys came into the offseason needing to show vast improvement in the red zone offense from a year ago. In their joint practice with the Rams, it was clear that an elevation in that regard has taken place. The team will have to open up the bank if they want to keep wide receiver George Pickens long term, but they can do so and still keep their other stars on the team. The preseason starts this weekend, and several veterans will be fighting to stay on the roster. Cowboys’ offense shows welcomed red zone improvement in joint practice with Rams – Jon Machota, The Athletic One of the biggest weaknesses of the Cowboys’ offense last season was red zone efficiency. During their scrimmage with the Rams, the improvement was noticeable. Offense • The first-team offense was very good in red zone work. Dak Prescott had two touchdown passes to CeeDee Lamb, one to KaVontae Turpin and another to tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford. The best highlight of the four was probably a back-shoulder throw to Lamb. Prescott also had a touchdown pass on a slant to Ryan Flournoy. That’s one of the biggest areas the Cowboys need to improve on from a year ago. The extra work they’ve been putting in during camp practices appears to be paying off. Overshown: ‘It felt good’ to see Cowboys’ improvements come to life in Rams joint practice – Todd Brock, Cowboys Wire It wasn’t the best showing for the Cowboys’ defense in their joint practice with the Rams in 2025. That changed earlier this week when the two teams linked up in Los Angeles. Hanging with- and even getting the better of- one of the preseason Super Bowl favorites, Overshown admitted, made it feel even better. “It’s good to hit a different color jersey. I feel like we’ve been going at it with our offense, and they’re one of the best in the league. So getting to see what we’ve got versus another top offense, it puts stuff in perspective,” he said. Joint practice exposes Dallas Cowboys flaw that raises serious questions right before the 2026 NFL season – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports The Cowboys had a bunch of positive things to take from their joint scrimmage with Rams. With that said, right tackle Terence Steele’s shortcomings are concerning. Steele struggles in Cowboys’ practice with Rams The Cowboys took on the Los Angeles Rams on a joint practice on Tuesday. And even though Myles Garrett was held out, Steele noticeable struggled in pass protection. The practice happened behind closed doors, so there’s limited video on it, but here’s a behind-enemy-lines look at how Steele’s day went. How the Cowboys can pay George Pickens and still keep their stars – One Cool Customer, Blogging The Boys The Cowboys won’t be getting a long-term deal done with George Pickens until the next offseason. However, thay can pay him and still keep a competitive roster. The 4-and-6 model This is the fundamental value of the rookie contract. Suppose four of those ten players are still on rookie deals, costing perhaps $4-6 million each rather than the roughly $26 million average you’d pay at the top of their respective markets. Suddenly, you’ve shaved roughly $80 million off the cost of your top ten players. That’s not a minor salary-cap advantage. That’s the mechanism that makes the entire roster possible. In a healthy roster-building cycle, you want something like six established players getting paid at or near market rates, while four of your best players are still providing production on cheap rookie contracts. Bubble ‘Boys: These Cowboys are battling for roster spots as preseason play begins – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Dallas will begin preseason play this weekend. Here’s a look at who is fighting to make the final 53-man roster. TE Luke Schoonmaker The Cowboys released their first unofficial depth chart Tuesday . There was one notable distinction. The Cowboys listed Brevyn Spann-Ford as their second tight end and Schoonmaker as their clear third. The former second-round pick is heading into a contract season and knew this was an important training camp for him. So far, he hasn’t flashed a ton and he’s had multiple drops. It also doesn’t help the Cowboys gave their biggest undrafted free agent deals this year to two tight ends. Mick Shots: Multiple benefits of Big Q extension – Mickey Spagnola, DallasCowboys.com Earlier this week, the Cowboys locked up defensive tackle Quinnen Williams for the foreseeable future. Here’s the advantages for Dallas getting the deal done. Next, this extension allows Dallas to restructure his remaining two base salaries to lower his cap charge, especially for 2026, by prorating the signing bonus over five years. That means for 2026, Williams’ $20.75 million base reduces to $1.3 million plus the $6 million proration, saving the Cowboys now a wallet full of salary cap space for this season. Also puts the $31 million in Williams’ bank account as soon as he signs the extension, so he doesn’t have to wait around for the weekly payments in 2026 to reach the $20.75 million total. Daily discussion question: Do you care if the Cowboys win their preseason games? Why or why not?

Per source, the #Broncos are no placing center Mike Deiter on season-ending IR and signing center Lecitus Smith. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) August 13, 2026 Deiter went down during practice earlier in the week and was carted off the field. Unfortunately for Deiter, he suffered a season-ending injury, according to Head Coach Sean Payton, and today the team placed the reserve center on the season-ending injured reserve. Lecitus Smith played his college ball at Virginia Tech and was a 6th-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft by the Arizona Cardinals. From there, he had stints with the Houston Texans, Philadelphia Eagles, Green Bay Packers, New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers, and, most recently, with the Green Bay Packers again. Throughout his career, Smith has appeared in 19 games and has 4 career starts, including a start last season with the Packers. Starter Luke Wattenberg has missed most of training camp thus far and has just returned to practice, but will likely not play in Friday’s preseason opener. Backup Alex Forsyth has been sidelined all this week and seems unlikely to play in the game, and as we know, third-string center Michael Deiter suffered a season-ending injury. So, they simply need some depth and bodies at the center position. Veteran offensive lineman Calvin Throckmorton and undrafted free agent Gavin Ortega have been taking snaps at center, but neither has much experience playing center. So, Smith could see a good amount of snaps and playing time during Friday’s game vs. the Falcons. Smith is a long shot to make the 53-man roster, but a good performance during the preseason could earn him a spot on the Broncos’ practice squad as their third-string center. He has experience, some starting experience and gives the Broncos some much-needed depth at the center position.

title: Broncos at Falcons: 3 players to watch in Week 1 of NFL preseason
summary: After a long wait, Denver Broncos football is finally back. This Friday, the Broncos kickoff their three-game preseason slate when they take on the Atlanta Falcons. Here are three players Broncos Country should keep their eye on closely during the game. Jonah Coleman — Running Back The first player on my radar to watch is […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - JANUARY 25: Denver Broncos mascot miles gets the crowd going during the first quarter against the New England Patriots at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, January 25, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images After a long wait, Denver Broncos football is finally back. This Friday, the Broncos kickoff their three-game preseason slate when they take on the Atlanta Falcons. Here are three players Broncos Country should keep their eye on closely during the game. Jonah Coleman — Running Back The first player on my radar to watch is running back Jonah Coleman. Throughout training camp, the rookie has impressed. Last week, Head Coach Sean Payton regarded him as one of camp’s most pleasant surprises to date. He has performed well and according to Payton, doesn’t show signs of being a rookie. Denver struggled to run the ball when J.K. Dobbins missed the latter portion of the season with an injury. While Dobbins has ‘pinky promised’ to stay healthy in 2026, he had a soft tissue injury during Monday’s practice. Denver needs a contingency plan in the event he misses time this season. That’s where Coleman factors into the equation. He was a battering ram during his collegiate years and averaged 5.5 yards per carry. Additionally, he the draft’s best backs when it came to yards after contact. The Washington Huskies standout has a nose for the endzone and notched 34 rushing touchdowns over four seasons of play. Those are all reasons why I’m excited to watch the rookie in action on Friday. Red Murdock — Inside Linebacker The top spots at inside linebacker are set in stone for the Broncos in 2026. Veterans Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad will hold down the starting positions. Who ends up winning the depth spots behind them has been one of the most intriguing camp battles thus far. One player who factors into the equation is rookie linebacker Red Murdock. Drafted with the final pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Murdock was incredibly productive during his collegiate career and made a lot of big plays. He topped Khalil Mack’s FBS all-time forced fumbles record with seventeen during his time at the University of Buffalo. Last week after practice, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph praised the rookie linebacker for his progress to date and mentioned he was eager to see him in his first NFL game this Friday. “Red’s job is a little different. He’s making the It took him a couple days to kind of get used to making the calls and playing fast. Now, he’s doing that. I’m looking forward to Friday night to see him play live action with organic looks. It’s going to be fun to see,” stated Joseph. Jahdae Barron — Cornerback For my third and final player, I’ll be zoning in on Jahdae Barron. The first-round pick spent most of his rookie season as a backup player. For the entire 2025 season, Barron played in 30-percent of the team’s defensive snaps. However, he did show some promise when on the field. With Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian Denver’s top cornerback trio, it will be interesting to see how he fits into the defensive equation in 2026. But before that happens, he needs to perform well in the preseason and make some plays on the ball. I’m not sure how much the starters will play for Denver throughout the preseason. Nevertheless, I expect Barron to get a lot of playing time leading up to the season opener against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football . I’m anxious to see if that’s primarily on the outside or at nickelback.

title: Sean Payton isn’t surprised by Pat Bryant’s progress and development
summary: When the Denver Broncos took Illinois wide receiver Pat Bryant in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, it was a pick widely criticized by pundits. Many analysts thought it was several rounds too high. Moreover, a lot of fans across Broncos Country were hoping for the franchise to address other needs earlier. But […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 06: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos runs with the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second quarter in the game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 06, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Denver Broncos took Illinois wide receiver Pat Bryant in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, it was a pick widely criticized by pundits. Many analysts thought it was several rounds too high. Moreover, a lot of fans across Broncos Country were hoping for the franchise to address other needs earlier. But the Broncos didn’t care. They got their guy—a player they believed was a perfect fit for their scheme. Not only that but Bryant’s size and traits lined up with what Head Coach Sean Payton covets at the position. For them, all those made him a no-brain decision when they were on the clock. Appearing in fifteen games with seven starts as a rookie, Bryant reeled in 31 receptions for 378 yards and 1 touchdown. He worked well operating over the middle of the field and came down with a lot of tough, contested catches. Moreover, he was one of the Broncos’ clutch performers when it came to moving the chains. Additionally, he was a fixture in Denver’s 11 personnel groupings. His prowess as a run blocker was a significant reason for Denver’s early season rushing success with J.K. Dobbins. Yesterday after practice, Payton was asked if he was surprised with the second-year wide receiver’s camp performance to date. “No. I’m excited, I’m happy because you kind of saw the beginning of it last year, but like any young player, maybe you didn’t see it as consistently as you’re seeing now. He’s a confident player with strong hands. That ability to be on the ground and not alter your feet or your foot path, I think really serves him well,” stated Payton. Bryant was the tenth wide receiver selected in his class. However, the former Illini standout outperformed a handful of players selected before him including first-round pick Matthew Golden and second-round wide receiver Tre Harris. Overall, he ranked seventh in receptions and receiving yards. A promising start to his career especially in a Broncos’ wide receiver room that saw a lot of rotation. This season, he is looking to increase his target share in a crowded wide receiver room that now features Jaylen Waddle. On the team’s initial depth chart , he is listed as a second-team player backing up longtime veteran Courtland Sutton at the ‘X’ position. Nevertheless, Bryant figures to get a lot of run this season. Appearing on the Up & Adams show with Kay Adams, Payton noted it will be hard to keep him off the field. Since being drafted, Payton and the rest of the coaching staff and players, have watched Bryant’s growth first-hand. Flashing in camp on a daily basis, Payton believes the vision they had when they made him the 74th overall selection in the 2025 NFL Draft is coming into focus. “We felt size, strong hands. He had three or four last play of the game, like fourth-and-whatever, and he catches an in-cut, and then scores and the game’s over. He had three or four of those unique, we call it walk-off touchdowns. But again, you’re projecting what you think. Then it’s certainly fun when all of a sudden you start to see that,” added Payton.

summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos tout one of the best secondaries in the league. However, the Broncos might be interested in adding some experienced depth at safety. According […]

However, the Broncos might be interested in adding some experienced depth at safety. According to Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post , the Broncos recently worked out veteran safety Taylor Rapp. A second-round draft pick of the Los Angeles Rams in the 2019 NFL Draft, Rapp has played in 93 games with 72 starts. Over seven seasons, he has notched 488 tackles, 12 interceptions, and 31 passes defended. He has been a productive player, though several hip and knee injuries have impacted his availability throughout his career. After Jones and Hufanga, five players are battling it out in training camp for depth spots on the backend of their secondary. Those players are JL Skinner, Devon Key, Tycen Anderson, Miles Scott, and Parker Robertson. Skinner, Key, and Anderson have all been top-notch special teams’ players during their time in the NFL. Scott and Robertson are both rookies this season. With P.J. Locke’s departure to the Dallas Cowboys in free agency, Denver may be looking for a more experienced player to assume his role with the team. None of the five players vying for a backup role have any significant in-game snaps. For perspective, Locke had over 1,800 defensive snaps during his time with the Broncos as a reserve and pinch-starter. Rapp has over 4,800 defensive snaps in his career. Maybe it means nothing, but maybe it means something. In the event either Jones or Hufanga missed time, it could be wise to have a veteran player who has a lot of starting experience as one of their depth players. What do you think, Broncos Country? Would you be interested in the Broncos signing Rapp? Let me know in the comments section. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: Ahmed Hassanein called his shot, sacking Joe Burrow on 1st snap
summary: Detroit Lions defensive end Ahmed Hassanein had to compose himself. He had just accomplished a life-long dream of his and was breaking down and crying. But it was third down, and the second-team Lions defense was trying to get an early stop going against the Cincinnati Bengals. Let’s back up. Before Thursday night’s preseason opener, […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive lineman Ahmed Hassanein (61) speaks after practice during rookie mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 9, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Detroit Lions defensive end Ahmed Hassanein had to compose himself. He had just accomplished a life-long dream of his and was breaking down and crying. But it was third down, and the second-team Lions defense was trying to get an early stop going against the Cincinnati Bengals. Let’s back up. Before Thursday night’s preseason opener, Hassanein was getting in one last cram session. He was watching tape, preparing for his first football action since last preseason, and, more importantly, he was manifesting. He knew he was going up against one of the best quarterbacks in football in Joe Burrow. All he wanted was to sack Burrow. So he spent all day telling everyone—coach Dan Campbell, his wife—that he was going to do just that. “I truly, truly prayed about it and I manifested it,” Hassanein said after the game. “And I said, I’m going to sack him before the game. And coach Campbell said the same thing. I just kept telling my wife, ‘I’m going to sack Joe Burrow, I’m going to get him.’ I just kept talking to God about it.” Then, on the Lions’ fourth defensive snap of the game, Hassanein substituted in for his first snap of preseason football. You already know what happened next: Ahmed got 'em! pic.twitter.com/qLYfqIXgVr — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 13, 2026 After initially getting stymied, Hassanein made an inside move, tapped into his relentless motor, and took down Burrow. And when it happened, the emotions overtook the moment. “I cried. I didn’t know what to do. I literally broke down,” Hassanein said. “But I had to go back on defense.” Hassanein has been one of the biggest stories of Lions training camp. Coming into 2026, he was still considered a very raw player with a great story and an even greater football character, but expectations remained relatively low. However, he’s been one of the most explosive and consistent playmakers on defense since camp opened up. And by translating that promise on game days, he’s starting to earn the trust of his coaches. “I don’t feel like I’m surprised,” coach Dan Campbell said Thursday night. “I felt like they came out and made plays. Just the way Ahmed played, the things he’s able to do, you feel like it would translate, certainly with this preseason. It was good to see, it was maximum effort.” Hassanein wasn’t even done for the night. In the third quarter, he bent around the Bengals left tackle, and swatted the ball out of Josh Johnson’s hands for a third-down strip sack. That, too, was the result of his relentless preparation. “We always credit (defensive line) coach Kacy Rodgers. When you get a rush, you have to reach for it,” Hassanein said. “When the ball is going to be there—we call it a tomahawk on air—you just reach, reach, reach, reach. And then the ball is going to be there.” Hassanein’s story has now become much more than just a feel-good narrative to take you through the offseason. He has a real chance to not only make the roster, but to make an impact on defense this year. But the second-year defensive lineman is not thinking too far down the road. “There is so much work to be done, and I have a feeling I’m going to get so much better because I’m going to keep working,” Hassanein said. “I’m going to keep stacking, and I’m just going to not look too far ahead and too far behind.”

full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals running back Tahj Brooks (25) runs with the ball against Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (2) in the first half at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions had a couple of injury scares during their preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals. But it appears it’s mostly—if not, all—good news for Detroit. After the game, Lions coach Dan Campbell said that Ennis Rakestraw appears to have avoided a major injury. At the start of the second quarter, Rakestraw took some friendly fire from linebacker Devin White, and a few plays later he made a low tackle on a play and did not initially come up. After walking off the field under his own power and going into the medical tent, he went into the locker room and did not return. However, Rakestraw got an x-ray which showed no structural damage , and Campbell says it could be something as small as an arm contusion. “It’s not major. It ended up being—it’s not a head shot—we just think he got a little contusion in the arm,” Campbell said. “It kinda made it numb, so I think he’ll be alright.” Later in the second quarter, third-year defensive tackle Mekhi Wingo suffered an injury and did not return. Campbell downplayed the injury but did admit he may be entering concussion protocol. “He just got a little bit of a—got his bell rung a little bit,” Campbell said. “So he could be (in) concussion protocol—but I don’t feel like any of those (injuries) are serious.” The last player injured could be the one that may be more serious. Lions safety Loren Strickland came up limping while chasing down a receiver in the second half. Campbell said he’s still hopeful for Strickland, but they need to do some imaging first. “I think all of those guys are okay. Strickland, I think, right now is the one that’s going to be—don’t know. We’ve got to get an image on that,” Campbell said. Overall, that’s all pretty good news to get out of Cincinnati with minimal injuries.
