title: 6 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ 16-14 loss to the Bengals
summary: It’s that time of year again; football is back in action! While it’s just a preseason game, this is still the first full game the Detroit Lions have had since January, a long seven months ago. In the preseason opener, the Lions traveled to Cincinnati to take on the Cincinnati Bengals. While the Lions played […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Tight end Jack Endries #84 of the Cincinnati Bengals scores a touchdown in a preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals on August 13, 2026, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s that time of year again; football is back in action! While it’s just a preseason game, this is still the first full game the Detroit Lions have had since January, a long seven months ago. In the preseason opener, the Lions traveled to Cincinnati to take on the Cincinnati Bengals. While the Lions played a few starters, the Bengals trouted out the majority, if not all, of theirs. The Detroit offensive starters who played were right tackle Blake Miller, left guard Christian Mahogany, and wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa. On the defensive side, safety Chuck Clark (projected to start with Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch on PUP) was out there along with Tyler Lacy. These preseason games are less about winning and losing and more about how players competing for a starting job or a roster spot perform. These are games where someone can make the roster, and someone else could be sent home. It’s only the first of three games, so while this game is important, it’s not the end-all, be-all. Here are my six takeaways from the Lions’ Preseason Week 1 16-14 loss. Jacob Saylors could be a threat for RB3 The running back position might have an unexpected battle at the RB3 spot. Jahmyr Gibbs is clearly the starting running back after signing a new contract extension earlier in August, making him the highest-paid running back in the NFL. Behind him is no longer David Montgomery, but Isiah Pacheco. At third string, it’s presumed that Sione Vaki will lock that job up. Unfortunately, the injury bug has continued to strike Vaki, this time resulting in a broken nose and an eye injury. That has led to fourth-string running back Jacob Saylors getting a lot of playing time in training camp, with Gibbs holding in before his extension was signed, and Pacheco and Vaki battling injuries. In the game Thursday night, Saylors had a strong showing, getting eight carries for 55 yards and three catches for 28 yards. Saylors was RB4 last year, primarily on kick return for special teams, but if he can continue to have good days like Thursday, he might upend Vaki for the third-string spot. With the rest of August to prove himself, this is a good start for Saylors to have a bigger role in the Lions offense. Ahmed Hassanein continues to impress Last year, the former sixth-round pick, EDGE Ahmed Hassanein, was doing well in the preseason and showed promise for a bright future. Unfortunately, he suffered a pec injury, which led the Lions to release him while he rehabbed. He was brought back in November 2025 and remained on the practice squad for the entire 2025 season. This year, Hassanein is healthy and has been impressing in training camp so far. On the Lions’ first defensive drive, he sacked Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. Ahmed got 'em! pic.twitter.com/qLYfqIXgVr — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 13, 2026 Hassanein finished the game with four tackles, two sacks, and a forced fumble. Hassanein is a great story and a pass rusher that the team has been needing on its roster. With him back healthy, he will bring a great fire to the defensive line this season if he can keep this up. Offensive line with a rough performance With only two starting offensive linemen playing, it was a lot of players mixing and moving around with different teammates next to them. Rookie right tackle Blake Miller looked well, not allowing a sack and keeping both quarterbacks upright. Offensive lineman Miles Frazier, who has played everywhere but center so far this preseason, had a rough game. Third-string center Seth McLaughlin got the start with injuries to starting center Cade Mays and backup Juice Scruggs, showed why he’s a third-stringer. The biggest story of the offensive line was Mahogany struggling, getting called for two penalties. Mahogany had a rough season last year, and with his job not yet secure, the type of game he had wasn’t what you wanted to see. He’s had limited competition behind him, as backup guard Ben Bartch has been dealing with an injury, with Frazier and Scruggs bouncing around the offensive line. The good news is that Frazier and McLaughlin aren’t projected to start, but these players and others were playing alongside people they haven’t had much time to gel with. It’s tough to showcase what you can do when you don’t have the experience with the guy next to you. The chemistry you can build with the rest of your offensive line is important, and it showed Thursday night. Isaac TeSlaa’s rough preseason continues With the Lions moving on from wide receiver Kalif Raymond, that means TeSlaa moves up to the WR3 spot. After impressing with multiple one-handed catches in his rookie season last year, expectations are a bit higher for TeSlaa in 2026. With TeSlaa having higher expectations, the pressure might be getting to him. He’s been having a tough camp so far, getting challenged early and often. Against the Bengals, he had a chance to rebound. Instead of bouncing back, his struggles continued. In the first quarter, Lions quarterback Luke Altmyer threw a pass to TeSlaa, and it bounced off TeSlaa’s helmet up high and was picked off by the Bengals. After punting on their next offensive series, the Lions came out afterward, drove down the field, and went for it on fourth down. Altmyer threw a pass right into TeSlaa’s hands, and he dropped it, causing a turnover on downs. With three targets, TeSlaa came up empty-handed Thursday night. I don’t think his job is in jeopardy, but he could still fall down the depth chart back to WR4 if things don’t improve soon. Injury scares arise on the defense So far in the preseason, the injuries have begun to strike the roster. On Thursday night, the Lions saw two defensive players leave with injuries. The first was cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr., who left the game in the second quarter and didn’t return. Rakestraw is currently battling for the CB2 job with veteran Rock Ya-Sin and has Nick Whiteside right behind him. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said after the game that they don’t believe Rakestraw’s injury is serious and could just be a contusion. The other was defensive tackle Mekhi Wingo, who also left in the second quarter and didn’t return. Wingo is battling for a roster spot on the defensive line, where competition is fierce, as his job is more in jeopardy than Rakestraw’s. Campbell said after the game that Wingo “got his bell rung” and could be in concussion protocol. If both injuries don’t keep either player out for long, they should hopefully return for next week’s game. Defense outperformed the offense Sure, a majority of the starters overall didn’t play, but it’s presumed that the offense is the better side of the football over the defense. Against the Bengals, the defense stood out, giving the Lions a chance to win. The defense forced four fumbles, recovering one, and sacked the quarterback twice. The offense saw some ups and downs, with the quarterback battle between Altmyer and Joshua Dobbs not showing much separation, as both showed positives and negatives. The running game provided the spark, and no receivers made multiple big plays. With the offensive line inconsistent and drawing five of the team’s nine penalties, it made it more difficult for the others to have success. If the defense can play this well in the regular season, the team could have a truly balanced approach. With a good defense to complement their high-powered offense, the Lions could have a legit chance not just to win the NFC North, but to be a threat in the NFC and appear in the Super Bowl.
author: Brandon Knapp

full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold (6) speaks to media members after practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co According to several reports, former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold is signing with the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks. Earlier this offseason, the Lions released their 2024 first-round pick after he was arrested. He’s currently facing eight felony charges. “You never want to let go of a player, especially somebody that you’ve been around for a while here and you drafted and all that,” Campbell said at the start of training camp. “And it’s unfortunate that we made the move we felt was best for us.” Arnold spent just two seasons with the Lions before the team opted to waive him back in June. Through his first two seasons, Arnold played in 24 games—starting 22 of them—tallied 91 tackles, 18 passes defended and one interception. Without Arnold the Lions are poised to move forward with D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin as their starting cornerbacks with Nick Whiteside and Ennis Rakestraw as the primary backups.

title: Lions vs. Bengals recap: Ennis Rakestraw injured in preseason loss
summary: The one thing everyone is hoping for during any NFL preseason game is a lack of injuries. Unfortunately, the Detroit Lions suffered one in their preseason opener that could impact their already-thin depth at the cornerback position. In the second quarter of their game against the Cincinnati Bengals, third-year cornerback Ennis Rakestraw suffered an injury […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (2) is injured on a play in the second quarter of the NFL Preseason game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Detroit Lions at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Thursday, Aug. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The one thing everyone is hoping for during any NFL preseason game is a lack of injuries. Unfortunately, the Detroit Lions suffered one in their preseason opener that could impact their already-thin depth at the cornerback position. In the second quarter of their game against the Cincinnati Bengals, third-year cornerback Ennis Rakestraw suffered an injury on a low tackle attempt and did not return to the game. After cutting Terrion Arnold this offseason (who is reportedly signing with the Seahawks), the Lions have found themselves relatively shorthanded behind presumed starters D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin. At this point, we don’t know the seriousness of Rakestraw’s injury. UPDATE: Lions coach Dan Campbell said they don’t believe Rakestraw’s injury is serious. It may just be an arm contusion. Addtionally, Mekhi Wingo, who also suffered an injury, may be going into concussion protocol after getting his “bell rung.” As for the rest of the game, it was a bit sloppy with rain and slick conditions. There were several dropped snaps, fumbled balls, and slipping on the turf. But there were also a handful of standouts. Detroit would end up losing by a score of: Here’s a full recap of Lions vs. Bengals with highlights: First quarter The Bengals won the toss and deferred, giving the ball to the Lions and rookie quarterback Luke Altmyer first. The drive got off to a promising start. Altmyer delivered a nice swing pass to Jacob Saylors for an early third-down conversion, and he hit Cedrick Wilson on a beautiful ball for a 23-yard gain. However, on the next play, Altmyer’s pass bounced high off of Isaac TeSlaa’s face and was picked off. Jordan Battle starts his preseason with an opening drive INT Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LXe5BflZvi — NFL (@NFL) August 13, 2026 Joe Burrow and the Bengals took over and he quickly hit Ja’Marr Chase for a 17-yard gain to move Cincy to midfield. But a second-down sack from Ahmed Hassanein forced a third-and-long. A screen pass was stopped 10-yards short of the sticks, and the Bengals punted it away. Ahmed got 'em! pic.twitter.com/qLYfqIXgVr — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 13, 2026 Detroit followed with a three-and-out after an Altmyer pass was tipped at the line and his third-down attempt to TeSlaa went incomplete. Burrow was able to then drive the Bengals into Lions territory, but thanks to a nice run stuff from Trevor Nowaske and a quarterback hit by Eric O’Neill, Detroit forced a fourth down. Bengals kicker Evan McPherson drilled a 56-yard field goal to give the Bengals a 3-0 lead with 3:42 left in the first quarter. Again, Altmyer led a promising drive into Bengals territory, including a nice leak play to tight end Jackson Meeks for 17 yards. Jackson Meeks gets loose for 17 pic.twitter.com/XWDo7mV35O — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 13, 2026 But Detroit faced a third-and-short, and another money-down attempt to TeSlaa was broken up to force a turnover on downs. Back on defense, the Lions stood tall early—with now Joe Flacco in at quarterback for the Bengals. Ennis Rakestraw kicked things off with a nice pass breakup. 🙅‍♂️ @EnnisRakestraw pic.twitter.com/JqlNszHFkm — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 13, 2026 A botched snap on second down set up a third-and-long on the other end of the quarter break. Second quarter Cincinnati was able to convert on third down with a pass against Rakestraw in coverage. The Bengals started to pick on Rakestraw, including another third down where the Bengals gained 8 yards with nine needed. They went for it on fourth down and converted with a short run up the gut. A few plays later, Rakestraw made a low tackle attempt and appeared to suffer an injury. He went to the locker room after being evaluated in the blue tent. The Bengals were in field goal range, but running back Kendall Milton fumbled the ball in the red zone and Lions rookie cornerback Keith Abney recovered. . @keithabneyjr scoops it up! pic.twitter.com/vTqAhl2RMK — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 13, 2026 After a holding call on the Lions offensive line, Detroit fumbled the ball right back when Altmyer’s handoff attempt was botched and Cincy recovered. A few plays later, Flacco connected with Jack Endes on a 4-yard touchdown with Aamaris Brown and Thomas Harper trailing in coverage. 10-0, Bengals. JACK ATTACK! pic.twitter.com/MI48yvg5El — Cincinnati Bengals (@Bengals) August 13, 2026 Josh Dobbs came in for the Lions, and led a promising drive for Detroit. Dominic Lovett picked up on a nice 10-yard curl that he turned into 15 yards. Then, Dobbs scrambled for 9 yards, moving the chains once again. However, a third-and-10 sack drove the Lions out of field goal range and they punted away. Detroit’s defense was able to force a three-and-out after Nick Whiteside batted away a underthrown deep shot on third down. The Lions offense took over at their own 36-yard line with 2:50 remaining in the half. Thanks to a defensive pass interference, Detroit converted an early third-and-10. Jacob Saylors ripped off a nice 27-yard run. Ok Saylors! pic.twitter.com/1ocIid6dzy — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 14, 2026 A couple of holding calls on Miles Frazier pushed the Lions back, and forced a 46-yard attempt by Jake Bates—he drilled it. But a penalty on the Bengals gave the Lions 5 more yards, and Dan Campbell looked like he was going to go for it on fourth-and-11. Instead, they tried to draw Cincinnati offsides, and then trotted Bates back out there for a 41-yard attempt and he made that one, too. 10-3, Bengals. The Bengals returned the kickoff all the way to Detroit’s 47-yard line, with kicker Jake Bates making the touchdown-saving tackle. That turned out to be huge because Detroit got a four-and-out on defense. Rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard got a pressure that forced a fourth-down intentional grounding, and the Lions took over on the Bengals side of the field with 7 seconds left. Jalen Rivers beaten badly pic.twitter.com/1XMRD2S0qt — Goodberry (@JoeGoodberry) August 14, 2026 A 9-yard Jacob Saylors run set up a 52-yard field goal from Bates, and he drilled it again. 10-6, Bengals. Third quarter Detroit’s defense got a quick three-and-out, but their offense started inside their own 10-yard line after a muffed punt return from Dominic Lovett and a block in the back. Luke Altmyer was back in the game at quarterback to start the second half. However, he led a quick three-and-out after Lovett dropped a low pass and his third-down pass was batted down at the line. The Bengals ended the stalemate with a steady drive into Lions territory. They converted a third-and-11 with a quick slant that went for 13 yards against Khalil Dorsey. The Lions cornerback made up for it with a nice open field tackle on the nice play, and two plays later on a third-and-9, the Bengals beat the blitz with a pass up the middle for 15. We see you, Ahmed ‼️ pic.twitter.com/dtlaXHya03 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 14, 2026 The Bengals settled for a short field goal to make it 13-6, Bengals. Detroit was able to move into Bengals territory with a 24-yard run from Raheem Blackshear, who was aided by a nice block from center Michael Niese. Raheem Blackshear breaks free for a gain of 24 pic.twitter.com/gVSjIW6AU2 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 14, 2026 But a botched snap on third down ended the drive and Detroit punted away. title: 10 Lions who can improve their stock vs. Bengals in preseason
summary: The Detroit Lions will travel to Cincinnati on Thursday night to take on the Bengals in both teams’ first game of the 2026 preseason, and we have produced a few articles to help fans prep for the contest, including How to Watch the game, 90-man roster listings by number/name, and an updated look at the […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (2) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions will travel to Cincinnati on Thursday night to take on the Bengals in both teams’ first game of the 2026 preseason, and we have produced a few articles to help fans prep for the contest, including How to Watch the game , 90-man roster listings by number/name , and an updated look at the Depth Chart . Over the past two weeks, the Lions have held 11 training camp practices, and Pride of Detroit has been in attendance for all of them, credentialing as many as three writers on certain days. Through those observations, we have written a litany of articles, updating fans on the team’s progress . Coach Dan Campbell said that they plan to rest many of their starters in this game, but several players will be looking to solidify their spots on the roster, while others are looking to prove they belong on an NFL roster. Here’s a look at 10 players who can improve their stock in this game. QB Luke Altmyer Following the sudden retirement of backup Teddy Bridgewater , Altmyer finds himself in a terrific position to challenge for the QB2 role. The Lions did sign veteran QB Josh Dobbs this week for depth, but Altmyer is expected to get the majority of reps in this game, giving him a massive advantage in the competition. Altmyer was targeted by the Lions as an undrafted free agent because of his experience and stylistic fit in a similar pro-style system—and he has played with confidence in training camp. While the Lions have historically leaned on a veteran, like Dobbs, for their backup role, Altmyer could force them to change their strategy if he performs well in the preseason. RB Jacob Saylors The Lions appear comfortable with their first three options at running back, with Jahmyr Gibbs the starter, Isiah Pacheco the backup, and Sione Vaki a staple on special teams. But the Lions have rostered four running backs in recent years, setting up a battle between last year’s RB4 Jacob Saylors and Jabari Small; a competition Campbell has said is very close. With Gibbs unlikely to play in this preseason game, along with Pacheco, Vaki, and Small nursing injuries, this could be a big opportunity for Saylors to separate himself amongst the reserve competition. WR Tay Martin With the top four receivers—Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, and Greg Dortch—presumably locked in, the Lions have a wide-open competition for the remaining WR5 and WR6 (if they keep a sixth) roles on the roster. Campbell has called the receiver room the deepest he’s ever had during his tenure in Detroit and believes anyone could win the remaining role(s). With the last spots on the roster likely coming down to special teams contributions, it’s worth noting that Campbell has brought up Tay Martin as one of the best contributors in this area. If he can show well on offense and continue to ascend on special teams, he’ll have a chance to be a sleeper for a remaining roster spot. TE Jackson Meeks Jackson Meeks quietly converted from WR-X to tight end in the middle of last season and has risen up the depth chart this offseason, partially due to the injury bug hitting the tight end room. While a bit undersized for the position, he brings a unique ability to separate as a receiving tight end and has been in competition for a TE4 role all camp. With rookie Miles Kitselman now on injured reserve, Meeks’ path to the roster is a bit easier, and with a good performance in the preseason, he will have a chance to hold off Thomas Gordon and prove to coaches that they should keep a fourth tight end on the 53-man roster. C Seth McLaughlin With starting center Cade Mays expected to miss the beginning of the season , and presumed replacement Juice Scruggs nursing a soft tissue injury, the Lions have promoted McLaughlin to the starting lineup in practices, and he is expected to start this game. This is a big opportunity for the second-year offensive lineman, who suddenly finds himself not only staring at a potential backup role on the 53-man roster, but also being given a chance to compete with Scruggs for a starting role for Week 1 of the regular season. DL Skyler Gill-Howard Gill-Howard has a terrific backstory, making him an easy rookie to root for, but he had a slow start to camp as he was learning to trust himself again after finishing his final collegiate season injured . Over the past week, Gill-Howard has begun to seize the opportunities in front of him and has been working higher up the depth chart, playing in multiple spots along the defensive line. With Mekhi Wingo returning from injury and potentially not playing in this game, Gill-Howard should have a fantastic opportunity to get on the field early in this game and continue his ascent. EDGE Ahmed Hassanein One of the great feel-good stories of camp has been Hassanein returning to full health and switching from “Rush End” to “Big End.” After missing all of his rookie season due to injury and changing positions, Hassanein has come into camp stronger and more explosive than ever. A fireball of energy, Hassanein hasn’t played in a game in almost a year, and if he can corral his emotions, he’ll have a great chance to solidify his spot on the roster with a solid performance. LB Erick Hunter A UDFA rookie fan favorite, Erick Hunter has taken advantage of reps higher up the depth chart due to injuries to Malcolm Rodriguez and Damone Clark. Already a dynamic special teamer, Hunter should see the field early in this game, likely once veteran Devin White exits, and if he can perform as he did in the Lions’ inter-scrimmage , he can prove that he deserves to be in the conversation for a LB6 role. CB Ennis Rakestraw Ennis Rakestraw opened camp in competition for a starting role with Rock Ya-Sin, but in the past two weeks, he’s seen Ya-Sin lock down the role, and Nick Whiteside pass him on the depth chart. While others around him have been taking developmental steps, Rakestraw has been slow to progress. Some of that could be because the Lions have shuffled him between outside corner and nickelback, but he needs to get back on track and take some positive steps before he falls further behind. There may not be a player on the roster who needs a big game more than Rakestraw. CB Roger McCreary Similar to Rakestraw, McCreary opened camp as the Lions’ starting nickel, but he has been slow to develop and has been passed on the depth chart by players like Christian Izien at nickel and Khalil Dorsey on the outside. If the Lions elect to keep just six corners on their roster, McCreary could be fighting for a spot on the roster and will need a good performance against the Bengals in order to stay in the cornerback conversation.

One guy’s a little bit ahead. The next day, the other guy’s a little bit ahead. And I love where they’re at on special teams because that’ll be big for both of those players. title: Discussion: Which Detroit Lions need the most preseason reps?
summary: Welcome to Detroit Lions gameday for the first time in the 2026 season preseason! The path to the Super Bowl begins now, and while most Lions starters are not expected to play Thursday night against the Cincinnati Bengals, it is still an important step for the franchise. Some young players will play and get valuable […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback Keith Abney II (28) during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Welcome to Detroit Lions gameday for the first time in the 2026 season preseason! The path to the Super Bowl begins now, and while most Lions starters are not expected to play Thursday night against the Cincinnati Bengals, it is still an important step for the franchise. Some young players will play and get valuable experience, while other reserves who will undoubtedly play a role during the regular season will also look to hone their craft against a Bengals team that IS expected to play their starters. So, while fans may not be as excited about a preseason game, it is an important night for the team. It is also a very important night for a ton of players on the 90-man roster. For now, let’s talk about the players who need this game the most. Today’s Question of the Day is: Which Detroit Lions player needs the most playing time during the 2026 preseason? My answer: Well, if we’re talking about potential starters, coach Dan Campbell may have answered this question on his own. He’s already revealed that first-round pick Blake Miller will play on Thursday night despite the fact that the rest of the starters won’t. Miller has exclusively repped with the first-team offense in training camp, so there’s little doubt he has “won” the starting job. However, Campbell’s strategy suggests they believe he still needs to get up to speed for them to have comfort in his abilities for Week 1. “It’s a work in progress,” Campbell said. “And I think a lot of it right now is the pass protection. I like the run game, but it’s really–it’s the whole game. But listen, he’s in a good spot. And we are going to douse him with reps. We are going to find a way, and he will find a way to be the guy.” Beyond Miller, there are a few key players who need to be all over the field this preseason. Primarily, I think this is drastically important for Ennis Rakestraw. He’s starting to slide down the depth chart, but the Lions still believe in his overall ability. Unfortunately for the Lions’ 2024 second-round pick, he simply has not had much playing time both in training camp and in the season due to injury. So these next three exhibition games are critical to his development, and I’m hoping he gets at least a full half in each game. Finally, there’s fifth-round rookie Keith Abney. He’s been a bit quiet in training camp, with a lot of up-and-down play as he adjusts to the nickel position. I believe he could truly be the starter at that position in 2027, but he needs to log reps as he continues to learn the nuances of nickel cornerback play. He’s another one I hope plays at least a half per game, even though I do not expect him to win the nickel job at any point in 2026. full_text: Green Bay Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd (32) runs through a drill during the second day of training camp on Thursday, July 24, 2025, at Ray Nitschke Field in Ashwaubenon, Wis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co We’ve spent nearly two years waiting to see what MarShawn Lloyd can become. Tonight against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Packers may finally get a semi-meaningful opportunity to find out. Lloyd has NFL talent, but can you guess how many regular season games he’s appeared in since being drafted in 2024? If you guessed 1, please report to the stage after the article to get your fish fry coupon. A recurring hamstring injury wiped out his 2025 season, while other injuries have repeatedly interrupted his development. As Bill Huber of Sports Illustrated noted ahead of Thursday’s preseason opener, there is still a fundamental question surrounding Lloyd: How good is he? That question is difficult to answer on a practice field without live tackling. Tonight changes that. The early returns from training camp have been encouraging. Packers.com reported in July that Lloyd had avoided setbacks after working with a California sports specialist and had rediscovered the burst and one-cut explosiveness that initially caught the attention of pro scouts. Then came perhaps his biggest statement yet. With Josh Jacobs sidelined during an Aug. 6 practice, Lloyd scored twice while working with the first-team offense. He was subsequently admonished for an ensuing celebratory backflip. Though, I can’t say I blame him. Offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich has confirmed Lloyd would play this preseason, noting that every healthy practice increases his confidence that the running back has moved beyond his injury problems. The Packers need to see Lloyd catch the ball, protect Jordan Love, handle contact and, most importantly, finish the preseason healthy. If he can check those boxes while showcasing the explosiveness Green Bay has seen in practice, Lloyd could find himself a sneaky important player on this roster — for better or for worse. title: Texans drop the preseason opener to the Chargers
summary: It’s only preseason football. Keeping telling yourself that. The Texans dropped the preseason opener to the Los Angeles Chargers 27-7 on Thursday night. The opening drive was a good one for the Texans starting offensive line. Everything after that was mostly forgettable. Of course, none of the premium first string skill position players saw the […]
full_text: It’s only preseason football. Keeping telling yourself that. The Texans dropped the preseason opener to the Los Angeles Chargers 27-7 on Thursday night. The opening drive was a good one for the Texans starting offensive line. Everything after that was mostly forgettable. Of course, none of the premium first string skill position players saw the field. It is hard to get any good data overall from the preseason by design. No coach wants to show anything they will actually use in the regular season. When the NFL moved from four preseason games to three, the games increasingly became about finding those last few roster spots and finding those key practice squad guys that can be elevated throughout the season when injuries occur. So, much of what we do here is focus on individual guys and whether their stock is up or down. I’m sure DeMeco Ryans wants the scrubs to play better because it means his overall program is working. Yet, we are looking at an overwhelming majority of guys that will be selling insurance and bagging groceries when September roles around. The stars of the game will likely be Kamari Ramsey on defense following a near pick six and a successful interception later in the second quarter. He has been making plays throughout camp and as a fifth round pick looks like a pretty good bet to make the team. Jared Wayne is the star on offense as he hauled in the game’s only touchdown for the Texans as one of his team leading three catches. Noah Whittington also had a nice game with eleven carries and 35 yards. It won’t make anyone forget Arian Foster, but he probably at least gets to play another game or two before he is cut. It’s been a long and lonely slog since the Texans last played in January. So, it is just good to see any football at this point. The number one rule for the preseason is to get out healthy. The Texans lost Graham Mertz in the first half and Joshua Pitsenberger in the second half. Neither of those guys are likely to make the final 53, but Mertz likely will be a practice squad guy. Otherwise the team lives to fight another day. The Texans will play the Las Vegas Raiders on Thursday August 20th and the Carolina Panthers on Friday August 28th. After that, we get to look forward to real football.

title: Houston Texans: 6 Players to Watch Vs. The Chargers
summary: Today, the Houston Texans will host the Los Angeles Chargers in their first preseason game of the 2026 season at NRG Stadium at 7:00 PM CST. This will be the team’s first opportunity to put on a Super-Bowl sized show for their Houston fanbase, who are ravenous for some Texans action in this highly anticipated […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 09: Houston Texans defensive end Solomon Byrd (50) looks on before the NFL preseason game between the Houston Texans and Minnesota Vikings on August 9th, 2025, in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Today, the Houston Texans will host the Los Angeles Chargers in their first preseason game of the 2026 season at NRG Stadium at 7:00 PM CST. This will be the team’s first opportunity to put on a Super-Bowl sized show for their Houston fanbase, who are ravenous for some Texans action in this highly anticipated 25th season of the franchise. The Texans have arguably never been as close to a championship as they are now, with a virtually impenetrable defense and a (hopefully) resurgent offense to boot. The free agent signings, draftees, and other offseason moves this summer have been like repeated jabs of adrenaline coursing through the veins of Texans fans every time they pick up their phones and see general manager Nick Caserio has made another deal. Just last week, the Texans added another layer to their comically deep roster when they brought back Jadeveon Clowney after a seven year-long career away from Houston. On paper, this team seems unbeatable…but now, with the preseason mere hours away, it is time to see this team in action! Okay, well we won’t be seeing the Super Bowl-caliber Texans in full force tonight, but we will at least bear witness to the last of the training camp stars duke it out for the final spots on a loaded depth chart. On a team as talented as this, even the preseason players will be athletic freaks willing to tear the field to shreds to get the edge over their teammate. It’ll make for some seriously cutthroat competition this August, and I think there are three players on offense and three players on defense that are worth your attention this preseason: OFFENSE: # 1: RB Noah Whittington (#26) Height: 5’ 8” Weight: 203 lbs. Age: 24 Year drafted/signed: 2026 (UDFA) by Texans With third-string running back Jawhar Jordan sidelined for the next several days with a “hip flexor strain ,” and fourth-stringer British Brooks recovering from surgery to his broken hand, this upcoming preseason game against the Chargers will be a chance for some roster-hopefuls to impress the Texans coaching staff. Lead backs David Montgomery and Woody Marks will get very few – if any – snaps in the first preseason game, so the majority of the matchup against the Harbaughs will feature newly signed tailback Owen Wright, undrafted rookie Joshua Pitsenberger from Yale, and undrafted rookie Noah Whittington from Oregon. Wright’s NFL experience with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Pitsenberger’s success at Yale shouldn’t be overlooked, but Whittington is my favorite of the group thanks to his bowling-ball frame (5’8”, 203 lbs.) and shocking acceleration. Whittington is not a huge running back, but, much like Jawhar Jordan when he was drafted out of Louisville in 2024, Whittington has this ability to literally launch himself forward when he’s found an opening, as if the earth below him is springing Whittington forward. Add to that his otherworldly contact balance and you’ve got a recipe for a fantastic backup tailback that would make a perfect depth piece behind Woody Marks! Even as an undrafted player, Whittington came into Houston’s training camp with some hype, and it appears he’s already making an impression on head coach DeMeco Ryans. Ryans was asked about the RB depth chart by reporter Landry Locker yesterday, and had this to say: Noah seems to make a play every day. He has a really good feel for pressing blocks and his vision. Just knowing when to cut, when to take the ball outside, when to…you know, make a cut back up inside. You feel a guy… I see a guy who plays with really great vision, great feel at the running back spot. So, when you see guys that are lower on the depth chart in these preseason games, some of those running backs are going to shine. – DeMeco Ryans Asked DeMeco Ryans about backend depth chart RB’s. Specifically Noah Whittington, who has at the very least made you think about RB3. pic.twitter.com/yl68hCfgUT — Landry Locker (@LandryLocker) August 12, 2026 He’s got experience, he’s got training camp highlights, and he’s got the coach’s approval. What’s the next box for Noah Whittington to check on his way to sneaking onto the 53-man roster? Having a breakout preseason game. Watch out for him tonight, because if he shows out, the RB #4 spot might have a true leader. #2: WR Lewis Bond (#82) Height: 5’ 11” Weight: 190 lbs. Age: 23 Year drafted/signed: 2026 (6th, 204th overall) by Texans Another unlikely name making plays in training camp is rookie sixth-round pick Lewis Bond out of Boston College. Bond had over 100 catches and nearly 1,000 receiving yards in college last year, but he still fell to the sixth round, mostly due to his lack of NFL size and speed. But, his route-running skills are second to maybe only Tank Dell on Houston’s roster, and he’s been one of the most celebrated young players during training camp: Clean win for Lewis Bond. #Texans rookie continues to make plays. pic.twitter.com/FP71CoWePM — Greg Bailey (@GregBailey13) August 5, 2026 #Texans rookie receiver Lewis Bond Play of the Day @KPRC2 pic.twitter.com/NHmpEnNyLr — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) August 8, 2026 While many, many things can be blamed for quarterback C.J. Stroud’s regression from year one to year three in the NFL, not having a true route-specialist that could get open quickly was a hurdle he often struggled to clear. Tank Dell was clearly a favorite target of Stroud’s when he was available, and besides him, route-runners like Stefon Diggs, Robert Woods, or Noah Brown absorbed plenty of Stroud’s attention when they were on the Texans. The guy has a thing for receivers that can get open fast, maybe that’s a reflection of how quickly he gets pressured or how fast his eyes dart to the check-down option, but regardless of the reason, Stroud is getting exactly what he’s looking for in Lewis Bond. It’s time for Bond to prove it against more and more NFL talent, though. His 4.59s 40-yard dash was clearly a red flag to general managers everywhere back in April, so it’ll only be a matter of time before this weakness makes itself apparent at the professional level. But, if he’s able to respond to this weakness with even twitchier movement during the preseason, the Texans might have found more depth at one of their few shallow spots on the roster. It will be very interesting to see how the competition for the final WR spot unfolds this preseason between Bond, practice squad receivers Jared Wayne and Josh Kelly, and former Tennessee Titans returner Jha’Quan Jackson. Bond has his limitations, but his excellence on offense might overpower any deficiencies in speed or special teams ability. #3: OT James Neal III (#70) Height: 6’ 6” Weight: 325 lbs. Age: 23 Year drafted/signed: 2026 (UDFA) by Texans After receiving the most lucrative contract of any Texans undrafted rookie this year , plenty of eyes drifted towards LT during training camp to see what former Iowa State Cyclone James Neal III has to offer the Houston Texans. So far, he hasn’t exploded onto the scene, so tonight’s preseason game will be a great opportunity for him to strike a good first impression. A three-year starter (primarily at LT) for Iowa State, Neal moves with impressive fluidity for his size and can be a mighty force in the run-game. He mixed his time between LT and LG in 2024, showing some versatility, but his primary role in college was LT, where his run-blocking improved and his pass-blocking…remained inconsistent and mediocre. His pass protection varied greatly from game-to-game, but when James Neal was on a heater, he’s hard to beat. Whether or not he’ll be able to push Blake Fisher for the #2 LT spot remains to be seen, but he may impress enough this preseason to earn a roster spot over similar…

title: Ten Houston Texans to Watch in the First Preseason Game vs Chargers
summary: We’ve made it. The light at the end of the tunnel has been reached. It’s football time once again. We’ll have to wait a few more weeks for meaningful football, but don’t tel that to the players vying for a spot on one of the most competitive rosters in the league. The Houston Texans are […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - DECEMBER 31: Brevin Jordan #9 of the Houston Texans scores a touchdown during the second quarter of a game against the Tennessee Titans at NRG Stadium on December 31, 2023 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve made it. The light at the end of the tunnel has been reached. It’s football time once again. We’ll have to wait a few more weeks for meaningful football, but don’t tel that to the players vying for a spot on one of the most competitive rosters in the league. The Houston Texans are taking on the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday at 7pm CST in the first preseason game of the season. Most of the notable starters will sit out this game, a move rooted in simple caution and the reality that preseason reps offer little value for established players. The focus shifts to depth pieces and roster hopefuls who actually need these snaps. That opens up reps for players across the roster who have the most to prove from a dominant performance tomorrow. Below are the ten Texans to keep track of that have the most to gain: Jaylin Smith, CB #22 Smith enters his second year in Houston after an injury-riddled rookie campaign. The cornerback shows promise at camp and receives accolades from the starting cornerbacks. He should be the first backup cornerback, a position that was surely missed last season when Kamari Lassiter went down, He is slated to play a ton of reps this preseason with Lassiter and Derek Stingley Jr. likely playing a limited role. For Thursday, he needs to excel against backups and prove why the Texans selected him in the third round last year. Lewis Bond, WR #82 Let’s see if the hype is real with Bond. From the moment he entered rookie minicamp the receiver from Boston College has been hailed for being a savvy route running and well adjusted to the NFL playbook. Can he separate from NFL-quality defensive backs? As a primarily slot receiver, his role will be interesting to watch develop given the Texans will run more two tight end sets rather than three WR sets. Jared Wayne, WR #89 Wayne has been one of the most highly regarded players this training camp. Sitting on the outside looking in, his job is to make the staff’s decision at wide receiver as difficult as possible. He needs to force a conversation about keeping a sixth or even seventh option. His versatility helps that cause, since he can line up at every receiver spot and brings true long speed to the field. Marte Mapu, LB #14 Through no action of his own, Mapu has moved from the edge of the roster into a backup role. Injuries to Jake Hansen and E J Speed thinned this group fast and pushed Mapu into the spotlight for this preseason game. His main goal is proving he can handle the defense as the backup WILL lineback. Even if these expected to start this preseason game, he still needs separate himself from rookies Wade Woodaz and Aiden Fisher on the depth chart. If all things are equal, the team will choose to keep rookies every time. Cade Stover, TE #8 Stover leapfrogged TE Brevin Jordan during the first week of training camp. Jordan is also sidelined with a short-term injury, which offers Stover a unique opportunity to separate himself from Jordan on the depth chart. With veterans Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau likely not participating in the preseason game, Stover will have the opportunity to run with the first string offense. Both the run game and pass game need to run through Stover in this preseason game. Jawhar Jordan, RB #25 Jordan may not be healthy enough to play this preseason game, which makes his presence all the more necessary. The breakout performance against Arizona last year, where he ran for 101 yards, cannot be a one-hit-wonder. He needs steadier production for the staff to trust him as part of the RB rotation rather than viewing him as only a special team option. If he can play, Jordan should receive the lion’s share of the carries in the first half before the UDFAs rotate in. His biggest completion is from Noah Whittington, whose downhill running style fits what the Texans are looking for. Jordan’s acceleration and short area quickness have shown up throughout camp, but he needs a strong preseason to fend off challengers for the RB3 role. Febechi Nwaiwu, OG/OC #64 Very, very little has been said about the rookie from Oklahoma since he joined the team. That’s never a great thing, but at least he’s healthy and participating (couldn’t say the same about Kenyon Green his rookie year). It will be interesting to see where he plays along the offensive line. Currently, he’s slated to be on the roster solely due to being drafted in the fourth round. Is there more to his game than what the Texans are letting on? We’ll find out on Thursday. Collin Wright, CB #37 The undrafted rookie from Stanford receives more praise and makes more plays than 2/3 of the draft class. The Missouri City product had an interception on Graham Mertz early in training camp and is vying for the last CB spot. The 6-foot corner fits well into Houston’s scheme and is competing directly with second-year UDFA Alijah Huzzie and veteran Tremon Smith. Graham Mertz INTERCEPTED by Collin Wright. pic.twitter.com/OyEATS2Whz — Will Kunkel (@WillKunkelV) August 4, 2026 Dominique Robinson, DE #94 Jadeveon Clowney was signed because the coaches weren’t seeing enough out of the defensive end depth. That “depth” has a name and its Dominique Robinson. The long and athletic DE played four years in Chicago before joining Houston this offseason. His position on the roster is extremely tenuous and he needs to show out to remain in the competition. Kai Kroeger, P #38 I could have gone OT Blake Fisher here, but who wants to watch a career backup OT? Let’s give a nod to the special teams. While writing this article, Jonathan M. Alexander posted that the Texans cut Jack Stonehouse, ending the embarrassing punting competition that occurred at camp. Nick Caserio brought in 2-3 punters over the weekend for a tryout. Even with the news, Kroeger hasn’t faired well this camp and is in jeopardy of losing his job after roster cuts occur. His competition is solely against himself as Houston could easily add a punter who gets cut from their own team at the 53-man roster decision.
author: Kenneth Levy

title: The X-Factor of Tank Dell
summary: 2 of the most electric players in Houston Texans history have been Will Fuller V and Tank Dell. Both wide receiver speedsters. Both a threat to score any time they touched the ball. Both undersized and (so far) unable to remain healthy for a full run at the Houston Texans schedule. Both also elevated the […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - JUNE 04: Tank Dell #1 of the Houston Texans catches a pass during OTA Offseason Workouts at Houston Methodist Training Center on June 04, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images 2 of the most electric players in Houston Texans history have been Will Fuller V and Tank Dell. Both wide receiver speedsters. Both a threat to score any time they touched the ball. Both undersized and (so far) unable to remain healthy for a full run at the Houston Texans schedule. Both also elevated the play of their respective quarterbacks when on they were on the field. Before hearing his name called on draft day by H-Town general manager Nick Caserio, Dell spent the prior 3 years at the University of Houston, where he totaled 3155 yards off 228 catches, 32 touchdowns, a 13.8 yard per reception average over the course of 35 games. In the run up to the NFL draft, Dell met then-future Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud and the 2 rookies-to-be struck up a friendship that grew exponentially at the NFL Draft Combine. Once Stroud was picked by the Texans, he went to work lobbying for Caserio to take Dell, which he did in the 3rd round. The combination immediately paid dividends for the Texans. Over the course of his time in the NFL, Dell has been shot, recovered and came back stronger, only to suffer a brutal leg injury on a touchdown catch against the Kansas City Chiefs in the 2024 season. It’s easy to point to that leg injury as (another) down-turn in the career of Stroud also, who is under a ridiculous amount of pressure this off-season due to his recent playoff failures. Foxnsports.com When asked after the game how he was able to recover from the heartbreaking scene, Stroud spoke about his faith. “All you can do is really pray. At the end of the day, God still gets the glory. Always, no matter what happens to me, I always know that I’m even up here because of the grace of Jesus and the grace of who He is in my life and Tank’s life. For anything how it goes, left or right or up or down, I always have to praise my Lord and Savior.” Tank Dell on CJ Stroud during his return from injury: “He was with me the whole time. From the first day it happened, to today. Long conversations, I go to his house, he come to my house. Long conversations about the future we want to build with each other on the field. Off the… pic.twitter.com/YiF1n7zk69 — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) August 8, 2026 Now that Dell has returned from an injury that would have ended lesser careers – again – a lot of people in the know are saying not only is he back, he’s better than ever. The ability to recover from being shot and play NFL ball at a high level speaks volumes to the “size of the dog in the fight”. Coming back better than ever from what could have been a career-ending leg injury even more so. Tank Dell wants to be better than what he was: “When I got hurt I wrote the goal down to be better than what I left off that Chiefs game. I wanna come not like ‘oh is he gunna be the same?’, I want to come back better than where I was.” pic.twitter.com/3cooEXAYpO — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) August 9, 2026 TRENDING: Tank Dell looks MORE EXPLOSIVE than he’s ever been at camp. Dell has reportedly looked “more fluid” in his routes than he did before his injuries. The Texans WR constantly looks like he’s moving in 2X SPEED 😳 pic.twitter.com/MBysumOwqP — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) August 10, 2026 “There’s two ways you can separate. With speed or your ability to stop faster than your defender. Tank Dell does both of those at a really high level.” @Hawk has Tank Dell on his comeback watch list 👀✍️ pic.twitter.com/5Gk5A1Ag4z — Get Up (@GetUpESPN) August 11, 2026 Not only is Dell one of the quickest receivers in the league, he’s also one of the slipperiest ones with defender after defender losing track of the speedster time and again. If Dell is truly back better than before the Texans offensive line is decidedly improved David Montgomery can keep the running game on track Nick Calley can call a professional quality game and C.J. Stroud can minimize mistakes and find his receivers more often then this team is a legit Super Bowl contender. Having Dell back isn’t the singular ingredient in getting this offense back on track, but it’s sure a welcome return of a very exciting player who has a heart twice the size of his body. CJ Stroud on @nflnetwork on Tank Dell: “I’m super proud of that guy. I can’t wait to get him back on the field, our chemistry is lights out. I’m very excited to get him back.” pic.twitter.com/4q3z0vLNzc — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) August 6, 2026 It wouldn’t be wise to put Dell on the field for tonight’s Houston Texans game against the Chargers, since it’s just week one of the preseason. But, you can bet when Dell and Stroud are on the field together again, if the defense loses Dell, he’s going to make them regret it. Los Angeles Chargers at Houston Texans Thursday August 13th 7pm Reliant Stadium Houston Texas
author: Mike Bullock

title: Colts have plenty to evaluate after preseason opener tie with Patriots
summary: For the Indianapolis Colts, the 13-13 preseason opener stalemate does not reflect the numerous missed opportunities to step on the necks of the reining AFC-champions, punch the ball into the end zone, or for either quarterback to claim their job on the depth chart. The Colts turned the ball over four times through the first […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. #5 runs with the football near the goal line during an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium —August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the Indianapolis Colts, the 13-13 preseason opener stalemate does not reflect the numerous missed opportunities to step on the necks of the reining AFC-champions, punch the ball into the end zone, or for either quarterback to claim their job on the depth chart. The Colts turned the ball over four times through the first three quarters, or five counting turnovers on downs. There were two drives that started past their own 45-yard-line, plus another that started inside the Patriots’ 30-yard-line, that Indy ultimately came away with zero points. The Colts leaned on their young quarterbacks and a pair of late field goals to settle for a tie with the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. Indianapolis’ offense struggled to find any early rhythm as three turnovers ended the Colts’ first four possessions. Quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. commnaded the second unit throughout the entire first half. He spiked his first pass attempt at the line of scrimmage, but ultimately finished a solid 11-of-14 passing for 145 yards and rushed for 53 yards on just six carries. Richardson did throw an interception on a tipped pass intended for receiver Coleman Owen and later lost a fumble after Patriots linebacker K.J. Britt punched the ball loose on a 12-yard scramble. It looked bleak before the final play of the first quarter as the 24-year-old had completed just two screen passes. Richardson then fired a dart on a deep comeback route to receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhene for nearly 20 yards to close the first frame with an explosive play and some momentum. He broke loose for a 22-yard run on a read-option to start the second quarter, then later added a 7-yard scramble before stepping out of bounds just shy of the goal line. The Colts lost another fumble on a rookie mistake as seventh-round running back Seth McGowan coughed it up just short of the goal line to terminate their second possession. Looks like McGowan's forearm was down before it came out. How is this not being reviewed? #Colts #ForTheShoe #Patriots #INDvsNE pic.twitter.com/SjqihgTaJu — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) August 14, 2026 The Patriots made it necessary to target cornerback Jonathan Edwards. Quarterback Tommy DeVito ignited their fourth drive executing the run-pass-option and hit receiver Mack Hollins on a slant against Edwards for 17 yards. Faced with third-and-short from midfield, he hit receiver Efton Chism III on a crosser for a 20-yard gain against Edwards. DeVito punctuated the 12-play drive by throwing a fade to receiver Kyle Williams, who burst past Edwards for a 12-yard touchdown to extend the Patriots’ lead to 10-0 with four minutes left in the first half. It seemed that the final two drives would be the most important for Richardson and the second-unit to finish strong and figure out how to get some points on the scoreboard. Richardson thrived off the play action fakes for three consecutive plays as he hit receiver D.J. Montgomery over the middle for 13 yards. He found tight end Will Mallory on a crosser for 18 yards, then caught a break with just enough touch on the final play before the two-minute warning. His underthrown pass was barely tipped by cornerback Channing Canada, but luckily still fell into the lap of Mallory for 19 more yards. Mallory led with a game-high six catches on seven targets for 80 receiving yards, proving he deserves some looks in the pass game this season. Richardson dumped off a brilliant screen pass to running back Ulysses Bentley IV while facing an all out blitz, which allowed the offense to set up shop near the goal line. The 250-pound dual threat QB then plunged into the end zone for the first touchdown of the preseason as the Colts cut the deficit to 10-7 with one minute left in the opening half. AR takes it in for 6. 📺 #INDvsNE | 8/13 on FOX59 pic.twitter.com/Z7sDOCsYMp — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) August 14, 2026 The Colts collected a dozen combined defensive stops, including seven tackles for loss and five pass breakups. The defensive front made its presence felt throughout the first half as Adetomiwa Adebawore pounced into the backfield to help force a sack that was finished by rookie George Gumbs Jr. Rookie Cayden Curry stood out with a team-high six tackles, three QB hits, two tackles for loss, two pass deflections, and one sack. Rookie linebacker Bryce Boettcher and safety AJ Haulcy also added three solid tackles in their first NFL action. Indianapolis was able to limit New England’s rushing attack, holding the Patriots to just 83 rushing yards on 32 carries, just 2.6 yards per rush. The third stringers continued to struggle to get into any sort of flow as Riley Leonard’s first two possessions lasted just three plays apiece. He was flooded with heavy pressure from the first snap and his second throw felt more like it was fungoed into centerfield before it was intercepted by Patriots safety John Saunders Jr, which set up the Patriots inside Colts territory for their final scoring drive. Leonard led a pair of methodical late drives in the fourth quarter, feeding receiver Raylen Sharpe on multiple short completions while adding an 11-yard scramble of his own. The sixth-rounder finished 10-for-21 passing for just 89 passing yards and one interception. Colts kicker Spencer Shrader connected on a 46-yard field goal to cut the deficit in half midway through the fourth, then later drilled a 61-yard field goal to tie it with just 1:16 remaining. Both teams had one final possession and moved the ball to their own 45-yard line, but neither team could find the winning points. Four turnovers, a turnover on downs and inconsistency remains from the ongoing quarterback and kicking battle. Richardson still was able to showcase his explosive running ability, coming just two yards shy of the game-high and Leonard engineered a late rally to level the score in the clutch. The Colts head back to Droplight Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, Ind. to host a pair of light weekend practices at 4 p.m.
author: Thomas Butler-Guerrero

title: Colts’ key takeaways from preseason opener, 13-13 tie, against Patriots
summary: Colts Football is officially back, well sort of. The Indianapolis Colts traveled to the New England Patriots for the Preseason Opener, and here are some of the key takeaways from their, 13-13 tie, during Week 1 of preseason: Offense Defense Special Teams
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. (5) scrambles with the ball during the first half against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Colts Football is officially back, well sort of. The Indianapolis Colts traveled to the New England Patriots for the Preseason Opener, and here are some of the key takeaways from their, 13-13 tie, during Week 1 of preseason: Offense QB Anthony Richardson Sr.: Running with the starting ‘2nd-team offense,’ Richardson Sr. looked initially rusty, with an errant first throw and then an interception, that while it wasn’t the most accurate throw (or even the right decision in Richardson’s progressions of reads), should’ve been caught by wideout Coleman Owen. As the game progressed, Richardson Sr. looked more comfortable, and showcased what makes him such a special athlete at the position, the dynamic ability to run the football. There were still some erratic plays. For instance, the fumble where he should’ve just slid after picking up 10 yards early in the 2nd quarter. Despite critics clearly piling on early, Richardson settled in, finishing his night by completing 11 of 14 pass attempts for 145 total passing yards, 0 touchdowns, an interception, as well as rushed for 53 total yards and a touchdown on 6 carries. Richardson Sr. still needs to eliminate some of the outlier negative plays, but how he played on Thursday night would play for the Colts as their QB2. QB Riley Leonard: Like Richardson Sr., some grace should be given to the 2nd-year quarterback because not only was he likely shaking off some rust, but he was also playing with the third-team offense, which it’s not a secret that offensive line play collectively gets worse the further you dig deeper into the depth chart. Leonard’s night started out rough as he was sacked , only to then get intercepted —which didn’t appear to be a good decision or throw for that matter, with pass pressure again right in his face. He was 10 of 21 for 89 passing yards, an interception, and 12 rushing yards on 2 carries. He’ll be the preseason starter next week at home hosting the Atlanta Falcons. RB Seth McGowan: Perhaps the darkhorse for the RB2 job behind star workhorse Jonathan Taylor throughout training camp so far, Seth McGowan had a middling final line, rushing for 17 total rushing yards on 5 carries (3.4 ypc. avg.), but had some nice runs . Still, early in the second quarter, he should’ve had a rushing touchdown to boost that middling line, which inexplicably was ruled a fumble along the goal line without an official review. Ahhh… the joys of preseason football. TE Will Mallory: It’ll be interesting to see where Will Mallory fits in a crowded Colts tight end room, and with 2nd-year pro Tyler Warren entrenched as the team’s top receiving option at the position, whereas veteran Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree perform more of the ‘dirty work’ blocking in-line. Still, Mallory has been a nice productive receiving option throughout camp to-date and was the Colts leading receiver in this one with 6 receptions for 80 total receiving yards. He seemed to have nice chemistry with Richardson Sr. and had a handful of productive catches to add to his early preseason resume. Defense LB Bryce Boettcher: The rookie 4th round pick looked fast and instinctive in this one starting with the second-team defense. He flew to the football, and as the season progresses, it wouldn’t be surprising to see him make an instant impact and perhaps eventually push for a starting linebacker job with the defense. Boettcher looked like a breath of fresh air for a Colts defense that unfortunately, looked too old, slow, and unathletic at the 2nd-level last season. For what’s it’s worth, his running linebacker mate, Jaylon Carlies also made some nice plays for the defense out there. Edge Jaylahn Tuimoloau: The 2025 2nd round pick of the Colts has yet to really impress as a young pass rusher on the football field and didn’t really stand out in this one at all. It’s one preseason game, but Tuimoloau didn’t do himself any favors regarding potentially catching veteran Arden Key for a starting job—and more nights like this, could mean losing rotational time too. Edge George Gumbs Jr: Thought to be more of a developmental ‘Day 3’ pass rusher, the rookie has flashed at camp, and even made some impact plays in this one , including a sack in his preseason debut. He looks like a rotational edge early on that the Colts will definitely keep around on the 53-man. Edge Caden Curry: Another rookie edge, who was a 6th round pick of Indianapolis, looked really good out there running with the 3s. He finished with 6 tackles (3 solo), a sack, 2 tackles for loss, 2 passes defensed, and 3 QB hits. He was very active out there and stuffed the stat sheet in his preseason debut. Mekhi Blackmon and Johnathan Edwards: It was a tough showing for these two at cornerback for the Colts (penalties for Blackmon, but Edwards regarding pass coverage in particular!). The Colts have to hope Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward stay healthy all season along the outside for depth reasons. It’s Week 1 of preseason, but these two will want to play a lot better than they showed in this one, and it would be hard to believe they can’t. Specifically, Edwards got torched on one Patriots offensive drive, eventually capped off by giving up the touchdown in coverage. AJ Haulcy: Relatively quiet preseason debut for the rook (which isn’t necessarily a bad thing at safety!), but he did have a solid tackle to keep the Patriots short of the sticks on 3rd down late in the first quarter to force 4th down. He finished with 3 tackles in this one. Hunter Wohler: Wohler and the Colts received another preseason injury scare, when he left the game early on due to concussion testing. However, Wohler would return and had 3 tackles (2 solo) in this one. Special Teams Colts Kickers: Blake Grupe finished 0-1, but I wouldn’t read too much into his lone miss, as it was a 61-yard field goal attempt that was wide right into the closing seconds headed into halftime. He did make his only extra point attempt. To his credit, challenger Spencer Shrader was a perfect 2 for 2 in field goal attempts, including converting his own long attempt of 61 total yards. ST Coach Brian Mason: Thoughts go out to Coach Mason, who appears to have suffered a significant leg injury along the sideline after the final play of the game. We’ll have to get an update on that one.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: Breaking down Anthony Richardson’s game vs the Patriots
summary: Anthony Richardson got the start against the Patriots and played the entire first half. Let’s break down each and every play of his. Throw 1 Richardson comes out with a stinker on a designed roll out that left the tight end completely open in the flats. He fails to open up and align his upper […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Anthony Richardson Sr. #5 of the Indianapolis Colts looks to pass during an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Anthony Richardson got the start against the Patriots and played the entire first half. Let’s break down each and every play of his. Throw 1 Oh no… #Colts #ForTheShoe #Patriots #INDvsNE pic.twitter.com/RJhw28ZMO1 — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) August 13, 2026 Richardson comes out with a stinker on a designed roll out that left the tight end completely open in the flats. He fails to open up and align his upper body which results in his body staying closed to the target and one hopping it. Throw 2 Nice RAC for Ogletree. #Colts #ForTheShoe #Patriots #INDvsNE pic.twitter.com/DDut0VHhNG — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) August 13, 2026 A screen pass here so nothing to break down. Throw 3 Ohhhhh noooooo #Colts #ForTheShoe #Patriots #INDvsNE pic.twitter.com/oRSRGh6Fz8 — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) August 13, 2026 While the majority of the blame should go to the receiver, Richardson definitely deserves blame for the read, which was completely wrong, and for the placement of the ball. He decided to throw to a receiver in the flats with a trailing defensive back and another one sitting over the top. He then decides to whip a fastball high that forces the receiver to jump high for it. Owen should’ve caught the ball but that ball never should’ve gone there. Scramble 1 At least he tried to get out of bounds. #Colts #ForTheShoe #Patriots #INDvsNE pic.twitter.com/XfkbeDX2tD — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) August 14, 2026 This is what Richardson does best and that’s using his legs to create. He does a nice job of getting 7 yards here. With 2 timeouts, it’s also a good read. Throw 12 Another nice throw and catch on this drive. #Colts #ForTheShoe #Patriots #INDvsNE pic.twitter.com/tQU34IhYt0 — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) August 14, 2026 This is Richardson’s best throw of the game. An absolute strike on the money to the tight end in stride and he gets out of bounds to get the Colts across the 50. Throw 13 This will set up an insanely long Field Goal attempt for Blake Groupe. #Colts #ForTheShoe #Patriots #INDvsNE pic.twitter.com/856CK0l0E9 — Chris Shepherd (@NFLscheme) August 14, 2026 And because of the last throw and decision that got the player out of bounds, it allowed the Colts to run one more play to get into field goal range. This was a very well executed drive by Richardson. Overall Recap It was a very rough start for Richardson, but he settled in nicely on the last few drives. The stat line will show 2 turnovers and he’s at fault or partially at fault for both of them. Nevertheless, it was the usual highs and lows from Richardson that we’ve come to see over the years, so while the highs were good, there’s still no consistency from him and that’s concerning. After all these years with him, I still come back to the same conclusion that there should be an Anthony Richardson package with designed runs, RPOs and a few pass plays that he likes best because he isn’t ready to command a full NFL offense but 5-10 plays a game to show off the explosiveness could be a nice median. It sounds like the Colts are well beyond that and tonight’s game was more of a showcase, but let’s see what the future holds.

(Photo by John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images On Thursday night, the Indianapolis Colts (0-0) travel to the New England Patriots (0-0) at Gillette Stadium to kick off preseason against their former longtime arch nemesis. The game begins at 7:30 PM EST and can be viewed on FOX59 locally, as well as listened to on 93.5 and 107.5 The Fan and 97.1 Hank FM. Rick Venturi will be handling local analyst duties for those watching, while Matt Taylor (play-by-play) and Charles Arbuckle (analyst) will be handling the radio call. While tensions between the two franchises have since softened since their glory “Peyton Manning vs. Tom Brady” yester-years—and what was once a bitter rivalry, as evidenced by the willingness to host joint training camp practice together this week, the preseason opener will still be an important initial measuring stick for both sides. Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. has been given the start in this one, while Riley Leonard will come in relief of Richardson Sr. during the second half of action. A strong performance by either could help their cause for earning the QB2 job behind starting quarterback Daniel Jones—who will be resting all of preseason. It appears unlikely that Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will start in this one either, which means primary backup quarterback Tommy DeVito will garner the start in his absence. Other Patriots starters are not reportedly expected to play either. For the Colts, the positions I’ll be looking at are the ones that remain the most undecided, particularly at QB2, WR2 and RB2 on offense, as well as at DE2, LBs1-2, S2, and PK. title: Jacksonville Jaguars vs. New Orleans Saints Preseason Week 1 stats, matchup preview
summary: Holy crap! We’re only a few days away from competitive Jacksonville Jaguars football! As the Jags prepare to play the New Orleans Saints in Preseason Week 1, we sat down with Nic Jennings of Canal Street Chronicles to learn more about the opposing side. Question 1: After consecutive fourth-place finishes in the NFC South, what […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - DECEMBER 28: Head Coach Kellen Moore congratulates Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints on the sidelines after a touchdown during a game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. The Saints defeated the Titans 34-26. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Holy crap! We’re only a few days away from competitive Jacksonville Jaguars football! As the Jags prepare to play the New Orleans Saints in Preseason Week 1, we sat down with Nic Jennings of Canal Street Chronicles to learn more about the opposing side. Question 1: After consecutive fourth-place finishes in the NFC South, what are local expectations for the Saints this season? A winning season? A division title? Dare I suggest- a playoff push? If you were to ask the Who Dat Nation, they’d probably tell you this team could go all the way. But in all seriousness, considering the vibes around the facility and the talent on paper, the sky’s the limit for this Saints team. If Tyler Shough can build off his strong finish to his rookie season, I think this team will go as far as he can take them. For me personally, I see a division title in sight. Time will tell if they can achieve that and turn it into a deep playoff run, but so far, Kellen Moore appears to be doing all the right things and has his team ready to compete in 2026. Question 2: Eighth overall pick Jordyn Tyson has drawn plenty of hype in recent weeks, perhaps as much as any other NFL player during training camp this year. How do you see him meshing with WR Chris Olave and QB Tyler Shough in Kellen Moore’s offense? Using a similar phrase to my previous answer, the sky’s the limit for that trio. Chris Olave has shown that he is a superstar when healthy after earning Second-Team All-Pro honors last season. Tyler Shough has shown the ability to distribute the football to all of his playmakers and put them in favorable situations. Then you have Tyson, whose raw talent and physical ability are impossible to ignore. For Tyson, it all comes down to staying healthy. He dealt with injury concerns throughout his college career, but when he’s healthy, much like Olave, he looks like a superstar in the making. Like you said, Tyson has been lighting up the Saints’ offseason program, and the entire fanbase is excited to see him and Olave wreak havoc on opposing defenses. Question 3: The Saints defense was quietly one of the most-improved and under-appreciated units in the league last season. What has that side of the ball excelled at under Brandon Staley, and which areas did they identify in the offseason as needing more growth? Staley has done a great job with this defensive unit since his arrival. One thing to watch will be how the defense responds following the loss of field general Demario Davis. However, the Saints reunited with Kaden Elliss this offseason, and he has steadily developed into one of the league’s most underrated and versatile linebackers. One area that has really excelled under Staley is the pass rush. New Orleans had dealt with inconsistency on the edge for years before Staley arrived. Last season, we saw a rejuvenated Cam Jordan post his seventh season with double-digit sacks, while Chase Young recorded the first double-digit sack season of his career. Young is steadily developing into one of the league’s premier pass rushers, while Carl Granderson has proven that he can consistently produce as well. New Orleans also traded for Tyree Wilson during the draft and added Anfernee Jennings, so the pass rush should be a major strength for the Saints this season. As far as an area that needs more growth, I’d personally point to the cornerback room. Kool-Aid McKinstry is expected to take a significant leap this season, while Quincy Riley now has a season under his belt after a decent rookie year. The questions start after those two, though. The Saints added Martin Emerson, but he didn’t play a single snap in 2025 and has dealt with injuries throughout his career. Seventh-round pick TJ Hall has made a name for himself during camp, but veteran Isaac Yiadom has really struggled. The depth in that room could become a concern down the stretch of the season, so it’ll be interesting to see how they hold up against Jacksonville this week. Question 4: What is the No. 1 question you have about the Saints that you’re hoping to have an answer to by the end of Saturday’s game? Someone has to win this kicking competition, and so far, neither Charlie Smyth nor Tanner Brown has really established himself. Smyth has the leg power, but he’s dealt with consistency issues throughout camp. The Irishman was expected to enter the season with a firm lead in the battle as he heads into his third season with the team, but Brown has kept the competition alive. If both kickers struggle on Saturday, it could force New Orleans to explore the veteran market at the position. That’s probably the biggest thing I’ll be watching throughout the game. Question 5: Do you expect the Saints to cover as 3.5-point favorites, and do you have a favorite player prop for the game? I do. I think this Saints team is ready to show its home crowd that it’s hungry and prepared for the upcoming season. If I had to pick a player prop, I’m going with Zach Wilson to throw a touchdown pass in the second half of Saturday’s game to help the Saints come out on top. Thanks to Nic for taking the time to answer our questions! What are your thoughts on the Preseason Week 1 matchup, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments!
