summary: After Tuesday’s training camp practice for the Kansas City Chiefs in St. Joe, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo spoke to local media at the podium. As he discussed what he wants to see more from his defense moving forward this preseason, he reiterated a point he has made previously in camp: he wants to see more […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - JUNE 09: Kenneth Walker #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs carries the ball during mandatory minicamp at The University of Kansas Hospital Arrowhead Training Complex on June 09, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images After Tuesday’s training camp practice for the Kansas City Chiefs in St. Joe, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo spoke to local media at the podium. As he discussed what he wants to see more from his defense moving forward this preseason, he reiterated a point he has made previously in camp: he wants to see more physicality, more violence from his defense. It’s hard to simulate in practice, but as he spoke, it was clear that the Chiefs’ offense has been putting the defense in more positions to need physicality in this year’s camp as compared to previous seasons. “Yesterday, I didn’t like the fact that a lot of run plays — and we’re getting a lot more run plays than we used to — a lot of those run plays were going right down the middle of our defense,” Spagnuolo said. If you listen to all of the coaches’ press conferences, it always stands out that the defensive coach is the most unbuttoned about telling local media how he feels about his team or how certain players are performing. On Tuesday, he all but confirmed the much-anticipated shift from Kansas City’s offense to feature the run game and running back Kenneth Walker.

After the lighter, 10-10-10 session of practice, head coach Andy Reid stood at the podium and updated local media on the injury status of a few players. He also confirmed that Chiefs […]

(Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs practiced on Thursday for the last time before the first exhibition game against the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday. After the lighter, 10-10-10 session of practice, head coach Andy Reid stood at the podium and updated local media on the injury status of a few players. Patrick Mahomes will not play on Saturday, per Coach Reid. Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun will split up the game. — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs_Matt) August 13, 2026 He also confirmed that Chiefs starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes will not be playing in Saturday’s game . Chamarri Conner According to Nate Taylor of ESPN, Reid shared that safety Chamarri Conner missed practice due to “banging knees” with wide receiver Tyquan Thornton during Wednesday’s practice. Kader Kohou Veteran slot cornerback Kader Kohou was also held out of Thursday’s practice. Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reported that a sore knee kept Kohou off the practice field . title: Travis Kelce’s 2026 goal: ‘Play at a better level than last year’
summary: On Wednesday, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce addressed the media from his 14th training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph. Kelce returns for what is widely expected to be the final season of a Hall of Fame career. With little more to accomplish either in franchise or league record books, […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Travis Kelce #87 walks to the field during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Wednesday, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce addressed the media from his 14th training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph. Kelce returns for what is widely expected to be the final season of a Hall of Fame career. With little more to accomplish either in franchise or league record books, his motivation to continue playing is more intrinsic. “I’ve still got a lot of love for this game,” Kelce declared. “I still think I can go out and play at a high level, and I want to go out there and prove to myself that I can play at a better level than I did last year. I think that’s probably the biggest thing for me is making sure that I’m accountable for the guys in this room every single play that I’m out there.” What does that better level of football mean for a player who may be the best to ever play his position? “All aspects of football,” Kelce explained. “Being more accountable when the ball is in the air. There were a few games last year that I felt like I put on myself. In the blocking world, being able to get my guys so we can spring guys for bigger gains. And then on top of that, just being a better leader. When we get stuck with adversity hidden, who’s going to want you in that foxhole with them? That’s one of those things that I want — to be one of those guys that everybody counts on to be there and get us out of that foxhole.” Mahomes to Kelce on the sideline in 7 on 7 pic.twitter.com/dn0CAFDdrq — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 5, 2026 Once upon a time, Kelce was not even assured of making the team, let alone setting all major franchise receiving records. At this point, he is focused on making the most of his remaining time with head coach Andy Reid and longtime teammates such as quarterback Patrick Mahomes, defensive tackle Chris Jones and defensive end George Karlaftis. He also has his eye on setting a standard for some of Kansas City’s younger offensive players. “Year One, I was just trying to make the team,” he recalled. “So, I think this year, not only making the team, but trying to figure out how I can bring guys along with me and show them how to play championship football. I think that’s a big thing. And then be able to just enjoy these moments with the guys that I built this culture with. Coach Reid and guys like Pat and Chris Jones and George and everybody.” Many fans have worried about the Chiefs’ wide receiver corps, fearing that the group will underwhelm and again put too much pressure on Kelce. The franchise icon is high on what the group can do to alleviate some of the sticky coverage he has played through in recent seasons. “We’ve got a lot of great players on this offense,” he observed. “It’s not just me. We’ve got some young guys that can play in Cyrus Allen [and] Jalen Royals. Obviously, Quan [Tyquan Thornton] is coming back. He’s looking great running down the field. Then, we’ve got Xavier Worthy, who if you’ve see him in the offseason, we’ve just got to get him a little healthy right now. But he’s a man on a mission right now, and I love the way he’s working and his attention to detail and how he’s running his routes and just the aggression that he’s running his routes in. “When we get him back out here, we’ll be a full arsenal, and I think Pat has done an unbelievable job of not only getting himself ready for here but working with these receivers and making sure that everybody’s living up to that standard of how we’re going to play this year. And you can’t forget Rashee Rice, man. Rashee Rice is out here working his tail off, trying to get right as well, and we love 4 [Rice] for getting out here and getting through these dog days, knowing he’s coming off a knee surgery.” After a well-publicized offseason wedding and celebrity lifestyle, one would expect a difficult transition to dorm life in St. Joseph. If this is Kelce’s last time through Chiefs camp, he will take away an appreciation for the experience. “It’s always going to be my sanctuary,” he remarked. “I think St. Joe’s got a special place in my heart. You need to have these days. You need to have this time of grinding with the guys, being around them all day, every day. You start to create that chemistry and that standard of how we’re going to do things. This year, it’s ramped up even more, especially on the offensive side of the ball. It feels good to have the leaders out there all feeling the same thing.”

When he does reportedly sign, there will need to be a corresponding move on the 90-man offseason roster. One local source is reporting who that will be. Kansas City Chiefs’ latest roster move sees UDFA cut before preseason Week 1 to make room for veteran DE Emmanuel Ogbah | A to Z Sports The Kansas City Chiefs officially announced they have signed veteran defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah. This comes after a few days of maneuvering between the official announcement of Ogbah’s return and his travel to Chiefs training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri, to pass a physical and sign his deal with the team. With a full roster, Kansas City needed to make a corresponding roster move. According to Chiefs Digest’s Matt Derrick, the team has waived undrafted free agent CB Bryce Phillips. Five Observations from Wednesday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/12 | The Mothership 3. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes connected with wide receiver Tyquan Thornton for a deep completion on the first snap of 11-on-11 drills. Mahomes zipped a beautiful deep ball into the arms of Thornton on the very first play of 11-on-11 drills on Wednesday morning, continuing what has been a strong connection throughout camp so far. Notably, Thornton was a standout just a few days ago with multiple catches during Monday’s practice before logging another impressive performance on Wednesday. Why Kenneth Walker III has Chiefs like Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce dreaming big | The Athletic “Make a play out of nothing to a 20-yard gain,” Mahomes said. “That’s going to be the biggest impact I think we’ll have.” Another future Hall of Famer is seeing things a similar way. Tight end Travis Kelce, when asked about his first impression of Walker this week, first answered with a sound instead of words: “Woooo!” “Ken Walker is going to be a hell of a ballplayer for us, if you didn’t know that already,” Kelce said. “He’s got every trait you can possibly want at the running back position.” These Chiefs rookies are turning heads at training camp. Here’s what they bring to the team | FOX4 Woods represents first-round investment, Allen showcases talent emerging into a potential NFL role, and Benson embodies proving to everyone why you belong. All three are competing in positions that the Chiefs needed refinement or an upgrade at; given things pan out, positive implications could be coming to Kansas City football. For now, these three players have emerged as three of the most intriguing in St.Joseph and give Kansas City a reason to keep watching as the season approaches. Brittany Mahomes and children visit Patrick at Kansas City Chiefs training camp | FOX4 The 30-year-old entrepreneur, wife, mother of three and former professional women’s soccer star took to Instagram Tuesday to share photos of her three children – 5-year-old Sterling Skye, 3-year-old Patrick “Bronze,” and 1-year-old Golden Raye – cheering on their dad at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Missouri, during training camp. he photo dump featured the young family of five posing for several photos on Aug. 4, as well as numerous candid shots of the celebrity parents embracing their children at the fun family outing. Seven observations from Day 13 of Chiefs camp: Emmett Johnson gets 1st-team test | The Kansas City Star Running back Emmett Johnson earned a touch with the first team in 11-on-11, which has been a rarity for him so far this camp. Andy Reid seemingly has a lot of candidates for jet action — including Thornton, Cyrus Allen and Xavier Worthy — but it’s been a while since Worthy has participated in team periods as he recovers from a shoulder injury. Around the NFL Report: TE Waller Joining QB Young, Panthers on one-year deal | NFL.com Darren Waller’s comeback from retirement isn’t ending with a swansong for the Miami Dolphins. Waller is signing a one-year deal with the Carolina Panthers, ESPN Insider Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday night. Waller has played for the Baltimore Ravens, Raiders, New York Giants and, last year, with the Dolphins. Daniels sends cease and desist to LSU after Pickett given No. 5 | ESPN At the center of the dispute, according to a statement from Daniels’ spokesperson to ESPN, is that the Tigers are allowing sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett to wear the No. 5 jersey that Daniels wore when he became LSU’s third Heisman Trophy winner in 2023. While Daniels’ jersey hasn’t been retired by the Tigers, it’s the first time a player has worn No. 5 since he left the program for the NFL. WWE reportedly has contract waiting for NFL rookie | NJ.com Ringsidenews.com reported that the WWE has already been watching Rechsteiner “for years” and that “one WWE higher-up believes an offer is essentially guaranteed” whenever Rechsteiner hangs up his cleats. The wide receiver was hit with a six-game suspension last week, according to ESPN.com. A reason for the suspension was not given. Luckily for him, the suspension will not prevent him from participating in preseason games and practices. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Film breakdown: What can Emmanuel Ogbah give the Chiefs in Year 11? There should be no illusions that Ogbah is here to save the day; the edge unit will still be thin even with the addition, but what he can provide the Chiefs is a veteran presence and a player with a decent floor for 2026. George Karlaftis is the only edge rusher on the Chiefs roster with extensive experience, and at the bare minimum, Ogbah should be able to step in and eat up snaps as a run defender and help provide leadership to the Chiefs’young defensive line. The best-case scenario would be for Ogbah to return to the form he displayed during the 2024 season, but this may not be in the cards for him at this point either. title: Chargers-Texans Game Recap: RB Amar Johnson scores twice as Bolts beat Houston 27-7
summary: The Chargers did not play many of their starters, but that didn’t stop the offense from putting up 27 points and the defense from recording a pair of turnover on downs against the Texans in a lopsided win on the road. Second-year running back Amar Johnson caught a pair of passes for 68 yards and […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 13: Trey Lance #5 of the Los Angeles Chargers hands the ball off to Jaquae Jackson #82 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the second quarter of a preseason game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers did not play many of their starters, but that didn’t stop the offense from putting up 27 points and the defense from recording a pair of turnover on downs against the Texans in a lopsided win on the road. Second-year running back Amar Johnson caught a pair of passes for 68 yards and rushed for a pair of touchdowns to lead the Chargers offense. Wide receiver KeAndre-Lambert Smith led the team with four receptions (58 yards) as he played most of the first half with Trey Lance at quarterback. Lance threw for 164 yards on 12-of-20 passing with a pick through two-plus quarters of work while also leading the team with 27 rushing yards. D.J. Uiagalelei completed six-of-nine attempts for 120 yards and a three-yard touchdown to wideout Devonte Ross. Defensively, linebacker Emany Johnson led the team with eight tackles and a tackle for loss. Defensive tackle Jahmeer Carter also chipped in two TFLs and the Chargers’ only sack of the night. First-round pick Akheem Mesidor played roughly two drives and looked good coming off the ball with explosion and power. Second-rounder Jake Slaughter looked comfortable at guard, showing his athleticism and intelligence in dissecting a stunt up front with Branson Taylor at left tackle. The Chargers will be back at SoFi Stadium next week to host the 49ers on August 20th. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. PT. First Quarter The Chargers received the opening kickoff and Trey Lance got the start with the offense. After two runs were stuffed to begin the game, the Bolts got some momentum back thanks to a facemask penalty called on Houston. From there, Lance found wideout KeAndre Lambert-Smith for a pair of receptions to help get the Bolts down the field. Tight end Oronde Gadsden II caught a pass for seven yards and Vidal rushed for four more to give the Chargers a fresh set of downs at the Texans 15-yard line. Unfortunately the offense sputtered with three consecutive incompletions before Cameron Dicker came on to give LA a three-point lead with a 34-yard field goal. The Texans responded with their own 11-play drive that ended in a touchdown from Davis Mills to Jared Wayne which gave Houston a 7-3 lead. The Chargers looked to have earned a stop near the red zone but rookie safety Genesis Smith was called for pass interference and the Texans were given an automatic first at the LAC 18. On the very next play after being flagged, Smith nearly hauled in a one-handed interception but could not get both feet inbounds. Second Quarter After forcing a three-and-out by the Texans to begin the quarter, the Chargers offense — with a shuffled offensive line from the first quarter — looked like a unit with a bit more juice out of the break. Lance led an eight-play, 67-yard drive that featured Brenen Thompson’s first NFL catch, a 14-yard catch-and-run by Gadsden, and a seven-yard touchdown run from second-year running back Amar Johnson. go off, amar !!! pic.twitter.com/k5F37BJcqg — Los Angeles Chargers (@chargers) August 14, 2026 The Texans responded with another impressive drive that featured a healthy mix of both the run and the pass, led by Graham Mertz at quarterback. It took just five plays to get inside the red zone but the Chargers defense clamped down and stopped a third-down run and a QB sneak on fourth to force a turnover on downs. Lance got the Chargers offense to the Texans 24-yard line with a minute left in the half. He had gains of 16 yards to Thompson and 15 yards to running back Jaret Patterson, but tossed an interception that looked as if he never saw the safety over the top sitting on the deep slant route. Houston returned the interception near midfield but could not muster much offense before time ticked out in the half. Third Quarter The Chargers defense came out strong to begin the second half, holding the Texans to 18 yards and six plays on their opening drive. Lance and the Bolts took over, showing some life remained despite the interception to end the first half. With gains of 14 and 19 through the air, plus a 15-yard run, Lance brought the offense to the Houston 26-yard line before things sputtered. An illegal formation penalty on first down was followed by a seven0yard sack to set up 2nd-and-22. After a pair of four-yard runs, Dicker came on and booted a 48-yard kick to increase the Chargers’ lead to 13-7. Third-string quarterback D.J. Uiagalelei replaced Lance and got the Chargers offense moving with throws of 13 and 11 yards just before the end of the quarter. Fourth Quarter On the third play after the break, Uiaglelei hit Johnson in stride on a swing pass to the left. Johnson skipped past the first defender and sprinted 55 yards up the sideline before a defender tripped him up at the one-yard line. On the next play, Johnson scored his second touchdown of the night with a dive up the middle and then rushed for a two-point conversion. + then he scored 😏 pic.twitter.com/gcBJLYIP1l — Los Angeles Chargers (@chargers) August 14, 2026 The Texans had the ball back for just three plays before a blitz from safety Myles Purchase led to a fumble by Davis Mills which was then recovered by rookie linebacker Lander Barton and returned to the Houston 21. UDFA running back Greg Desrosiers took three consecutive carries to begin the drive with gains of seven, nine, and three. After his fourth carry went for a loss of one yard, the Chargers called a play-action boot to the left and Uiagalelei found wideout Devonte Ross for a touchdown to push the lead to 27-7 after Dicker missed the extra point. With Mills still in at quarterback for Houston, the Texans went six plays before once again failing to convert a fourth-and-one agains the Bolts defense. Cornerback Avery Smith came off the edge to trip the running back and the Chargers were back in possession at their 39-yard line. With 2:50 left in regulation, Uiagalelei avoided a sack and broke the pocket before finding Dalevon Campbell for what looked to be a big gain. At the end of Campbell’s catch-and-run, he was stripped by a Texans defender and Houston recovered at their own 32-yard line. The Texans would go on to drain the rest of the clock and the Bolts would go on to leave Reliant Stadium with a 27-7 victory in their first preseason game of the year.

summary: When the Los Angeles Rams travel to take on the Kansas City Chiefs Saturday, the most anticipated competition won’t be between the two teams on the field—it will be Stetson Bennett against Ty Simpson. Bennett has the upper hand as the starter in sultry Kansas City. He will enjoy a far superior supporting cast. Simpson […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 28: Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 28, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Los Angeles Rams travel to take on the Kansas City Chiefs Saturday, the most anticipated competition won’t be between the two teams on the field—it will be Stetson Bennett against Ty Simpson. Bennett has the upper hand as the starter in sultry Kansas City. He will enjoy a far superior supporting cast. Simpson could be joined by players who may not be on the roster in as soon as a few weeks. Savvy spectators will attempt to gauge the quarterbacks not by outcomes but by process. It could look ugly overall for the Rams offense by the time Simpson steps onto the field. Pinpoint passes could fall incomplete. Rushers could go unblocked. Adequate offensive linemen are a finite commodity at the professional level. Most NFL teams can barely field a competent starting five, let alone go two or three deep at the position. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sean McVay calls plays for the Los Angeles Rams and that isn’t likely to change in 2026, but the head coach is once again using the preseason as an opportunity to give play calling experience to the offensive coordinator. McVay officially announced on Thursday that new offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase will call plays against the Kansas City Chiefs in the Rams’ season opener on Saturday . Scheelhaase, considered one of the rising stars of NFL coordinators, first called plays in a preseason game against the L.A. Chargers last year. So this will be his second go-around, and potentially his last year in a role under McVay as he is likely tabbed for more head coaching interviews in 2027. “That production helped Scheelhaase become a legitimate head-coaching candidate despite having only two seasons of NFL coaching experience at the time. He interviewed for multiple vacancies during the 2026 hiring cycle, with interest from Baltimore, Cleveland, Pittsburgh and Las Vegas. ESPN reported he ultimately interviewed for five head-coaching jobs before remaining with Los Angeles. NFL Media’s Daniel Jeremiah also reported that Scheelhaase impressed during those interviews, with his relative lack of experience viewed as one of the few knocks against him. Saturday therefore offers something more valuable than simply another preseason assignment: experience.” The 35-year-old Scheelhaase started his coaching career in 2015 with Illinois, and his first OC role with Iowa State in 2023. He is now entering his third season in the NFL and as an assistant under McVay. It would be an upset if he didn’t become a head coach, following in the footsteps of: Matt LaFleuer Mike LaFleur Kevin O’Connell Zac Taylor (never an OC with the Rams) Raheem Morris (DC) Brandon Staley (DC) Liam Coen Of course, none of the offensive coordinators called plays in the regular season under McVay. This didn’t stop them from being promoted, and Scheelhaase is likely to be in the same boat eventually. Can he call a perfect game for Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson on Saturday? That’s what McVay, and other teams, look to find out.

title: Rams’ rivals sign CB facing 8 felony charges
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are expected to sign cornerback Terrion Arnold, a former first-round pick who was released by the Detroit Lions after he was charged with eight felonies related to an alleged armed robbery. The signing was first teased on HBO’s Hard Knocks on Tuesday, but ESPN’s Adam Schefter says that the deal is now […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold (0) answers a question during rookie minicamp at Detroit Lions headquarters and practice facility in Allen Park on Friday, May 10, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Seattle Seahawks are expected to sign cornerback Terrion Arnold, a former first-round pick who was released by the Detroit Lions after he was charged with eight felonies related to an alleged armed robbery. The signing was first teased on HBO’s Hard Knocks on Tuesday, but ESPN’s Adam Schefter says that the deal is now happening. The Los Angeles Rams do not face the Seahawks until Weeks 16 and 18, meaning that if Arnold manages to get clear of these charges, he could be fully-integrated into Seattle’s defense when the two NFC West rivals finally meet. ESPN sources: former Lions CB Terrion Arnold plans to sign with the Seattle Seahawks. Arnold also had visited the Texans, Saints and Giants. Next the NFL must decide whether to put Arnold on the Commissioner’s Exempt List after he was arrested on felony charges in connection… pic.twitter.com/bVTooM8r6L — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 13, 2026 The signing, and interest shown by other teams including the Giants, Saints, and Texans, indicate a belief around the league that Arnold will eventually be able to play in the NFL again despite facing charges that carry a sentence up to life in prison. Arnold, a 6’ cornerback out of Alabama, was not faring very well with the Lions prior to his problems this year. He was likely competing just to have a role on the defense after struggling for a year and a half and then undergoing shoulder surgery. So even if he does play for the Seahawks, it has yet to be proven that Arnold is good. Furthermore, Arnold is surely facing a suspension even if the charges are dropped or a plea deal with no jail time is reached. That suspension could be relatively short, like six games, or the entire season. But it’s doubtful Arnold would escape a suspension entirely and he’s sure to go on the commissioner’s exempt list immediately. Should the Rams have signed Arnold? Probably not. They’ve done a good job redoing their cornerback room in the offseason. Without these off-field problems.

title: Will Nick Bosa be healthy enough for week one against the Rams?
summary: Nick Bosa, star pass rusher of the San Francisco 49ers, has tendonitis in his right knee and his status for Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams is in doubt. Bosa, who has five sacks against the Rams in 10 career games, tore his ACL in 2025 and missed all but three contests. However, it […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 27: Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco reacts after making a tackle during an NFL Football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Levi's Stadium on October 27, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nick Bosa, star pass rusher of the San Francisco 49ers, has tendonitis in his right knee and his status for Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams is in doubt. Bosa, who has five sacks against the Rams in 10 career games, tore his ACL in 2025 and missed all but three contests. However, it is now tendonitis in the same knee that could cause his absence to extend into the 2026 season. #49ers DE Nick Bosa, who is returning from a torn ACL, is now considered week-to-week due to tendinitis in his surgically repaired knee, per HC Kyle Shanahan. pic.twitter.com/ktLwJ2ILOz — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 11, 2026 Although George Kittle is on track to play against the Rams after tearing his Achilles in the playoffs , a remarkable recovery turnaround, Bosa’s setback is another in a long line of injury problems for the 49ers . Bosa has a history of ACL issues This is the third time Bosa has torn an ACL. He tore his right ACL in high school, his left ACL in 2020, and his right ACL again last year in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals. While this tear was being repaired, his doctor also addressed some tendonitis from the high school injury. Bosa had high hopes after that, as he explains to Albert Breer in a recent interview: “I had a little tendinitis from my high school ACL, and he cleaned that up while he [fixed] my ACL,” Bosa explained. “That’s gone. So it’s like an improvement. So once I’m through this rehab, I feel like my right knee—because that was kind of a chronic issue that I had a little bit, and he cleaned that up in my quad tendon and that hasn’t been an issue at all—could feel better when I’m done with this recovery.” As that interview took place only 10 days ago and Bosa had no known issues with his knee up until that point, this must have been quite concerning to Bosa and Shanahan when it flared up. Shanahan is downplaying any worries, saying it’s a normal thing for an ACL repair and they’ll be looking at it week by week. Week 1 is only four weeks away Will Bosa be healthy enough to fly to Australia to face the Rams? Even if he does, will the inability to work out and the lack of practice mean he’s less than 100%? Interestingly, many of San Francisco’s backups are also hurt. As the depth chart stands, the 49ers have Sam Okuayinonu (ankle issue) behind Bosa, as well as former Ram Ogbo Okoronkwo and rookie third-round pick Romello Height (elbow). Opposite of Bosa would be second-year man Mykel Williams (ACL), but he is also injured, as he’s on PUP and not practicing,. Behind him is Keion White, whose been dealing with a groin injury. Shanahan and Bosa know better than anybody that the Niners’ defense revolves around Bosa. As he goes, so goes the pass rush. If there’s a chance that playing in the game exacerbates the problem, further affecting him this year, will he sit out an extra week? I can’t imagine any Rams fans being disappointed if he does.

Bennett gets the first nod under center in a heated quarterback competition. Bennett and Simpson are competing for the backup job behind Matthew Stafford. The fact that […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - JANUARY 10: Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on January 10, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay announced Thursday that Stetson Bennett will start Saturday in the preseason against the Kansas City Chiefs. Ty Simpson will also play. Bennett gets the first nod under center in a heated quarterback competition. Stetson Bennett will start Saturday’s preseason game against the Chiefs. He and Ty Simpson will both play in the game. OC Nathan Scheelhaase will call the plays, with Sean McVay still serving as head coach. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) August 13, 2026 Bennett and Simpson are competing for the backup job behind Matthew Stafford. The fact that Bennett will play on Saturday tells us this battle may be closer than initially thought. Stafford has been resting on an every-other-day basis after missing the entirety of training camp last year. Bennett has largely been working with the first-string in Stafford’s absence. Simpson mostly has played with the reserves. But Bennett has seemed to struggle with turnovers of late. He threw at least two interceptions in Tuesday’s joint practice session with the Dallas Cowboys. After what reportedly was a hot start to camp, Bennett has cooled. There have not been many reports on how Simpson has fared in practice, especially since camp at Loyola Marymount as concluded and the team moved back to their facility at Woodland Hills. The preseason will be telling for the first-round rookie, and if all goes according to plan he will be put back on the shelf for the regular season. The Rams, of course, hope that Stafford will continue his string of good health and be available for all 17 regular season games in 2026. While Bennett and Simpson should earn the right to backup last year’s MVP, it’s in the best interest of the team that they don’t see the field—except for when LA could rest starters in a meaningless Week 18 contest. Saturday in Kansas City will be an important check-in on the quarterback competition. The outcome could be swayed by how each of Bennett and Simpson perform. Bennett seemed to have a significant lead on the rookie. Simpson may be able to pull ahead starting with a strong performance on the road.

title: Matthew Stafford ranked 1st in 2 categories by Dan Orlovsky
summary: Matthew Stafford has the best mechanics and ball placement of any quarterback in the NFL, according to his former Lions teammate Dan Orlovsky. In an article for ESPN, Orlovsky ranked quarterbacks by seven different traits that he considers to be important, and Stafford showed up four times in the top-4: Stafford did not place in […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff hugs Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford after the Lions' 24-23 win in the NFC wild-card game at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Jan, 14, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Matthew Stafford has the best mechanics and ball placement of any quarterback in the NFL, according to his former Lions teammate Dan Orlovsky. In an article for ESPN, Orlovsky ranked quarterbacks by seven different traits that he considers to be important , and Stafford showed up four times in the top-4: Ball Placement, 1st Mechanics, 1st Decision-Making, 2nd Arm Strength, 4th Stafford did not place in the top-10 in the other three categories, including Pocket Presence, Second-Reaction ability, and Rushing ability. One of the reasons it’s surprising Stafford didn’t make Orlovsky’s top-10 for second-reaction can be found in this paragraph: “I’m looking for creativity here, as well as the ability to throw from weird arm angles and platforms. You’ll notice a lot of the strongest arms make this list, too — that’s obviously key. But mobility and field vision also matter in a big way. So, it’s no shocker that I have Allen at No. 1. He shows all of those second-reaction traits, and he can obviously tuck and run if there’s nothing else available.” Although Orlovsky also mentions working outside the pocket, which quarterback better examplifies “creativity” and “weird arm angles” than Stafford? I get that Orlovsky means improvisation skills, outside of the pocket, when the plan breaks down. But Patrick Mahomes has cited Stafford as his inspiration for weird arm angles and platforms. And still nobody does a no-look pass like Stafford. 2025 MVP Matthew Stafford. pic.twitter.com/eiRlMObo1Q — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) July 13, 2026 Orlovsky did rank Stafford top-2 in three categories, however, like mechanics: “- Repeatable processes that don’t change from rep to rep, even when things get chaotic around the QB That last one is key for Stafford and Burrow. Defenses don’t know what’s coming because every throw looks exactly the same coming out. It’s amazing consistency. The tight connection between Stafford’s upper and lower body allows him to pull off all those no-look throws. Defenses can’t tell the difference until his release, and bam, the ball is going somewhere unexpected.“ Orlovsky wasn’t a fan of Stafford’s pocket presence, though. Stafford and Orlovsky shared a locker room for a couple of years in Detroit, and later Orlovsky had a short stint on the Rams in Sean McVay’s first stint, long before L.A. traded for Stafford. He’s always been a big supporter of Matthew Stafford’s and the Rams. Now he’s just putting a finer point on it.

title: Make 1 change to the Rams defense
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have built one of the NFL’s more aggressive and versatile defenses under Sean McVay and defensive coordinator Chris Shula. The unit has the talent to make life difficult for opposing offenses, but there is always room for improvement. As the Rams prepare for another season with Super Bowl aspirations, perhaps the […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have built one of the NFL’s more aggressive and versatile defenses under Sean McVay and defensive coordinator Chris Shula. The unit has the talent to make life difficult for opposing offenses, but there is always room for improvement. As the Rams prepare for another season with Super Bowl aspirations, perhaps the biggest question isn’t whether the defense needs a major overhaul, but whether one strategic change could make it even better. The interesting part is that there are several directions the Rams could take. There isn’t necessarily one obvious answer, and that is what makes this discussion worth having. Option 1: Change the Scheme The Rams have frequently utilized nickel and dime personnel, allowing them to put more defensive backs on the field and counter modern passing attacks. But could there be a point where the defense becomes too light? Teams such as the San Francisco 49ers, Philadelphia Eagles and Detroit Lions have shown an ability to generate offense against lighter defensive personnel. Physical offensive lines and strong rushing attacks can create problems when defenses prioritize speed and coverage over size. Perhaps the Rams should consider using more size in their base defense. That doesn’t mean abandoning nickel and dime packages. Those formations are essential in today’s NFL. But mixing in more traditional personnel could give the Rams another way to defend teams that want to establish the run and impose their physicality. Another question is coverage. Should the Rams lean more heavily into man-to-man coverage rather than relying so extensively on zone concepts? Man coverage could allow the pass rush more time to get home, but it also places greater responsibility on the defensive backs. Option 2: Change a Player Sometimes the simplest solution is who is on the field. The biggest question marks on the defense right now for the Rams are LB2 and CB3. The Rams could evaluate whether they have their ideal combination at off-ball linebacker. Nate Landman is clearly the Rams “MIKE” linebacker. But Omar Speights is a question mark, only producing middling results when on the field. Could Shaun Dolac or Grant Stuard provide something different? Neither player necessarily has to be viewed as a replacement right now. Instead, the question is whether the Rams could benefit from giving another linebacker more snaps and seeing whether that player provides improved instincts, tackling, coverage ability or physicality. Option 3: Change the Amount of Blitzing The Rams could also look at how frequently they send additional pressure. More blitzing could create more one-on-one opportunities for the defensive line and force quarterbacks to make quicker decisions. On the other hand, excessive blitzing can leave the secondary vulnerable and create explosive plays. Perhaps the answer isn’t simply “blitz more” or “blitz less.” It could be finding the right situations to bring pressure. Option 4: Add More Disguises Another possibility is changing what opposing quarterbacks see before the snap. The Rams have utilized plenty of quarters coverage over the last 5 seasons, but could they benefit from presenting more varied looks? Showing one coverage before the snap and rotating into another afterward can force quarterbacks to process information differently. The goal wouldn’t necessarily be to abandon what already works. It would be to make the defense more unpredictable. Option 5: Different Defensive Coordinator Chris Shula has done a good enough job for the Rams as the defensive coordinator in his two-plus seasons but is good enough what the Rams need? The Rams have a Super Bowl caliber roster. The team added Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, and Jaylen Watson this offseason. It’s time to deliver. Is Chris Shula the right man for the job? So, Rams fans, if you could make exactly one change to this defense, what would it be? Would you alter the scheme, change a player, adjust the amount of blitzing or add more pre-snap disguises, a new defensive coordinator? Or something else altogether? There may not be one correct answer. The fun is deciding which adjustment could give the Rams the biggest defensive advantage.

title: Puka Nacua really wants to stay with Rams
summary: Puka Nacua has been stating throughout the offseason that he wants to stay with the Los Angeles Rams, and that desire has not appeared to change. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Puka Nacua has been stating throughout the offseason that he wants to stay with the Los Angeles Rams, and that desire has not appeared to change. During an appearance on the Impaulsive podcast that premiered on Wednesday, Nacua reaffirmed that he wants to stay with the Rams long term. Does L.A. want to pony up the contract numbers that it will take to make it happen? Nacua’s been one of the best wide receivers in the league with the Rams and he’s also ( as is well documented ) been having a lot of fun in Los Angeles. Naturally, Puka wants to stay with the Rams. The other side of things is that Nacua has allegedly made some poor choices in the past. There’s no way around that, though he can learn and grow. He also may be prone to injury, though he’s shown he’s also one of the tougher players in the league. Those factors could be deterrents to the Rams wanting to extend Nacua. That’s the reality. The Rams and Nacua have a few potential scenarios ahead as L.A. can extend him, they can choose not to extend him, they can franchise tag him, they could trade him if there is a buyer. A lot of options for Nacua, but his preferred option, as he tells it, would be for the Rams to keep him in L.A. I’m told it could be a few days that it could sideline him for, which anyone would sign up for. Not having Puka for a few days, not a huge deal. But the Rams are being careful with him and that groin injury that he suffered yesterday. The same way they’re being careful with their prize defensive end, Myles Garrett, who has got some swelling in his knee.” Los Angeles Rams at Kansas City Chiefs: How to watch, listen to and live stream 2026 Preseason Week 1 (ramswire) “The Rams host the Chiefs on Saturday at Arrowhead Stadium to kick off their 2026 preseason. Joining Cynthia Frelund and Chris Rose on “Inside Training Camp,” Adams explained the similarities and differences between the two.“ “The biggest similarity is they can both spin it wherever they want,” Adams said. “The biggest difference is Matthew prefers not to give away anything to the defense before he throws the ball. I think that’s turned Aaron into who he is, being able to throw on the run, escape the pocket and throw it a certain way.” Rams unite communities through girls flag football with Club Team Initiative (therams) “The Los Angeles Rams are driven by the fact that talent is equally distributed, but opportunity is not. The teams recently launched Rams Community Club Team Initiative is their latest effort to unite communities through access to football and provide resources for young athletes to grow on and off the field. The Rams Club Team Initiative was created to build an accessible and community-rooted girls flag football ecosystem where athletes ages 6–18 can develop their skills, confidence, leadership, and lifelong connection to the game. Through a focus on accessibility, sustainability, culture, and development, the program aims to create opportunities for girls while establishing sustainable community-based programs across the Los Angeles market.“ NFL Team Values 2026: Cowboys Lead at $15.5B, Average Up 31% (sportico.com) “The Cincinnati Bengals have been parked at No. 32 for seven straight years in Sportico ’s annual NFL team valuations. title: Fernando Mendoza makes some plays in Raiders’ preseason debut
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders opened the 2026 NFL preseason Thursday night at home in a 27-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Here are some notes from game: Overall, it was a typical preseason game. There will ups and downs. The first-unit offense looked extremely sharp. Mendoza flashed as did Bech and Washington. The defnese? Well, […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders throws against the Arizona Cardinals in the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders opened the 2026 NFL preseason Thursday night at home in a 27-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Here are some notes from game: No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza debuted on the Raiders’ second drive, late in the first quarter. He played with the second-team offense after coach Klint Kubiak said he could play with some first-team offensive linemen. But potential starter Jack Bech played and converted his second third-down of the game, this time with Mendoza. Bech had nice connections with rookie Malik Benson and hit Bech for a touchdown (his third third down conversion) to tie the game at 14-14 on Mendoza’s second drive, which he was impressive on. He threw some darts. Mendoza played into the fourth quarter. He went 10 of 16 passing for 96 yards and was sacked once. Was it a great night for the rookie? No, was it a solid, nice, promising start that he and the team can build upon? For sure. Kubiak was pleased with Mendoza’s performance and called him “an ascending player.” The coach said Mendoza will continue to get a lot of reps in the preseason, though, it still seems Kirk Cousins is on track to start Week 1. In fact, Kubiak said it’s Cousins’ job to lose. Barring a big change, the job will be Cousins, as expected. Rookie Trey Zuhn played right tackle with the second team. He had been playing some recently, but has shown he’s versatile. Washington sparked a second-quarter touchdown drive with a beautiful 53-yard run and he then converted a fourth down. The fourth-round pick could be a big part of the offense. He has a burst. He also got a great block from left tackle Charles Grant, who could end up in the mix at right tackle. The first-team offense, led Cousins, started the game. Cousins hit Bech for a 10-yard catch on third down to open the game. Then, Ashton Jeanty had a nice run on third down, followed by big pass plays from Cousins to Tre Tucker and then a 13-yard touchdown pass to tight end Michael Mayer to cap a 10-play, 68-yard drive that took just more than five minutes. In Kubiak’s first drive (yes, it’s the preseason) as the Raiders’ head coach and offensive playcaller, he led a great drive. Cousins was 5 of 6 passing for 50 yards on the drive. They were three-for-three on third down on the drive. Cousins has been efficient all training camp and it translated to the preseason. The first-team offensive made holes for Jeanty and got a nice push. A nice start to the Rick Dennison era. The Raiders’ first-team defense didn’t far as well. The Cardinals sliced them up in the passing game, led by quarterback Jacoby Brissett. They had a 18-yard gainer on third and 11. Cornerbacks Eric Stokes and Darien Porter had a tough drive as Arizona tied the game late in the first quarter. Brissett hit Marvin Harrison Jr. for a game-tying score to cap a 10-play, 73-yard drive. Led by former Raider Gardner Minshew, the Cardinals went right down the field on their second drive to take a 14-7 lead. Linebacker Tommy Eichenberg and rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford has some struggles on the drive and the Raiders had some penalty issues. Backup linebacker Cody Lindenberg, a core special teamer as a rookie, looked good at linebacker. Rookie Jermod McCoy, playing in his first game since a 2024 knee injury, was beat for a touchdown on the drive. The Cardinals were 10-for 10 passing on the first two series. Minshew led another great offensive series as the Cardinals scored on their third series. McCoy had another rough series. The Cardinals were 15-for-15 passing in the first half and had 78 rushing yards in the half. The Raiders were sloppy (which predictable for this time of year) and had eight penalties for 75 yards. That’s something to work on next week. Star defensive end Maxx Crosby did not play in the game. Kubiak said earlier this week he didn’t know if Crosby, who is coming back from an offseason knee surgery, would play. He has been practicing during all of training camp. He was in pads during pre-game warmups, though. Part owner Tom Brady at the game as he has been in the past during the preseason. Raiders minority owner Tom Brady is here for the team's preseason opener. Walked out to the field with GM John Spytek and was talking with majority owner Mark Davis on the sidelines. pic.twitter.com/2G1ia8IawA — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) August 13, 2026 Jackson Powers-Johnson was starting at a guard spot and Caleb Rogers was with the backups. They had been rotating during camp in recent days, That battle will likely continue in training camp. Powers-Johnson played in the second quarter with Mendoza. Porter started while rookie Jermod McCoy and Zeke McCoy worked with the second team. Recent camp standout Decamerion Richardson wasn’t suited up. Also, second-year wide receiver Dont’e Thornton, who been out for an undisclosed reason for about a week, was also out. The Raiders haven’t named captains for the season yet, but Thursday night they were Brock Bowers, Nakobe Dean and Segun Olubi. Dean and Olubi were free-agent additions this offseason. Deven Thompkins and rookie running back Mike Washington started the game as kick returners. Washington also was on the field on the first drive some. Thompkins had a nice night returning kicks. Rookie kicker Kansei Matzuzawa kicked off to start the second half and it went out of bounds. He then missed a 38-yarder. Matt Gay may be in the driver’s seat to replace Daniel Carlson. On a night much of the defensive line struggled, undrafted free agent defensive tackle Gary Smith flashed some. Greedy Vance had a nice night at nickel corner on an otherwise rough night for the young defensive backs. Promising undrafted free-agent Cian Slone had a sack in the fourth quarter. No. 3 quarterback Aidan O’Connell finished the game and was 4 of 13 for 85 yards. He should get plenty of time in the final two games to perhaps try to drum up some trade interest. Pass-rusher Brennan Jackson injured his foot, according to Kubiak. Overall, it was a typical preseason game. There will ups and downs. The first-unit offense looked extremely sharp. Mendoza flashed as did Bech and Washington. The defnese? Well, it was a tough night against both the run and the pass. Now, it’s back to training camp with a month to go before the regular season starts.

title: 5 Las Vegas Raiders’ rookies to keep tabs on in preseason game against Arizona Cardinals
summary: Las Vegas Raiders football is finally back as they are set to have their first preseason game of the 2026 NFL season on Thursday against the Arizona Cardinals. Kickoff is at 5 p.m. PT. While Silver & Black Pride’s Bill Williamson noted a few players he’ll be keeping tabs on, including a few rookies, here […]
full_text: Jun 3, 2026; Henderson, NV, USA; Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Hezekiah Masses (35) runs a drill during organized team activities at Intermountain Health Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Las Vegas Raiders football is finally back as they are set to have their first preseason game of the 2026 NFL season on Thursday against the Arizona Cardinals. Kickoff is at 5 p.m. PT. While Silver & Black Pride’s Bill Williamson noted a few players he’ll be keeping tabs on , including a few rookies, here we’ll touch on other first-year pros worth watching and what they have to prove against the Cardinals. CB Hezekiah Masses If we’re picking the biggest winner of training camp in Las Vegas so far, Masses has to be the choice . The fifth-rounder had a strong showing during the spring and picked up where he left off when the team returned from break, getting reps with the first team defense this summer. He’s competing with second-year pro Darien Porter for a starting job, and those two will likely get plenty of reps against the Cardinals. Arizona isn’t exactly flush with talent at wide receiver, but rookie quarterback Carson Beck had an impressive showing in last week’s Hall of Fame game , completing 15 of 19 pass attempts (78.9%) for 188 yards and a touchdown to test the Raiders’ secondary. That led to a three-catch, 99-yard performance from wide receiver Jalen Brooks and five grabs for 66 yards for fellow receiver Reggie Virgil, so maybe the position group has more depth than what originally meets the eye. [Editor’s Note: NFL Insider Ian Rapoport reported that Beck won’t play for the Cardinals tonight due to a rib injury sustained in the Hall of Fame game.] WR Malik Benson If Masses is the big winner of training camp so far, Benson holds the second spot on the podium. Another Day 3 selection (sixth-round), he seems to have quickly found a connection with fellow rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Those two appear to have instant chemistry, with several camp reports noting that Mendoza has found the Oregon product on crossing routes, which are a staple of head coach Klint Kubiak’s playbook. Thursday will be the first stress test and opportunity for the duo to show the public what they’ve been building over the last couple of weeks, assuming they’ll get plenty of time on the field together. Also, Benson has the potential to contribute from the slot or out wide, so it will be interesting to see how the coaching staff decides to use him against Arizona. CB Jermod McCoy The organization is planning to have McCoy play in this game. The fourth-round pick has had a few days off and primarily worked with the second-team defense during camp despite being considered one of the most talented cornerbacks in the draft class. That’s because the Tennessee product missed all of last season with a torn ACL, which is also what makes him a good player to keep tabs on against the Cardinals. McCoy hasn’t played in a game since the Volunteers’ 42-17 loss to eventual National Champion Ohio State in the 2024 College Football Playoff. So, it will be interesting to see if he can pick up where he left off because the first-round talent’s tape was pretty impressive pre-knee injury. Again, that’s assuming he plays, though, which is unclear at the time of writing. DT Gary Smith III It’s no secret that the Raiders’ defense is looking for someone to step up at nose tackle, especially if defensive coordinator Rob Leonard is going to run a lot more 3-4 or odd fronts this season. There hasn’t been much reported about the position, but our Marcus Johnson noted that Smith caught his eye during this past Friday’s practice session. Despite being an undrafted free agent, the UCLA product has a chance to carve out a role as a gap filler in the trenches. Starting the preseason strong would be a good way to accomplish that goal and generate some buzz for the rest of the summer. WR E.J. Williams Along the same lines, Williams hasn’t received a ton of attention since Benson is seemingly stealing the show among the rookie wideouts. But a handful of reports from camp have noted that the Indiana product has made some plays to help catch the coaching staff’s eye. The Silver and Black are looking for a wideout or two to fill out the depth chart, and Thursday is an opportunity for Williams to stand out from the rest of the competition. If Mendoza gets a decent amount of playing time, it should help that the former Hoosier duo already has some chemistry.

title: 4 defensive areas of focus for  Las Vegas Raiders preseason opener
summary: Las Vegas Raiders open the 2026 preseason at home against the Arizona Cardinals on Thursday, August 13, 2026. While most of Raider Nation wants to focus on the offense, let’s actually take a look at some key spots on defense. During the offseason, the Raiders made multiple defensive free-agent acquisitions and drafted more defensive players […]
full_text: . | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders open the 2026 preseason at home against the Arizona Cardinals on Thursday, August 13, 2026. While most of Raider Nation wants to focus on the offense, let’s actually take a look at some key spots on defense. During the offseason, the Raiders made multiple defensive free-agent acquisitions and drafted more defensive players in April. On paper, this is one of the best defenses the Raiders have fielded in a long time. Maxx Crosby finally has some real star power and championship-caliber players around him. A front seven that looks absolutely ferocious. With a back end of speedy, physical cornerbacks and safeties. The defensive coordinator Leading these men and the holdovers from last season is first-year defensive coordinator Rob Leonard. Leonard got the promotion from run-game coordinator and defensive line coach. Leonard has previously worked under elite defensive minds such as Brian Flores, Tom Coughlin, Steve Spagnuolo, Patrick Graham and Mike MacDonald. He’s obviously not going to show his hand in game one of the preseason, but what we will see is what he emphasizes in fundamentals and mentality. The tenacity and edge he is trying to coax out of his players from the stars to the guys here for the summer. Tonka Hemingway Of all the additions made in the offseason, the defensive line was not one of them. Hemingway has been one of the talk of training camp thus far. When a player is applauded for gains made in the offseason, one can only be excited to see how it translates. Hemingway has been hard to stop and harder to block. Causing many to wonder just how good he can be. It’s one thing to have success against an offensive line on the rebound, but wreaking havoc on another team is a good barometer of where he’s at. The battle for the number 2 and nickel cornerback In the offseason, the Raiders set out to completely overhaul their secondary. Re-signing Eric Stokes to be the number one corner and traded a sixth-round draft pick for former Pro Bowl nickel/slot corner Taron Johnson. It was only the beginning because John Spytek had just warmed up the stove and was beginning to cook. Drafting cornerbacks Jermod McCoy in the fourth round and Hezekiah Masses in the fifth round has thus far given the Raiders a major shot in the arm. McCoy, when healthy, was considered a first-round-level talent. Masses has performed in training camp like a first-round-level talent. A switch in defensive philosophy to bigger, stronger and faster corners plays into a man-coverage-dominant scheme. Darrien Porter, in his second year, may benefit greatly from this switch as well. Iron sharpens iron and competition is good for everyone. With CB 2 up for grabs and a shot at nickel on the line it will be fun to see who snatches it. Treydan Stukes In the second round, Raider Nation wanted a wide receiver to pair with Fernando Mendoza; instead, they got Stukes. When Stukes wasn’t getting immediate first-team reps, some were ready to call it a waste of a pick. More prudent observers pointed out that being asked to watch from a broader vantage point was instructional. As training camp has progressed, so has Stukes. He’s getting some run with both the ones and twos and making quality plays in practice. He’s got all the size and athleticism and he is gaining confidence and knowledge by the day. This first preseason action will give us an indication of where he is. Health is wealth omissions Linebacker has been a position not properly addressed with elite-level players for far too long. Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean are so good we should only be teased with a quick series to see them knock off the rust and get off the field healthy. Maxx Crosby, we can imagine, is chomping at the bit and probably chewing it up like a racehorse in the blocks. Precisely why he shouldn’t participate in the first meaningless preseason game of the year. While he is itching to hit someone other than his teammates, keeping his snaps down and maintaining his health is more important. Unpopular as that opinion may be, Crosby’s health should be paramount to the team in more ways than one. Ideally, the first-team defense won’t play more than a series or two. Preferably, positions without battles going on get only the first series, and the positions with challengers get the second.

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - JULY 30: Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (2) and head coach Jeff Hafley talk on the field during the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on July 30, 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We are just one day away from the Miami Dolphins taking the field for their first preseason game in 2026. The team has undergone many major changes — from hiring new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan who brought in Jeff Hafley as the team’s new head coach, to dumping former first-round quarterback Tua Tagovailoa in favor of former Packers’ backup, Malik Willis. Speaking of Willis, Miami’s new signal-caller is expected to play in Friday’s preseason tilt against the Washington Commanders according to Hafley. When asked on Wednesday if he planned on getting the new Dolphins quarterback action this early during the preseason, Miami’s coach responded, “ I am. But, as you said, things can change. ” According to those in attendance, Miami’s offense struggled to produce against a strong Commanders defensive front during the teams’ joint practice yesterday. Assuming that was the case, expect Hafley to ask Willis and company to work on cleaning things up quickly in an effort to look competent when the action kicks off at 7:00 p.m. (eastern time) on Friday night. After filling in for injured starter Jordan Love at times during the 2025 NFL season — and accumulating 422 yards passing on 30 completions, while adding 123 yards rushing and scoring 5 total touchdowns — Willis signed a three-year, $67.5 million deal with the Dolphins. Miami’s new leadership group is hoping to be able to skip a few steps in the organization’s latest rebuild attempt by signing a young, mobile playmaker at the quarterback position and having him find success. He’ll seemingly get his first chance to do so tomorrow night in Landover, MD.

title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: The K1 Era Begins!
summary: Now that the decision has been made, we can argue about everything that occurred. Was it a true competition? Was it even a competition? Was it fair? Are the Vikings giving up on JJ already? Yada, yada, yada. Don’t really matter. It is as it should be. Kyler has done well in practices since being […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that the decision has been made, we can argue about everything that occurred. Was it a true competition? Was it even a competition? Was it fair? Are the Vikings giving up on JJ already? Yada, yada, yada. Don’t really matter. It is as it should be. Kyler has done well in practices since being named the starter though. That is what you want to see. During Day 11 of training camp, after being named starting quarterback, Kyler Murray responded with an exceptionally accurate performance. Operating exclusively with the first-team offense, Murray completed 15 of 16 pass attempts across 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 drills. His single incompletion of the day was a deep pass to Jordan Addison that fell just out of reach. He quickly rebounded, connecting with Addison on back-to-back plays—first on a perfectly timed out route and then on a touch pass to the sideline. Murray highlighted the afternoon by hitting Justin Jefferson Murray carried that high-efficiency momentum into Day 12, showcasing his ability to extend plays and test the defense deep. He completed 14 of 17 pass attempts, including a highly efficient 9-for-11 mark during 11-on-11 team periods. The practice featured several explosive highlights, including a deep completion downfield to Justin Jefferson and a play where Murray escaped defensive pressure to find tight end T.J. Hockenson along the sideline. He closed out another strong day by ripping a throw to Tai Felton in space and finding Jauan Jennings with a pinpoint pass. 2026 Vikings Training Camp Full Schedule https://www.vikings.com/schedule/vikings-events/training-camp/schedule DATE : TIME : PRACTICE Thursday, Aug. 13 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Monday, Aug. 17 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Wednesday, Aug. 19 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. : Joint Practice with Baltimore Ravens Thursday, Aug. 20 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. : Joint Practice with Baltimore Ravens The Minnesota Vikings 2026 preseason schedule features three matchups Week 1: Saturday, August 15 at New York Giants (1:00 PM ET) Week 2: Saturday, August 22 vs. Baltimore Ravens (12:00 PM ET) Week 3: Friday, August 28 at Denver Broncos (Time TBD) Minnesota Vikings News and Links Kyler Murray Quickly Off to Great Start as Vikings’ Official Starter https://www.si.com/nfl/vikings/onsi/kyler-murray-quickly-off-great-start-vikings-official-starter-01kzw818r42 g Murray spoke to the media after practice on Tuesday. His message about becoming the starting quarterback of the Minnesota Vikings couldn’t have been clearer. “It feels good. Obviously, any competitor, you play this game, you want a chance to lead the guys on Sunday and have an opportunity to go win. And whatever that calls for me to do on Sundays, Mondays, Thursdays — whatever it is, I take this job with great pride. There’s been a lot of great quarterback play here in the past, and I just hope to continue to carry on that tradition.” Murray said all the right things to the media, but he also did all the right things at practice. His incredibly accurate day throwing the football. He distributed the ball well to the Vikings receivers, including Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Tai Felton and others. Kyler Murray Immediately Rewards Vikings for Naming Him Starter https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/kyler-murray-immediately-rewards-vikings-001327155.html Then, the team went out for their first practice with the 29-year-old Murray officially crowned as QB1. And according to multiple reports from those who stuck around to watch… Kyler responded with hands down his best practice as a Viking. Whether psychological effect or coincidence, Kyler Murray just had easily one of his best practices of camp. Only one ball hit the ground all day. Several chunk gains through the air to Jefferson, Addison, Felton. Looked very comfortable with decision-making. — Will Ragatz (@WillRagatz) August 11, 2026 Vikings practice just ended. Thought Kyler Murray looked sharp today. Multiple corner routes to the right sideline. Believe Carson Wentz took more reps today than he has all camp, too. — Alec Lewis (@alec_lewis) August 11, 2026 Training camp recap, Day 12: https://www.purpleinsider.football/p/training-camp-recap-day-12 Training camp recap, Day 11: Kyler rolls as QB1 https://www.purpleinsider.football/p/training-camp-recap-day-11-kyler Vikings GM Nolan Teasley Doesn’t Hold Back on Kyler Murray Decision https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/vikings-gm-nolan-teasley-doesn-225136534.html With the Vikings now having a new QB1, the team’s general manager, Nolan Teasley, spoke about the reason for the decision. “Really excited about what Kyler can do in this system with this level of coaching. K.O., Josh McCown, Frank Smith is on staff here, Wes Phillips,” Teasley said in an Aug. 12 video from SiriusXM NFL Radio. “So right then and there, you’re really excited about the direction that he can go and the intricacies of the system, being a wide-zone scheme that is going to implement some keepers and use his athleticism, get him outside of the pocket. “That puts the defense in conflict. So yeah, I’m just really excited about the direction that we’re headed… Learning Kyler as the starter, what he does well, what he’s comfortable with and being able to focus in that regard, then allow that timing element with whether it’s [Justin Jefferson] or T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison and all the skill players that he’ll be surrounded with.” Moreover, Teasley didn’t forget to mention McCarthy and the effort he saw from the third-year player in his attempt to win the starting job. “Really appreciative of the way that J.J. McCarthy handled the news this morning,” Teasley added. “He’s a professional. Really, really excited about his trajectory in the system as well. It’s a competitive room. That was the goal from the outset, and so we’re still headed in that direction. “But I’m really excited about where we are today… Just really appreciative of the way that he handled it and that his story is not written, and we’re going to continue to coach and develop him.” Vikings Predicted to Be Playoff Bound With Kyler Murray With the decision now made in Minnesota, CBS Sports’ Emory Hunt shared an outlook on the Vikings with the team having Murray as QB1. “The expectations are to get to the postseason and win a postseason game because that’s why you go out and get Kyler Murray,” Hunt said in an Aug. 11 appearance on “CBS Sports HQ.” “If you didn’t want to enhance your chances of getting deep into the postseason and making perhaps a Super Bowl run, you would have stayed with J.J. McCarthy and rode the wave of improvement from week to week. “But you go and get Kyler Murray because you felt like you have a high-floor defense and a high-floor offense from a personnel perspective. So why not go get a quarterback that can help enhance that and move this thing forward? 11-6 is the floor for the Vikings. Anything they build on top of that is just gravy.” With Kyler Murray being named Vikings’ starting QB as expected, what becomes of J.J. McCarthy? https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/article/with-kyler-murray-being-named-vikings-starting-qb-as-expected-what-becomes-of-jj-mccarthy-173813293.html The bad part for J.J. McCarthy being named the Minnesota Vikings’ backup on Tuesday, before the Vikings even play a preseason game, isn’t that he lost the competition. It’s that Tuesday’s news announced by Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell that Kyler Murray had been named starting quarterback was confirmation that it was never really a competition at all. The NFL offseason can be long and some pumped up the “competition” between Kyler Murray and McCarthy like it was a real thing, but everyone should have known better. There was a small chance that McCarthy had a fantastic camp, showing…
