He’s a kid that, literally every install that we do, run and pass, he’s a kid that when you’re walking up in front of the group and you’re teaching, his eyes never leave you. Never. title: Jets injury update: Joseph Ossai is off the physically unable to perform list
summary: The Jets have activated defensive end Joseph Ossai from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. Ossai (6-4, 263) was placed on the Active/PUP list on July 28. He signed with the Jets in March after playing his first four seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals. During his time with the Bengals from 2022-25, Ossai played […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Joseph Ossai (58) walks for the locker room with trainers in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 14 game between the Buffalo Bills and the Cincinnati Bengals at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, N.Y., on Sunday, Dec. 7, 2025. The Bills overcame a halftime deficit to win 39-34. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Jets have activated defensive end Joseph Ossai from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. Ossai (6-4, 263) was placed on the Active/PUP list on July 28. He signed with the Jets in March after playing his first four seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals. During his time with the Bengals from 2022-25, Ossai played in 61 games while racking up 116 total tackles, 44 quarterback hits and 14.5 sacks. He recorded a career-high 5 sacks in each of the last two seasons. In 2025, Ossai set a personal best by playing 616 defensive snaps, and he also contributed 71 snaps on special teams. A player ends up on the PUP list if he is not able to practice the first day of training camp due to a football related injury. He can come off the list at any point in camp once he is ready to start practicing. The Jets did not disclose what injury put Ossai on the list, but the team is happy to have him back. He was one of the big free agent signings of the offseason. Ossai is projected to be a starting edge defender across from David Bailey. While Bailey will be the primary pass rusher off the edge, Ossai’s job will be to set the edge and collapse the pocket. It is very unlikely we will see Ossai in Friday night’s preseason opener, but he could make an appearance at some point in the exhibition season after he gets some practice time under his belt.

title: Eagles Training Camp Notes: Practice ends after a fight breaks out
summary: Today marked the eleventh Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES UP NEXT: The Eagles have a walkthrough closed to media access on Friday. Then they’ll travel down to Charm City on Saturday to play the Baltimore […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Moro Ojomo #97 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today marked the eleventh Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES FIGHT! After a rep where the Eagles ran the ball, Fred Johnson and Moro Ojomo were jawing at each other before the latter took a swing at the former. Ojomo’s punch did not connect and the two were quickly broken up. The Eagles had another running play rep and Johnson flattened Ojomo into the ground by basically tackling him. The two had words for each other and Ojomo swung again as Johnson walked away. While Johnson was walking away, Ty Robinson and some other Eagles defenders came up to Johnson to express their displeasure and stick up for Ojomo. While a group of bodies formed around Johnson, Ojomo ran over and dove into Johnson’s legs to take the big man down to the ground. This prompted some more shoving and shouting from other players before everything was eventually broken up. Nick Sirianni then decided to call practice for the day (there probably wasn’t too much time left anyway). We’re clearly at the point in camp where guys are tired of going up against each other and probably looking forward to being able to hit players on another team. Sirianni and Howie Roseman talking with Fred Johnson after practice. Sirianni dispatches Johnson with Jordan Mailata to go cool down with a @RitasItalianIce . pic.twitter.com/QEZz4kCkjP — PHLY Eagles (@PHLY_Eagles) August 13, 2026 Howie Roseman talking to Moro Ojomo after today’s practice: pic.twitter.com/5uFS2l7jn9 — EJ Smith (@EJSmith94) August 13, 2026 EAGLES INJURY REPORT: DID NOT PARTICIPATE: WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) Based on his pre-practice rehab work , Smith doesn’t seem far off from returning to the field. WR Makai Lemon (hamstring) In contrast to Smith, a Lemon return does not appear to be imminent. The rookie receiver has been unavailable for team drills in at least 11 of the team’s total 19 practices (eight spring, 11 summer) this offseason. Lemon did get some work in with Hurts after Thursday’s practice. CB Quinyon Mitchell (glute) Q got banged up in Tuesday’s practice. Seems like the Eagles are going to be cautious and rest him for a bit. CB Cooper DeJean (groin) This is a new injury. CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder) CB Tariq Castro-Fields (heel) S Cole Wisniewski (hamstring) EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby (ankle) RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring) LIMITED PARTICIPATION: WR Danny Gray (concussion) Gray was upgraded to limited today after missing multiple practices. RETURNED TO PRACTICE: WR Johnny Wilson (knee) was removed from the injury report after missing multiple days. He was wearing a compression sleeve on his right leg. IN-PRACTICE INJURY: RB Saquon Barkley was getting looked at by a trainer at one point, according to Brooks Kubena . Currently no indication of anything serious but something to keep an eye on. ACTIVE/PHYSICALLY UNABLE TO PERFORM EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) RESERVE/NON-FOOTBALL INJURY S Tucker Large JALEN HURTS UPDATE: THE BAD: One practice after becoming the first quarterback in NFL history to throw an interception in a practice setting , Hurts threw ANOTHER pick today. One can only wonder if the Eagles will SABOTAGE him once again by posting a clip of this play as well. Jokes aside, I thought Mac McWilliams made a really nice play to jump Hollywood Brown’s route in the flat to make the interception at the goal line and prevent a touchdown. Not a terrible throw or decision by any means. Just an even better play McWilliams. Hurts also did have a fade ball to Johnny Wilson get knocked down by Riq Woolen, who has the size to be very effective at defending those jump ball throws. Hurts threw a Donovan McNabb-like wormburner on a play action rollout to the right. THE GOOD: Hurts connected with Dontayvion Wicks a lot today. He found the receiver towards the sideline just shy of the pylon with McWilliams trailing to set the offense up near the goal line. Hurts hit Wicks again on a touchdown on a play where the receiver routed up Riq Woolen to create just enough separation for a catch along the right sideline in the end zone. Hurts ripped a ball to Dallas Goedert in bounds along the back of the end zone for a touchdown. Andrew Mukuba trailed on the play. Hurts hit Moore on an out route to the left to move the offense into goal-to-go territory. It’s become routine for Saquon Barkley to have some good looking runs in each practice. He looks primed for another big year. The run game as a whole has shown promise, for as much as I can tell from non-tackling practices. Michael Carter II had tight coverage to force Wicks to try to make a one-handed leaping grab in the end zone. Wicks’ effort was unsuccessful. DAILY DARIUS COOPER IS AWESOME REMINDER: Today was a rare day where I did not write Cooper’s name down in my notes, except for that he wasn’t getting as much first team run with Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore mostly ahead of him. I did ask Nick Sirianni about Cooper’s standout summer prior to practice. And perhaps it’s notable that Cooper’s post-practice media availability took place at the podium, as opposed to the off-camera “mixed zone” area typically reserved for the non-big name players. While outlining the Eagles’ WR position back in June, Nick Sirianni grouped Darius Cooper with Johnny Wilson as “dirty work” role guys. I asked Sirianni if Cooper, who’s had a great camp, has earned playing time on offense. Answer: pic.twitter.com/gEairaMbwe — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 13, 2026 I’d go stock up™ on McWilliams, who was taking first-team nickel corner reps today. He’s stacking his best days of the summer recently. I’d go stock down™ on Hollywood Brown. The veteran receiver has been the target on most of Hurts’ interceptions in training camp this summer. Brown also had a bad drop while wide open on a bubble screen. Brown received $5 million fully guaranteed when the Eagles signed him, so, the money doesn’t make it a no-brainer for the team to move on from the veteran receiver. But he just hasn’t had a great camp and he’s been outshined by other Eagles receivers. Brown got some extra work in with Hurts after practice to presumably help getting on the same page. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE UPDATE: Tanner McKee was first up at QB2 but I didn’t write down his name for anything notable. Andy Dalton had a nice connection with Will Shipley on the wheel route along the left sideline with Smael Mondon Jr. trailing. Dalton followed that up with overthrowing an open Gray in the end zone … on a play where it looked like both E.J. Jenkins and Darius Cooper were also open on the left side that he was rolling to. Dalton also threw a ball that appeared to be uncatchable out of the back of the end zone. Kelee Ringo saw some first-team outside cornerback reps with Quinyon Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, and Jonathan Jones all not practicing. He even had a rep where it looked like his tight coverage on Elijah Moore over the middle helped to force an incompletion. On the whole, Ringo has not had a good summer, and I don’t know if he definitely makes the team. He can contribute on special teams but it’s really hard to trust him on defense. But, hey, at least he had a positive moment today. Jakorian Bennett allowed a short catch to Danny Gray and didn’t look to be in good position to make a tackle if these were live drills. Gray avoided the corner as he turned upfield for YAC. Interesting change to the second-team offensive line configuration: LT Fred Johnson, LG John Ojukwu, C Drew Kendall, RG Willie Lampkin, RT Markel Bell. title: Jalen Carter is the 6th Eagles player named to the NFL Top 100 list
summary: The NFL has changed their roll-out of the Top 100 list, as voted by players, and it took several weeks before an Eagles player was named to the 2026 iteration — but now we’re up to six: The rest of the list will continue to be revealed two players per day, Monday through Friday, and […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 14: Zack Baun #53 of the Philadelphia Eagles carries the ball after an interception against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on December 14, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has changed their roll-out of the Top 100 list, as voted by players, and it took several weeks before an Eagles player was named to the 2026 iteration — but now we’re up to six: No. 29 — Jalen Carter, DT No. 34 — Saquon Barkley, RB No. 38 — Cooper DeJean, CB No. 45 — Zack Baun, LB No. 47 — Quinyon Mitchell, CB No. 56 — Jalen Hurts, QB The rest of the list will continue to be revealed two players per day, Monday through Friday, and then one player per day beginning Monday, August 24 through Friday, September 4. Here’s where Eagles players have ranked in the 2026 NFL Top 100 list up to this point: No. 29: Jalen Carter, DT The Eagles know how dominant Jalen Carter can be, which is why t hey signed him to a contract extension a year earlier than they needed and made him the highest paid DT in NFL history (at the time). Carter’s peers have high opinions about the defensive tackle, and how his power and football IQ make him one of the best in the league. No. 29 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles DT Jalen Carter! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/cFsPhA3dEB — NFL (@NFL) August 10, 2026 No. 34: Saquon Barkley, RB No. 34 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles RB Saquon Barkley! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/BfkAIueuXw — NFL (@NFL) August 6, 2026 No. 38: Cooper DeJean, CB No. 38 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles CB Cooper DeJean! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/5eeOr4WMgl — NFL (@NFL) August 4, 2026 No. 45: Zack Baun, LB The Eagles signed their defensive leader to a big money contract last offseason and he went on to prove that he was worth the commitment. Baun continued to dominate in 2025, finishing with 123 total tackles, 64 solo, 7 pass breakups, 3.5 sacks, a career-high two interceptions, and one forced fumble. The LB is just as committed as he’s been since arriving in Philly, and should have an equally impressive season in 2026. No. 45 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles LB Zack Baun! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/VUd3Bketx6 — NFL (@NFL) July 29, 2026 No. 47: Quinyon Mitchell , CB Coming off his second season, Mitchell earned All-Pro and was immediately recognized as one of the best corners in the league. He finished the 2025 season with 17 pass breakups, allowed just 39 completions, and allowed only 94 total yards after the catch all season. The expectations for his third season have only grown, but there’s no doubt he’s capable of rising to the occasion. ESPN’s Top 100 list, as voted on by coaches and executives, knocked Mitchell for his lack of interceptions up to this point in his career, but Mitchell is consistently and reliably doing his job and locking down the best receivers in the game — his peers, at least, seem to recognize how dominant he is. No. 47 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/bOQbShgDrv — NFL (@NFL) July 28, 2026 No. 56: Jalen Hurts, QB The former Super Bowl MVP dropped a bit in this year’s list, but still ranked higher than Lamar Jackson (No. 69), Jordan Love (No. 72), and Baker Mayfield (No. 77). Hurts has a lot on his shoulders this season as the Eagles embrace a new OC and scheme, but he has done nothing but prove time-after-time that he’s up for any challenge. He’s certainly spent the offseason focused on building a solid foundation with his offensive teammates, and every indication is he’s ready for another big season. NFL’s Jeremy Bergman explains Hurts’ ranking : “Hurts threw for a career-high 25 touchdowns and rushed for eight more en route to a third Pro Bowl bid in four years. The QB’s decreased completion percentage and use in the run game likely contributed to his 37-spot drop in this year’s list, his lowest ranking since before his 2023 debut at No. 3. But Hurts remains one of the NFL’s top dual-threat signal-callers entering his seventh NFL season, with or without the departed A.J. Brown.“ No. 56 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Eagles QB Jalen Hurts! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/vkX3kqTfSI — NFL (@NFL) July 22, 2026 Former Eagles on the list: No. 61 — CB Kevin Byard (Patriots) No. 78 — LB Josh Sweat (Cardinals) No. 80 — WR A.J. Brown (Patriots)

summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles’ social-media team highlights a Jalen Hurts interception – PFTThe Eagles’ social-media team on Wednesday decided to trumpet an interception made by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. The errant pass was thrown by quarterback Jalen Hurts. “Right on Q,” the caption declared. It’s a curious decision, given […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 07: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts #1 prepares to throw the ball during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 7th, 2026 at the Jefferson Health Training Complex on August 7th, 2026 in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles’ social-media team highlights a Jalen Hurts interception – PFT The Eagles’ social-media team on Wednesday decided to trumpet an interception made by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. The errant pass was thrown by quarterback Jalen Hurts. “Right on Q,” the caption declared. It’s a curious decision, given that the pressure seems to be increasing on Hurts. The Eagles, by all indications, expect him to run the offense as designed, and to execute the plays as called. As Derrick Gunn reported last season, internal frustration was growing over Hurts playing “his game” once the ball was snapped. Was it a situation of an intern gone rogue? Or was someone trying to send a message to Hurts, with the notion that it was simply a social-media intern gone rogue providing plausible deniability? [BLG Note: Lol, the way people are reacting to this clip is insane. It’s not that deep. Hurts, who’s had more ups than downs in camp, threw a pick to a really good cornerback. It happens! And it’s fine for the team to post it, just like they would post a clip of a touchdown catch where a defensive back gets beat!] "You have a great player making a great play against another great player." pic.twitter.com/KDRoee8daJ — PHLY Eagles (@PHLY_Eagles) August 13, 2026 Eagles depth chart revealed ahead of first preseason game – BGN Nothing shocking about how the wide receivers are listed but it is notable to see Lemon with the starters despite the fact he’s missed a lot of time in camp and didn’t stand out prior to getting hurt. Makai Lemon might not actually be a Week 1 starter with the likes of Darius Cooper and Elijah Moore having strong summers. Or at least there could be a heavier receiver rotation than there’s been in recent years. Whereas Lemon is listed with the starters, the Eagles aren’t even pretending that Eli Stowers is a top two tight end right now. With the way the Eagles laid out tight end on this chart (see below), I don’t know that he’s even necessarily TE3. I tend to think Stowers might be a healthy scratch … early in the season, at least. In Roob’s Observations: Growing concern over Makai Lemon’s extended layoff – NBCSP HOW MUCH CONCERN OVER MAKAI LEMON? It’s not panic time yet with Makai Lemon, but we’re not that far off. The more time the rookie WR misses the greater the chance that he won’t be WR2 once the season starts. Lemon not only missed most of the spring practices with a hamstring injury, he’s now been out for nearly two weeks with another hamstring injury, which he suffered in the indoor practice back on Aug. 3. That’s seven practices and counting that he’s missed. For a rookie trying to learn a new offense and work with new coaches and a new quarterback, this is really valuable time he’s missing. Mental reps are fine, but they’re no substitute for being out there with your teammates. But it’s not just that Lemon is missing so much time, the flip side of that is that it’s given the other receivers additional opportunities they wouldn’t have otherwise had, and Dontayvion Wicks, Elijah Moore and Darius Cooper in particular have made the most of the extra reps to leapfrog Lemon. They’ve developed chemistry with Jalen Hurts, they’ve grown comfortable in a new offense, they’ve earned the trust of their coaches. And they’ve all made play after play. We’re still four weeks from opening day, but Lemon has a lot of work to do in a short period of time to make up for the time he’s missed, and I’m not sure he can do it. Honestly, it would be surprising if Lemon can earn that WR2 role by the opener. If you’re Hurts, who would you rather throw to? Guys who’ve been out there every day grinding, working, improving since Day 1 of camp and building chemistry or someone who’s been watching from the sideline? Now, if Lemon can find his way back on the field next week, maybe he can get back to where he needs to be. But the reality is even before the injury Lemon wasn’t flashing, and Wicks, Moore and Cooper have all been outstanding. They haven’t missed a rep and Lemon is going to have to be very good once he does get back just to get on the field by the opener. Connections – Iggles Blitz You love to see this kind of bonding between players. Saquon Barkley has been very engaged this summer. He’s looked great. He has also talked a lot of trash and really been vocal with teammates. There is value in this type of competitive connection. Barkley is pushing his teammates to be their best. Some players have become more vocal as leaders. Jordan Davis has stepped up as a player and as a leader. He has really embraced being a key part of the team. His new contract seems to have brought out the best in him. Jordan Mailata has been more vocal this offseason. He’s become a key leader for the team. We’ve talked this offseason about how Jalen Hurts has embraced his role as the team leader. He’s been more vocal and spent more time in the spotlight. Hurts has always been a good leader. It just feels like he’s taken things to the next level. This connecting…being together is great, but now we need to see how it affects the performance of the players during the season. The 2017 team was tight and it led to a Super Bowl win. We’ll see what the 2026 team has in store for us. Why NFL teams battled the clock in 2025 — and how the Eagles can buck the trend – The Athletic The 2025 Eagles led the NFL with a style of play that to the layman’s eye can seem like lollygagging. The Eagles, who never totaled more than 37 plays snapped with one second left on the play clock in a given season under previous play callers Kellen Moore, Brian Johnson and Shane Steichen, led the league with 150 last-second plays under Patullo. The league average of plays with one second left on the play clock skyrocketed from 20.9 in 2024 to 73.2 in 2025, according to TruMedia. The league average hadn’t been greater than 23.4 since 2019. (The league average of total plays with three seconds or less also surged from 114.5 in 2024 to 200.9 in 2025.) There is a leading explanation for the surge, according to several coaches: Defensive play callers have been increasingly effective at disguising their coverages, and offenses adjusted by spending more time decoding at the line of scrimmage. That five teams other than the Eagles soared above 100 last-second plays in 2025 (the Pittsburgh Steelers, Jacksonville Jaguars, Buffalo Bills, Green Bay Packers and Carolina Panthers) builds the case for leaguewide heavy-thinking. Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, widely renowned for masking his coverages, said he has noticed teams trying to “get into the perfect play” and subsequently running into the play clock. Best Interceptions in Eagles History – PhiladelphiaEagles.com There are plenty to choose from, whether you fancy Cooper DeJean’s and Zack Baun’s interceptions in Super Bowl LIX, Patrick Robinson’s pick-6 in the 2017 NFC Championship Game, or a host of other game-altering plays. Enjoy them all here! Ranking NFL quarterbacks by trait: Best arm, accuracy, more – ESPN You’re going to hear us talk about quarterbacks a lot on “NFL Live” over the course of the 2026 season. There will be debates about all of them, from the best in the game to the borderline starters. But for a third straight year, I’m narrowing the focus here in the preseason. Who are the best signal-callers in the NFL at individual skills? Does anyone boast a better arm than Josh Allen? Does Joe Burrow or Matthew Stafford have the more refined mechanics? Is Lamar Jackson still the gold standard in QB rushing? I ranked the top 10 quarterbacks by seven different traits: arm…

title: Steelers stock report after their 28-9 preseason win over the Green Bay Packers
summary: It was a dominant win for the Pittsburgh Steelers in their first preseason game under Mike McCarthy. It was good to see fans in the stands, back at Acrisure Stadium as the team enters a new era. After several weeks of camp practices, we finally got to see some much-anticipated game action from plenty of […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Drew Allar #16 of the Pittsburgh Steelers carries the ball for a touchdown during the third quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a dominant win for the Pittsburgh Steelers in their first preseason game under Mike McCarthy. It was good to see fans in the stands, back at Acrisure Stadium as the team enters a new era. After several weeks of camp practices, we finally got to see some much-anticipated game action from plenty of players who could shape the future of the franchise. Let’s have a look at who shined and who hurt their stock after the Steelers’ first preseason game of the 2026 season. Stock up: WR Germie Bernard Perhaps we weren’t able to fully appreciate the skillset of rookie wideout Germie Bernard during the team’s practices in Latrobe with no live tackling. Bernard has always excelled after the catch and breaking tackles. The second-round pick picked up 22 yards after the catch on his third reception of the first half for a gain of 25. Bernard also nearly had a touchdown in the back of the end zone, holding onto the ball through a hard hit, but wasn’t able to get his second foot down. The rookie from Alabama finished the game with 4 catches for 51 yards, all coming in the first half. Bernard was clearly the top option for the Steelers’ passing attack with both DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. sitting tonight. Bernard is a player who will only continue to improve with more opportunities. CB Asante Samuel Jr. We are getting to the point with Asante Samuel Jr. that he is no longer a “camp darling,” but rather just a legitimately good football player. Samuel Jr. stepped up yet again with a pass breakup on a Jordan Love pass to stall the Packers’ opening drive. The following drive, the corner was lockstep with Green Bay receiver Savion Williams to the point where it was nearly impossible for the wideout to catch. The Steelers have found a hidden gem in Samuel Jr., and his playtime should increase in the regular season based on his performance in camp and now in the preseason. QB Drew Allar You simply cannot ask for a better debut from your rookie third-round project quarterback. Allar finished the contest scoring on all three of his drives. He went 9-for-12 passing for 154 yards, two passing touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown. The game did not seem to be too fast for Allar, who delivered throws on time and accurately. Even the layups and short stuff looked like a breeze for the young quarterback, who only had one noticeably off-target throw in the game. For as much talk about how much this game meant for Will Howard and Mason Rudolph in their battle for the backup quarterback job, Allar simply stole the show. Who cares who wins the backup job when you have Drew Allar waiting on the bench? — Joey Bray (@byjoeybray) August 14, 2026 This is not to say that any of the Steelers quarterbacks played poorly; in fact, it’s quite the opposite. The Steelers quarterbacks went a combined 27/33 passing. It was a great job of play calling by Mike McCarthy in his first game as head coach, and Allar ended up being the one to light up the stat sheet. WR Kaden Wetjen Wetjen was drafted to be the Steelers’ return specialist in the fourth round this past April, but he was the team’s leading receiver in his first preseason game. In the highlight of the game, Wetjen took a 10-yard completion from Drew Allar and turned it into a 74-yard catch that nearly went for a touchdown. We saw the breakaway speed that the Steelers were betting on when they took Wetjen. On the following drive, Allar found Wetjen in the end zone for a touchdown after the rookie created some serious separation for himself. We didn’t see any big gains in the return game for Wetjen, but it’s hard not to be impressed with his showing as a receiver. Drew 🤝 Kaden 📺: #GBvsPIT on KDKA pic.twitter.com/n3RghXtmzN — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) August 14, 2026 Stock down: The first team offensive line We got to see the first-team offensive line for the good majority of the first half, and it was not a great showing from the unit. Troy Fautanu looked rough in his first game action as the starting left tackle, as he picked up two penalties in the first half. Dylan Cook let up a sack early in the game, putting Mason Rudolph and the Steelers offense well behind the change. Funnily enough, the biggest winner on the Steelers offensive line might just have been rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor, who missed the game as he works his way back from a shoulder/neck injury. This game seemed to open the door a bit for Iheanachor to earn the starting right tackle role by week one. RB Kaleb Johnson Is everything okay? As far as we know, the Steelers RB3 job is wide open for anyone to take. Kaleb Johnson was the third Steelers running back to get a touch tonight after Travis Homer and Lew Nichols. Johnson turned his two carries into just three yards. Those two touches were the least by a Steelers running back in the contest. The reality of the situation right now is that Johnson is not involved, and it is starting to seem like the Steelers don’t have plans for him in their future. WR Roman Wilson After a red-hot start to training camp and injuries to DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., Wilson would head into the Steelers’ first preseason contest as one of the team’s top receiving options. The camp success did not translate to any preseason success this week, and Wilson caught just one pass for seven yards. Wilson did a good job of coming back to the ball on his lone catch as Mason Rudolph was rolling out to his right, but it was an overall disappointing showing for Wilson. Rookie receiver Germie Bernard seemed to be the primary option for Mason Rudolph with the Steelers’ first offensive grouping. We will see if Wilson continues to line up with the first team in practice this weekend after being outshone by his rookie counterpart. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Drew Allar shines with 3 total TDs in Steelers’ 28-9 win over Packers
summary: After eight long months filled with major changes and shake ups, the Pittsburgh Steelers took the field for the first time of 2026 in what would end up being a 28-9 win over the Green Bay packers The overarching story of the game for Pittsburgh, of course, was how their trio of quarterbacks would look […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Drew Allar #16 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks to pass during the third quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images After eight long months filled with major changes and shake ups, the Pittsburgh Steelers took the field for the first time of 2026 in what would end up being a 28-9 win over the Green Bay packers The overarching story of the game for Pittsburgh, of course, was how their trio of quarterbacks would look in the first game action of the season. And while all three played well, it was rookie Drew Allar who stole the show when the dust settled. On his first drive in the third quarter, Allar threw a strike to Kaden Wetjen on an in-breaker that saw the two-time Jet Award winner race 75 yards to the brink of the end zone. Two plays later. Mike McCarthy dialed up a read option and Allar took it in for a three-yard touchdown to put the Steelers on top 14-9. The Packers’ ensuing drive totaled just nine yards on five plays, as safety Israel Mukuamu broke into the backfield for a sack. And after a quick first drive, Allar then led a 10-play, 89-yard march that saw him go 7-of-8 and finish off the drive with a five-yard touchdown pass to Wetjen to extend the Steelers’ lead to 21-9. Allar wasn’t done, though. Late in the fourth quarter, the Steelers’ rookie put together another long drive, going 60 yards on 10 plays with Allar tossing a touchdown to fellow rookie and Big Ten product, Riley Nowakowski for the game’s final touchdown. Overall, Allar finished his night going 9-of-14 for 154 yards, two touchdown passes and an additional score on the ground to put a bow on a fantastic debut. While the biggest talking point from Week 1 of the preseason will be the play of Allar, he wasn’t the only quarterback who had a nice night. With Aaron Rodgers not partaking in the preseason opener, it was Mason Rudolph who was the first signal-caller under center, and he looked superb. After Pittsburgh went three-and-out on its first drive, Rudolph led a 16-play, 84-yard drive that featured completions of 13, 19, and 25 yards. It looked as if the long drive would be capped with a Lew Nichols touchdown, but a Troy Fautanu holding call negated the score. The Steelers were held out of the end zone after a Rudolph connection to Bernard was ruled out of bounds and the ensuing completion to Pat Freiermuth came up short of the goal line. And while the drive stalled out, Rudolph finished the night going 10-of-11 for 95 yards to give himself a very strong start to the exhibition slate. Several Steelers defenders made their presence known in between the first two offensive drives for Pittsburgh, as well. Asante Samuel Jr continued his dominance from training camp and forced two incompletions, one of which was a PBU on Jayden Reed. Doneiko Slaughter ran with the first-team at nickel and made a terrific play to force a fourth down, powering through a block by Christian Watson on a screen to tackle Marshawn Lloyd. Robert Spears-Jennings had a tackle for loss on the Packers’ third offensive drive, and Devan Boyki made a terrific series of plays, as well. He had a tackle for a two-yard loss to begin Green Bay’s fourth defensive drive, and then perfectly read a Kyle McCord pass and got his hands on it, nearly picking it off. Former first-round pick Jamin Davis also picked up a sack, and would add another later on in the night. The Acrisure Stadium crowd let out a collective roar as Will Howard entered the game for the first time as a member of the Steelers, though his first drive didn’t go as planned. The Steelers went three-and-out, which was capped off by a rough rep for Broderick Jones, allowing pressure to come off the left side, leading to a Howard scramble for a short gain. And while Howard’s first drive fizzled out quickly, he put together a masterful two-minute drill to close out the half. On fourth-and-inches, he hit Ben Skowronek for a first down, followed by a pair of big gains to Robert Tonyan to move the chains. Howard and Tonyan hooked up for a third time on the drive down the seam for what was originally ruled a touchdown, but overturned and ruled short. Howard sidestepped an interior rusher, stepped up, and fired a beautiful pass to the big tight end to set the Steelers up at the goal line. Lew Nichols ran the ball in on the next play to give the Steelers a 7-3 lead before Green Bay answered with a quick drive of their own and 57-yard Smack field goal to make it 7-6 at the half. Howard had one more drive that went six plays and ended with a punt. He finished the night going a very solid 7-of-9 for 86 yards. There are certainly things that need cleaned up, most notably the 11 penalties an 143 penalty yards. Those are things you’d rather have to clean up in August, though, rather than September. Regardless of the result, the biggest talking point was always going to be centered around the quarterback position, and Pittsburgh’s trio had a hat trick of quality performances. It makes the job of McCarthy and his staff harder to narrow down who the three quarterbacks will be (or if they decide to keep four), but it’s a problem you can bet they are okay with having.

Rodgers told reporters that he wanted to play at Lambeau, visit his former trainer’s room, stop at his favorite restaurant, Chives, and even squeeze in a quick nine holes at Green Bay Country Club. Rodgers did get his first opportunity to face his former team last season when the Packers visited Pittsburgh. He has consistently maintained that his relationship with Green Bay remains positive, despite the complicated circumstances surrounding his departure from the organization. Now, rather than returning to the stadium where he built his Hall of Fame résumé, Rodgers will face the Packers in Pittsburgh alongside Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, who also has deep ties to Green Bay. The matchup itself carries plenty of intrigue, but Rodgers’ comments make clear that the location matters to him. Lambeau Field was home for nearly two decades, and with his career nearing its conclusion, the chance to return there in uniform would have provided a rare opportunity to close that chapter on his own terms. Unfortunately for Rodgers, that opportunity will not come this preseason. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Our top on-site Seahawks training camp takeaways after a week in Seattle
summary: Seattle Seahawks training camp, for all intents and purposes, pretty much ends this week. Thursday marks the final public practice before the team’s preseason debut against the Dallas Cowboys, and while there are subsequent practices afterward (plus a joint scrimmage with the Tennessee Titans), preseason becomes a lot closer to a normal game week. Myself, […]
full_text: Seattle Seahawks training camp, for all intents and purposes, pretty much ends this week. Thursday marks the final public practice before the team’s preseason debut against the Dallas Cowboys, and while there are subsequent practices afterward (plus a joint scrimmage with the Tennessee Titans), preseason becomes a lot closer to a normal game week. Myself, Bryce Coutts, and Josh Hite were all at Seahawks training camp in some capacity last week. Bryce and I attended three practices, while Josh joined us to make it a Field Gulls trio at Lumen Field. We’ve each jotted down our biggest takeaways from camp. Mookie Alexander My biggest takeaway from Seahawks training camp was Brian Fleury’s emphasis on utilizing tight ends and running backs more, both pre-snap and post-snap. Unfortunately, we only saw Jadarian Price once last week, so we got even less of a percentage of what could’ve been worked on than what was planned. Still, more motioning of tight ends, more two-back looks, more running backs running actual routes instead of checkdowns, and greater use of tight ends split out instead of inline. Even if the percentage of targets to backs and TEs may not be particularly high given the embarrassment of riches at wide receiver, I believe Fleury is going to add to Klint Kubiak’s existing passing concepts by making sure everyone at every skill position is a pass-catching threat. We’ll see more misdirection and different types of matchup manipulation. My other takeaway is that Seattle’s pass rush wrinkle, if it does not necessarily involve more blitzing, may see a lot more involvement outside of traditional defensive line players. Seattle’s edge rush depth is three-deep with a TBD on Dante Fowler Jr. If one of Uchenna Nwosu, Derick Hall, or DeMarcus Lawrence has to miss considerable time, I’m nervous. But I think Mike Macdonald is cooking up some new things like having Tyrice Knight line up at edge, or have Rylie Mills play across pretty much every alignment. Nick Emmanwori and Devon Witherspoon are definitely going to be lurking at the line, but if D’Anthony Bell makes the roster he might do a lot of the same. It’s auxiliary pass rush in the absence of a 15+ sack beast like Myles Garrett. Bryce Coutts After spending several days watching the Seahawks up close at training camp, one of my biggest takeaways was just how comfortable and connected this team looks on both sides of the ball. From a coaching perspective, I was paying close attention to communication, alignment, tempo, technique and how quickly players were processing what was happening in front of them. Rylie Mills was one of the players who consistently stood out. He looked powerful, active and disruptive along the defensive front, showing the kind of strength and movement skills that can translate into a meaningful role in Mike Macdonald’s defense. Tyrice Knight was another player who impressed me throughout camp. He has been playing fast, confident football, and what makes his development especially intriguing is the number of different ways Macdonald may be able to use him. Knight’s athleticism, physicality and ability to operate in space could allow Seattle to move him around within its defensive structure rather than locking him into one traditional linebacker role. Considering how much Macdonald values versatility and creating uncertainty for opposing offenses, Knight could become a very interesting piece in some of the different personnel packages Seattle shows this season. Offensively, Sam Darnold and Cooper Kupp were two of the biggest reasons I left camp encouraged about where this unit could be headed. Darnold looks noticeably more comfortable in the offense, and that familiarity appears to be allowing him to operate at a much quicker and more precise pace. His reads look cleaner, he is getting through his progressions faster and the ball is coming out with more decisiveness. Instead of executing the play that is called, he looks like a quarterback who understands where his answers are and can get to them quickly based on what the defense is showing him. Kupp looks similarly comfortable within the structure of the offense, and that comfort makes him appear to be playing faster. It is not necessarily about an increase in raw speed; it is about how quickly he is processing leverage, identifying space, and getting to the correct spot within the concept. His route detail, timing and understanding of coverage were evident throughout the practices I watched. When you combine that growing comfort between Darnold and Kupp with the development of players like Mills and Knight, I came away from camp feeling that Seattle has both the talent and schematic flexibility to continue evolving on both sides of the football in 2026. Josh Hite My biggest takeaways from Fan Fest: First, Rylie Mills looks like a first round blue chip draft prospect. On one-on-one drills versus Anthony Bradford, it was hard to tell who one each rep, but I had Mills winning two out of the three slightly. In 11-on-11 drills, he regularly got into the backfield no matter who was blocking him. He looked like the Juggernaut out there, a pure unstoppable force. A second takeaway was the backup interior offensive linemen. Bryce Cabeldue had a rough outing, getting beat during 1-on-1’s, and having a rough time on 11-on-11’s. He was not able to really cement himself and was getting pushed back often. Christian Haynes looked more comfortable and seems to have taken a step up from the previous two seasons. Beau Stephens looks like he will need some time to develop and gain some more strength. And now it’s time for Seahawks preseason!

title: Seahawks first round pick Jadarian Price reveals how he spent his first NFL check
summary: There are several reasons nearly every kid dreams of being a professional athlete when they grow up, not least among them the idea that if you make it big time, you’ll be able to give your family a better life. For Seattle Seahawks first round pick Jadarian Price, that reason was top of his mind […]
full_text: There are several reasons nearly every kid dreams of being a professional athlete when they grow up, not least among them the idea that if you make it big time, you’ll be able to give your family a better life. For Seattle Seahawks first round pick Jadarian Price , that reason was top of his mind when he received his first NFL signing bonus of $8.7 million. In an article for ESPN , Price revealed he spent some of that figure on a home for his family in Denison, Texas, his hometown. “Checked that off the list,” Price said. He added that his family was all smiles when he shared the news with them. Some of how other rookies spent their first check included a CyberPower gaming PC for Jacksonville Jaguars’ third-round pick Albert Regis, a Rolex watch for Cincinnati Bengals third-rounder Tacario Davis, a Tempur-Pedic mattress for Miami Dolphins second-round linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, and stock market investment by Atlanta Falcons third-rounder Zachariah Branch. Price’s family hasn’t been the only ones smiling this offseason, as the No. 32 overall selection has continued to impress fans, coaches and fellow players alike at Seahawks’ training camp. Price turned heads during the first week, even being featured heavily on the first episode of ‘Hard Knocks.’ There are high expectations for the rookie, who will be stepping up to replace Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker while Zach Charbonnet heals from a torn ACL. Though he has been sidelined for a lower-body injury for the last week, all signs are pointing to the Seahawks’ top draft choice being ready for the season after he returned to practice on Wednesday .

title: Seahawks film review: Jalen Milroe enters Year 2 with more questions than answers
summary: Few positions receive more scrutiny in Seattle than quarterback, and that made Jalen Milroe one of the most fascinating rookies on the Seattle Seahawks’ roster in 2025. Milroe also joined an exclusive group. Since taking over personnel decisions, John Schneider has been remarkably selective when drafting quarterbacks. After landing Russell Wilson in 2012, Seattle didn’t […]
full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JUNE 04: Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks works out with Drew Lock #2 and Sam Darnold #14 during practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on June 04, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Few positions receive more scrutiny in Seattle than quarterback, and that made Jalen Milroe one of the most fascinating rookies on the Seattle Seahawks’ roster in 2025. Milroe also joined an exclusive group. Since taking over personnel decisions, John Schneider has been remarkably selective when drafting quarterbacks. After landing Russell Wilson in 2012, Seattle didn’t spend another draft pick at the position until selecting Alex McGough in the 7th round of 2018 , before finally adding Milroe in the 2025 NFL Draft . That rarity alone made the selection noteworthy. Unlike previous quarterback investments, however, Milroe arrived without any expectation of contributing immediately. The Seahawks had already committed to Sam Darnold as their starter, while Drew Lock provided an experienced backup. Regardless of how the season ultimately unfolded, Milroe entered perhaps the ideal developmental environment for a quarterback with significant physical gifts but equally significant refinement ahead of him. That context mattered because opinions on Milroe entering the draft varied dramatically. Some evaluators believed his athletic profile and arm talent justified Day 1 consideration as a high-upside project. Others questioned whether his inconsistencies as a passer made him anything more than a Day 3 prospect. Seattle ultimately bet on the upside, viewing Milroe as a developmental quarterback rather than someone expected to compete for immediate playing time. The Seahawks approached his rookie season accordingly. Rather than accelerating his development through live snaps, the priority appeared to be allowing him to rebuild parts of his game without the pressure of competing for the starting job. His rookie season, therefore, was never going to be judged by statistics. It would be judged by signs of growth. The challenge is that there simply wasn’t much regular-season tape to evaluate. What stood out on Jalen Milroe’s tape Seattle searched for ways to utilize his athleticism Despite entering the season as QB3, Seattle clearly wanted to explore Milroe's athleticism. The offense featured two-QB looks, designed runs and packages built around the explosive rushing ability that made him such an intriguing prospect coming out of Alabama. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-08-11T01:42:53.407Z Despite entering the year as the third quarterback, the coaching staff clearly wanted to explore ways of incorporating Milroe’s athletic ability into the offense. Seattle installed a handful of packages featuring two-quarterback looks, designed quarterback runs, and concepts intended to leverage the explosive rushing ability that made Milroe such an intriguing prospect coming out of Alabama. The sample size was too small to know how far Seattle planned to take Milroe's package. Bootlegs, play-action and movement throws could've stressed defenses horizontally while simplifying reads. His speed and arm strength fit those concepts, but the offense never got there. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-08-11T01:41:30.535Z The sample size remained extremely small, making it difficult to determine how expansive those packages might have become over the course of the season. It’s reasonable to believe the coaching staff envisioned eventually expanding that package beyond simple quarterback runs. Bootlegs, play-action concepts and movement throws could have created opportunities to stress defenses horizontally while simplifying Milroe’s reads. His combination of speed and arm strength naturally lends itself to those designs, particularly if he is attacking short and intermediate windows while threatening defenses as a runner. Unfortunately, the offense never reached that point. The opportunities disappeared almost immediately Milroe's rookie season effectively changed after the early fumble vs. Tampa Bay. His offensive role vanished, leaving him as Seattle's emergency QB3. With so few regular-season snaps, there's little NFL tape to evaluate his development beyond isolated packages and preseason reps. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-08-11T01:42:12.712Z Milroe’s rookie season effectively changed course following an early-season fumble on a pitch attempt (with Sam Darnold on motion) against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. After that mistake, his offensive role virtually disappeared. Rather than remaining part of a developing situational package, he became little more than the emergency third quarterback for the remainder of the season. Even in comfortable victories where additional snaps might have been available, Seattle turned to Drew Lock instead of giving Milroe valuable game experience. That leaves evaluators with remarkably little NFL tape from which to draw meaningful conclusions. Instead of evaluating sustained offensive growth, we’re left analyzing isolated preseason snaps and a handful of regular-season packages. Areas for improvement The developmental questions surrounding Milroe entering the draft remain largely the same today—not because he failed to answer them, but because he just didn’t play enough football. His throwing mechanics still require refinement, particularly in maintaining consistency throughout his delivery. Accuracy, especially on routine throws, has also been an area where greater consistency is needed. Decision-making remains another developmental priority. At Alabama, there were moments where processing speed and post-snap recognition lagged behind his physical tools. Nothing from his limited rookie action significantly changed that evaluation. Fortunately for Seattle, none of these concerns were unexpected. Milroe was drafted precisely because the organization believed those traits could improve over time. His elite athletic profile was always the foundation of the investment, while the passing game was expected to develop through coaching and repetition rather than immediate production. The problem is that meaningful repetition was difficult to find during his rookie season. Future outlook That reality makes the upcoming preseason arguably more important for Milroe than for anyone else on Seattle’s roster. The goal shouldn’t be to determine whether he suddenly looks like a future franchise quarterback. That would be an unrealistic expectation after one developmental season. Instead, the evaluation should focus on progress. Has the footwork become cleaner? Is the throwing motion more repeatable? Are decisions arriving more quickly? Is the ball consistently arriving where it’s supposed to? Those are the questions that matter. Even though preseason football comes against backups—and often alongside backup offensive units—it still provides a valuable comparison point against Milroe’s own rookie preseason. The standard isn’t perfection; it’s visible improvement. His place on the depth chart is unlikely to change entering 2026. Sam Darnold remains the starter, while Drew Lock continues to provide veteran insurance. Milroe is still firmly QB3, and that’s perfectly consistent with the original developmental plan. History also reminds us that quarterback development is rarely linear. Malik Willis serves as a recent example of a physically gifted quarterback whose career looked stalled before eventually finding a better developmental environment and rebuilding his value. That doesn’t mean Milroe will follow the same trajectory, but it illustrates why patience remains part of the process with athletic quarterback projects. Final thoughts Jalen Milroe’s rookie season ultimately provided fewer answers than anyone hoped—not because the talent disappeared, but because the opportunities did. The physical traits that convinced Seattle to draft him remain evident. The developmental concerns that made him…

title: Seahawks legend Matt Hasselbeck contributes to CTE research
summary: Matt Hasselbeck, one of the most beloved former players for the Seattle Seahawks, recently helped with the ongoing research on CTE. Currently, that disease can only be diagnosed after death. Hasselbeck is healthy and feeling good, yet still underwent testing which will be used to try and develop methods to diagnose CTE in living patients […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 01: Former Seattle Seahawks player Matt Hasselbeck is honored during the second intermission during the game between the Seattle Kraken and the Vegas Golden Knights at T-Mobile Park on January 01, 2024 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matt Hasselbeck, one of the most beloved former players for the Seattle Seahawks, recently helped with the ongoing research on CTE . Currently, that disease can only be diagnosed after death. Hasselbeck is healthy and feeling good, yet still underwent testing which will be used to try and develop methods to diagnose CTE in living patients noting that they need “people who are feeling good to step up to the plate and volunteer.” As a QB, Hasselbeck received his fair share of hard hits, but notes that many of his former teammates suffered more hits, particularly those in the trenches. That’s why the three-time Pro Bowl selection recently spent two days at Boston University going through a battery of scans and tests to determine how much all those collisions affected his brain. The hope is that it will be a small step toward a goal that has eluded doctors: diagnosing chronic traumatic encephalopathy in the living. “They need guys like me. They need people who are feeling good to step up to the plate and volunteer,” Hasselbeck said. “I played quarterback, so I didn’t take some of the hits that a lot of my teammates took. But the guys who were blocking for me, or playing special teams, or trying to get the ball back for me on defense, I wanted to do something. They had my back, so in a way I’d like to have their back.” The article notes that while there are similarities between CTE and Alzheimer’s, there are key differences that make the methods for diagnosing Alzheimer’s unable to be used for CTE, which can only be officially diagnosed after death. The study that Hasselbeck participated in is looking into these differences, with two types of participants: former football players, and those who didn’t play contact sports, but were diagnosed with Alzheimer’s. Compared to Alzheimer’s research, CTE studies are in their infancy. Hasselbeck admitted to having three concussions prior to starting college and suffering more before his playing days were over. He hopes that his contribution to this study will help further the research and lead to diagnosing CTE much earlier.

title: 49ers News: Rookies make a strong first impression in Titans preseason game
summary: What Kyle Shanahan and others said after 49ers’ 19-13 loss vs. Titans“Yeah, [Saleh and I are] not the biggest note takers, but we’re more FaceTimers. So, we sat there and FaceTimed a little bit the last two nights, just talking about what we saw from each other. It’s a little bit easier when you’re in […]
full_text: What Kyle Shanahan and others said after 49ers’ 19-13 loss vs. Titans “Yeah, [Saleh and I are] not the biggest note takers, but we’re more FaceTimers. So, we sat there and FaceTimed a little bit the last two nights, just talking about what we saw from each other. It’s a little bit easier when you’re in different conferences. You don’t have to lie as much. You can be a little bit more honest, but I know he definitely isn’t always. He’s still trying to find things out and so am I, but it was good for us to practice against each other, have someone that you know. Especially seeing [Tennessee Titans defensive coordinator] Gus [Bradley] and stuff and [Tennessee Titans defensive run game coordinator/defensive line coach Aaron] Whitecotton, who was here for a little bit, [Tennessee Titans defensive pass game coordinator/cornerbacks coach] Tony Oden. It was good to catch up with all those guys this week.” 49ers rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling stars in preseason opener, outshining Titans’ Carnell Tate (paywall) “Stribling caught the first pass of the game and remained a go-to guy on third downs over the course of three offensive drives. Hold your third-and-De’Zhaun outbursts for the end. Three of his catches came on third downs, including two conversions via a 32-yard back-shoulder bomb that Stribling grabbed up high and an 11-yard reception that Stribling turned into a first down with several yards after catch. Maybe he stepped out of bounds before converting the latter, but whatever, it’s preseason. He was downed a yard shy of the sticks on the other third-down catch.” 49ers QB Kurtis Rourke’s first game action in 601 days ends with injury (paywall) “Before his premature exit, Rourke completed 12 of 14 passes for 101 yards, and he rushed for 14 yards on three carries. The 2025 seventh-round pick left shortly after he was whacked by two defenders on a three-yard scramble midway through the second quarter. “They said ‘ribs’ and he was struggling to breathe, so they took him to the hospital just to check on everything, make sure it’s all right,” head coach Kyle Shanahan said. “The X-rays here didn’t show it was broken or anything, but we’ll see what we find out tomorrow.” 49ers preseason takeaways: De’Zhaun Stribling hype train rolling, Kurtis Rourke injured (paywall) “ Halton has had a nasty streak during training camp, and that showed up in back-to-back plays Thursday night. He would have had a sack, working through Titans starting linemen Peter Skoronski and Dan Moore Jr., if not for a defensive holding penalty in the secondary. On the next snap, Halton threw an offensive lineman to the side and wrapped up running back Tyjae Spears for a loss of a yard. “Once I get hot, it’s over with,” Halton said. “I win one, and then next thing you know, I’m in my head like, ‘OK, I got this.’ So I build that confidence, and it’s over.” What we learned as De’Zhaun Stribling stars in 49ers’ preseason-opening loss “Halton, a fourth-round pick from Oklahoma, is constantly around the ball and causing disruption in practices. He took advantage of his action on Thursday with three tackles in the first half, including a stop of running back Tyjae Spears for a 1-yard loss. Halton had a 14-yard sack of Cam Ward nullified by a defensive holding penalty on Jakob Robinson. Dugger started at the 49ers’ “fever backer” position and played the entire first half. He did not wait long to show some of his immense physical talent. On the second defensive snap, he ran down Ward to hold him for just a 2-yard gain on a scramble. Four plays later, he got stuck on right tackle JC Latham’s block on a third-and-10 play and could not prevent a short pass to that side going for 16 yards.”

title: 49ers injury updates: Kurtis Rourke went to the hospital; Nate Hobbs pulled his groin
summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided injury updates after the Niners’ preseason opener. Quarterback Kurtis Rourke was struggling to breathe after he left the game with a rib injury. Shanahan said he didn’t want to go too much in depth about the injury as he didn’t have updates. However, the team was concerned […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Kurtis Rourke #14 of the San Francisco 49ers roles out looking to pass against the Tennessee Titans in the first half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided injury updates after the Niners’ preseason opener. Quarterback Kurtis Rourke was struggling to breathe after he left the game with a rib injury. Shanahan said he didn’t want to go too much in depth about the injury as he didn’t have updates. However, the team was concerned enough to send Rourke to the hospital. Shanahan said he didn’t think the issue was serious, and that may have been a precautionary move. There was no update on whether Rourke broke his ribs. The initial X-Rays at Levi’s Stadium came back negative. Shanahan said they believe Rourke hurt himself on a quarterback draw near the goal line toward the end of the first half. At halftime, since there were no available quarterbacks other than Adrian Martinez, the team was teaching Brayden Willis how to take a snap and hand it off in case Martinez went down with an injury. Cornerback Nate Hobbs didn’t play in the opener. Shanahan said he pulled his groin during the joint practice against the Titans and will miss a few weeks. That is not good news for a veteran fighting for a roster spot. It also might explain why we saw Jakob Robinson start at nickel. Here’s a complete list of the injuries from Thursday night: Jack Jones (hand) Kurtis Rourke (ribs) Nick Martin (stinger) Marques Sigle (oblique) Nate Hobbs (groin) Martin was the only player who returned. We’ll see if this injury sidelines Sigle or Jones for more than a week. If the 49ers bring in multiple cornerbacks and safeties for visits next week, that’ll be our answer.

title: 49ers fall to the Titans, but De’Zhaun Stribling steals the show
summary: We were reminded of what preseason football looks like. It’s a precipitous drop-off from QB3 to QB4. But we also got to see some first-year players shine. The San Francisco 49ers entered the game with an intent to feature De’Zhaun Stribling. He caught a pass on the first play of the game. Stribling finished the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: De'zhaun Stribling #15 of the San Francisco 49ers catches a deep pass over Cor'dale Flott #18 of the Tennessee Titans in the first half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We were reminded of what preseason football looks like. It’s a precipitous drop-off from QB3 to QB4. But we also got to see some first-year players shine. The San Francisco 49ers entered the game with an intent to feature De’Zhaun Stribling. He caught a pass on the first play of the game. Stribling finished the evening with seven receptions for 63 yards on eight targets, including this beauty for 32 yards: It's a nice luxury to have a WR who can run by a DB but the most impressive part of this is Stribling keeping the ball away from his body and spinning away from the DB so he can't make a play. He might be good. Never know! pic.twitter.com/FjvjyxuxkW — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) August 14, 2026 We saw Stribling run routes out wide, from the slot, hang on to contested catches, and win down the field. He looked like the player the 49ers had hoped he’d be. It’s early, but it was a fantastic evening for the rookie. He wasn’t the only rookie to stand out. Gracen Halton had a series where he beat Peter Skoronowski, one of the best left guards in the game, three times in a series. Halton has the kind of juice the Niners desperately need at defensive tackle. And the good news is Halton wasn’t just winning one way, or flukey. I’d argue that Halton and Bryson Eason outplayed Alfred Collins, which might not be a great sign for Collins. Eason flashed a couple of times himself early in the game. Later on, James Thompson also showed well. Jaden Dugger was rangy, as expected. Watching him develop will be fascinating, as his athleticism is palpable. He looked more comfortable playing linebacker than Nick Martin — which again, might say more about Martin. He had a personal foul in the third quarter after failing to sink into the throwing lane. So it was a double whammy. Despite trailing at the half, the 49ers outgained the Titans in the first half. They went 6-for-11 on third down, and a lot of that was thanks to Kurtis Rourke, who left with a rib injury. He looked in control of the offense, going 12-for-14 for 101 yards, and scrambled three times for 14 yards. Rourke looked good enough to challenge for QB2. You cannot say the same about Adrian Martinez. You never know where the ball is going when he drops back to throw. Robert Jones played the entire first half at left guard, while Connor Colby played right guard. The 49ers are going to need to get a long look at Jones. In the second half, Carver Willis was next up at left guard. It didn’t take long to see why Colby got demoted after allowing a free runner early on in the game. Corliss Waitman had a couple of impressive punts, including a 58-yarder. Eddy Pineiro missed a 60+ yard attempt. In fairness to Pineiro, it should’ve been more like a 50-yard attempt, had Martinez not inexplicably stepped out of bounds. Once you get into the third quarter and beyond, you’re just hoping nobody gets hurt. On that note, cornerback Jack Jones left early in the game with an injury. That’s the last thing the 49ers want to see. Speaking of the secondary, it was tough sledding early on for Marques Sigle and Jakob Robinson. Missed tackles, poor run fits, and easy completions were a theme. It may not matter for Robinson, as he was playing nickel(Upton Stout’s spot). However, Sigle is in line to start, and that may not matter whether Malik Mustapha is healthy. Ultimately, we saw some positive things from players who will contribute this upcoming season, and that’s what you want coming out of the first preseason game.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Can Kaelon Black take over RB2 role in the preseason?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are back at Levi’s Stadium for the first time on Thursday, as they’ll take on the Tennessee Titans in the preseason opener, with kickoff slated for 6:00 p.m. Following the joint practices this week, head coach Kyle Shanahan doesn’t expect many starters to take the field on Thursday, which opens up […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Kaelon Black #26 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during training camp practice at SAP Performance Facility on July 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are back at Levi’s Stadium for the first time on Thursday, as they’ll take on the Tennessee Titans in the preseason opener, with kickoff slated for 6:00 p.m. Following the joint practices this week, head coach Kyle Shanahan doesn’t expect many starters to take the field on Thursday, which opens up opportunity for the backups and younger players to get some more reps. However, that unfortunately won’t apply at running back, as top backups Jordan James and Kaelon Black are both dealing with injuries that have limited them in training camp. James, a fifth-round pick last year, seemed to be the frontrunner for the No. 2 running back role heading into training camp, but he suffered a broken rib on the first day and has been out since. Black suffered an adductor injury as well, and he’s been out the last few days. It’s clear the 49ers are high on Black, whom they took in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Head coach Kyle Shanahan had even said that Black was their No. 2 running back in the draft, and he’s gotten a lot of opportunities so far this offseason. How are the 49ers handling the backup running back competition given the current state of injuries? “I think it’s always challenging when you have multiple guys out of the lineup practice and reps and obviously you want to evaluate everybody out there under the same circumstances,” run game coordinator Joe Graves said earlier in camp. “But, you know, injuries are a part of training camp. They’re a part of the season. And the guys that we have out there have been doing a great job competing, executing. And that’s really the mindset. That can happen during the year where you can, you can have a couple guys go down, and guys gotta step up. So they’re doing a good job, coaches and players, of rolling with the punches and getting, getting the most out of practice and doing everything the right way.” Through the early part of camp, Black had been drawing positive reviews for finding and hitting the hole, which the 49ers preach at running back. And that was something the team had identified on film from Black. “That was probably the number one thing that attracted us to him was just his mentality when he put his foot in the ground and the burst that he had,” Graves said of Black. “Really, it was just honing that in comes natural to him. Obviously, he had a couple good days there of training camp and still excited to see him out there. Just got to get him back [healthy] and continue to get better, continue to learn the offense, and hopefully we get him back out there soon.” Last year didn’t meet San Francisco’s expectations when it came to run game execution, and that has been a clear point from the staff this offseason. “Yeah, I think you go in the offseason, and you evaluate everything,” Graves added. “Scheme, how you’re coaching things, and all that stuff. We know that last year it wasn’t what we wanted in terms of where we ranked in the league and some of the outputs we had, but it’s no particular one thing. “Everybody shares the blame. Everybody shares credit, however you want to look at it. It’s just this offseason has just been a focus on us and doing what we do as best we can under any circumstance, and those are the things that are going to get us through the season and get us back to where we want to be in the run game.” Now, San Francisco has many of the same pieces in the room as last year, with Black being the primary newcomer. And the rookie believes he’s a great fit in the offense, especially considering the need for pass-catching at the position. “[The offense] feels great for me,” Black said, via NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco. “I feel like it really maximizes what a running back can truly do. A lot of the time, running backs aren’t asked to catch the ball a lot out of the backfield, but here it’s the complete opposite. You’re going to go out there, you’re going to run these different routes, and you’re almost going to feel like a receiver first, sometimes.” If the 49ers truly want to take McCaffrey off the field more to preserve him as they’ve been saying, they’ll need a viable pass-catching backup. While Black hadn’t shown much from that perspective at Indiana, he did show some pass-catching at James Madison through the first two years of his career. That could be key as he tries to win the No. 2 running back role.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers’ QB Brock Purdy ranked in the top 10 in 3 categories by ESPN
summary: ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky ranked the top quarterbacks in the NFL in several categories, ranging from arm strength to rushing ability. It’s a list that is as subjective as it gets. For example, mechanics were one of the categories. He had Daniel Jones listed third. I’d argue that Geno Smith, for all his faults, could be […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) during training at the Levi's Stadium practice field in Santa Clara on Sunday, July 26, 2026. (Photo by Santiago Mejia/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky ranked the top quarterbacks in the NFL in several categories , ranging from arm strength to rushing ability. It’s a list that is as subjective as it gets. For example, mechanics were one of the categories. He had Daniel Jones listed third. I’d argue that Geno Smith, for all his faults, could be No. 3 on the list. San Francisco 49ers’ Brock Purdy found himself in the top 10 in three categories. Purdy wasn’t listed for arm strength, but he checked in at No. 9 for ball placement. Here’s the top 10, according to Orlovsky: 1) Matthew Stafford 2) Drake Maye 3) Sam Darnold 4) Joe Burrow 5) Jared Goff 6) Jordan Love 7) Josh Allen 8) Lamar Jackson 9) Brock Purdy 10) Dak Prescott Sports Info Solutions has an “on-target percentage” stat. Stafford placed 24th in 2025, matching the likes of Marcus Mariota. Purdy was 14th. Purdy wasn’t listed for mechanics or decision-making, although Josh Allen was No. 1 for decision-making. Purdy did check in at No. 8 for pocket presence. Here’s the top 10: 1) Maye 2) Burrow 3) Darnold 4) Herbert 5) Prescott 6) Jackson 7) Caleb Williams 8) Purdy 9) Daniel Jones 10) Trevor Lawrence Darnold has long been known for his top-tier pocket presence. Maybe there are two Daniel Joneses that we aren’t aware of? The final category where Purdy made the top-10 was second-reaction ability. Here’s how it was described: The flip side is working outside the pocket. There’s obviously always a plan when the ball is snapped, but NFL defenses are pretty dang good at derailing things. So, what happens when Plan A doesn’t work? Can the quarterback pull something out of thin air and still make a positive play? I’m looking for creativity here, as well as the ability to throw from weird arm angles and platforms. You’ll notice a lot of the strongest arms make this list, too — that’s obviously key. But mobility and field vision also matter in a big way. Here’s a look at the top 10: 1) Allen 2) Caleb Williams 3) Patrick Mahomes 4) Maye 5) Darnold 6) Bo Nix 7) Purdy 8) Jackson 9) Jayden Daniels 10) Baker Mayfield Purdy was not listed for his rushing ability (Baker, Bo, and Jalen Hurts were). These say more about the author than the quarterbacks, but it still felt worth a share, so you can see how “professionals” feel Purdy ranks amongst his peers.

title: Which 49ers player are you looking forward to seeing the most in their preseason opener?
summary: Tonight should be entertaining because we get to see the players we’ve been reading and hearing about for three weeks in action. Which San Francisco 49ers players will stand out? Which players will look like they don’t belong? We know there are still some position battles to be determined. The same is true for some […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 11: Alfred Collins #95 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 11, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tonight should be entertaining because we get to see the players we’ve been reading and hearing about for three weeks in action. Which San Francisco 49ers players will stand out? Which players will look like they don’t belong? We know there are still some position battles to be determined. The same is true for some of the depth spots, as the team needs to find out which players can be counted on during the season, whether it’s for specific roles or if (when) there are injuries that arise. For tonight’s preseason game, we’re asking which player you’re looking forward to seeing the most. I tend to gravitate toward the younger players coming from bad situations in college — looking at you, Larry Worth III. Everyone wants to see the rookies. It’ll be telling if De’Zhaun Stribling is treated like a veteran and his playing time is limited. He’s quickly turning into one of the more important pieces for the offense. But other rookies, like Carver Willis, have something to prove during the preseason. Which 49ers player are you looking forward to seeing the most in their preseason opener? My answer: Alfred Collins. It’s not easy to assess defensive linemen in practice settings because you can’t take running backs to the ground, and if you get close to the quarterback, you get yelled at. Collins started training camp on the active/PUP list, but has had a couple of weeks to get his feet under him. Collins is the antithesis of Osa Odighizuwa. He’s not flashy, isn’t going to wow you, and is unlikely to stuff the stat sheet. He’s still a critical piece of the 49ers’ defense. The Titans are going to play their starters. They’re a young team. So Collins will go against their starters for maybe a quarter or so. I want to see Collins look like a top-50 pick. How are you looking forward to watching? Let us know in the comments.
