title: What is one thing every new 49ers fan needs to know?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have a game today. Yes, it’s a preseason game, but it is their first game on a football field for the 2026 season. No doubt we have a lot of new faces here on the site, but we, as fans, probably have a lot of new faces in the fanbase. Over […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JANUARY 01: Banjo man, a major 49ers fan won the right to sound the horn before the regular season game between the Seattle Seahawks and the San Francisco 49ers held January 1, 2017 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. Final score: Seahawks- 25, 49ers- 23. (Photo by Allan Hamilton/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have a game today. Yes, it’s a preseason game, but it is their first game on a football field for the 2026 season. No doubt we have a lot of new faces here on the site, but we, as fans, probably have a lot of new faces in the fanbase. Over on 49ers Reddit, a question popped up from a new member of the 49ers Faithful: What do they need to know as a new fan? It got me thinking to steal their question and just ask everyone here what you think is the one thing, the absolute most pressing piece of advice every new 49ers fan coming into the 2026 season should have. Rather than give a history or a bandwagoner’s guide , I thought it’d be fun for us to single out one piece of advice we’d give a new fan. And given the 49ers’ history, there are a lot of things to pick from. And if you are a new fan, welcome! For me, the one thing I would tell fans will seem a bit more pessimistic. It’s not anticipating injuries or telling them to research sub-station theories before sitting down to a game. It’s just knowing they are a fan of a team that had its glory days in the 80s and early 90s. We’re in 2026 now—those glory days are gone, and with the way the division and the league are trending, they are never coming back . If you expect the 49ers to compete for a three-peat, you might be in for a bad time. Nowadays, we have what I call The Great Disappointment to look forward to. So maybe a less facetious way of saying it: make sure you manage your expectations. If you are joining up because of the great history of Joe Montana, Steve Young, Jerry Rice and others, that’s great, because many of us joined during their heyday. In my case, what was a three-year-old to do? But just because they were a powerhouse then doesn’t mean they are a powerhouse now. It’d be like a basketball fan becoming a fan of the Bulls in 2026 because Michael Jordan played there decades ago and they think the Bulls still got championships after his retirement. The 49ers dynasty ended over 30 years ago, and the only holdover we’ve had since the 1994 season is the Quest for Six. So that’s my advice: curb your expectations. Know you are rooting for a team of good people on and off the field as well as a good coach, but don’t expect them to steamroll everyone for 16 weeks and win a Super Bowl every other year. That said, this is fun. When the 49ers are winning, it’s an incredible high. Welcome to the Faithful. So what do you think every new fan needs to know? I’m curious: do you think my curbing expectations bit is essential, or is the history of Sourdough Sam more appropriate, or something specific to 2026?

title: 49ers-Titans preview: 5 players with something to prove tonight
summary: We’ll get our first look at several San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night, as they host the Tennessee Titans in their preseason opener. It’s unlikely we see many, if any, of the starters tonight. That doesn’t mean there won’t be meaningful football, though, as roster spots will be decided. Here are five players fighting for […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Bryson Eason #67 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during training camp practice at SAP Performance Facility on July 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ll get our first look at several San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night, as they host the Tennessee Titans in their preseason opener. It’s unlikely we see many, if any, of the starters tonight. That doesn’t mean there won’t be meaningful football, though, as roster spots will be decided. Here are five players fighting for roles this upcoming season. WR Jordan Watkins Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Deebo Samuel. Those are the four wideouts we can write in a Sharpie to make the roster. Without Ricky Pearsall, there’s room for another. We’ve yet to see veteran Christian Kirk. The clock is ticking for Jacob Cowing, as he deals with a hip flexor that’s kept him out the past week. As much as some folks wanted Junior Bergen to become a thing during the preseason, the team would rather get a look at the other options on the team, as he was waived the day before the game. That’s a signal that the team is comfortable with Watkins returning alongside Deebo, and potentially as the lead punt returner. It’s also a sign they’re not convinced Bergen can contribute meaningful snaps offensively. That’s where Watkins comes in—the same Watkins who was reportedly playing with Adrian Martinez, the fourth-string quarterback. The former fourth-round pick missed his opportunity to make an impact as a rookie in 2025 due to injury. Now he’s in a situation where he can show the coaching staff he can make plays against a different colored jersey. If you remember last preseason, Watkins had a big play before suffering a high-ankle sprain. Catching the ball cleanly has supposedly been an issue for Watkins in camp. If he can finish plays with his speed over the middle and in contested situations, that could be enough to cement a spot in the rotation, not just on the roster. Carver Willis The last man standing will win the left guard job. For the past week or so, it’s been Robert Jones. That might say more about Connor Colby than it does about Jones, who missed 2025 with a neck injury. Rookie Carver Willis is waiting in the weeds for his opportunity. He’s not going to win the job in Week 1 of the preseason. But Willis can certainly earn more reps with the starters as the preseason goes along. If Jones plays a series or two — he still has some rust to knock off himself — then Willis should play a quarter or two. And that’s just at left guard. Willis should also see time at center, but until Jones is named the official starter, the 49ers will take a long look at him at left guard. Jack Jones Jones is 28. He’s played nearly 2,800 career snaps. There’s no secret as to who he’s been during his NFL career. He’s the definition of variance at cornerback. In baseball, the term “three true outcomes” gets thrown around colloquially. You either get walked, strike out, or hit a home run. Jones is the football version of that at defensive back. He’ll gamble and get beaten deep. He’ll guess right and come up with the interception or break the pass up. It’s how you end up with a career completion percentage allowed just over 56% with 25 pass breakups and eight interceptions, but also surrender 14 touchdowns in the previous two seasons with an average of yards per target of 7.5. Whether due to injury or dissatisfaction with Raheem Morris, it’s not hard to imagine the 49ers switching up their secondary at some point this season. They’re not going to do that if there isn’t another defensive back worth playing on the roster. One of the reasons Seattle had such a special season last year was because they were seven deep at defensive back. If Jones can show he’s moved away from his boom-or-bust ways this preseason and is more Steady Eddie, he could see snaps during the regular season. Nick Martin We can expect plenty of flash from Jaden Dugger and Larry Worth as they roam the field. The 49ers need to find out what they have in Nick Martin and if he can play in the event of an injury. He’s a third-rounder. That should be a starter—maybe not a Dominick Puni-level starter, but a starter nonetheless. When the 49ers hosted running back Blake Watson for a visit this past Monday , I rewatched his touches against the Niners last preseason. Both of his highlight plays came when he made Martin miss twice. Martin needs to show that he’s more than a “run and chase” player. There’s more to linebacker than “see ball, get ball.” You have to have instincts. You need to process what’s happening around you. You can’t expect to run around blocks and get away with it. It’s why Fred Warner has evolved into the very best at his position and why the Niners defense struggled mightily without Dre Greenlaw. Both players are ruthless when it comes to taking on blocks. Martin is another player who should be on the field closer to a half than a series, if not more. Martin might be the player on the roster with the most to prove this preseason. Bryson Eason There may not be room for both of the undrafted rookie free agent defensive tackles to make the roster. One might even be a stretch. But James Thompson Jr. and Bryson Eason sure can give Kris Kocurek and the Niners something to think about. My money is on Eason to make the roster. The preseason setting is perfect for his skill set. He’s listed at 315 pounds, although he weighed 323 pounds at the NFL Combine. Despite that, he had a broad jump in the 85th percentile. He carries his weight extremely well. To me, one of the reasons the team moved on from Evan Anderson was his lack of range. The play needed to be at Anderson for him to be a factor. Eason got the best of Bengals rookie Dylan Fairchild a couple of times, a third-rounder, when the two faced off in college. In that game, you saw Eason display the range that Anderson lacked. While he’s far from a pass-rushing threat, the tools are there where Eason can be just pesky enough. If he is anywhere as good against the run as he was at Tennessee during the preseason, Eason could sneak onto the roster.

title: 49ers News: Game day against the Tennessee Titans
summary: We get to watch the San Francisco 49ers play football. Maybe not the starters, but there will be enough battles that play out during preseason that’ll be worth the watch. Onto today’s links. Top five things to watch for in the 49ers’ preseason opener vs. Titans (paywall) “The decision between a third stack linebacker, a fifth defensive back at nickel or a fifth on-the-ball lineman seemed to lead Morris to that newly named fever backer position. The idea is to have a player capable of handling the responsibilities for three different positions, all in one. Nick Martin and Jaden Dugger, a raw rookie who played safety, linebacker and stand-up edge in college, have gotten familiar with the role. Morris has even thrown Romello Height, a dynamic rookie speed rusher, into the fever backer conversation. It would make sense for all three, none of whom are established starters, to play Thursday. The position boils down to the 11th man providing versatility, which makes things more difficult for an offense trying to read the defense before the snap. “Obviously, you know what traditional backers look like,” Morris said. “Stand-up guys that can move around. Those fever backers are kind of those guys that bring you subtle changes, subtle different things. … They can play star (nickel) for you. They can play outside edge and play sort of a big nickel. They can get at the line of scrimmage.” Morris was asked whether fever backer is a staple or more situational in his defense; he said it depends. The preseason may offer a sense of how much.” 49ers’ Brock Purdy carved up the Titans, but offensive line concerns are growing (paywall) “Niners defensive coordinator Raheem Morris came up with the nickname early in training camp when talking about the quarterback’s touch, though Purdy is not the biggest fan of it. Why? “Our quarterbacks coach, Mick Lombardi, doesn’t like the word ‘layer.’ He thinks everything should be driven,” Purdy said with a smile. “It’s cool that Raheem notices that, so I guess it’s a part of my game. But obviously, I like to think I can make any throw in the field, not just that one.” 49ers roster moves: RB Zamir White among 3 signed; 3 players waived “Throughout his four-year NFL career with the Raiders (2022-25), Zamir White has appeared in 45 games (nine starts) and registered 198 carries for 736 yards and two touchdowns on the ground, along with 25 receptions for 152 yards through the air. In 2025, White appeared in six games and totaled 12 carries for 32 yards and added four receptions for 24 yards.” What 49ers rookie Kaelon Black has learned watching Christian McCaffrey practice “The way that he runs his routes, how efficient he is,” Black said. “When I watch him at practice, he has no wasted movement. “I asked him, ‘What do you do to limit your wasted movement?’ And he said, ’It’s all about timing and just being yourself.’” Rookie Kaelon Black outlines why 49ers’ offensive system is perfect fit for him “It really maximizes what a running back can truly do. A lot of times running backs aren’t asked to catch the ball a lot out of the backfield. But here, it’s the complete opposite. You’re going to go out there and run different routes and you’re almost going to feel like a receiver first sometimes.” Kawakami: Brock Purdy and the 3 WRs who are saving the first part of 49ers camp (paywall) “I didn’t think it was feasible that Deebo could run the ball more than once or twice a game; I thought his wide back days were over. And yet … Deebo has lined up at RB at times from the moment he returned to the 49ers and he was by far their most dangerous RB on Tuesday. He also caught a couple of passes as a WR and generally was a major problem for the Titans throughout.” 49ers add a running back ahead of the preseason opener; waive Junior Bergen “Bergen might be a surprise, as some reporters who were present at practice went so far as to say he could sneak onto the roster and was viewed as the top option at punt returner. The team felt differently. They could bring Bergen back if he clears waivers, but the 49ers being comfortable with losing him on waivers with a slew of injuries at the position tells us how they feel about him.”

title: Titans win preseason opener 19-13 over 49ers
summary: Robert Saleh got a win in his debut as the head coach of the Tennessee Titans, 19-13 over the San Francisco 49ers. It was a tough night for Cam Ward. He did lead a 95-yard touchdown drive the first time the Titans had the ball, but finished the night just 5 of 12 for 57 […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Head coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans looks on while his team warms up prior to the start of the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Robert Saleh got a win in his debut as the head coach of the Tennessee Titans, 19-13 over the San Francisco 49ers. It was a tough night for Cam Ward. He did lead a 95-yard touchdown drive the first time the Titans had the ball, but finished the night just 5 of 12 for 57 yards. Some of the issues that haunted him last season still haunted him tonight. The first-team defense also had a tough night, especially in the secondary. There were too many guys running open down the field when they were in the game. The good news is it is still August, so there is plenty of time for the Titans to fix the issues they had tonight before the games actually count. Both Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears looked good running the ball. Spears had a run where he bounced off a couple of guys for a 25-yard gain. It was Pollard who had the touchdown on the first drive of the game. Julius Chestnut, who always runs the ball well in the preseason, finished the game with 47 yards rushing. Wan’Dale Robinson had two catches on four targets. The Titans gave him a big contract this season, and you can tell that he is going to be a focal part of this offense. Rookie WR Carnell Tate was targeted three times but was held without a catch. What stood out to you in the Titans preseason opener?

title: Cam Ward struggles in Titans preseason opener
summary: It was a tough start to the 2026 preseason for Tennessee Titans second-year quarterback Cam Ward. The most concerning thing about it was that he showed a lot of the same issues that gave him problems last year. There were a couple of layup throws that he missed because he didn’t set his feet or […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans warms up prior to the start of the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a tough start to the 2026 preseason for Tennessee Titans second-year quarterback Cam Ward. The most concerning thing about it was that he showed a lot of the same issues that gave him problems last year. There were a couple of layup throws that he missed because he didn’t set his feet or didn’t put any touch on the pass. His footwork was supposed to be one of the things he really focused on this offseason. He also had a couple of plays where he hung onto the ball too long and took an unnecessary hit. There was also a play where he ran backwards and then tried to throw the ball away, but it slipped out of his hand, resulting in an intentional grounding penalty. With all of that being said, it is still way too early to panic with Ward. It was his first game in the new system, and some of the mistakes could just be chalked up to first-game jitters. The most important thing is to see him fix some of the mistakes he made tonight when the Titans take on the Seattle Seahawks at home next Sunday.

title: Washington Commanders 91-man 2026 preseason Game 1 roster/depth chart
summary: Reviewing the roster limit As you are probably aware, the NFL CBA allows each team to have 90 players on its offseason roster, but it also makes provisions for a 91st player who joins the team via the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. For the last several years, the Commanders have made use of this […]
full_text: Reviewing the roster limit As you are probably aware, the NFL CBA allows each team to have 90 players on its offseason roster, but it also makes provisions for a 91st player who joins the team via the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. For the last several years, the Commanders have made use of this IPP exemption, as they have again this season, so Washington’s offseason roster limit is once again 91 players. Washington’s 91st player via the IPP is currently edge rusher TJ Maguranyanga , who spent the 2025 season with the Commanders as well. Incredible level or roster change since the beginning of training camp I’m not sure how obvious it’s been to casual observers, but in the 15 days that have passed since players took the field for the first day of training camp, the Commanders have announced 22 roster transactions! There is at least one more to come when the team announces Laremy Tunsil ’s revised status by the end of the month (he may not go onto IR until the initial cutdown to 53 players for ‘technical’ reasons). I have grouped the transactions by type rather than chronological order for ease and digestibility: Retired (3) LB Nick Bellore CB Ahkello Witherspoon DT DJ Davidson Released/waived (8) Edge Andre Carter TE Anthony Firsker CB Tre Hawkins OG Tyler Cooper OG Tim McKay OG Sala Aumavae-Laulu WR Chris Hilton Jr S Robert McDaniel Signed (10) WR Stefon Diggs WR River Cracraft OT Nicholas Petit-Frere P Matt Haack OL Max Scharping OL Trey Hill OL Daniel Brunskill ILB Curtis Jacobs DT Byron Cowart CB Fabian Moreau You will notice, perhaps, that there have been 11 departures but only 10 new players signed. This is because, on the first day of camp, I had already listed Rasul Douglas on the depth chart — listing 92 players at that time — without a corresponding move. Nick Bellore ’s retirement, announced at the start of camp, was that corresponding move. Accounting for Laremy Tunsil Conversely, while today’s chart lists 91 players, we know already that one of those players, LT Laremy Tunsil , will not be on the active roster in Week 1. Timing counts for a lot with players who suffer major injuries in training camp. Here’s a quick explanation of the considerations under the relevant NFL rules: 1. The Pre-Cutdown Rule (Season-Ending) If the Commanders place Tunsil on IR during training camp before the final 53-man roster reduction deadline on August 30, 2026, he is automatically ruled out for the entire season . He would not be allowed to practice or play for Washington at any point during the year. If doctors determine, post-surgery, that Tunsil will not be able to return to play prior to mid-February, then the Commanders might choose to exercise this option. 2. The Cutdown Day Exception (Designated to Return) NFL rules allow teams: a. to designate, on cutdown day, up to two injured players to return from IR during the season b. alternatively, the team can carry him onto the initial 53-man roster and move him to IR the following day (Option A is almost certainly the one that the Commanders would choose in Tunsil’s case) This approach allows Tunsil to keep his season alive since it leaves the door open for him to return after sitting out a minimum of four games (obviously, in Tunsil’s case, it would be closer to 4 months than 4 games). If doctors determine, post-surgery, that Tunsil’s return to play could happen prior to mid-February, then the Commanders might choose this option to keep all possibilities on the table for their left tackle. The only cost to the team is the opportunity to carry one more player on the training camp roster for two weeks. Not your typical depth chart The chart below is only a depth chart insofar as it assigns players to positions and stacks them in an order. The primary purpose of the chart is to keep track of the 91 guys that currently comprise the training camp roster, not to predict gameday alignments. You will note, for example, that I have 12 offensive position stacks and 13 defensive position stacks on the chart, despite the fact that a team can only field 11 players at one time. You will also note that each player’s name appears only once regardless of the fact that he may play in multiple alignments or positions ( e.g., an interior offensive lineman who can play center and both guard spots will appear at only one of those positions, not all of them ). Again, this is by design since the goal is to provide handy visual reference of the 91 individual players while also offering an overall snapshot of team strength and depth. The bias, though, is to provide a visual list of the full roster, not so much to create a game-ready depth chart. Finally, you will also note that, where players are capable of playing more than one position (and likely to do so on game days), my decision on where to align them may be very different from your idea of where they belong. A few changes since the previous iteration of the preseason 91-man depth chart Position consolidation At s ome position groups where players frequently change alignments, I have consolidated the chart somewhat. With the offensive line, for the most part, starters align in the same position nearly all the time, barring injury, though backup offensive linemen tend to cover at least two different positions. For the OL, I have not consolidated the chart. Here are my notes on recent consolidation of certain other position groups: Inside linebacker It’s unclear how many ILBs will be on the field at the same time from down to down. Traditionally, in a 3-4 defense, there would be two, but Daronte Jones could opt for just one in certain 3-safety alignments, or three in 4-3 alignments or when using one of them as a ‘walk up’ LB as part of a simulated or actual pass rush. I have one group for ILB displayed graphically in 3 stacks. Defensive line Similary, DL personnel packages and alignments are expected to be fluid in Daronte Jones’ scheme. Daron Payne , for example, could line up as a 3-tech on 1st down, nose tackle on 2nd down, and 5-tech on 3rd down. Like the ILBs, I have one group for the DL, displayed graphically in 3 stacks. Slot/Z receiver The Commanders are blessed with a lot of players — Stefon Diggs , Luke McCaffrey , Jaylin Lane , Antonio Williams — who have the ability to play either in the slot or as the ‘z’ receiver (or even ‘x’ when Terry McLaurin is off the field). Here is the alignment by offensive snap count for these receivers in 2024 and/or 2025 (as indicated in chart): Rather than dividing the group into slot vs ‘z’ on the chart, I have grouped 8 receivers into two stacks on the right side of the offensive chart. Running back With Bill Croskey-Merritt ’s offseason work as a pass catcher and the proven ability of Rachaad White , Jeremy McNichols and Jerome Ford to run inside and/or outside zone in addition to being capable-to-outstanding receivers out of the backfield, I have eliminated the 3rd-down back distinction and presented the team’s 6 RBs graphically in 2 stacks. Other notes on players of interest: Cornerback With the retirement of Ahkello Witherspoon and reports that Trey Amos is expected to be healthy enough to play Week 1, I have moved Mikey Sainristil from backup slot corner to wide corner in the stack with Rasul Douglas . This simply reflects my belief that his primary competition is now with Douglas rather than with Amik Robertson . I expect the rest of training camp and preseason to have a big impact on which players we see in which roles in the defensive secondary during the September regular season games. Safety Recent camp reports taken in the context of comments by Dan Quinn have led me to list Jeremy Reaves ahead of Will Harris for one of the safety positions. title: Commanders preseason: Colson Yankoff among players to watch vs. Dolphins
summary: We’ve got a Commanders game on the immediate horizon, with live tackling and everything. It has been a while since the Burgundy and Gold teed it up, but they’ll do exactly that on Friday night against the Miami Dolphins at Northwest Stadium.   While it’s real football, it’s also a preseason game that doesn’t really […]
full_text: We’ve got a Commanders game on the immediate horizon, with live tackling and everything. It has been a while since the Burgundy and Gold teed it up, but they’ll do exactly that on Friday night against the Miami Dolphins at Northwest Stadium. While it’s real football, it’s also a preseason game that doesn’t really count. Nothing’s official yet, but it’s hard to imagine many, if any, frontline Commanders players entering the fray on Friday. That’s especially true on the heels of Wednesday’s joint practice with Miami, when intensity cranked up in a more controlled environment with less injury risk. That doesn’t make Friday’s action a waste of your time. There’s plenty to settle this preseason, with positional battles being waged and important roles being figured out. You should keep an eye on the players below, plus a few others, to get a greater grasp on Washington’s roster and its progress learning new offensive and defensive schemes. I’ll select eight (okay, technically nine) right now and pick two more from your article comments below for additional pre-game discussion. One caveat: Those additional two players must have great odds of playing againt the Dolphins. As I said, I’ll add two players to watch and your explanation/analysis from the comments to the main story on Friday morning. TE Colson Yankoff The UCLA product and tight end convert has been awesome during training camp, with several big plays in camp practice. He has looked really good as a receiver and is pushing for an offensive role after primarily being a core special teams player in his first two years in the league. Colson Yankoff has been the training camp MVP. https://t.co/uUN5dcE4dn — Josh Taylor (@JoshTaylorFB) August 11, 2026 Showing well in games will only serve to strengthen his argument for playing time and targets on offense. He could be a high-volume target in preseason games, especially if Ben Sinnott doesn’t play many snaps. RB Kaytron Allen Top running backs rarely get run during preseason games – why take the punishment in games that don’t count? — so it seems likely that Bill Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White won’t play Friday. Jeremy McNichols is dealing with a quad injury, per Ben Standig , so sixth-round rookie Kaytron Allen should get fair amounts of work. KAYTRON ALLEN 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LXPaVF9N3S — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) August 8, 2026 Allen’s a tough, punishing runner with some solid camp moments, but we’ll get a better view of him and the Commanders running game in a contest with live tackling. EDGE Joshua Josephs Observers have had good things to say about Joshua Josephs, a fifth-round draft pick out of Tennessee, to this point in training camp. The Commanders need a capable rotation at the edge behind Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson. Having Josephs fit into that rotation is vital, considering his roster spot is virtually secure. Watch him work as a pass rusher and an edge setter in run defense. He’ll need to perform well in both areas to be trusted in key moments of regular-season games. K Drew Stevens/Jake Moody The Commanders kicking battle heated up during this week’s training camp practices. Incumbent Jake Moody had some pronounced struggles on kicking days, though both guys had a rough go on Monday. It’s assumed that both kickers will participate in each game, with the pressure ramped up in those situations. Stevens seems to have the early edge on the kicker job, but there’s time for Moody to make a comeback starting on Friday. DL Johnny Newton The former second-round pick started to assert himself in 2025, as our MattinBrisVegas explained in this detailed article on the interior defensive lineman. Mark Tyler also believes Newton could be a breakout player in 2026, citing the idea that new coordinator Daronte Jones’ scheme could fit him well. That’s all I need to hear. Now I need to see Newton’s dominance in action. DB Quan Martin Quan Martin got an “-OR-” designation at free safety on Washington’s unofficial depth chart , meaning he and Jeremy Reaves are in a position battle to be a regular at that spot. Martin must show well in the preseason to help secure his spot. Also, how will he be featured in these games? As a deep safety? Will he see time in the slot? Is he part of the three-safety looks we assume we’ll get under Jones? Martin must answer lots of questions this summer to earn a prominent role in this defense. C Julian Good-Jones Presumptive starter Nick Allegretti suffered a calf strain during the first camp practice and hasn’t returned. He could be back as early as Sunday, leaving little time for backup Julian Good-Jones to inspire confidence in him as a depth piece. While it’s uncertain if the first-unit offensive line will play on Friday, it would behoove the Commanders to give Good-Jones plenty of snaps to evaluate him at the center spot. Fans are clamoring for the team to look outside the organization for center help. Good-Jones could slow those demands with a good performance on Friday night. He must also stave off competition from Matt Gulbin and newcomer Daniel Brunskill, making these games key. WR Jaden Bradley An undrafted rookie out of UNLV, Jaden Bradley has been well-hyped this summer and Terry McLaurin has taken Bradley under his wing. On-site reporters say Bradley has looked like an NFL-quality receiver, and he must continue to support that argument in the preseason. The Stefon Diggs addition heightened competition at receiver, meaning it’ll be tough for the undrafted rookie to secure a 53-man roster spot. Bradley can force the issue with big plays and solid blocking in the run game. He could push for a practice-squad spot as well, by building confidence through quality performances. Who else deserves to be on this list? As a reminder, I’ll add two of your suggestions from the article comments — be sure to add a short explainer/analysis — to this story on Friday morning.

title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels camp gives cease-and-desist letter to LSU
summary: UPDATE: Jayden Daniels posted the following message on his Instagram Stories Thursday afternoon, a statement relating to the LSU/NIL issue below: An attorney speaking for Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has given LSU a cease-and-desist letter stating the school can not use is name, image and likeness, per an Wednesday evening ESPN report.   Mark Schlabach […]
full_text: UPDATE: Jayden Daniels posted the following message on his Instagram Stories Thursday afternoon, a statement relating to the LSU/NIL issue below: Jayden Daniels posted this on his IG Stories, a message relating to the LSU issue pic.twitter.com/vn0d3jiGH5 — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 13, 2026 An attorney speaking for Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has given LSU a cease-and-desist letter stating the school can not use is name, image and likeness, per an Wednesday evening ESPN report . Mark Schlabach received a copy of the letter, which was sent to LSU athletic director Verge Ausberry on Aug. 5. The letter from Jayden Daniels’ attorney Adam Kenner to LSU football stating the program “must immediately cease and desist from any further use, display, publication, distribution, promotion, commercialization, or other exploitation of Mr. Daniels’ NIL in any manner or medium.” pic.twitter.com/QdX6Tl1evG — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 13, 2026 A spokesman for Daniels told ESPN that the letter was sent largely sent because the school is allowing cornerback DJ Pickett to don the No. 5 jersey that Daniels wore during his two seasons at LSU (2022-23), including when he won the Heisman Trophy representing the school in 2023 . Daniels’ jersey was not retired by LSU, but it hadn’t been worn by anyone since he left the school. “The Daniels family is deeply disappointed and feels profoundly disrespected by LSU’s decision to give Jayden’s number to another player,” a statement from Daniels’ spokesperson read, per ESPN. “Jayden and his family had every reason to believe that his number would remain a meaningful part of his LSU legacy and would be honored and protected in recognition of his extraordinary contributions to the university.” Pickett wore No. 3 in 2025 but was given No. 5 this season. Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin responded somewhat to the issue, saying No. 5 was promised to him during the recruiting process, which occurred under the Brian Kelly regime. Kiffin chose to honor that promise. “DJ is in [No.] 5, and that was a situation that was promised to him in recruiting here, for him to sign here,” Kiffin said on Aug. 5. “I’ve done a lot of research on that with the family and the representatives and the people, so really I didn’t have a decision to make. It was promised to the kid. It wasn’t done for whatever [reason]. I’m not going to get into that. “I’m not going to judge something [that was done] when I wasn’t here. But when a kid is promised something to come to a school, he should wear it. So at that point, I don’t think that’s really my decision. We should honor what he was told.” Daniels’ camp didn’t appreciate that decision, which led to the NIL letter. “Jayden made it clear that he did not want his number given to another player, and he believed his wishes would be respected,” the statement said. “His Heisman Trophy-winning season and everything he accomplished on and off the field cemented his place in LSU history. To see his number given to another player is incredibly disappointing and feels like a failure to honor the significance of what Jayden accomplished at LSU.” Daniels’ camp has legal authority to request the cease-and-desist, with LSU only legally allowed to use his NIL for 180 days after his final game at LSU. Former ESPN analyst and LSU alum Ryan Clark added insight on the matter, saying he has spoken to both sides on the matter. Before the rumor mill runs wild, or things get taken out of context, hoping to provide some clarity- The Daniels’ camp understands that the No. 5 jersey is not retired at LSU, nor have they ever asked for it to be. The cease-and-desist is not about the number itself or about DJ… — Ryan Clark (@Realrclark25) August 13, 2026

title: Details of Stefon Diggs contract with Washington Commanders unveiled
summary: News of the Commanders signing receiver Stefon Diggs was followed shortly after by initial terms of his contract, a one-year deal worth up to $12 million.   Anytime you see the “up to” phrasing, that includes incentives and escalators beyond the base terms of the deal. That’s no different in this case.   More complete […]
full_text: News of the Commanders signing receiver Stefon Diggs was followed shortly after by initial terms of his contract, a one-year deal worth up to $12 million. Anytime you see the “up to” phrasing, that includes incentives and escalators beyond the base terms of the deal. That’s no different in this case. More complete terms of the deal were provided by sports finance site Spotrac, which broke down the details of the Diggs deal. The star receiver signed a one-year deal with $7.15 million guaranteed. He received a $2 million signing bonus and will make a $5.15 million base salary. There are also $850k worth of per game roster bonuses that can increase the deal to $8 million. There is another $4 million in incentives that can be earned to reach the $12 million maximum possible within the structure of the deal. At the time of this story’s original publication, those incentives were not available. This story will be updated once those terms are known. The Diggs contract carries an $8 million cap hit – it also requires $9.7 million in cash — which doesn’t matter much to a Commanders team with significant amounts of cap space. Per Spotrac, the Commanders still have $37 million in overall cap space.

title: Is Washington Commanders DL Johnny Newton on cusp of a breakout season?
summary: The conventional wisdom on Jer’Zhan “Johnny” Newton is that he has yet to play up to the expectations of his NFL draft status.  They were set very high by GM Adam Peters’ comments after picking Newton No. 36 overall in the second round of the 2024 draft: …Johnny, we could not believe he was still […]
full_text: The conventional wisdom on Jer’Zhan “Johnny” Newton is that he has yet to play up to the expectations of his NFL draft status. They were set very high by GM Adam Peters’ comments after picking Newton No. 36 overall in the second round of the 2024 draft: …Johnny, we could not believe he was still there. We were a little nervous that he wasn’t going to make it to us at 36. We looked at moving up to get him, very surprising. We had a first-round grade on him and he is an explosive, violent player. He’s a team captain. He got the Commander tag and he’s exactly who we want to bring in this building. We think he’s an advanced player who can come in and play right away. Really a three-down player who you can play on the run downs, play on pass downs, skilled, hands and feet are tied together. And he arrives violently when he gets to the ball and he plays just like we want him to play. So just thrilled to get Johnny. Heading into his third NFL season, his first playing in Daronte Jones’ exotic defense, questions abound about whether Newton was worth the Commanders’ investment of an early-second round pick . In his first two seasons, Newton has filled a rotational role in the Commanders’ defensive front. His rookie season was hampered by recovery from offseason foot surgeries . Nevertheless, he stepped up when starter Jonathan Allen missed nine games, and ended up playing 51% of regular-season defensive snaps, the second largest share among interior defensive linemen. In 2025, his playing time dropped to 38% of defensive snaps, placing him third in the rotation behind starters Javon Kinlaw (63.6%) and Daron Payne (53.3%). Newton’s production totals to date have been relatively modest. As we’ll see in a minute, though, raw production stats taken out of context can be deceiving. But before we get to that, we need to take a look at what kind of player Newton is. That will tell us what performance matters. Simplistically speaking, we can think of two poles of defensive line play. Space-eating defensive linemen use size and power to clog running lanes and occupy blocks to allow their teammates to make plays in the running and passing games. At a listed weight of 6-foot-2 and 295 pounds, Newton lacks the bulk we typically associate with two-gapping iDL, and he lacks the power to make up for his less than prototypical size. He will likely never be the guy to hold the point of attack in the running game or eat double teams to free up edge defenders and blitzers in the pass rush. Toward the other pole of the position group are the gap shooters. Newton is an example of the typically smaller interior defenders who win with explosiveness to gain penetration and make plays in the backfield. In addition to exceptional athleticism, Newton’s skillset includes good anticipation, advanced hand fighting skills to defeat blocks and unexpected pursuit speed to catch runners from behind and chase plays across the formation. So, why hasn’t that skillset translated to high-level sack production or tackles for loss totals after two years in the league? Or has it? My previous article on UDFA WR hopeful, Jaden Bradley used an analytical technique to look through the veil of confounding factors to see how good receivers really are at coming down with the football. This one uses a lot simpler math to adjust for the one factor which bedevils most comparisons between players based on statistical totals – differences in playing time. Players are frequently ranked based on production stats , which are based on cumulative totals. Such comparisons can be revealing — to a certain extent. But using raw production stats can lead to erroneous conclusions, like Emmitt Smith being a better running back than Barry Sanders. Adjusting production totals for differences in numbers of opportunities or playing time gives productivity stats (e.g. yards per carry). Productivity stats tell us more about a player’s ability to produce on the field than which player got the most playing time or opportunities to compile stats. This becomes particularly important when evaluating players with limited playing time, like Newton. To evaluate where Newton is, and where he might be headed, this analysis will focus on stats that speak to performance at making high-impact plays in his role as a penetrating interior defender. These include metrics for the pass rush, stopping the run short of its goal and generating turnovers. NFL official stat totals To start things off, let’s take a step back and have a look at the official NFL cumulative stats, as reported by Pro Football Reference . While I have already pointed out some limitations, these stats illustrated below are most often used to rank and compare players. The bar graphs show Newton’s regular- plus post-season totals in 2024 (gold) and 2025 (burgundy). Numbers above the bars indicate his rank among the top 96 NFL starters and major contributors at iDL in each season (2024: min. 365 defensive snaps; 2025: min. 400 defensive snaps). Newton played 586 defensive snaps, with 11 starts, as a rookie. He finished the season around the middle of the pack among major contributors at iDL in both sacks (rank 55, 43 rd percentile) and QB hits (rank 42, 56 th percentile). He was above league average at generating tackles for loss (rank 28, 71 st percentile). Despite common perceptions, the production total was not bad at all for a rookie coming back from offseason foot surgery. Johnny’s numbers did got a boost from playing in three more games than players on teams that failed to make the playoffs. But that is balanced to some extent by the fact that he did not get as much playing time as most designated starters, even counting the nine games when he filled in for Jonathan Allen , because of the relatively flat distribution of snaps in Joe Whitt’s defensive-line rotation. Newton’s playing time diminished to 432 snaps with two starts in 2025, playing third in the defensive-line rotation behind Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne in just 17 regular season games, with no postseason. Nevertheless, his sack production more than doubled, and his quarterback hit total increased as well. Newton led Commanders interior defensive linemen in sacks despite only playing 60% as many snaps as primary starter Javon Kinlaw. His sack total was the 19 th highest among 98 iDL (min 400 snaps). The one area where Newton’s production took a backward step was tackles for loss, dropping from seven as a rookie to just four (rank 58, 40 th percentile) in his sophomore season. While this could be taken as an indication of a step back in run defense, since most TFLs occur on running plays, they don’t tell the whole story. There is better metric of impact in the running game, which we’ll get to in a minute. Overall, the raw, unadjusted production stats show Newton starting out as a middle of the pack pass rusher in his rookie season with a knack for catching ball carriers in the backfield. His impact in the pass rush took a big step forward in his second season, despite getting less playing time. While TFL production took a big step backward. Now, let’s see what playing-time-adjusted and advanced stats have to say. Productivity and Advanced Stats Pass Rush Productivity The increase in pass-rush production despite a drop in playing time suggests that Newton made a big jump in productivity in his sophomore campaign. To get a more meaningful measure of his improvement in the pass rush, let’s look at two metrics: pressure rate and sack rate. Pressure rate (Press %), derived from PFF’s total pressures, is the percentage of pass-rush snaps on which a rusher generated pressure (sacks, QB hits or hurries). It provides a more comprehensive view of a player’s impact in the pass rush than just sacks and QB hits. The third component, hurries, is an advanced stat, derived from film breakdowns. Scoring hurries involves an element of subjectivity, which leads to skepticism among some fans. For that reason, I also included sack…

title: 2026 NFL preseason Week 1: Takeaways, analysis
summary: The NFL preseason is underway! How did rookies and players in new places perform in their debuts?
full_text:
The first week of the  2026 NFL preseason kicked off Thursday, giving us our first look at rookies and players making debuts with new teams.

 To keep you updated on how teams fared, our NFL Nation reporters are summarizing the games below.

 
 Quick links: 
 Full schedule | Where to watch |  Depth charts 
 Fantasy football draft guide | Sign up to play 

 
 

 Thursday's games 

 Cardinals 27, Raiders 14 
 

 Cardinals:  No. 3 draft pick  Jeremiyah Love showcased his quick feet and power running during his time on the field Thursday night. It resulted in 11 carries for 58 yards, an average of 5.3 yards per carry. That average showed his ability to find holes and the strength to take on hits. He also had three catches for 14 yards with a long of 7 yards.

 Second-round pick Chase Bisontis left the game in the third quarter with a knee injury and did not return. He went down holding the back of his left knee and was rolling in agony as he was attended to by trainers.

 Wide receiver Reggie Virgil , Arizona's fifth-round pick, made an impressive one-handed catch for a 24-yard gain.  -- Josh Weinfuss 

 Next game: vs.  Dallas Cowboy s (Aug. 22, 10 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Raiders:   The Raiders' quarterback battle between Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza was on full display. Cousins played only the opening drive, which resulted in a touchdown. After he completed a 10-yard pass to Jack Bech and a 16-yard pass to Tre Tucker , he found tight end Michael Mayer for a 13-yard touchdown, which capped off a 10-play, 68-yard drive to begin the game. Cousins completed 5 of 6 passes for 50 yards.

 As for the No. 1 pick, Mendoza, he showed off his resilience, a trait admired by the coaching staff. His first drive wasn't great -- he had two incompletions and the Raiders were forced to punt. His second stint was a different story. He completed a 19-yard pass to rookie wide receiver Malik Benson , fitting the ball through a tight window. Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr . then rushed for 53 yards before Mendoza zipped the ball over the middle to Bech for a 6-yard touchdown pass on third down.

 His third drive resulted in a three-and-out. But his fourth and final drive of the evening ended with him putting the Raiders into field goal range. He finished the night completing 10 of 16 passes for 97 yards. Mendoza did struggle against pressure. He was pressured on 38.9% of dropbacks, going 2-for-6 with 11 yards and a 42.4 passer rating. He was sacked once.  -- Ryan McFadden 

 Next game: at  Houston Texans  (Aug. 20, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN)

 

 

 Steelers 28, Packers 9 

 

 Steelers:  Welcome to the NFL (kind of), rookies! The Steelers' rookie class had a solid showing in its preseason debut behind quarterback Drew Allar , who led the team to three touchdowns in his first appearance.

 The third-rounder's first came on third-and-7 in the third quarter when he connected with fourth-round receiver  Kaden Wetjen for a 74-yard catch-and-run. Two plays later, Allar kept the ball on a read-option and ran it into the end zone for a 3-yard score. Allar and Wetjen connected again midway through the fourth quarter, this time in the end zone on a 5-yard touchdown. Allar put a bow on the night with a third touchdown on a 4-yard pass to rookie FB Riley Nowakowski .

 Playing with the first team, second-round wide receiver Germie Bernard also showed off his yards after catch ability with a 25-yard catch-and-run in the first half. Defensively, sixth-round defensive end  Gabriel Rubio stood out with six tackles.  -- Brooke Pryor 

 Next game: vs.  New York Jets  (Aug. 21, 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Packers:  Rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse looks comfortable as a starting cornerback. New defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon isn't afraid to blitz. And veteran free agent receiver Skyy Moore looks like an upgrade as a punt returner (and he might also be able to help on offense). But perhaps more importantly, after some shaky practices, rookie kicker Trey Smack came through in a big way in this game. Officially, Smack made field goals of 37, 58 and 38 yards. He also nailed another 58-yarder, but a Steelers penalty gave the Packers a first down, so coach Matt LaFleur took the points off the board. First-year QB Kyle McCord (12-for-14, 102 yards) had a strong showing.  -- Rob Demovsky 

 Next game: at  Denver Broncos  (Aug. 21, 9 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Bengals 16, Lions 14 

 

 Bengals:  Of all the newcomers who played in the preseason opener, a couple of rookies had very bright moments. DE Cashius Howell , the team's second-round pick, took advantage of a slick ball and recovered a fumble on a botched handoff. And WR Colbie Young , the team's fourth-round selection, had a couple of nice catches in the first half against the Lions. Howell has had a strong camp and had one QB pressure in his nine snaps Thursday, per NFL Next Gen Stats. -- Ben Baby 

 Next game: vs.  Chicago Bears  (Aug. 22, 7 p.m. ET)

 

 Lions:   After the sudden retirement of veteran QB Teddy Bridgewater during training camp, all eyes turned to rookie Luke Altmyer , who got the start in his preseason debut.

 Altmyer, an undrafted free agent out of Illinois, went 13-for-21 for 130 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in a solid performance.

 The Lions also signed backup QB Joshua Dobbs to a one-year deal earlier this week, in the wake of Bridgewater's retirement, as the backup returns for a second stint in Detroit. Dobbs entered the game in the second quarter, splitting snaps with Altmyer in the first half, and ended with 32 passing yards. He completed 4 of 8 attempts as the two compete for the QB2 spot behind Jared Goff .

 Blake Miller , the 17th pick of the draft, also made his debut, starting at right tackle, where he got off to a strong start this preseason. -- Eric Woodyard 

 Next game: vs.  Washington Commanders  (Aug. 22, noon ET)

 

 

 Patriots 13, Colts 13 
 

 Patriots:  Seventh-round RB Jam Miller (Alabama) was the rookie headliner, which was timely as the competition for the team's No. 3 running back took an unexpected twist when the Patriots placed leading candidate Terrell Jennings on injured reserve before the game. The 5-foot-10, 209-pound Miller started and ran hard, totaling 55 yards on 14 carries (3.9 YPC), and now might have the inside track on the RB3 role. Elsewhere, first-round pick Caleb Lomu started at right tackle and was called for a borderline ineligible man downfield penalty that negated a big play.  -- Mike Reiss 

 Next game: vs.  Philadelphia Eagles  (Aug. 22, 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Colts:  Rookie linebacker Bryce Boettcher (three tackles) made an obvious impact in his first pro action, showing he can handle responsibilities while still bringing the physicality he has displayed throughout camp. The fourth-round pick's continued development is a great sign for a linebacking corps with many questions.

 Fifth-round pick George Gumbs Jr . had two tackles and a sack as he continues his bid to carve out a role in the defensive end rotation. Caden Curry , another rookie pass rusher, had a sack on an impressive inside move, a team-high five tackles, two tackles for loss and two pass deflections as he makes a bid for a roster spot.

 Finally, third-round selection  A.J. Haulcy played fast from his safety position, showing versatility in playing the single-high role and at strong safety in the tackle box.  -- Stephen Holder 

 Next game: vs.  Atlanta Falcons  (Aug. 22, 7 p.m. ET)

 

 Chargers 27, Texans 7 
 

 Chargers: Rookie left guard Jake Slaughter fared well, picking up a stunt during his time at left guard and looking comfortable under pressure. First-round edge rusher Akheem Mesidor didn't flash much, playing only eight snaps. Undrafted rookie Nadame Tucker led the outside linebacker group with two pressures, showing the pass-rush ability that's flashed throughout training camp. Wide receiver Brenen Thompson was mostly quiet but finished with two…

title: 2026 Arizona Cardinals training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Cardinals training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Cardinals reporter Josh Weinfuss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Cardinals camp. How will Arizona's quarterback situation shake out with  Jacoby Brissett  back on a reworked contract? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Cardinals' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest on the Cardinals 
 
 Tyler Allgeier 'building' relationship with rookie RB Jeremiyah Love 
 Source: Cardinals' Brissett guaranteed $15.5M in reworked deal 
 Cardinals TE Trey McBride walks back dig at Arizona fanbase 
 Sweat (knee) among four Cards added to PUP list 
 With deal done, Brissett can focus on Cardinals' playbook 
 
 

 

 Who was the Cardinals' top performer at camp? 

 Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love showcased his complete arsenal of skills throughout camp. His quick footwork stood out from the first day of camp and once the team put on pads, Love displayed his vision and speed through holes in the line. And when Love caught passes, he showed an asset of his game that has been talked highly about but to see it in real time expressed how dynamic of a player the third-overall player can be.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 How quickly can the offense get on the same page in Mike LaFleur's new scheme after quarterback Jacoby Brissett missed OTAs and minicamp while waiting for a new deal?

 

 Aug. 11 
 The Cardinals' starters will make their preseason debut Thursday night on the road against the Las Vegas Raiders , coach Mike LaFleur said Tuesday. They'll play one drive, for sure, and possibly two at most.

 Quarterback Jacoby Brissett said he's looking forward to getting hit for the first time since January and starting to run the Cardinals' new offense in real time. But the goal in a drive or two is simple, he said.

 "Obviously, new coach, new system, operation hearing him in the headset, going out there in the game and just clean communication and operation in and out of the huddle, I think that's the mindset of this game," Brissett said.

 More observations: 

 
 The Cardinals broke training camp at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Tuesday. They'll fly to Las Vegas on Wednesday, play the Raiders on Thursday and when they practice again over the weekend, it'll be at their practice facility in Tempe. 
 Second-year defensive lineman Walter Nolen III was wearing a brace on his left elbow and had both his hands wrapped. LaFleur said Nolen's hands were "good." 
 

 

 Aug. 10 
 Despite expressing his desire to keep Michael Wilson in Arizona long-term, Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort didn't seem too sure that he'd be able to get an extension done with the receiver.

 When asked Monday if he expects to get a long-term deal done with Wilson, who had his first 1,000-yard season in 2025, Ossenfort wouldn't commit to the idea.

 "He's a guy that we want around here a long time," Ossenfort said. "There's no question about it. So, I mean, expect, that's a tough word.

 "I mean, I think our interest is in keeping him here and Michael's been a good player for us. He's going to continue to be a good player for us. So, I know coach [Mike] LaFleur feels the same way and we want Michael here for a long time."

 The two sides have already been negotiating, however, a deal has yet to be agreed upon.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Ossenfort didn't want to get into talks about an extension with left tackle  Paris Johnson Jr ., whose fifth-year option the team picked up for next season. "Honestly, just going to keep extension talks between us. Never really talked about that and don't really want to plan on getting into that." 
 Ossenfort said he always thought he'd get a new deal done with quarterback Jacoby Brissett and said that sometimes negotiations take a while. "This one was no different. And so I think that involves communication back and forth. And we had a lot of conversations over the course of those, the spring, throughout the summer up into training camp. So no, there's never a doubt in my mind that it was going to get done." 
 

 

 Aug. 9 

 Cardinals starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett struggled with the deep ball throughout practice Sunday, missing approximately seven deep balls. Some were long. Some were wide. Four were to Marvin Harrison Jr .

 It was an atypical performance from Brissett, who, until Sunday, had been consistent with his deep balls throughout training camp, typically putting them in a place where only his receivers can catch them.

 After practice, Brissett set out to rectify his misses.

 He and Harrison spent about 15 minutes working on deep balls from approximately 30 yards. It looked as though Brissett was working on his deep touch to get his passes where Harrison can make a play.

 
 Rookie quarterback Carson Beck had a strong finish to Sunday's practice. He hit rookie wide receiver  Reggie Virgil  for a touchdown in the back of the end zone and had a quiet celebration to himself afterward. That came after Beck hit wide receiver Bryson Green on a deep ball but then threw an interception. 
 The Cardinals tried a variety of defensive lineups Sunday. At one point, third-year cornerback Elijah Jones , who has played defense in just one game in his career, took first-team snaps. Second-year defensive back Kitan Crawford , who played 12 games on defense last season, also got some first-team reps. 
 Wide receiver Ihmir Smith-Marsette continued his impressive camp with another touchdown Sunday. He continues to make big catches and has been consistently making plays throughout camp. 
 

 

 Aug. 4 
 Thursday night's Hall of Fame game will not just be a run-through for the players, it will also be the first time the Cardinals' coaching staff will have a chance to be together during a game.

 "I think that's another great thing for us to have this game, to just get a little quick dry run-through on how game day operations go, just from time management, all that stuff," offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett said. "I think it's going to be great for all of us and there'll be some ups and downs and you work through those and grow every day."

 Hackett said he'll be in the booth watching the action unfold from above but with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and quarterback coach Matt Schaub handling Carson Beck , Hackett will be able to help whoever needs help. But that'll also be part of this staff's first time together: Figuring out his role in all of it.

 More observations: 

 
 Even though Josh Sweat hasn't practiced this camp and there isn't a set timeline for his return, defensive coordinator Nick Rallis said Tuesday that Sweat is "locked in" with meetings and post-practice tape. 
 

 
 Aug. 3 
 Deep balls were the theme of the day for the Cardinals as Jacoby Brissett ,  Gardner Minshew II  and Carson Beck put on an aerial display.

 Brissett unleashed a bomb to Marvin Harrison Jr ., who, after letting a deep ball earlier in practice go off his fingertips, came down with a diving grab that would have gained more than 50 yards.

 Beck showed off his deep ball, hitting fellow rookie Reggie Virgil on a beautiful pass. On another deep shot, Beck froze two defenders in the second level before finding a receiver who made the catch a step in front of a defender.

 More observations from the day:  

 
 Tight end Trey McBride was banged up briefly after he was hit in the middle of the field. He went down and was slow to get up but later returned to the offensive drills.…

title: 2026 Atlanta Falcons training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Falcons training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Falcons reporter Marc Raimondi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Falcons camp. How will the QB battle play out between  Michael Penix Jr . and  Tua Tagovailoa for QB1? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Falcons' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Falcons stories 
 
 Sources: Falcons, RB Robinson reach 3-year deal worth up to $75M 
 Falcons sign Matthew Bergeron to four-year, $96M extension 
 Falcons' Jalon Walker tore ACL, out for season 
 Wife of DC Ulbrich dies of cancer 
 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 Who is the Falcons' top performer so far at camp? 

 Drake London . No one has had more receptions in Falcons training camp than their star wide receiver. And it definitely seems like his injury issues (knee, shoulder) from 2025 are in the rearview mirror. London has done it against a good secondary, too. Top cornerback AJ Terrell has also had a great camp, even getting the better of London in 1-on-1 drills. Safety Xavier Watts has been a standout, as well.

 But London, with his big frame [6-4, 215] and sure hands, has been a safety net for a quarterback group all getting used to a new system under head coach Kevin Stefanski and offensive coordinator/playcaller Tommy Rees.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

  Who will start at quarterback? It seems like Tua Tagovailoa will be the guy in Week 1, especially since Michael Penix Jr . has still not yet been cleared to practice fully. Penix has been out there every day, in many cases excelling in 7-on-7 sessions. But the Falcons (and Penix himself) are still not ready to throw him out there with a pass rush.

 Stefanski announced Wednesday that Tagovailoa would start the first preseason game Friday night. But he was not yet ready to make a decision on who the starting quarterback will be to begin the season. That indicates that Penix is not out of the race.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 Falcons practice Wednesday was a short one, mainly consisting of two-minute drills, with the team's first preseason game coming up Friday.

 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa had some success, but was unable to get the ball into the end zone. He was 5-of-9 passing in the 11-on-11, two-minute drill sessions. Tagovailoa was intercepted on the final play of the session by safety Jammie Robinson on a pass that appeared to be meant for tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr ..

 Tagovailoa nearly had a beautiful touchdown pass down the right side to wide receiver  Olamide Zaccheaus , but the ball was slightly overthrown.

 Cooper Rush , who will back up Tagovailoa in the exhibition Friday, was 5-of-10 and also unable to score a touchdown.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa has been a full participant in practice for about a week now. And his performances have really turned the corner since late last week.

 Tagovailoa was 7-of-7 passing in 11-on-11 team sessions Tuesday. The tight back issue seems to be in the rearview mirror and Tagovailoa is starting to show comfortability with this new offense under head coach Kevin Stefanski and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees.

 "Oh, he's getting better every day," Falcons quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt said Tuesday. "I think he's becoming more comfortable with the system and the play calls and protection adjustments and everything. It's tough always to come into a new system. So, picking that up -- missing the first part of camp set him back just a little bit -- but really the last three or four days he's really come on."

 
 The Falcons defense is dealing with some injuries. Safety Jessie Bates III (back), inside linebacker Divine Deablo , defensive back Natrone Brooks and cornerback Avieon Terrell all missed practice Tuesday. Defensive tackle  Da'Shawn Hand  has been out since last week. 
 The Falcons signed veteran running back Trey Sermon to add depth behind Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr ., who has gotten some run as a kick returner. Sermon will complete with Tyler Goodson , Nathan Carter and Cash Jones to make the 53-man roster. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Quarterback Michael Penix Jr . is still not cleared for 11-on-11 sessions, but he has mostly been sharp in practice lately.

 On Monday, Penix was 9-of-11 passing during a 7-on-7 series, including a beautiful completion to tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr . down the right sideline. The throw was right in the bucket and would have gone for a big gain. Penix did get picked off by cornerback Clark Phillips III on his final throw.

 Tua Tagovailoa was 4-of-6 in 11s and working more on pushing the ball down the field.

 Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said he has not yet made a decision on whether Tagovailoa will play in the team's first preseason game Friday against the Denver Broncos . As for Penix, he can't play in any game until he is cleared for 11s in practice, Stefanski said.

 More observations: 

 
 The Falcons signed defensive end Cameron Sample , who was waived last week by the San Francisco 49ers . Sample will provide depth off the edge after second-year standout Jalon Walker went down with a torn ACL last week. 
 Right tackle Jawaan Taylor was activated from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He is likely to be the team's starting right tackle. The Falcons have been rotating Michael Jerrell , Brandon Walton and rookie seventh-rounder Ethan Onianwa in that spot. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa had his best practice of camp, though it did not last long. The practice, that is.

 Lightning halted the Falcons' open practice at Lanier High School in Sugar Hill, Georgia, early on Saturday night. There was still more than 30 minutes left when things were called on the field of a packed stadium.

 Tagovailoa was 6-of-8 passing in 11-on-11 drills, including his best two passes of training camp: a 30-yarder with touch to wide receiver Jahan Dotson and a play-action rollout lob to wide receiver Drake London .

 Tagovailoa returned to full practices earlier this week after dealing with a tight back to start camp.

 
 

 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa hit running back Bijan Robinson on a wheel route that would have gone for a 90-yard touchdown or so during an 11-on-11 session Friday. The series was situational. The Falcons offense was backed up against the opposite goal line and Tagovailoa floated it nicely to Robinson, who had complete daylight.

 It was just another play in another practice this summer here in Flowery Branch, Georgia. But it also felt like more than that, something symbolic. Like a sigh of relief.

 For the first time this training camp, Tagovailoa and Robinson were both full participants in practice. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and Robinson was a hold-in before signing a three-year contract extension Wednesday that is worth up to $75 million. Robinson got his first carries in 11s Friday.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Michael Penix Jr . is still not cleared for 11s, but has looked sharper lately in 7-on-7 work. On Friday, he was 6-of-9 in the red zone, helped out by a diving catch from wide receiver Keelan Marion . 
 Matt Ryan, the team's president of football and former franchise quarterback, threw to wide receivers Drake London and Jahan Dotson separated from everyone else during a drill Friday. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Michael Penix Jr . explained his current situation in the clearest way possible Wednesday.

 "If I can't be on the field," Penix said, "how am I going to…

title: 2026 Baltimore Ravens training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Ravens training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Ravens reporter Jamison Hensley has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Ravens camp. Can new coach Jesse Minter get  Lamar Jackson  and the Ravens to the Super Bowl? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Ravens' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Ravens camp 
 
 Zay Flowers, Ravens agree to four-year, $140M extension 
 Derrick Henry, entering 11th year, not thinking about retirement 
 Ravens waive rookie Diego Pavia to make room for Ethan Pocic 
 Ravens' Madubuike (neck) practices for 1st time in 10 months 
 
 

 

 Who has been the Ravens' top performer so far at camp? 
 Wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane . The rookie third-round pick has put together one of the best camps ever by a Ravens rookie, delivering a highlight reel catch almost every day. In going against Baltimore's top defenders, Lane has shown speed, leaping ability and a huge catch radius.

 Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said Lane reminds him of former Saints wide receiver Mike Thomas . "Thomas had these strong hands where he could pull it down in a way, and you threw it in the vicinity, and you felt like he was going to go get it," Doyle said. "There is a lot of that feeling. He is a very friendly guy to throw to."

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Decide on a starting center. The Ravens are hoping the preseason can bring clarity on who is replacing Pro Bowler Tyler Linderbaum , who signed with the Raiders in free agency. Danny Pinter is currently at the top of the depth chart. Other options are Corey Bullock , Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic . "We're still a ways away from being able to determine exactly who that guy is," Doyle said before the preseason opener.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson produced his sharpest practice of training camp.

 Jackson completed 11-of-12 passes (91.6%) in team drills and 7-on-7 sessions. His only incompletion was on a throw that went off wide receiver  Rashod Bateman 's hands over the middle.

 Jackson's longest pass was a 40-yard toss to Bateman down the sideline, which continued the emphasis of explosive plays with new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. He later showed great touch on a pass that sailed over a couple of defenders and dropped into the hands of Devontez Walker .

 "He's aging like fine wine," Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork said of Jackson, who turns 30 in January. "He's getting better. He's highly motivated this year."

 More observations: 

 
 Injured starting cornerbacks Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey could potentially be back by next week. Both left practice early this week. "Both are trending very well," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. 
 Minter indicated first-round pick  Olaivavega Ioane  will play in Saturday's preseason opener. The No. 14 overall pick is expected to be Baltimore's starting right guard. "I'd be comfortable getting him just a little bit of game action and getting his feet wet," Minter said. 
 Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike could ramp up his participation over the next couple of weeks, according to Minter. Madubuike has not participated in team drills in training camp. He has primarily worked off to the side with DC Anthony Weaver during positional drills. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 The Baltimore Ravens ' cornerback depth is being tested this week after both of their starting cornerbacks exited practice early.

 A day after Nate Wiggins was carted off the field with a knee injury, Marlon Humphrey walked off the practice field midway through Wednesday's practice with a trainer. It is unclear what he injured.

 Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said after practice that he expects both Wiggins and Humphrey to return soon.

 "We would love to have those guys [Wiggins and Humphrey] out there," Weaver said. "Thoughts and prayers that they get back as fast as they can."

 With Wiggins and Humphrey not on the field, the Ravens' most experienced cornerbacks are Chidobe Awuzie and T.J. Tampa . Baltimore also have promising young corners in rookie Chandler Rivers ,  Bilhal Kone  and Keyon Martin .

 In Wednesday's play of the day, Rivers dislodged the ball from wide receiver Xavier Guillory , knocking the ball high in the air. Martin pulled in the loose ball for a turnover.

 "There are a bunch of guys I think that could step in if needed," Weaver said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike participated in positional drills for the first time in training camp. Madubuike, who underwent neck surgery in April, had been limited to individual drills for the first two weeks of camp. "He looks phenomenal," Weaver said. "I know he wants to be just doing everything he can to be back out there, and when he is out there, I expect him to look like the Nnamdi we have grown to know and love throughout the years." 
 Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane continues his hot streak. He caught a 45-yard touchdown from Lamar Jackson in a one-on-one drill and then boxed out Tampa for a 35-yard catch downfield. 
 Tight end Mark Andrews had his best day of camp, catching a touchdown pass from Lamar Jackson in the red zone. 
 Lamar Jackson showed leadership after he misconnected with wide receiver LaJohntay Wester in the red zone. Jackson first talked to Wester about his route and then took him to a tablet where they could rewatch the play again. 
 The Ravens placed No. 3 QB Skylar Thompson on injured reserve and signed QB Austin Reed , who was with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle at the Bears' training camp last season. With Lamar Jackson not playing in Saturday's preseason opener, the expectation is for Tyler Huntley to start and undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to play a bulk of the game.

 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers surprisingly returned to practice after suffering a quad contusion on Saturday. He missed one practice.

 Flowers ran before Tuesday's practice and participated in positional drills. He looked fast and smooth cutting around the cones before heading early into the team facility.

 "That was all part of the plan as he's working back just through the soreness of the quad," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "I expect him to be Zay here any day."

 In other encouraging injury news, starting nose tackle Travis Jones was activated off the Physically Unable to Perform list and practiced for the first time this summer. He worked in positional drills after missing the first two weeks of training camp with a pectoral injury.

 "He's been chomping at the bit," Minter said. "He'll be a guy that in the first few days we'll probably have to hold him back, which is sometimes a good thing. But, 'Trav' looks amazing striking the sled. He's been putting in a ton of work off the field, in the weight room [and in] conditioning. I expect big, big things from 'Trav'."

 Other observations: 

 
 
 Ravens QB   Lamar Jackson   and other "established players" won't play in Saturday's preseason opener against the   Philadelphia Eagles , Minter said. Jackson hasn't played in the preseason since 2021.
