title: Inside Lamar Jackson's adjustments to Ravens' new offense
summary: Under new OC Declan Doyle, Lamar Jackson has the opportunity to embrace a new vision.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- About a week ago, quarterback Lamar Jackson was ticked off at Baltimore Ravens training camp, spiking his helmet down to the ground with both hands. 
 
 Toward the end of a two-minute drill, Jackson hit tight end Durham Smythe down the seam to move the ball just outside the end zone with six seconds remaining. With the clock ticking, Jackson and the rest of his offensive teammates rushed to the line of scrimmage to get one more play off. But time expired and Jackson let everyone know his frustration. 
 
 Jackson has experienced his share of ups and downs this summer while learning a new offensive system under coordinator Declan Doyle. There are plenty of practices where Jackson makes several great passes deep downfield and then throws an interception, including one to a 310-pound defensive lineman. 
 
 But Jackson's track record suggests he will have more success in adapting to a new scheme than any of the other 21 teams that have a new offensive coordinator this season. Jackson has won the NFL Most Valuable Player award the past two times he has worked with a new offensive coordinator. 
 
 In 2019, Jackson became only the second unanimous selection for MVP in his first season under Greg Roman. Four years later, he won MVP for a second time in his first season under Todd Monken. 
 
 Now, under Doyle, Jackson has the opportunity to continue the trend where he embraces a new vision -- featuring a different alignment, cadence and targets -- to become the league's most acclaimed player again in 2026. 
 
 
 
 "Lamar continues each and every year to push himself and learn and grow and find new ways to innovate," Ravens tight end Mark Andrews said. "Especially when you learn a new offense, you're able to kind of add some things to your repertoire and do some different things that other people haven't seen. He's the most adaptable, smoothest player in the league." 
 
 In Doyle's offense, he stresses being physical and explosive. The biggest buzz word with Doyle is detailed. He wants his players to be students of the game, which starts with Jackson, or "L" as Doyle often refers to him. 
 
 On every pass, the challenge for Jackson is to find where the defense is most vulnerable for a big play. Doyle believes, if Jackson is using the proper footwork and looking at the right spots, he will know where to distribute the ball. 
 
 Doyle has emphasized making the plays as efficient and "schemed up" as possible. The Ravens are trying to take pressure off Jackson by limiting the number of times that Jackson has to go off script when a play breaks down. 
 
 Jackson has been more engaged than ever. He attended the voluntary workouts in the spring. He's constantly talking with Doyle on the field, calling the first-time playcaller "a wizard." 
 
 Doyle hasn't held back when coaching Jackson. During the spring minicamp, Doyle called out Jackson for pitching the ball instead of running a bootleg. 
 
 "I feel like he is doing a great job at that [by] challenging us each and every play," Jackson said. "Even with the huddle, and how the huddle is set up, he challenges us to get to the line of scrimmage fast, execute, break down the defense and process everything fast so that it's a process of elimination when we get to the line of scrimmage." 
 
 Jackson's teammates feel he has achieved a comfort level with the new offense this summer, just like he has done in the past. 
 
 "Honestly, I do not know how he picks up on systems so fast," wide receiver Zay Flowers said. "It is crazy. I have to study a lot with this [system]. He just picks it up quick. I honestly do not know." 
 
 

 
 

 THE LAST TIME Jackson took an extensive amount of snaps under center in games was youth football. That's likely to change this season. 
 
 After primarily working out of the pistol or shotgun formations in his first eight NFL seasons, Jackson has been taking more snaps under center than any previous training camp. Jackson expects this change to continue into the regular season. 
 
 "With this balanced type of offense, I feel like it will help us out a lot -- identifying the defense, really keeping the defense on their toes," Jackson said. 
 
 Playing less in the pistol and shotgun will be a different look for Jackson, who has been under center for 5% of his career snaps in the NFL. Since 2018, Jackson's 226 snaps under center are the second fewest among quarterbacks with at least 50 starts behind Kyler Murray (202 snaps under center). 
 
 Even though Jackson hasn't played under center much, he has been very effective when he does. Over the past eight seasons, Jackson has the highest QBR in the NFL (81.2) when under center, throwing 20 touchdowns and one interception. 
 
 Jackson has looked natural under center in training camp, according to Doyle. 
 
 "You would never notice that he hasn't been under there that much," Doyle said. "He has the ability to really do all three: He can be under [center], he can be in the pistol, [and] he can be in shotgun. There's a lot of versatility in his game." 
 
 Doyle added, "You want to be able to mix all those things and make the defense have to deal with the multiplicity of those sets as [much as] you can. He provides us a lot of value in his ability to go under center and run some of the offense that way."  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 KEEPING DEFENSES ON  their toes goes beyond where Jackson lines up for the Ravens. Jackson's cadence can give an edge to Baltimore. 
 
 Doyle has made the point that snap count is the one aspect that the offense knows and the defense does not. So, the Ravens have been working with Jackson's verbal and rhythmic sequence before the snap. 
 
 "Lamar is a very quick learner when you start working with him, and so I have been happy with what we have done," Doyle said. "We are trying to kind of keep the defense honest, and yet, at the same point in time, there are times where cadence might provide an advantage to be able to try to create a big play. So, it all kind of ties together, but there is certainly an emphasis on the tempo in which we break the huddle [and] the cadence we use. That stuff is all a huge piece to what happens post-snap." 
 
 Getting defenses to jump offside has been a struggle for Jackson and the Ravens. Since Jackson's first full season in 2019, Baltimore has drawn defenses offside 33 times. Only two teams have had fewer (New Orleans and New England). 
 
 According to ESPN Research, that has resulted in 48 "free plays" for Baltimore -- when the flag is thrown on the defense and the offense knows any negative outcome can be erased by the penalty -- which is tied for the fifth fewest in that span. Jackson has one career completion on a free play: a 6-yard pass to Flowers in 2023 at the Browns. 
 
 During this summer's training camp, there have been some hiccups along the way. On Sunday, the Ravens varied their cadences to get the defense off-kilter and it had the opposite effect. The offense was flagged for false start eight times. 
 
 But, once Jackson and his teammates can get these cadences down, it can lead to the defense jumping into the neutral zone. And when Jackson sees that flag thrown, he is looking to take advantage of that more than he has in the past. 
 
 "Free plays, free yards -- we need it all," Jackson said. We're trying to put points on the board."  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 THIS YEAR'S DRAFT  gave Jackson more than improved pass protection. He received more targets in the passing game. 
 
 After selecting guard Vega Ioane with the No. 14 pick, Baltimore drafted two wide receivers ( Ja'Kobi Lane in the third round and Elijah Sarratt in the fourth) and two tight ends ( Matthew Hibner in the fourth round and Josh Cuevas in the fifth). 
 
 Asked what advice he could give the rookies to mesh with Jackson, Flowers said, "If I am being honest, Lamar can adjust to everybody. He knows everybody is different. Everybody's play style is different."

title: Ranking NFL quarterbacks by trait: Best arm, accuracy, more
summary: Does Josh Allen have the league's strongest arm? Is Lamar Jackson still the most unstoppable QB rusher? And where does Caleb Williams stand among the best improvisers?
full_text:
You're going to hear us talk about quarterbacks a lot on " NFL Live " over the course of the 2026 season . There will be debates about all of them, from the best in the game to the borderline starters. But for a third straight year , I'm narrowing the focus here in the preseason . Who are the best signal-callers in the NFL at individual skills?

 Does anyone boast a better arm than Josh Allen ? Does Joe Burrow or Matthew Stafford have the more refined mechanics? Is Lamar Jackson still the gold standard in QB rushing?

 I ranked the top 10 quarterbacks by seven different traits: arm strength, ball placement, mechanics, decision-making, pocket presence, second-reaction creativity and rushing ability. These lists are based on current performance and expectations for the 2026 season. It is how I would rank the QB group at this exact moment. I included only starters  and leaned on what I see on tape to form the rankings.

 

 
 Jump to a section: 
 Arm strength  | Ball placement  |  Mechanics 
 Decision-making  |  Pocket presence 
 Second reaction | Rushing ability 

 
 

 Arm strength 
 1. Josh Allen , Bills 
2. Justin Herbert , Chargers 
3. Caleb Williams , Bears 
4. Matthew Stafford , Rams 
5. Patrick Mahomes , Chiefs 
6. Baker Mayfield , Buccaneers 
7. Drake Maye , Patriots 
8. Joe Burrow , Bengals 
9. Lamar Jackson , Ravens 
10. Dak Prescott , Cowboys 

 There are different kinds of arm strength. Everyone immediately looks at deep balls -- the 60-yard Hail Marys down the sideline. It's all about who can throw the rock the furthest, right? You need a live arm to connect on those shot plays, no doubt. But I focus more on passes into tight windows in the intermediate areas of the field and the pure power throws from what I call "funny body" positions. Quarterbacks don't have the strong base to fall back on here; there is no loading up and driving through the pass. Instead, they need to rely almost entirely on their arm to get the ball where it needs to go with velocity.

 Allen is still No. 1 in this department. His ability to get zip on his throws from uncomfortable positions really stands out. He just flicks his wrist, and the ball is suddenly in his receiver's hands on a rope. Not every QB1 can do that, and yet he does it with consistency.

 

 But there are some challengers for his top spot this year. Herbert gets real pop on his throws by driving it. No one has completed more tight-window balls over the past five years than Herbert (162). Williams got legit consideration for No. 1, too. He made some miraculous passes from unorthodox positions in 2025, including a 40-plus-yard strike to the end zone late in the divisional round  -- while back-pedaling.

 Mahomes can wing it with the best of them, and Stafford and Maye are both elite on downfield balls. Stafford completed 37 passes of 20 or more air yards last season, easily the most in the NFL. And I also want to call out Mayfield -- I still think he has the most slept-on arm in the NFL. The one quarterback I really wanted to get into the top 10 was Trevor Lawrence . He also has some underrated arm talent and makes difficult throws look easy. Hey, it's tough to limit these lists to just 10 guys.

 

 

 Ball placement 
 1. Matthew Stafford , Rams 
2. Drake Maye , Patriots 
3. Sam Darnold , Seahawks 
4. Joe Burrow , Bengals 
5. Jared Goff , Lions 
6. Jordan Love , Packers 
7. Josh Allen , Bills 
8. Lamar Jackson , Ravens 
9. Brock Purdy , 49ers 
10. Dak Prescott , Cowboys 

 How do you find the best quarterbacks in ball placement? Their receivers are never truly considered "covered."

 I say this every year in this space, but it's worth refreshing: Accuracy and ball placement aren't the same thing. Accuracy means putting the ball on the receiver so he can make the play. Ball placement means putting the ball on the receiver in the perfect spot so he can make the play -- and no one else can. The names at the top of this list -- including some MVP candidates last season in Stafford and Maye -- routinely keep the ball away from the defender. It's all about precision.

 Let's start by addressing a big shift at the top. Burrow was the top-ranked QB in ball placement on each of the past two lists I've put together. He's now No. 4. He's still extremely good in this area, able to pin the ball to his receivers. But injuries did cost him more than half of the 2025 season, and it opened the door for some others to move up the list a little bit. Fair or not, I'm factoring in time on task. And Stafford came out every Sunday and fired bull's-eyes with conviction.

 If you're looking at the stats, Maye would have a pretty good case to be the new No. 1, too. He settles for second here, but there's no knocking his league-best 72.0% completion rate and 9.1% completion rate above expectation (per NFL Next Gen Stats). And unlike every other QB in the top five, he wasn't playing with an All-Pro receiver. Maye was especially good with trajectory going downfield, dropping it in a bucket. I can't wait to see what he does with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs in 2026.

 Goff is sneaky good in this trait, and we see it at all levels of the field. Purdy displays incredible touch, layering the ball in. His 10.7% off-target rate was fourth-best in the NFL last season. Love and Prescott have an impressive ability to float the pass in and set their receiver up for yards after the catch. It's another list that was hard to sort through at the bottom, but I think every name on here is deserving.

 Tua Tagovailoa has been a mainstay in the ball placement top 10, and he was all the way up at No. 2 in 2024 when I first started doing this annual project. But he has declined a bit here, and his QB1 battle in Atlanta disqualifies him, anyway. Geno Smith also slid out after making the list in back-to-back years; he didn't look like the same quarterback last season at 35 years old.

 

 

 

 Mechanics 
 1. Matthew Stafford , Rams 
2. Joe Burrow , Bengals 
3. Daniel Jones , Colts 
4. Jared Goff , Lions 
5. Dak Prescott , Cowboys 
6. C.J. Stroud , Texans 
7. Caleb Williams , Bears 
8. Jayden Daniels , Commanders 
9. Josh Allen , Bills 
10. Lamar Jackson , Ravens 

 It's neck and neck between Stafford and Burrow. Things that matter here:

 
 Clean, smooth throwing motions from start to finish 
 Strong bases that keep the QB in rhythm and firm 
 Repeatable processes that don't change from rep to rep, even when things get chaotic around the QB 
 
 That last one is key for Stafford and Burrow. Defenses don't know what's coming because every throw looks exactly the same coming out. It's amazing consistency. The tight connection between Stafford's upper and lower body allows him to pull off all those no-look throws. Defenses can't tell the difference until his release, and bam, the ball is going somewhere unexpected.

 You might be surprised to see Jones at No. 3. I was, too. But watching the tape again, I was taken aback by how good his mechanics were in Indianapolis last season. The Colts ran many different forms of RPOs, and that means his mechanics need to be sound. They were.

 Goff, Prescott and Stroud are such pure passers, with beautiful, natural motions. Daniels' mechanics have shades of Stroud. And I was impressed with how much Williams improved here last season. He might be more known for the off-platform plays, but he's solid from a mechanics standpoint. I had a hard time leaving Justin Herbert off. He probably should be on the list. Aaron Rodgers was also a tough cut, even in Year 22.

 

 

 Decision-making with the football 
 1. Josh Allen , Bills 
2. Matthew Stafford , Rams 
3. Jordan Love , Packers 
4. Drake Maye , Patriots 
5. Jayden Daniels , Commanders 
6. Dak Prescott , Cowboys 
7. Lamar Jackson , Ravens 
8. Joe Burrow , Bengals 
9. Patrick Mahomes , Chiefs 
10. Jalen Hurts , Eagles

title: 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bills training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Bills reporter Alaina Getzenberg has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bills camp. How will the transition to Jim Leonhard's defense go? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Bills' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bills camp 
 
 Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson carted off with leg injury 
 Josh Allen on Bills' alternate uniforms: 'Stop hating on the jerseys' 
 Bills unveil new 'Nickel City' alternate uniforms 
 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp preview 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 One key player the Bills are looking forward to having back on the field for the regular season is edge rusher  Michael Hoecht . Hoecht has been a full participant for much of training camp while working back from a torn right Achilles suffered in November.

 Coach Joe Brady said that the plan is for Hoecht to play in a preseason game, but did not want to disclose if that would be this week or in the future. Hoecht also said after practice that he believes it's a game-time decision.

 "[Hoecht's] way ahead of schedule, seeing what he's able to do," Brady said. "And so, if it's not this week, I do want to get him preseason football. Shoot, he's gonna want to do preseason season football."

 Other observations:  

 
 C Connor McGovern , RB Ty Johnson , WR Skyler Bell . CB Maxwell Hairston .and CB Kani Walker are all facing injuries, while S Cole Bishop and S C.J. Gardner-Johnson did not participate in practice. Hairston and Bishop did do some work inside the team's fieldhouse while the rest of the team was outside. 
 Offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael will be in the coaching booth instead of the sideline for Saturday's preseason game. Carmichael has traditionally coached on the sideline, but Brady wants to experiment with him in each place during the preseason. 
 Quarterback Shane Buechele threw interceptions on back-to-back plays during 11-on-11 drills. The first was a pick-six by defensive back Te'Cory Couch and the second was on an errant throw taken away by linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo . 
 

 

 Who is the Bills' top performer so far at camp? 
 Nickel corner Dee Alford . Quarterback Josh Allen put it best, "Dee Alford's been making a lot of plays." This could go to a couple of players, including receiver DJ Moore , but Alford has stood out on a defense that is undergoing major change. His training camp performance featured three interceptions off Allen.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Where does this defense stand? This is the part of the team that underwent the biggest change this offseason, going from a 4-3 base under Sean McDermott the last nine seasons to a 3-4 with new coordinator Jim Leonhard. Getting a look at this unit in game action will continue to help in seeing more and more of what to expect. Keep in mind, however, that multiple defensive secondary starters are dealing with injuries, including safeties Bishop and Gardner-Johnson and CB Hairston.

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 The Bills wide receivers room is a popular topic of conversation. While DJ Moore 's connection with quarterback Josh Allen has been a camp highlight, it was Joshua Palmer who stood out with a couple of nice grabs in Tuesday's practice.

 Palmer's first season with the Bills was disrupted by injuries, especially a left ankle injury, but the receiver said he is now feeling much more comfortable. Getting significant, and reliable, contributions from players such as Palmer would be big for Joe Brady's offense.

 "I don't have to question any of my movements," Palmer said. "I don't have to think before the route. I don't have to ... I'm not stressed before I go on the field. I just go out and play."

 Other observations: 

 
 Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said that he thinks the plan is for starters to play in the preseason opener Saturday but that it is TBD how much they will play. "It's gonna be exciting for guys to get out there and just kind of let it rip," Leonhard said. Leonhard said tackling is a big evaluation piece for the defense in the game, noting that getting offensive players to the ground and finishing plays was an "Achilles' heel" in Buffalo last year. 
 Rookie DT Zane Durant returned to practice, but a number of starters were still not participating. Among those not practicing are safeties C.J. Gardner-Johnson and Cole Bishop and center Connor McGovern . Cornerback Maxwell Hairston was doing some work on the side. The team has not disclosed injuries. 
 Nickel corner Dee Alford continues to be a camp standout. On Tuesday, he intercepted Allen for the third time in camp with a jump on a ball that was intended for receiver Keon Coleman . Alford said that he adjusted the call based on what they saw on film. "[Allen is] the best quarterback in the league, MVP. So ... any time you can catch an interception from him, man, it just shows what type of defender you are." 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Injuries were the theme of the day as the Buffalo Bills held their first training camp practice at the team's facility in Orchard Park, New York.

 Several starters did not participate, including safety Cole Bishop , cornerback Maxwell Hairston and center Connor McGovern . Also not taking part were running back Ty Johnson , wide receivers Skyler Bell and Ja'Mori Maclin , defensive tackle Zane Durant , defensive back D.J. Miller and punter Mitch Wishnowsky .

 The team did not disclose the nature of the injuries.

 Starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson , who missed two practices with a right calf strain, also left practice early after falling to the ground while making a pass breakup in the end zone. Athletic trainers looked at his right leg. He eventually walked to the locker room on his own.

 Practice was held inside the Kaleida Health Performance Center as rain and lightning once again threatened.

 More observations: 

 
 Veteran Lloyd Cushenberry III continued to work with the first-team offense at center in place of McGovern. 
 Top camp standouts include tight end Keleki Latu and cornerback Kani Walker . 
 Offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael attended the Pro Football Hall of Fame ceremony Saturday. He was there in support of Drew Brees, whom he coached in New Orleans. "It was really special," Carmichael said. "Special moment. It was great to see not only Drew and Coach [Sean] Payton but the whole group of guys that had come out just to be there on his behalf." 
 

 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 On Saturday night, the Bills held their annual "Return of the Blue and Red" practice at Highmark Stadium. It was the Bills' first football activities in their new $2.1 billion home.

 The official welcome featured plenty of fireworks, quite literally.

 One of the biggest came during a two-minute drill, when quarterback Josh Allen found wide receiver Khalil Shakir , as he darted past safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson  and twisted his way into the end zone. Moments later, Allen joined him in the celebration by sliding into the end zone.

 As coach Joe Brady described it, "Josh throwing an unbelievable play to Khalil."

 The night went smoothly, outside of a brief downpour midpractice, and players later marveled at the arena.

 "Wow," tight end Dawson Knox said. "... I got here four hours early. I was just walking around on the field, taking myself on a little tour around everything, just kind of looking at all the details and just taking it in, because it still doesn't feel real yet. ... It's the coolest place I've ever played…

title: Allen, Bills starters to play Saturday in 1st game at new stadium

title: 2026 Carolina Panthers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Panthers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Panthers writer Mike Kaye will have the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Panthers camp. Will QB Bryce Young and the Panthers take another step forward after making the playoffs in 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Panthers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 Who is the Panthers' top performer so far at camp? 

 Third-year wide receiver Jalen Coker 's immediate returns after receiving a three-year, $34 million contract extension in July have made the Panthers' brass look wise this summer. The former undrafted playmaker has gotten open with regularity and caught the ball cleanly and consistently throughout training camp.

 Coker has looked dynamic opposite Tetairoa McMillan , who has impressed in his own right. The top tandem's summer production has been encouraging, especially with third-round pick  Chris Brazzell II  (knee) out for the season and 2024 first-round pick Xavier Legette still working to live up to his draft pedigree.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Will the offensive line be able to overcome a litany of injury adversity to begin the season?

 The Panthers' longtime starting tackles,  Ikem Ekwonu  (knee) and Taylor Moton (blood clot), will be sidelined into the regular season. They'll be replaced by free-agent addition Rasheed Walker at left tackle and first-round pick Monroe Freeling at right tackle, respectively. Walker has plenty of starting experience, but Freeling is switching to the opposite side of the line as a rookie.

 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) and right guard Rob Hunt (back) missed several practices during the first few weeks of training camp. Brady Christensen , a versatile backup, will be an important insurance policy for both.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 The Carolina Panthers consider running back Chuba Hubbard to be "week-to-week" after he injured his hamstring in Wednesday's practice.

 Head coach Dave Canales said Hubbard underwent an MRI on Thursday before practice and the starting running back will be sidelined for the second preseason matchup against the Buffalo Bills in Orchard Park, New York on Saturday.

 According to Canales, Hubbard sustained the injury during a one-on-one drill.

 With Hubbard sidelined, Jonathon Brooks and Trevor Etienne will rotate in with the starters for a couple of series, Canales said. A.J. Dillon will also receive an early workload against Buffalo.

 Other observations: 

 
 Defensive end Derrick Brown (knee) and outside linebacker Pat Jones (illness) wore uniforms during Thursday's non-padded practice. Brown took part in individual drills after working with a trainer before practice. 
 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) and right guard Rob Hunt (back) took team reps together. They were replaced by Chandler Zavala and Brady Christensen later in practice. 
 Wide receiver Jimmy Horn Jr . was getting open with ease throughout practice, but he was rarely targeted by the quarterbacks. 
 Starting quarterback Bryce Young had an excellent sequence to end practice during the two-minute drill in 11-on-11 work. He hit wide receiver Xavier Legette on a shallow cross and the playmaker sped up the field untouched for a touchdown. On the next and final play, Young rolled around the pocket with no one open and zipped a laser through defenders to tight end Tommy Tremble for a touchdown. 
 Tight end Darren Waller didn't make his practice debut on Thursday because he had to undergo a physical. The team still needs to make a corresponding move to fit him on the roster. A source with knowledge of the situation told ESPN the team plans to sign Waller following the preseason matchup against the Bills on Saturday. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has gotten "bigger and stronger" this offseason, according to head coach Dave Canales . And that improved physique was on display throughout Wednesday's practice in Charlotte.

 McMillan started the day with a nifty double move against starting cornerback Mike Jackson in one-on-one drills. McMillan was able to create increased separation with his route progression after beating Jackson off the line. The wideout then hauled in the ball for a touchdown a few paces in front of Jackson.

 "At the line of scrimmage, just hasn't really had an issue this camp," Canales said. "Getting off the line, I think that he's really translating all the work he did in the offseason. ... I'm really excited where he's at."

 Later, during team drills, the connection between quarterback Bryce Young and McMillan was apparent.

 Young was picked off by Jackson on an early rep while targeting McMillan. But following that miscue, the starting quarterback connected with McMillan on more than a handful of tosses.

 Other observations: 

 
 Along with Jackson's interception against Young in team drills, safety  Demani Richardson  intercepted a pass from backup QB Kenny Pickett in 11-on-11 drills. 
 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) returned to practice in pads after missing several workouts during the first two weeks of camp. He took part in individual drills. He isn't expected to play against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday, per Canales. 
 Outside linebacker Pat Jones (illness) was a new absence. Defensive end Derrick Brown (knee soreness) also missed practice. Brown hasn't worked with his teammates in a week. 
 Rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling , the team's first-round pick, had a pair of strong reps against outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips , the team's prized free-agent addition, in individual pass rush drills. Following the first rep, veteran lineman Brady Christensen clapped in approval. After the second try, offensive line coach Joe Gilbert loudly praised Freeling's technique. 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 A competition is brewing at inside linebacker next to one of the Carolina Panthers ' biggest offseason additions.

 Trevin Wallace is competing with veteran Claudin Cherelus for the second starting linebacker job opposite All-Pro defender Devin Lloyd , head coach Dave Canales confirmed Monday. 

 The Panthers signed Lloyd to a three-year, $41.9 million deal in March to lead their defense. However, when defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero uses a base set, the play-caller will deploy two inside linebackers, which is why the competition becomes paramount for the unit. Wallace, a 2024 third-round pick, has been limited to 25 games (20 starts) during his first two seasons. He has sustained back-to-back season-ending shoulder ailments and underwent surgery for the latest setback after landing on injured reserve in December of last year. 

 Despite his injury struggles over the past two years, Wallace was expected to be the first man up next to Lloyd. Now, he'll need to earn that spot in the lineup. Both Wallace and Cherelus played in the first half during Thursday's 33-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame game in Canton, Ohio.

 Other observations: 

 
 Several players were forced to break up a tussle between center Luke Fortner and cornerback Mike Jackson in the middle of the scrum following an 11-on-11 rep. At one point, Fortner and Jackson, while hanging onto each other, slammed down to the ground. The bout was quickly separated, but backup offensive tackle Stone Forsythe was also pushed to the ground.  
 Canales acknowledged that the defense bounced back on Monday after being one-upped by the offense on Sunday. Backup linebacker Bam Martin-Scott , rookie cornerback Cam…

title: Confident Caleb Wlliams has Bears flying high
summary: Williams is starting to show the grasp and confidence Johnson believes will help the Bears take the next step.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- If the goal of Tuesday's lengthy, humid practice was to "create evidence" for Ben Johnson and his coaching staff to know where the Bears stand at the halfway point of training camp, Caleb Williams gave his head coach exactly what he was looking for.

 Towards the end of the near two-hour session, Williams and the offense began the final move-the-ball period backed up at their own 1-yard line. Like majority of practice, this exercise was completely off-script, with the objective for Williams' unit to convert two first downs to win the drill.

 One play after Dillon Thieneman blitzed off the edge and nearly ran Williams out of the back of the end zone, the quarterback slipped through a gap as he felt pressure to his right and fired off pass to Rome Odunze , who scampered 58 yards down field on a catch-and-run.

 Moments later, Willams briefly lost Scotty Miller -- "that's what happens when you're on the shorter end," Williams quipped -- before he caught a glimpse of the veteran wide receiver streaking open on a crossing route and ripped the ball for another big gain to win the drill.

 It was an exclamation point on the type of practice Williams said the Bears needed; one that helps build callouses for an offense looking to continue its late-game dominance from a year ago when it became the first team in NFL history to pull off a total of seven fourth-quarter comebacks.

 "He's taken complete control of what we're trying to do, and so we're on the right track," Johnson said. Williams' search for consistency through the Bears' first 11 practices has been a focal point of camp. The quarterback who had to curtail the urge to text his head coach throughout the offseason as he eagerly awaited the start of their second year together was red hot during the opening stretch of camp.

 His operation from the huddle to the snap was crisp. His connections with Odunze, Colston Loveland , Luther Burden III and Kalif Raymond showed what this offense is capable of at full strength. Just about every practice featured a "wow!" moment from Williams, who showed up to camp down 10-15 pounds and with sky-high confidence.

 Then came the lull, to which Johnson shouldered some responsibility. It wasn't as if the issues that routinely plagued Williams last training camp were resurfacing. Unlike a year ago, the quarterback hardly felt like he was drowning. Having his head above water meant surviving an intense installation period designed to see how much the quarterback can handle.

 "Those first four practices I thought were really, really good, and then as the volume has continued to go up -- and it's my fault as much as anything, just because I think I've put in more this year on offense than I did a year ago by design," Johnson said. "I want it to feel like a lot right now -- that there's been a level of plateau up to this point. Now that things will slow down from an installation point, I think we're going to see him continue to go on the upswing."

 By every account, Tuesday's practice snapped that lull. Even in the areas where Williams still seeks improvement, like with his accuracy, the quarterback's growth is tangible in different areas. While the Bears built themselves into the kings of the fourth quarter, the offense's ability to score before halftime was an issue in 2025. Most practices end with the team repping crunch-time moments with situations that force the offense into hurry-up mode and the two-minute drill.

 On Aug. 8, Williams delivered one of those wow moments during an end-of-half situation. With the offense facing a third-and-10 with 12 seconds until halftime, Williams bought time when dropping back before throwing a 17-yard laser to Odunze, who high-pointed the ball between two defenders in the back of the end zone for a touchdown.

 Mastering moments like these allows Williams to fulfill Johnson's objective of throwing as much as he can at the quarterback in film and walkthrough sessions to see what he can retain and execute at full speed on the practice field.

 "One, it takes reps," Williams said. "That's always important. I think, two, it takes a bit of failure, it takes a bit of maybe plateauing and going up and down. Taking one step up, one step down and kind of being at the same level trying to figure things out so that when you get to the season, now you're rolling. When you get to the season, the confidence is there.

 "When you get to the season, it's everything is coming together and like I said, that's the point of this moment, this time, being able to go out there and fail. Go out there and come back to the film room and correct it and go out there the next day in walkthrough or whatever it is and get out there and correct it and get it right so that Coach has the proper confidence in myself but also the team to be able to go out there on game days."

 But nothing carries a bigger endorsement for where Williams is at this point of training camp than how Johnson sees an extension of himself on the field. Rather than coaches leading the charge in afternoon walk-throughs from practice hours before, players, particularly Williams, are now focusing on where corrections need to be made.

 "He certainly is leading that charge," Johnson said. "He knows when it's not good enough; he's huddling us back up and let's get it right.

 "I felt that in practice [the other day] too. You guys might've noticed it; we broke the huddle and things weren't quite right and he's regrouping us. So, I think that's a huge step in the right direction. I know those guys really value what he has to say. They're getting extra reps when the horn is done for the day and continuing to working on hooking up in the passing game with all the pass catchers, and that's only going to pay dividends down the road."

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Bears reporter Courtney Cronin has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bears camp. Will the defense step up and lead the Bears back to the NFC North title? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Bears' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Bears news 
 
 Darnell Wright agrees to record deal 
 New Bears safety Coby Bryant out 8-10 weeks with injury 
 Bears CB Johnson views 2026 as 'definitely a contract year' 
 Ben Johnson: Bears motivated to spurn 'regression' label 
 
 

 Who is the Bears' top performer so far at camp? 

 What a difference a year makes for Caleb Williams . In his second offseason with Ben Johnson, the quarterback has the Bears' offense in position to be one of the NFL's most explosive units. There are areas he needs to continue to improve in, like with his accuracy, but Williams' command of the playbook has been evident in camp by the chemistry he quickly created with new center Garrett Bradbury and his routine distribution to the likes of tight end Colston Loveland and wide receivers Rome Odunze , Luther Burden III , Zavion Thomas and Kalif Raymond . There hasn't been a single practice over the first half of camp where the offense walked off the field looking like it was in dire straits. Williams' growth and capacity for withstanding a giant install is a big reason why the Bears are in position for their offense to be the catalyst in wins.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Injuries have been a problem in the Bears' secondary. Nickel corner Kyler Gordon is on PUP (calf) with no timeline for his return, safety Coby Bryant is out four-to-six months after knee surgery and the DB depth has been decimated with injuries to Cam Lewis , Terell Smith and Jaylon Jones in addition to top backup safety Elijah Hicks , who remains on PUP. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will use Chicago's three preseason games to determine his starters are at slot corner and free safety and which backups with little to no NFL experience can be trusted in reserve roles.

 
 Aug. 11 
 Tuesday's practice was about "creating evidence" for the coaching staff to be able to evaluate where players stand in specific roles and who is climbing their way into the 53-man roster.

 "Up to this point, it's been a lot more get the plays in, let's get them repped once or twice and now they can actually execute and go out there and play ball," coach Ben Johnson said. Coaches sent out a game plan Monday night for players to study in hopes of seeing who could play fast and adjust to not knowing what was coming their way.

 With the offense and defense having 98% of their installs in, the 11th practice of camp opened with focusing on short-yardage goal line team drills to build the intensity and competition that Johnson envisioned carrying over to the rest of practice. The starting offense dominated that period with chunk runs from  D'Andre Swift  and Kyle Monangai , who each scored. In the first move-the-ball period, Swift got loose and found his way down the right sideline for a 62-yard TD.

 Quarterback Caleb Williams  and the starters aced a tough test towards the end of practice with the offense backed up at its own 1-yard line. The goal for the drill was to get two first downs, which Williams accomplished by creating space to find Rome Odunze for a 50-plus yard catch-and-run followed by a big gain to Scotty Miller .

 Both the first and second-team offenses weren't as crisp in the situational drills at the end of practice, but Williams exited practice feeling confident in his ability to adjust on the fly and stack strong practices throughout the first two weeks of camp.

 "I just I want to keep getting better for the guys," Williams said. "I want to be faster with my process, to be able to help the O-line throughout you know long games and things like that, they're sitting in their stances, be able to get the communication throughout, you know whether it's on the ball or whether it's in the huddle, just be smoother and faster and everything so that I can be better for the guys and ultimately that helps us win."

 More observations:  

 
 Johnson dropped a major injury bombshell before practice and announced safety Coby Bryant will be out four to six months after undergoing knee surgery. According to that timeline, the Bears would hope for a Bryant return in the playoffs. 
 While the Bears are being cautious with  Luther Burden III 's groin injury and holding him out for the rest of the preseason, Johnson expressed optimism about left tackle Ozzy Trapilo , who is recovering from a ruptured patellar tendon. Months ago, Bears' brass thought they might not have Trapilo at all in 2026. Now, there's a chance, according to Johnson, that he could return at the end of training camp. 
 Safety Cam Lewis returned to practice for stretching and individual drills but went inside during 11-on-11. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson had a solid day and may have thought he came away with an interception (the officials did not call the play dead despite the ball touching the ground) but was not on the field for the final period, as he was replaced by Malik Muhammad . 
 Jedrick Wills Jr . and Kiran Amegadjie both got reps with the first-team offensive line, but it's hard to tell who is separating themselves in the left tackle competition between the two. Braxton Jones remains out after getting injured last Thursday. 
 The Bears practiced a fire-drill field goal, which went wide ride (44 yards). Cairo Santos connected on kicks of 43, 48 and 53 yards during the field goal period. 
 Williams and the starters had another clean practice with no turnovers while the backup units accounted for three turnovers. Linebacker Devin Bush picked off Tyson Bagent , who also threw an interception to Skyler Thomas on the final play of practice. Roschon Johnson was popped inside the 1-yard line by DB Dontae Manning , and linebacker Jon Rhattigan recovered the fumble. 
 

 

 
 Aug. 9 
 Practice No. 10 of training camp -- the Bears' fifth in pads -- moved indoors after a lengthy lightning delay and opened with physical, downhill run drills. D'Andre Swift has looked terrific through the first two weeks and was seemingly everywhere Sunday: in the run game, passing game and taking a direct snap during 11-on-11 reps.

 Swift picked up two big runs as the Bears repped their four-minute offense at the end of a two-hour session.

 Luther Burden III missed practice because of a groin injury and is expected to miss "a little bit of time," according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. In Burden's absence, Jahdae Walker had back-to-back solid practices and hauled in the best catch of the day from Caleb Williams on a busted-coverage deep ball.

 Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen worked in his dime package and emphasized blitzes/different pressures in 11-on-11 reps. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson , who battled through injury during Saturday's practice, picked off Williams' pass on an out route to Rome Odunze .

 In addition to Burden, the Bears were also missing Cam Lewis , Montez Sweat , Braxton Jones , Jaylon Jones , D'Marco Jackson , Terell Smith and Coby Bryant .

 Rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas appeared to injure his knee during 7-on-7 drills. He left practice with a trainer and did not return.

title: 2026 Cincinnati Bengals training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Bengals training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Bengals reporter Ben Baby has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bengals camp. Will Dexter Lawrence II spark a defensive resurgence to get the Bengals back in the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Bears' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Bengals stories 
 
 Joe Burrow, Bengals find camaraderie on unusual battlefield 
 Bengals DE Stewart out multiple weeks with hyperextended knee 
 Bengals' top storylines at training camp 
 

 

 

 Who has been the Bengals' top performer so far at camp? 

 There are a couple of good options, but rookie DE Cashius Howell has been incredibly disruptive. He's done a good job of winning against the back-up offensive linemen and earning reps with the first-team defense. The defensive line has arguably been the strongest unit in training camp, which is exactly what the Bengals hoped for when they addressed the roster this offseason.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Who will win some of the last roster battles? Inside cornerback is the only intriguing question when it comes to starter sports. But swing tackle (OT3) and how the back end of the receiver group shakes out will be things to keep an eye on in the preseason.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Expect to see Cincinnati's stars in the preseason opener on Thursday. QB Joe Burrow , WR Ja'Marr Chase , WR Tee Higgins and DT  Dexter Lawrence II  will see some snaps in the home game against the Lions, coach Zac Taylor said.

 "[Fans will] get a chance to enjoy some of our players there," Taylor said. "But how long I keep them out there remains to be seen."

 Last year, Burrow played in a career-high 21.2% of the team's preseason offseason snaps, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The effectiveness was hard to gauge since Burrow suffered a turf toe injury on Week 2.

 
 After the first 30 minutes of practice, Cincinnati had to shift indoors following a massive storm that rolled in. It looked like a scene out of a tornado movie. 
 The Bengals had just one team period. There were some mixed moments for the offense. But the secondary had another good moment when safety Jordan Battle had an easy interception for a potential TD ball intended for Chase. 
 Rookie center Connor Lew took snaps with the first-team offense as veteran Ted Karras received a bit of a breather. 
 Those who are confirmed out against Detroit: S Bryan Cook , CB Dax Hill , TE Erick All Jr . and Lew. Cook and Hill are battling injuries and will continue to be evaluated next week. 
 DT B.J. Hill (PUP) and DE Shemar Stewart (hyperextended left knee) are making good progress to returning to play, Taylor said. 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Chalk it up to a good day for the offense. The first-team unit had some good moments on a Sunday afternoon that featured two extensive move-the-ball drills. One of them ended with a corner touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Tee Higgins . The running game also had some moments, which is a good sign for an offense looking to find bigger gains on the ground.

 

 
 Bengals safety Bryan Cook and cornerback Dax Hill did not practice. Both have been battling muscle tightness in recent days. The indication on Cook, who suffered his injury in the team's Friday night practice, is that his issue is nothing significant. 
 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Cincinnati wants to find bigger gains in the ground game in 2026. There was a healthy amount of that in the limited portion of practice that was inside Paycor Stadium on Friday night.

 Running back Chase Brown reeled off a long run for a TD, which is a good sign for team that lacked explosive rushing plays last season. The Bengals were tied for 24th in the NFL in gains of 10 or more yards on the ground by running backs, according to ESPN Research.

 More observations: 

 
 The team spent the bulk of the practice at its indoor bubble because of thunderstorms that were in the area. They came back to Paycor Stadium for a few periods for the fans that stayed. 
 Safety Bryan Cook received some treatment from trainers after favoring his left hamstring. He didn't come back out with the first-team defense for its final drive. 
 Others who did not practice today: CB Dax Hill , CB Jalen Davis , DT Jonathan Allen  and WR Tee Higgins . Hill has been limited with muscle tightness the past few days. 
 DT  Dexter Lawrence II  knocked QB Joe Burrow to the ground during team drills inside the stadium. It was a light brush. 
 For a passing offense that has struggled at times in camp, it had a good moment inside the stadium. Burrow connected on a deep throw to WR  Ja'Marr Chase  behind the Cincinnati secondary. 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The offensive tinkering continued on Thursday as the Bengals try to find different ways to put pressure on opposing defenses. Throughout training camp, Cincinnati has had a ton of reps with QB Joe Burrow under center, which is not typically how the Bengals like to operate. But it's clear that finding ways to mix up the offensive formations is a strategy that will be critical to creating a more explosive offense. And offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher is OK with any lumps that are taken during the process.

 "We just wanna have a lot of tools at our disposal," Pitcher said on Thursday. "And that's what we're developing right now."

 
 The offense and defense traded pre-snap victories during an unscripted 11-on-11 drill. First, the defense forced a delay of game. But the offense responded by drawing the defense offsides. 
 Rookie defensive end Cashius Howell continues to turn heads. Howell took reps with the first team and created pressure off the edge. The second-round pick has been one of the camp's biggest stars. 
 Cincinnati appears to be experimenting with its back-up offensive tackles. Cody Ford and Andrew Coker swapped between the left and right sides during second-team reps. Cincinnati is looking to solidify the swing tackle spot behind starters Orlando Brown Jr . and Amarius Mims . 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 The defense continues its strong start to training camp. That was punctuated by a two-play exchange that started with a pass deflection by CB  DJ Turner  on a deep ball intended for WR Ja'Marr Chase , before safety S Bryan Cook had a pick-six off QB Joe Burrow during a team drill. Coordinator Al Golden's group has looked nothing like the team that has struggled in each of the past two seasons.

 "I think as a defense, we have an edge," Golden said. "We gotta continue to have that edge. We haven't done anything."

 
 Bengals CB DJ Ivey took first-team reps with Dax Hill sidelined. Hill was dealing with a bit of tightness and was limited for precautionary reasons. 
 DT Jonathan Allen was not at practice in what appeared to be a vet rest day. Allen also missed a day last week before quickly returning. 
 Cincinnati released S Isaiah Nwokobia on Tuesday. He had not practiced in back-to-back days. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The first day of pads belonged to the Bengals' defense. And in what has become a recurring theme, the defensive line was able to bring some good pressure. Boye Mafe continued to affect the quarterback and rookie Cashius Howell had a clean win off the edge against the second-team defense.

 The defense isn't letting any camp success get to their heads. "We haven't scratched the surface, which is the encouraging thing," said linebacker Barrett Carter . "Our floor right now is high. I'm not trying to jinx us or put expectations on us, but we're…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Browns reporter Daniel Oyefusi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Browns camp. The biggest question for Cleveland remains who will be the starting QB? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Cowboys' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Browns stories 
 
 What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition? 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders 
 GM Andrew Berry 'hopeful' Browns can reunite with Jadeveon Clowney 
 Sources: Browns, Grant Delpit agree to 3-year, $48M extension 
 

 
 
 

 Who has been the Browns' top performer so far at camp? 
 WR Denzel Boston . The No. 39 overall pick is trending to be Cleveland's No. 1 receiver sooner rather than later. Boston has dazzled with plenty of highlights, using his 6-foot-4, 215-pound frame to make contested catches almost daily. He's also made himself a friendly target for quarterbacks as a smooth route runner. Boston recently got promoted to the No. 1 offense as Cleveland's boundary receiver.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Who will be the Browns' starting quarterback? Deshaun Watson will start the preseason opener;  Shedeur Sanders will start the second preseason game. The exhibition matches will allow Todd Monken to evaluate the quarterbacks in a bevy of game-like situations. The first-year head coach is placing an importance on pre-snap operation and playmaking ability.

 
 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Browns are hoping quarterback  Deshaun Watson 's return to health will mean a return to the Pro Bowl form he displayed with the Texans, but Watson said Wednesday that "my game has definitely changed."

 "I'm different, man," Watson said before practice. "I think ever since I've been here early on, bringing up Houston was cool, but I'm 30 now. I had some injuries and things like that. So, my game has definitely changed. But the mentality in how I play and how I approach it doesn't."

 Watson was one of the NFL's top dual-threat passers in Houston, but suspension and injuries have limited him to just 19 games since Cleveland traded for him in March 2022.

 "I think you have to be who you are because if you try to be something you're not, you're not going to play at the highest level of your skill set," coach Todd Monken said. "So it's just the way it is with him; he's going to have to play or utilize his athleticism in order to play at the top of his skill set. ... But one of the superpowers is his athleticism. I mean, that always has been. So you can't take that away or you've basically taken away a part of what made him special."

 More observations: 

 
 In a lighter practice ahead of the team's preseason opener against the Bears, Watson and Shedeur Sanders led successful two-minute drills to cap the session. Both quarterbacks connected on deep passes during their possession. Sanders had a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond , who made a diving catch. Watson lofted a pass to receiver Luke Floriea along the offense's sideline. 
 Teven Jenkins and Tyre Phillips split snaps at right guard with the No. 1 offense. 
 Cornerback Denzel Ward and offensive tackle Izavion Miller returned to practice. Cornerback Tyron Herring left practice with a member of the team's medical staff during individual drills. 
 Fifteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Cedric Tillman (new absence), D'Angelo Ross , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall, Parker Brailsford , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Elgton Jenkins , Dae'Quan Wright , Jack Stoll , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis . Veteran edge rusher Tyus Bowser had a tryout with the Browns on Wednesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Four days before their preseason opener against the Chicago Bears on Saturday, the Browns listed " Deshaun Watson  OR Shedeur Sanders " at starting quarterback in their first unofficial depth chart.

 Coach Todd Monken has yet to announce which quarterback will start in Chicago, but spoke about the value the preseason adds for evaluating the two passers.

 "It does, in terms of getting the ball out, got to learn to get the ball out. Got to learn how to slide," Monken said. "You're not going to be able to just run around. I do want playmaking ability, so there is a balance there between playmaking ability and taking some sacks. You're going to have to live with that to an extent.

 "The other part is stacking plays, where it matters, because they got the scoreboard on in terms of points you put on the board. In terms of the flow of the game, that's a big part of it. We're going to be on the road. The ebbs and flows of positive plays and negative plays, overcoming that. I think there's a part of the quarterback's body language, how they are around the team. Do I sense, 'Hey, that's over. I've moved on to the next play.' So there's a number of things you get to evaluate once you get to the closest we have in terms of games, which is preseason."

 With rookie Spencer Fano securing a starting role at left tackle, Monken said the only starting position on the offensive line up in the air is right guard. Teven Jenkins and KT Leveston have been rotating at the spot.

 "I think Teven has the advantage there from experience," Monken said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Special teams coordinator Byron Storer said the team is "definitely taking a hard look at" punters Wes Pahl and Nik Constantinou , but "It's Corey [Bojorquez]'s job to lose." 
 Monken said he is "hopeful" that defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr . will return to practice "soon." Hall hasn't practiced since Aug. 3. 
 On the second-team offensive line, the Browns moved Dawand Jones from left tackle to right tackle and rookie Austin Barber from right tackle to left tackle. 
 Cornerback Damarri Mathis left practice on the back of a cart after he sustained an injury in coverage during a 1-on-1 drill. The team later placed Mathis on injured reserve. 
 Defensive tackle Travis Bell left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. 
 Fifteen players did not practice Tuesday: Joe Royer ,  D'Angelo Ross , Denzel Ward (new absence), Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger ,  Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Jack Stoll , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . 
 The Browns claimed tight end Dae'Quan Wright off waivers from the Eagles, per the NFL transaction wire. 
 The Browns had three tight ends in for a tryout today, per the NFL transaction wire: Sal Cannella , Matt Lauter and  Jermaine Terry II . 
 

 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Coach Todd Monken explained the change in the quarterback rotation last Saturday.

 Though Monken said before the practice that Shedeur Sanders would get a "majority" of first-team reps, he said he was later informed that Sanders had received more padded practices with the starters than Watson in the week. So Monken changed the order of reps.

 Sanders practiced with the starting offense Monday, while Watson led the No. 2 offense.

 "As long as we're still sharing reps, it's a competition," Monken said.

title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Cowboys training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Cowboys' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Sources: Cowboys, Quinnen Williams reach 3-year, $105.9M deal 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Who is the Cowboys' top performer so far at camp? 

 George Pickens . He has essentially made a big play in every practice as he gets set to play on the $27.3 million franchise tag. Whatever disenchantment some may have felt Pickens would have without the long-term deal has been unfounded. Coaches have noted his attention in the meeting rooms since the start of training camp.

 He and Dak Prescott have picked up where they left off in 2025 when he had career highs in catches, yards and touchdowns. Does that mean he will surpass those figures again in 2026? Not necessarily, but his performance so far has shown a focused player as the season inches closer.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Since the Cowboys aren't going to play their starters in the preseason, it's not possible to completely answer anything about the defense. There have been encouraging signs there, but let's look to the offense for what can be answered in the preseason games: Who will back up Prescott?

 Joe Milton III and Sam Howell have alternated as Prescott's backup in practice and both have had good moments and not-so-good moments. The Cowboys believe they have line play and skill players to give both QBs a fair shot to perform in the preseason and not have them running for their lives.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 Over the years in training camp in Oxnard, the Cowboys have been accustomed to welcoming stars of all kinds to training camp. Magic Johnson stopped by. Denzel Washington, Jamie Foxx and Kevin Costner watched a couple of practices too.

 On Thursday, it was Dustin Hoffman's turn. Owner and general manager Jerry Jones referenced "The Graduate" when asked what his favorite Hoffman movie is. That and Marathon Man, "when they pulled his teeth."

 "He's a great guy. He's really a great guy. And why wouldn't he be?" Jones said. "But we sure enjoyed his interest on us out here."

 Hoffman admitted he did not know anything about football but liked what he saw.

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Dak Prescott struggled some Thursday, completing 11 of 24 passes in team drills. He was intercepted once when Markquese Bell took away a deep ball to the post. He had passes knocked down by Dee Winters , Cobie Durant , Caleb Downs and Shavon Revel Jr . There was even a botched snap on the exchange with Cooper Beebe . 
 Winters has come on lately with noticeable work in the past three practices. He was strong against the run in the joint practice versus the Rams on Tuesday and was able to stay within distance of CeeDee Lamb on an over route to take away Prescott's path for the throw. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 It was not a perfect performance for the Cowboys defense against the Los Angeles Rams Tuesday, but it was a lot better than the work against the Rams in last year's joint practices.

 "It's just showing what we've been building on from the spring up until now," linebacker DeMarvion Overshown said. "It was good to hit a different color jersey. I feel like we've been going at it with our offense. They're one of the best in the league so getting to see what we got against another top offense, it puts stuff in perspective. Just another block that we're building on."

 On the first series of team drills,  Shavon Revel Jr . was able to close on a deep ball from Matthew Stafford to  Puka Nacua  and break up the play. Later, DaRon Bland was able to bat away a fade to Davante Adams .

 The Rams' run game was able to get a couple of good runs, but nothing out of the ordinary.

 "We just looked at it as another opportunity to get better. We know [Stafford] is one of the best in the business, then their receiver corps, the running backs and O-line, so we know it wasn't going to be no just easy come in, handle our work and get back on the bus and not break a sweat," Overshown said. "We got some good work in, but I feel like it was good for them to see what we got on our side of the ball as well. I know it's completely different than when they came to Oxnard last year and damn near had a field day."

 More observations: 

 
 The player of the day without question was linebacker Justin Barron . He intercepted three passes, including one on the final play of the two-minute drive off of  Stetson Bennett IV . Barron also had a few stops in the run game. 
 Fresh off agreeing to a three-year, $105.9 million extension, Quinnen Williams was stout in the middle of the defense. On the first set of team drills against the Rams, Williams stopped the running back cold and flexed his right biceps in celebration. He had a couple of tackles for loss. 
 After a slow start, the Cowboys run game was better in the second portion of drills. Tyler Smith had a block to open up a Javonte Williams run. After a fumble, Jaydon Blue was able to get a positive gain on a wide run. 
 Rams OLB Byron Young gave the Cowboys' pass protection some fits early on, getting to the edge on right tackle Terence Steele , which would have negated a completion to George Pickens . 
 The Rams' biggest completion for the first teamers may have been to tight end Terrance Ferguson , who was able to sneak down the sideline against outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku . Stafford gently laid the pass over the top for Ferguson to run under. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Coach Brian Schottenheimer already announced that the starters won't play in the preseason, so the joint practices against the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints will take on added importance over the next two weeks.

 The Cowboys practice against the Rams on Tuesday -- could it be the first of three meetings? The Cowboys play the Rams at SoFi Stadium in the regular season. Could there be a playoff rematch? It has crossed quarterback  Dak Prescott 's mind.

 "It's all you can ask for," Prescott said. "... This is a team that we're going to play in the season, and it's probably a team that if we want to get to where we want to get to, we're going to have to see them again. So call this probably one of the first of three meetings, I'd assume, if everybody takes care of business.

 "So it's definitely going to be a test. It's going to be fun. It's going to be two great teams competing against each other. And at the end of the day, it's practice. We'll have a lot of time after that to clean it up and to say, 'This is what we got to get better,' but we can't go out here and also have a hell of a practice and think we've done something."

 Last year, the Rams' offense toyed with the Cowboys' defense. The Cowboys' offense had some good moments, but now will have to contend with pass rusher Myles Garrett , which will test tackles Tyler Guyton and Terence Steele .

title: 2026 Denver Broncos training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Broncos training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Denver Broncos camp is taking place in Englewood, Colorado, and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Broncos camp. We will update this file often as we track the Broncos' push toward getting to the Super Bowl after falling one game short last season. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Broncos opting to sit QB Bo Nix for preseason opener 
 Why 2026 is a crucial season for Nix and the Broncos 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 

 

 

 Who has been the Broncos' top performer at camp so far? 

 It is a close race between two receivers, second-year man Pat Bryant and Marvin Mims Jr ., with Bryant getting the nod in part due to Mims being slowed recently by a leg injury suffered last Friday.

 Mims started camp with a flourish, creating impact plays until he was limited by a soft-tissue injury that knocked him out of practice for a couple days. Bryant swooped in to be the big-play creator in Mims' absence. Bryant continues to ascend with precise routes and a seemingly fanatical desire to win the ball in the air every time. And on a team where most of the depth chart is settled, his efforts have been the most noteworthy.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 The Broncos suddenly have an issue at center, as starter Luke Wattenberg and backup Alex Forsyth have missed significant practice time with injuries while the No. 3 center -- Michael Deiter -- suffered a season-ending thigh injury this past week. It has put Calvin Throckmorton , who has gotten far more work at guard in his time with Denver, as the starting center, with undrafted rookie Gavin Ortega backing him up. Until either Wattenberg or Forsyth return to practice, center is a spot that could significantly impact how effective the Broncos are upfront.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 Since Bo Nix will not play in Friday's preseason opener in Atlanta, there will be a chance for Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger to continue what has been one of the most spirited position battles of camp. On a team that returns 20 of 22 starters on offense and defense from the AFC Championship Game and returns most of the backups, too, Stidham and Ehlinger have had a heated battle to be the No. 2 quarterback. And Friday might be their best chance to show what they can do given Nix is expected to play some snaps in the Broncos' two other preseason games.

 Coach Sean Payton said after Wednesday's practice that each of the quarterbacks will play a half against the Falcons. Stidham is expected to start the game and play the first half.

 "They're focused on like their best stuff, they're competing against the 31 other quarterbacks (in the league) like any other position," Payton said. "... It's a great room, they get along well."

 Ehlinger, who led the team with 412 yards passing last preseason, has been consistently lauded by Payton for his work in camp and has routinely moved the second- and third-team offenses in practices. Stidham led the quarterbacks in touchdown passes last preseason, with four in three games.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton expects most of the healthy starters to get about 15 plays against the Falcons and said some of the injured players will remain back in Denver to continue to rehab their injuries. Wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr ., who are both working back from leg injuries in camp, are expected to be among the group that remains in Denver. 
 When asked why he, unlike many other coaches, will likely have several starters play in all three preseason games, Payton said: "[You're] trying to win everything, I just believe in that." 
 Veteran center Michael Deiter , who was carted off the field during Tuesday's practice, will miss the remainder of the season with a thigh injury that will require surgery. "[I] feel bad for him and where he's at," Payton said. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Broncos owner/CEO Greg Penner, who had not spoken publicly since the league meetings in March, covered a variety of topics with local media on Tuesday. At one point he was asked about his expectations for the season, and he made it clear a team that returns all but two starters from the AFC Championship Game has the same expectations from him as the next year's team and the ones that come after that.

 "Our goal is to compete for championships every year and if we put ourselves in that position every year, we're going to be successful and win Super Bowls," he said.

 He also talked about the new five-year deal for coach Sean Payton that Payton signed in June, saying: "I've been really pleased with what he's built here, the culture, the performance on the field (and) it enabled us to line up he and [general manager] George [Paton's] contracts now. George has done a fantastic job building this roster."

 More observations: 

 
 Center is suddenly a trouble spot, as injuries continue to happen at the position. The Broncos' top two centers -- Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth -- have missed time in camp and on Tuesday Michael Deiter -- who was signed for depth in the offseason after spending seven seasons in Miami, Houston and Washington -- was carted to the locker room. Calvin Throckmorton slid in as the first-team center, with undrafted rookie free agent Gavin Ortega providing depth. All-Pro guard Quinn Meinerz played some center early in his NFL career and could shift over if needed, but moving one of the NFL's best guards to another position is not ideal. 
 Sam Ehlinger continues to flash in his quest for the No. 2 quarterback job. He has consistently moved the offense in team drills during camp, and his throw to undrafted rookie wide receiver Kolbe Katsis for a touchdown in situational red zone work with the third-team offense was one of the best plays of the day. 
 Running back J.K. Dobbins , who left Monday's practice with what Sean Payton referred to as a soft tissue injury, returned to practice Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 A recent spate of what Sean Payton called "soft-tissue" injuries prompted the coach to adjust the end of practice. After the two-and-half-hour workout, Payton had the strength and conditioning staff add a longer, more formal warm-down period. Payton said he expected to continue to have the players go through the longer warm down in the days ahead.

 

 "Got to get a handle on some of the soft-tissue stuff. ... Strains, hamstring or groins, [we] continue to fight through that," Payton said. "I don't think it's heat related. ... You always try to look at your pre-practice routine, your hydration obviously."

 Running back J.K. Dobbins left the practice field with an injury and did not return. Wide receivers Marvin Mims Jr . -- who returned to practice Monday -- and Jaylen Waddle have also had similar injuries in recent weeks.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton said he will play most, if not all, of the healthy starters for at least some snaps in Friday's preseason opener in Atlanta. Payton said the coaches hadn't yet formalized the snap counts yet, but that he wanted regulars to get at least some work. "You have to build callouses," he said.

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.
