 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Lions camp 
 
 QB Teddy Bridgewater on retirement: 'This time it's official' 
 Lions OL Mays out into season; RB Pacheco hurts knee 
 Lions make Jahmyr Gibbs highest-paid running back in NFL history 
 
 

 Who has been the Lions' top performer so far at camp? 
 Jameson Williams . This offseason, the Lions receiver emphasized working on his catching ability and was able to make some big plays throughout training camp. Veteran QB Jared Goff has appreciated his development from year to year as they were able to connect on several deep balls during team periods this summer and Williams seems primed for a big season.

 "He just continues to get better," Goff said of Williams on Aug. 10. "And the stuff that he's doing now that's nuanced, that you can't really teach, you can feel coverage and he can change his stem of his route, that little stuff has been so cool to see him start to adopt that and understand coverage and understand space. And that's the next level for him and he's done a great job of it."

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Who will begin the season as Detroit's starting center? Former Panthers center Cade Mays was targeted this offseason as an unrestricted free agent to help the unit after the Lions' offensive line struggled in 2025. However, Detroit suffered a significant blow when Mays experienced a wrist injury during training camp, which is expected to sideline him for 8-10 weeks. Without Mays, the Lions are expected to experiment with Juice Scruggs , Seth McLaughlin and Michael Niese at center as they attempt to find the best fit at the position before the season opener against New Orleans on Sept. 13, but this could potentially be a major problem if they're not able to get it right.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph is currently away from the team while dealing with a personal issue.

 But his rehab process for his knee injury is coming along "very well," according to head coach Dan Campbell.

 It's still unlikely that Joseph will be back ahead of Week 1, but the Lions envision him returning around the same time as Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch , who is also coming off a season-ending Achilles injury in 2025, for practices in late training camp or possibly early September.

 "And Branch is doing well, too," Campbell said ahead of Tuesday's practice. "So, those guys, we're talking about on down the road, the season's already begun. But I like where Kerby's at."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Newly signed Lions QB Joshua Dobbs participated in his first full practice after being signed on Monday. Dobbs has begun his second stint with the Lions. He was previously on Detroit's practice squad in 2022 and felt comfortable returning to the team's facility. "It felt really good. A lot of familiar faces. Some change but not much so I've really enjoyed that," Dobbs said following Tuesday's practice. "Just being able to kind of at least know where everything is, as you get your feet under you to get ready to practice." 
 The Lions will be sporting their new Rivalries uniforms against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 on Nov. 1. 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Veteran OL Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury that is expected to sideline him for 8-10 weeks. In his absence,  Seth McLaughlin took first-team reps at center, where he battled against former Ohio State teammate Tyleik Williams and DT Alim McNeill  during Monday's practice. OL Michael Niese took the bulk of the second team reps at center as Detroit tries to identify the best starting unit ahead of the regular season.

 "I'm taking it one practice at a time, getting better," McLaughlin said. "With practice, it's (Day) 11 at camp and you're not who you wanna be on the first day of the regular season so there's a long way to go to keep getting better."

 Prior to Monday's practice, Lions QB Jared Goff didn't have many reps with McLaughlin, but has been impressed with him so far as he continues to adjust to the role. Throughout OTAs and the offseason, Goff mainly worked with Mays and veteran OL  Juice Scruggs , who is also expected to be in the mix for the starting role once he returns from a soft tissue injury that has kept him out.

 "He did a good job. He really did," Goff said of McLaughlin. "He stepped in there. He had good authority with his calls. He was sharp. He was decisive. I think that's all you can ask for."

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff , and most of the starters, will not play in the preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals this week but could see some action against Washington on Aug. 22, according to head coach Dan Campbell. Undrafted rookie QB Lions  Luke Altmyer will now continue in the QB2 role behind Goff and is expected to take heavy snaps on Thursday, but Detroit will likely be adding another veteran QB for depth purposes as early as this week after Teddy Bridgewater decided to step away from the team. Altmyer says he's "excited" for the opportunity ahead.

 "I've played at a high level with the Big Ten and I've played in football games but it's a different level and I think that's the challenge is can you maintain emotions because it can get you really high and really excited," Altmyer said after Sunday's practice. "But, trusting my abilities, trusting my preparation, trusting my teammates. I think that's the word trust."

 Other observations:  

 
 Lions veteran QB Teddy Bridgewater has decided to step away from the team amid training camp and was officially placed on the reserved/retired list ahead of Sunday's practice. Campbell says he will be "missed" but this retirement could be for good. 
 Lions HC Dan Campbell and his wife Holly attended the Pro Football Hall of Fame induction ceremony in Canton to support legendary New Orleans Saints QB Drew Brees on Saturday on an off day. Campbell was an assistant/tight ends coach in New Orleans from 2016-20 and signed with the Saints as a player in 2009. "It was a reminder. It was refreshing just to be able to stand in the presence of greatness with those guys," Campbell said. 
 The Lions signed CB Ryan Cooper and LB Amen Ogbongbemiga and waived TE Nick Muse . 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 The connection between Jared Goff and  Amon-Ra St. Brown  was on display as St. Brown scored a touchdown in Friday's scrimmage off a slant at the goal line through tight coverage. St. Brown had a two-point conversion while also converting multiple fourth downs on a monster day in which his playmaking was consistently on display. WRs coach Scottie Montgomery credits Goff and St. Brown's friendship as the driving force of their on-field chemistry.

 "These guys, their timing is correct, but their off-the-field relationship also gives us an opportunity that a lot of people don't have," Montgomery said. "The communication between the two of them is probably what makes them as consistent as they are. There's certain things and there's nonverbal communication that happened between them now because of where we are in the offense, where they are in their relationship away from the building."

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Packers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 Aaron Rodgers wishes game at Lambeau, discusses retirement return 
 Packers QB Love expected to play in first preseason game 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Who is the Packers' top performer so far at camp? 

 Not that Xavier McKinney didn't play well last season -- he was second-team All-Pro after all -- but so far this looks more like the version of McKinney from 2024, when he was first-team All-Pro and had a career-best eight interceptions. McKinney looks like the perfect fit in new coordinator Jonathan Gannon's system, moving all over the field and finding himself in the middle of more action. Between McKinney, Evan Williams and Javon Bullard , the Packers could have one of the best safety trios in the league.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 When will the offensive line jell? One underrated thing that ruined last season was inconsistent offensive line play. Given that the starters won't play much in the preseason games, it's worth wondering when that group will finally come together.

 While there has been some shifting of personnel, most notably new left tackle Jordan Morgan , the preferred group of five has yet to get any 11-on-11 snaps together. Left guard Aaron Banks (knee) has been limited to individual drills in practice, and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele has slowly integrated back into practice. There's also competition at guard with Jacob Monk , Anthony Belton and rookie Jager Burton . Monk may have usurped Belton for the right guard spot, while Jager has looked solid at left guard in place of Banks.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Three weeks and 11 practices into training camp, and something's missing: fighting.

 
There hasn't even been so much as a scuffle or shoving match.

 
This is training camp No. 7 for veteran safety Xavier McKinney and when asked if this is the deepest into training camp he has ever gone without seeing a fight, McKinney didn't hesitate.

 
"Hell yeah," he said. "For sure."

 
But McKinney doesn't think that's a bad thing. Nor is it a sign that the players are not competitive enough.

 
"I think we're past that, to be honest," McKinney said. "I think we have a bigger goal, and that bigger goal is to get over this hump that we've been kind of dealing with these last couple years. We're not focused on fighting. Nobody's trying to get kicked out of practice. Nobody's trying to have practice stop early. We're just trying to focus on our technique. We're trying to find ways where we can improve as individuals. We want to be the best group that we can possibly be. We want to be better than what we were last year."

 
The Packers also haven't had a joint practice yet. So even McKinney said all bets are off when the Cardinals come to town for a practice Aug. 26.

 
"That always happens," McKinney said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Just when it looked like the injury list would keep getting longer, a few key players returned to practice. Receivers Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle) were back after missing two practices. So was tight end Josh Whyle (neck). All took part in team (11-on-11) periods. Cornerback Carrington Valentine , who dropped out of practice Aug. 2 because of a hamstring injury, returned for individual drills only. The only new addition to the DNP list was rookie edge Dani Dennis-Sutton , but it was because of an illness. 
 The Packers had a pair of new defensive backs on the field after signing Trey Dean III and Travion Fluellen . They both worked with the safeties during individual drills. Safety Javon Bullard (foot) remained out. 
 After taking reps with both the second- and third-string defenses Monday, Keisean Nixon was back at his regular left cornerback spot with the No. 1 defense. In fact, he worked exclusively with that group and appeared to be on the field for every snap that the starters took. Brandon Cisse continued to work as the No. 1 right cornerback. 
 Trey Smack went 4-for-5 during a field goal period. His miss was wide right on a 45-yarder. He hit the right upright on a 41-yarder but it still went through. He's now 20-for-28 (71.4%) during camp. 
 A day after the NFL said it will allow head coaches to designate a member of their sideline staff to initiate replay challenges , coach Matt LaFleur said he doesn't plan to pass off the red challenge flag. "I probably should give it up based on past actions," LaFleur joked. "So no, I'll probably hold the challenge flag." 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 It was the kind of practice that would have excited a young, backup quarterback.

 But what about a 37-year-old going into his 16th NFL season?

 
"Oh yeah, the game still excites me," Tyrod Taylor said.

 
In what was perhaps Taylor's best practice since he signed with the Packers this offseason, he completed passes of all varieties. There was a deep post to Kisean Johnson . A quick-hitting slant to Will Sheppard for a first down. A 20-yarder to Sheppard down the left sideline. A big gain over the middle to J. Michael Sturdivant .

 
It didn't matter to Taylor that it was all with backup receivers -- many of whom might not make the team.

 
"There's a healthy rotation of guys that's going in and out with the group that I'm running with, and it's just up to me to communicate, get them in the right position but also give them a chance to make plays," Taylor said. "We've got a ton of playmakers at our skill positions."

 
The Packers had one of the best backup quarterbacks in the NFL last season with Malik Willis , who signed with the Dolphins as a free agent. Now, they have one of the most experienced.

 "I'm a firm believer that your actions speak louder than your words, especially early on," said Taylor, who has played in 100 career games (with 62 starts) for seven teams. "It's about me coming in, being myself, preparing on the field, off the field, being ready for the opportunities and taking advantage of them as well, and then gradually growing into more of a vocal leader and speaking on things when they fit."

 Other observations: 

 
 As if it weren't unusual enough to see cornerback Keisean Nixon with the second-string defense Sunday, it was even more surprising to see him taking snaps with the third-stringers Monday. In the very next period, he was back with the No. 1 defense, but it's a baffling way to handle a player who last season was considered the team's No. 1 cornerback. When Nixon wasn't with the starters, Benjamin St-Juste was in his spot along with rookie Brandon Cisse on the other side. Could it be a sign the Packers are thinking about demoting Nixon? "There's always competition," coach Matt LaFleur said. "All these guys got to be prepared for that. As far as the substitution, that's not something that I'm always micromanaging. A lot of that's on the position coach."

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Texans reporter D.J. Bien-Aime has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Texans camp 
 
 Tank Dell returns to practice for first time since 2024 
 Houston bringing back former No. 1 pick Clowney 
 Texans have 'productive' contract talks with Stroud 
 

 

 

 Who has been the Texans' top performer so far at camp? 

 Cornerback Collin Wright is an undrafted rookie but has made noticeable plays throughout camp. His biggest highlight came when he intercepted quarterback C.J. Stroud during team drills a couple of days before Houston's first preseason game.

 Wright has had reps with the first team, so he's gearing up to make the team through unlikely odds.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How does center Keylan Rutledge look against other competition? He's brought a toughness by mixing it up with Houston's star defensive linemen  Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter . That attitude has been missed in recent years, so let's see how that translates to a game.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Coach DeMeco Ryans called Tuesday's indoor practice "outstanding," after characterizing Monday's practice as subpar. You would have never thought there's a Thursday preseason game against the Chargers looming as the physicality was intense. There were several plays with players driven to the ground or tackled.

 There was even a dust-up between center Keylan Rutledge and All-Pro defensive end  Will Anderson Jr . that exceeded the typical millisecond hand locking of helmets. Anderson and Rutledge engaged in shoving even through their teammates' attempts at separation.

 The defense forced turnovers, highlighted by linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair intercepting quarterback  C.J. Stroud 's tipped pass. But Stroud also connected for a 80-yard touchdown to running back David Montgomery down the sideline.

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 For the Texans' first preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers  on Thursday, coach DeMeco Ryans said, "We'll have a select group of guys who will not go out there and play."

 So don't expect the key starters to play much. Anticipate seeing only rookie starters, such as center Keylan Rutledge , and a few second-year players, such as wideout Jayden Higgins  and left tackle Aireontae Ersery .

 The preseason opener will be about early impressions from younger players and seeing where they are with depth. It'll be about seeing the guys they'll have to make decisions on to fill out the back end of the roster with limited spots among the starters being unsettled.

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 The Texans held a night practice on Saturday. It was not pretty for the Texans offense as quarterback C.J. Stroud had many incompletions and the run game had little running room.

 However, the defense displayed the potential of a top-three unit in the NFL. There were plenty of sacks, an interception from Pro Bowl safety  Calen Bullock  and pass break ups. But most importantly, they're not satisfied. Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke's assessment of the defense was "okay."

 Burke said Houston is chasing perfection defensively.

 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 

 After an off day, the Texans dialed back their intensity as they went through drills without pads, but notably, wide receiver  Tank Dell practiced for the second straight day of training camp, albeit in a limited capacity.

 It's another step in Dell's recovery, with Wednesday being his first time practicing since he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in Week 16 of 2024.

 Speaking to the media for the first time, Dell said he had no fear in the strength of his knee, pointing towards Houston's doctor stating his knee is "100 percent stable." 

 "Trusting the work you put in prior to going out there," said Dell when asked about trusting in his health. "Going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the training staff and what they had set out for me. So when I got out here, I wasn't scared."﻿

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Wideout Tank Dell made his return to the practice field, participating in limited capacity. It marked the first time he engaged in any sort of team padded practice since Week 16 of 2024 after the 2023 third-round pick suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Chiefs.

 He caught a few passes from quarterback C.J. Stroud during individual drills and ran full speed routes.

 Dell didn't do much more after that, but this is the step in the right direction. Coach DeMeco Ryans won't rush Dell back and said "Tank is on the right plan." The goal is have him ready for team 11-on-11 contact reps. He still has a ways to go, but this is positive progress.

 Other observation:  

 Wideout Jayden Higgins continue to flash throughout practice. He made another impressive catch with Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. It was a tightly contested catch but that's always a positive because it's against an All-Pro corner.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Texans wideout Jayden Higgins is starting to blossom as he's entering Year 2. When Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins  was asked about Higgins' progression he said "He's hooping right now, and I can't wait to see him rock out when it really matters."

 During Tuesday's practice, Higgins made multiple catches with All-Pro cornerback  Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. One of those receptions occurred during a team third-down period for a 20-yard gain. The other one was during 1-on-1s -- where Stingley tried to aggressively jam Higgins, but he avoided the powerful jab and broke free for an easy toss from quarterback C.J. Stroud .

 Early in camp, Stroud said he expected Higgins to have a "dominant" Year 2, and so far we are starting to see it.

 Other observation:  

 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was slow to get up after a collision with tight end Dalton Schultz . Al-Shaair was fine shortly after.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 This was Day 1 of padded practices, and the defense shined. Quarterback C.J. Stroud  was forced to hold the ball longer than he would like as the secondary coverage was stout.

 Stroud occasionally scrambled more than usual to buy time to make throws and the defensive line forced a few sacks. Safety Calen Bullock intercepted Stroud.

 Also coach DeMeco Ryans used exotic blitzes throughout the day, and the offense sometimes had answers and other times didn't. Ryans deemed the first day in full pads as "successful." 

 Other observation: 

 First-round pick Keylan Rutledge is adding an extra juice of aggression to the unit. He got into a mini tussle with defensive end Danielle Hunter after a successful run play by running back Woody Marks .

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Saturday's padless practice featured more back and forth from the offense and defense. Some periods the defense dominated and others, the offense was able to counter their blitzing.

 The Texans start padded practices on Monday and that will be a "big part" of the evaluation process for the team according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

 The fourth-year head coach said: "There's a lot of all-stars in shorts," and later added the staff wouldn't be fooled by what players have done without pads.

 Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr collided with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and was slow to get up, but he shook it off and was back on the field.

title: 2026 Indianapolis Colts training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Colts training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Colts reporter Stephen Holder has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Colts camp. Will quarterback  Daniel Jones return to early-2025 form after a serious injury? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Colts' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Colts stories 
 
 Tons at stake as Colts' Daniel Jones enters proving ground 
 Colts won't give Richardson away 
 Colts extend Jonathan Taylor for 2 years, $44 million 
 
 

 

 Who has been the Colts' top performer at camp so far? 
 There are strong cases to be made for players like Josh Downs , Sauce Gardner and Tyler Warren . But given the context, what quarterback Daniel Jones displayed during camp was thoroughly impressive. After spending his offseason recovering from an Achilles tear sustained in December, Jones proved he is ready for the season by performing well on a consistent basis. His ability to drop back from under center, throw on the run and scramble with elusiveness likely put any doubts the Colts had to rest. Jones is unlikely to play in the preseason, but he will be full go for Week 1.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 The situation at linebacker remains a concern. The Colts don't appear to have clear, established regulars at the position and will consider using something of a rotation according to defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo. Rookie middle linebacker CJ Allen is perhaps the most likely candidate to play every down, but his training camp has already been interrupted by two different injuries. Only free agent addition Akeem Davis-Gaither has full-time starting experience, with rookie Bryce Boettcher , Austin Ajiake and Jaylon Carlies in the mix as well. Can anyone in this unit establish themselves during the remaining practices and preseason games? Or will the coaches have to cycle through players based on game situations and opponents?

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Coach Shane Steichen previewed some of his plans for Thursday's preseason opener following the Colts' joint practice with the New England Patriots on Tuesday.

 Quarterback Daniel Jones won't play against the Patriots, but backup Anthony Richardson Sr . will start and play the entirety of the first half, according to Steichen. He will give way to Riley Leonard , with whom he's competing for the No. 2 quarterback role, in the second half. Next week, during their home game against the Atlanta Falcons , the roles will be reversed, Steichen said. Leonard will start against Atlanta and Richardson will relieve him.

 Jones, who is coming off a torn Achilles tendon but appears fully recovered, won't play at all in the preseason.

 "I don't want to take any chances with Daniel out there in the preseason right now," Steichen said.

 More observations:  

 
 Steichen was particularly complimentary about his starting offense's performance in a two-minute situation against the Patriots on Tuesday. In a mock scenario where the Colts trailed by seven, Jones led them to a score with a touchdown pass to receiver Josh Downs . "I was really pleased," Steichen said.

 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 One year after being in contention to be the Colts' starting quarterback, Anthony Richardson Sr . now finds himself in a fight for the Colts' No. 2 quarterback spot behind Daniel Jones .

 
Sunday was another day of evaluation for the Colts, with Richardson displaying some ups and downs throughout the workout before finishing with an impressive 2-minute drill that led to a touchdown. Meanwhile, Riley Leonard , his competition, has had a strong couple of days after battling his own inconsistency.

 
Richardson requested a trade in February and was granted permission to speak with other clubs to see if a deal might materialize. Nothing did, so Richardson is back trying to re-establish himself with the organization. Richardson on Sunday said his accuracy needs to be more consistent.

 
"I feel like I can improve a lot of things," Richardson said. "My decision making, I feel like I'm on point with the ball and I feel like I'm [throwing] to the right spot. Sometimes I don't throw the best ball, but I feel like my decision making is pretty good so far."

 
Richardson and Leonard will split preseason snaps.

 Other observations:

 
 Receiver Josh Downs (groin) could potentially return to the lineup in Tuesday's joint practice at New England, coach Shane Steichen said. 
 Jones had his second and third interceptions of camp on Sunday, but both came on passes that appeared catchable. Receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhine saw one pass go off his fingertips to safety A.J. Haulcy . Later, running back Jonathan Taylor had a pass go through his hands, landing squarely in the hands of safety Cam Bynum . 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Colts are still working to identify their best lineup at linebacker, and it's beginning to look like they might not have the luxury of settling in with a consistent starting group.

 Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo left open the possibility that the Colts might use a rotation of players at the position, with situations dictating who plays when. The issues are being currently exacerbated by the absence of projected starting middle linebacker CJ Allen (hamstring), the team's second-round pick.

 "At the end of the day, I think we're going to have a lot of guys in that room that play for us this year in different types of roles," Anarumo said.

 Having two rookies -- Allen and Bryce Boettcher -- among the leading candidates to start, is a factor, Anarumo said. Streamlining young players' responsibilities can allow for faster growth.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Receiver Josh Downs missed practice with a groin injury, leaving the Colts without their top two wideouts. Alec Pierce remains sidelined after offseason ankle surgery, and the Colts have provided no specific timeline for his return. 
 Riley Leonard was the second-team quarterback behind Daniel Jones , with Anthony Richardson Sr . playing with the third team. 
 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Starting quarterback Daniel Jones had one of his best days in Thursday's evening practice, connecting on a number of aggressive, downfield throws. But the same could not be said of the quarterbacks behind him on the depth chart.

 Anthony Richardson Sr . and Riley Leonard , locked in a battle for the backup job, have yet to establish the consistency that coach Shane Steichen is seeking. That continued on Thursday, when Leonard threw an interception to linebacker Austin Ajiake and Richardson was inefficient in his time under center.

 "The guy that's most consistent is going to win that job," Steichen said. "Those guys are battling. It's back and forth right now." He added, "There's been flashes, but yeah, there's work to done for sure."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 One week into camp and perhaps the biggest question is not a question at all.

 Quarterback Daniel Jones has not missed a single snap with the first-team offense and has not taken any days off from practice. This comes in spite of him only recently being fully cleared to practice in full-team drills following his Achilles tendon tear in December. If there were any uncertainties entering this camp, Jones has put them to rest.

 "I've felt good through the whole camp so far," Jones said. "I knew I would. You try to push yourself in the rehab in preparation for camp, knowing what to expect. I felt really good and I stay on the recovery part of it to make sure I'm available and out here every…

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jaguars' camp 
 
 Jaguars' Travis Hunter feeling faster after 10-pound weight gain 
 
 

 Who has been the top performer so far at camp? 
 WR Parker Washington has been QB Trevor Lawrence 's favorite target, and he always seems to be open.

 While the first-team offense has mainly faced the second-team defense in 11-on-11 work, Washington also has thrived in one-on-ones against the Jaguars' top corners. The last time the Jaguars matched the first-team offense against the first-team defense, Washington beat CB Travis Hunter at the line of scrimmage and caught a deep pass down the sideline for a touchdown. Washington, who had three 100-yard games in the final four games (including playoffs) last season, has established himself as the Jaguars' WR1.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Can the offensive line survive a rash of injuries? Starting RT Cole Van Lanen (knee) is still on PUP, starting RG Patrick Mekari (back) has been limited in team work, and key reserve Walker Little (ankle) -- who can start at either tackle and guard spot -- is expected to miss at least another week. The replacements -- notably Chuma Edoga , Jonah Monheim , and Wyatt Milum -- have been up and down, which is to be expected because they're facing the top defensive front.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Jaguars coach Liam Coen is the offensive playcaller so he naturally wants to see that side of the ball have success in practice. When it doesn't -- which happened on Tuesday -- he's still learning not to get mad.

 The offensive line is dealing with injuries to five players -- including three likely starters -- and as a result struggled to run the ball in 11-on-11 work against what was the top rush defensive in the NFL last season.

 "I thought the defense came out with more energy and better mindset and mentality," Coen said. "Some of the pass game stuff was good, but they kind of took the fight to us for the run game today. We're the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, so it's not going to always be perfect. You're expecting the defense to do some good things, even though it pisses me off at times."

 Tackle Cole Van Lanen (PUP), tackle/guard Walker Little , right guard Patrick Mekari , left guard Ezra Cleveland , and backup left guard Emmanuel Pregnon either did not practice at all or participated only in individual drills. Because the run game struggled so much, Coen decided to cut the practice short. They'll have a light walkthrough on Wednesday and have a joint practice in New Orleans on Thursday.

 "We were supposed to do four-minute [offense] today and go, hit, bang, another four-minute [period] run, run, run, run, run," Coen said. "And the way that those guys came out on defense [and dominated], at the end of the day, I'm the head coach [and] I've got to be happy with something."

 More observations: 

 
 Coen said starters will not play in the preseason opener against New Orleans on Saturday. They will get the majority of the reps in the joint practice against the Saints on Thursday. 
 CB/WR Travis Hunter played 14 snaps in 11-on-11 work (8 defense, 6 offense) and had two catches on three targets. WR Parker Washington beat him off the line of scrimmage and hauled in a deep throw from Trevor Lawrence down the left sideline. 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Head coach Liam Coen is handing over playcalling duty to offensive coordinator Grant Udinski for the preseason games.

 The Jaguars will have a joint practice with the New Orleans Saints on Thursday and two days later will play the Saints at the Caesars Superdome at 4 p.m. ET. Starters are expected to get most of the reps in the joint practice and most will not play against the Saints.

 "Looking forward to it," Udinski said Sunday. "... So we'll put together a call sheet and a game plan accordingly so that way we can see what these guys can do and let them go out there and hopefully compete and have some fun."

 Udinski is in his second season as the Jaguars' offensive coordinator after joining Coen's staff last season following three seasons in Minnesota, moving from the assistant to head coach Kevin O'Connell/special projects in 2022 to the assistant offensive coordinator/assistant quarterbacks coach in 2024.

 Udinski, 30, interviewed for the head coaching jobs in Cleveland and Buffalo in the offseason.

 
 S Eric Murray notched his third interception of camp. Picked off  Trevor Lawrence .

 S Rayuan Lane III punched the ball away from RB J'Mari Taylor  recovered the fumble. 
 OT Walker Little , TE Quintin Morris , DE Zach Durfee missed Sunday's practice with injuries. DT Arik Armstead had a vet day off. 
 

 

 Friday Aug. 7 
 Parker Washington picked up right where he left off at the end of the 2025 season: As the Jaguars' top pass catcher.

 Washington caught passes for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' Teal & White mock game on Friday (unofficial stats). He had a 50-yard catch and run and also had a 22-yard reception to go along with his 3-yard touchdown pass, one of three that quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw in the Teal's 19-12 victory.

 "It was nice to see Parker, Jakobi [WR Jakobi Meyers ], B.T. [WR Brian Thomas Jr .] make some plays and just getting the guys trying to spread it around a little bit and go execute," head coach Liam Coen said.

 Washington was thrust into a bigger role in the offense last season because of injuries to Travis Hunter and Thomas and by the end of the season was Lawrence's favorite target. Washington had 19 catches on 29 targets for 347 yards and two touchdowns in the final three games of the regular season. He also had seven catches for 107 yards and a touchdown in the playoff loss to Buffalo.

 Other unofficial stats and notes from the mock game: 

 
 Hunter played 14 snaps on defense and seven on offense. All of his snaps came while playing on the first units. He had no catches on two targets but he did carry the ball for 10 yards on a jet sweep. 
 Lawrence completed 15 of 29 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns. Washington, Thomas, and RB LeQuint Allen Jr . each had TD catches. 
 RG Patrick Mekari did not participate and RG Walker Little and LG Emmanuel Pregnon and were both injured during the mock game and did not return. LT Cole Van Lanen (knee) and OL Garrett DiGiorgio were already on PUP. This is potentially a problem area if the injuries to Mekari, Little and Pregnon linger. 
 CB Montaric Brown intercepted Nick Mullens to stop a drive in the red zone. CB Keni-H Lovely dropped an interception against Lawrence. 
 Second-year player B.J. Green II had at least two sacks and a tackle for loss. 
 Rookie S Jalen Huskey knocked the ball away from WR Chandler Brayboy and also recovered the fumble. 
 DE Josh Hines-Allen had a veteran rest day and did not participate.

title: Travis Kelce calls MSG wedding with Taylor Swift 'best night of my life'
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs tight end shared his first public comments Wednesday regarding his wedding with Taylor Swift.
full_text:
Just over a month since marrying Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce shared his first public comments about the wedding on Wednesday, calling it "the best night of my life."

 

 The Kansas City Chiefs star tight end and the pop superstar wed July 3 at Madison Square Garden in front of 1,000 guests. The festivities included a star-studded list of attendees , including Patrick Mahomes , Ed Sheeran, Wayne Gretzky and Selena Gomez.

 Comedian and actor Adam Sandler officiated the ceremony. There were no groomsmen, with Swift's brother serving as her man of honor and Kelce's brother, Jason, serving as his best man.

 Kelce offered some information about the night following Chiefs practice Wednesday.

 "It was a fun offseason, man. The wedding was the best night of my life. I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and had fun with us," he said. "It was a crazy night, and it was full of a lot of celebrations."

 

 Set in midtown Manhattan, the location initially was a surprise. But the self-styled World's Most Famous Arena holds a special place in Kelce's heart, he explained.

 Kelce always told himself that he would visit the arena for a playoff game when "the Knicks  were rocking." Swift wound up doing exactly that during the 2026 NBA Finals, attending New York's miraculous comeback in Game 4.

 The three-time Super Bowl champion was unable to attend since he was at Chiefs minicamp. But a potentially better alternative? Getting married in the building.

 "It's kind of cool to be able to live out my childhood dream of being in that venue, the mecca of all sports venues, to be able to get married in there," he said. "I can't thank the owners of MSG [enough] for allowing us to get the opportunity to do that, knowing that we wanted a private event. It was perfect, and the AC was cooking, baby. That was the best part."

 Few details have emerged from Kelce and Swift's wedding, and their post-wedding honeymoon plans have remained private. However, Kelce has been a constant presence at Kansas City's offseason program and training camp.

 Heading into his 14th NFL campaign, the four-time first-team All-Pro added Wednesday that he can still "play at a high level." Kelce had 76 receptions for 851 yards and five touchdowns last season.

 ESPN's Nate Taylor contributed to this report.

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  Latest news from Chiefs camp 
 
 Tight end Travis Kelce says he can still 'play at a high level' 
 OC Eric Bieniemy returns to Chiefs after shooting of wife 
 Reid: Mahomes unlikely to play in preseason opener 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 Chiefs' Reid: Eric Bieniemy's wife out of ICU, 'doing great' 
 
 
 
 

 Who has been the Chiefs' top performer so far at camp? 
 Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods has been a revelation. Not only has the first-round pick made an impact in each practice, Woods has quickly shown that he has the athleticism, quickness and strength to be a potential impact player next to pass rusher Chris Jones . Several veterans -- such as center Creed Humphrey , right guard Trey Smith and defensive end George Karlaftis -- have praised Woods throughout camp.

 Woods' explosive ability has led to him having highlight moments in the trenches, whether blowing by Humphrey on a running play or showing off his pass-rush skills in 1-on-1 drills. Just last week, the 6-foot-3, 310-pound Woods sprinted to chase down Patrick Mahomes , impressing the nine-year veteran quarterback.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 The lone major position battle is at the right tackle position. Coach Andy Reid is eager to see how Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, performs in the preseason.

 The Chiefs have given Benson most of the first-team reps, hoping he can provide true competition to Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran. If Benson continues to overachieve, even in the preseason -- especially since he's expected to play snaps at right tackle and right guard -- the Chiefs will have to decide if they feel comfortable with him protecting  Patrick Mahomes  despite not having any NFL experience.

 Moore is the safer option, but Benson should have plenty of snaps to demonstrate that he's ready for the spotlight that is opening night on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos on "Monday Night Football."

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 As expected, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Thursday that quarterback Patrick Mahomes will not play in the preseason opener Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams . Reid said the decision to not play Mahomes is a precautionary measure since the quarterback is still recovering from the surgery he had in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in left knee.

 "It'll be Justin [Fields] and then Garrett [Nussmeier] and then Chris [Oladokun] will take it from there," Reid said of Saturday's quarterback rotation. "We'll just see how the reps go as we work through that."

 Without Mahomes, Reid could decide to not play several starters against the Rams, a decision that would be different from previous years. One of those veterans who requested to not be in uniform was pass rusher Chris Jones , the defense's longest-tenured member.

 "Why play the starters?" Jones said. "I mean, it's so much risk you're taking to play the starters in the preseason. I hope Coach Reid [will] be like, 'You know what, starters don't play.'"

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Thursday's practice were safety Chamarri Conner (sore knee), right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed (rest) and Kader Kohou (sore ankle), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Although he wasn't selected in the NFL draft, Chiefs rookie right tackle Kahlil Benson was confident he'd be able to compete for a roster spot. Benson, however, has impressed the Chiefs enough so far into their training camp that he has a chance to win a starting spot on the offensive line. Benson will get his opportunity to make a strong first impression Saturday when the Chiefs host the Los Angeles Rams for their preseason opener.

 "Honestly, I kept my head down and knew my time was going to come," Benson said after Wednesday's practice. "I really just stayed humbled, stayed faithful and just kept praying to God that I was ready to be on-call when it was that time."

 Against the Rams, Benson is expected to play two positions in the first half: right tackle and right guard. This week, Benson has taken all his reps at right guard since starter Trey Smith has been out with a hip injury. When the second-team offense enters the game, Benson is expected to slide to the right tackle spot. Showing quality versatility could be a factor in Benson winning the right tackle role over five-year veteran Jaylon Moore .

 "I don't really feel like it's a challenge," Benson said of switching positions. "You've got to be able to adjust when it's time and your number is being called. You just never know what could happen."

 More conversations: 

 
 Three players left the field before Wednesday's practice ended. The Chiefs said linebacker Nick Bolton left with an illness, tight end Jared Wiley sustained a strained hamstring and rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods had an ankle injury that occurred late in a team period. 
 The players who missed Wednesday's practice were Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 One player fans should be interested to see in Saturday's preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams is receiver Andrew Armstrong .

 A second-year player who was cut last year by the Miami Dolphins , Armstrong joined the Chiefs in January and has been impressive throughout training camp. When fellow receivers Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy were out last week, Armstrong had several highlights with quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the rest of the first-team offense.

 "I've been out there being the best I can be and learning," Armstrong said after Tuesday's practice. "One of the main goals is being trustworthy for the quarterback. I'm trying to build that with [Mahomes].

 "This has been my favorite team since I was a little kid. I really wanted to be around a serious environment and this is an extremely serious environment. I love that."

 Armstrong is in a tight competition with second-year player Jalen Royals for the sixth and potential final receiver spot on the initial 53-man roster. If Armstrong performs well against the Rams, he could gain a sizable lead in the battle.

 "Oh, it's going to feel great, just looking and seeing all the red," Armstrong said of playing inside Arrowhead Stadium. "It's different playing on a [video] game than in real life. I know it's going to feel amazing."

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Tuesday's practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 Before Tuesday's practice, the Chiefs agreed to sign defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah to a one-year deal. A 10-year veteran, Ogbah was with the Chiefs in 2019, the year the team won the Super Bowl. "I always had an affection for E," defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo said. "I've always periodically been in touch with him. If he's part of our group, I'll be excited about that."

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 The starter at left guard. These games will be essential for the team to find its fifth and final offensive line starter. Their battle is a lengthy one with five players in the mix: Kayode Awosika , Trevor Penning , Branson Taylor , Jake Slaughter  and  Trey Pipkins III ..

 Coach Jim Harbaugh wants to make a decision soon, and his rough timeline ends before the team's second preseason game. So Thursday night's preseason game against the Texans will be significant in the race for the starter.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 The defense dominated Tuesday's padded practice, with defensive tackle Teair Tart and cornerback Donte Jackson among the most active players.

 Tart had at least two pressures that likely would have resulted in sacks of quarterback Justin Herbert , bursting through the interior offensive line. Khalil Mack also appeared to share one of those would-be sacks with Tart. Tart was disruptive against the run throughout practice as well.

 Jackson had two interceptions and a pass breakup. He first intercepted Herbert after jumping a route on a pass intended for JaQuae Jackson . Later, Donte Jackson made a nearly identical play against DJ Uiagalelei , jumping another pass intended for JaQuae Jackson.

 More observations: 

 
 
 Wide receiver  Tre' Harris  got a win against cornerback Donte Jackson in 1-on-1s, making a contested catch as he fell to the ground despite tight coverage from Jackson.

 
 
 Tight end Charlie Kolar had a nice catch over safety  Derwin James Jr . on a good ball from Justin Herbert .

 
 
 Outside linebacker Akheem Mesidor blew by OL Travis Burke on a rep that might have resulted in a sack of QB Trey Lance . Mesidor also easily shed OL Branson Taylor on a Kimani Vidal run that likely would've been stopped in the backfield.

 
 
 Defensive tacke Jahmeer Carter has stood out recently. He had a powerful win against Jake Slaughter in 1-on-1s that knocked Slaughter off balance. Carter also blew up a Vidal run in 11-on-11.

 
 
 Safety Devin Grant intercepted quarterback Uiagalelei.

 
 
 Linebackers Daiyan Henley and Bud Dupree and OL Cole Strange left the team period early and worked off to the side with strength coach Ben Herbert.

 
 
 Outside linebacker Andre Carter , who had his first practice yesterday, batted down a Lance pass at the line of scrimmage.

 
 
 Wide receiver Derius Davis had a nice catch down the sideline near the end of practice. It was an impressive throw from Justin Herbert, who fit the ball over a cornerback underneath and a safety over the top.

 
 
 Slaughter, Taylor and Kayode Awosika rotated at left guard.

 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 

 Left tackle Rashawn Slater and cornerback Tarheeb Still missed practice for the third straight day. Coach Jim Harbaugh originally said Slater's absence two days ago was part of a veteran rest day, but his continued absence suggests there may be more to it. The Chargers have not provided a reason for Still's absence.

 In Slater's absence, Branson Taylor and  Trey Pipkins III  have played left tackle, and Cam Hart has taken the bulk of snaps at outside in place of Still. Before, Still and Hart rotated with the first group.

 More observations: 

 
 Jake Slaughter and Kayode Awosika rotated at left guard, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said "no one's eliminated themselves from the tournament." 
 McDaniel ran across the field yelling, "Great job,  Joe Alt " during practice Monday after Alt blocked outside linebacker Khalil Mack on a screen, something the Chargers have struggled to do throughout camp. McDaniel said Alt has "exceeded my expectations that were pretty high coming in" and called him an "over-the-top pleasant surprise." 
 McDaniel said he'll use running backs Omarion Hampton , Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell in probably every game this season, with the workload depending on the opponent and "hot hand." 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 During the first 11v11 period of Sunday's practice, the crowd roared for a Quentin Johnston reception that quarterback Justin Herbert perfectly placed by the outstretched arms of cornerback Nikko Reed .

 But had this not been training camp, Herbert likely would've been on his back or running for life before that ball had the chance to be released. Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu -- rushing from the interior on a front that featured Justin Eboigbe , Akheem Mesidor and Khalil Mack -- put a swift spin move on center Tyler Biadasz and was in Herbert's lap as the play was beginning. This sequence was a microcosm of Sunday's practice, as the defensive line controlled the day, constantly putting pressure on quarterbacks and stopping running plays before they could begin.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Branson Taylor , Kayode Awosika and Jake Slaughter rotated at left guard throughout practice. 
 Cornerback Tarheeb Still and left tackle Rashawn Slater both missed practice for a second straight day. Trey Pipkins and Taylor played left tackle in his absence. 
 Tre' Harris was active throughout practice with several receptions. 
 Avery Smith blew up a running play on a blitz, drawing celebrations from the defense. 
 Junior Colson pressured DJ Uiagalelei into a throw that landed in the hands of cornerback Isas Waxter , but Waxter dropped the interception. 
 Kyle Kennard had perhaps his best practice of camp, with several impressive wins in one-on-ones and pressures during 11-on-11 periods. 
 Trevor Penning had a good day, holding up well in one-on-ones and during team periods while working with the second and third groups. 
 Mesidor had one of the most impressive one-on-one wins of practice, beating Joe Alt cleanly with a spin move. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 

 Rookie left guard Jake Slaughter got his first reps with the group blocking for Justin Herbert in a padded practice this training camp. The Chargers drafted Slaughter -- who played only center in college -- to be the team's starter at left guard, but he seemed to fall out of favor through camp as veteran Kayode Awosika and second-year lineman Branson Taylor emerged.

 Slaughter fared well in his reps at guard, showing a firm anchor when pressured from defensive tackles and the ability to pick up defensive stunts. His best moment came on a pancake block of defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson , but he was also beaten badly on a rep by defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe .

 More observations: 

 
 Offensve lineman Trevor Penning appears to be falling back in the competition for the starting left guard job. He continues to work largely with the group, blocking…

title: 2026 Los Angeles Rams training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Rams training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Rams reporter Sarah Barshop has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Rams camp. Can the Rams live up to the hype? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Bears' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Rams camp 
 
 Rams' Myles Garrett misses practice again; Puka Nacua exits early 
 Sean McVay praises Aaron Donald as Rams await DT's decision 
 Myles Garrett out third straight day with soreness 
 Puka Nacua says it 'never crossed my mind' to not take part in camp 
 Rams unveil two new alternate uniforms for 2026 
 

 

 Who is the Rams' top performer so far at camp? 
 CB  Trent McDuffie . The Rams ended last season with a clear weakness in the cornerback room. Los Angeles addressed that by trading for McDuffie, an All-Pro, and by signing his former teammate Jaylen Watson in free agency. McDuffie has been a standout during training camp on a roster not lacking star talent. Veteran wide receiver Davante Adams said he's not sure he'll get a better look this season than what he has seen going against McDuffie during training camp.

 "Trent's out there doing something every single play," Adams said. "... He's always got the right technique. He's got a great way of reading you out. He understands his position on any given play, whether it's his leverage or situationally a smart player and great technique.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How does rookie quarterback Ty Simpson look?

 The No. 13 pick hasn't gotten as many reps during training camp as starting quarterback Matthew Stafford or 2023 fourth-round pick  Stetson Bennett IV , but he should get ample snaps during the preseason. Heading into the first preseason game, it appears that Bennett will be the team's backup quarterback going into the season, and Simpson will serve as the third-string quarterback. But if Simpson plays significant snaps -- and it seems he will -- the Rams will get their first extended look at their rookie quarterback to see how he operates coach Sean McVay's offense.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

After the Rams' final practice before the preseason opener against the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday, coach Sean McVay said 2023 fourth-round pick Stetson Bennett IV will start the game. 

McVay said rookie quarterback Ty Simpson will also play.

Bennett, who played in the Rams' first two preseason games a year ago, said he feels a difference in his confidence playing in his offense compared to a year ago.

"Yeah, for sure, Bennett said. "And I think that just comes with being better at your job and having more ownership, knowing the offense more, being closer with the guys."

Bennett took the majority of the second-team reps on days Matthew Stafford was practicing and the first-team reps when Stafford was not.

 

 More observations: 
 
 Rams offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase will call plays in Saturday's game. McVay is the Rams' offensive playcaller during the regular season but usually hands over responsibility to a coordinator or assistant coach during the preseason to let them get reps. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 With Myles Garrett missing the Rams' joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys while dealing with swelling in his knee, outside linebackers Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart stood out as part of the Rams' pass rush.

 Rams head coach Sean McVay said he wanted to look back at the tape because he was bouncing between the two fields, but said he noticed the pressure from the Rams' edge rushers.

 "I did see that," McVay said. "... [Cowboys quarterback] Dak Prescott  does a good job being able to move in the pocket and I think there's some excellent players on the perimeter that we were able to get some really good looks at, but it did feel like those guys were able to make their presence felt."

 McVay said he's not concerned about Garrett missing time, saying the pass rusher told him he feels "about 85 percent" healthy.

 "When he's been out there, he has certainly made his impact felt, but we want to make sure that when he returns to play, he's able to return to full performance and feel like himself," McVay said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Cowboys linebacker Justin Barron had three interceptions on Tuesday, including one of Matthew Stafford . McVay said he thought Stafford "was great," during the practice but said "there was one where just a little bit late over the middle." McVay said in general, Stafford "kept the ball in play" and "saw coverage really well." 
 McVay said he hasn't made a decision on how he will handle the quarterback reps during the Rams' preseason opener in Kansas City on Saturday. McVay has previously said Stafford will not play and that rookie quarterback Ty Simpson will "definitely" play. McVay said he is still deciding whether Stetson Bennett IV will get reps during the preseason. 
 Similarly to how the Rams have operated throughout training camp, Bennett got most of the second-team reps against the Cowboys. 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Tuesday will mark the first joint practice of training camp for the Rams, as they will host the Dallas Cowboys at their Woodland Hills facility. Because head coach Sean McVay does not play his starters or key backups during the preseason, he especially values the chance to get his starters in these competitive, but more controlled environments.

 McVay said he tries to schedule at least two joint practices during the preseason; the Rams will host the New Orleans Saints for a joint practice on Aug. 20.

 The Rams don't gameplan for the practice, but McVay said he's looking forward to "the competition" of going against a different team than his players see practicing against each other.

 "I think when you go against each other as much as we've done up to this point, it's good to be able to just change it up and get a feel to go against different schemes and great players," McVay said.

 
 Monday's practice was a rest day for quarterback Matthew Stafford . He is scheduled to practice against the Cowboys on Tuesday. 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 In the Rams' return to their Woodland Hills facility for the remainder of the preseason, "the defense was outstanding," coach Sean McVay said.

 "There was great coverage, some great individual plays, disrupting timing and rhythm," McVay said. "It was a great day for the defense. Offensively they were able to run the football with some success, but throwing and catching was a real struggle."

 McVay said he was not discouraged by the performance by the offense, because the takeaways "were more of a reflection of great individual plays than necessarily poor execution."

 "What I get upset about is when the other opponent or whether the other side of the ball doesn't have to earn it because it's sloppy -- whether it's poor execution or communication on one side or the other," McVay said. "The plays that happened today, there was a handful of turnovers, but I thought it was a really great reflection of excellent execution defensively, some outstanding individual plays. And sometimes that's the price of doing business."

 And that defense might even get stronger as the Rams await the news of a possible return from defensive tackle Aaron Donald. McVay said Saturday that he did not have an update on Donald's decision.

 Other observations: 

 
 First-round pick Ty Simpson will "definitely" play in the first preseason game next Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs , McVay said. 
 McVay said he has not made a…
