title: 2026 Las Vegas Raiders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Raiders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Las Vegas Raiders  camp is taking place at Intermountain Health Performance Center in Henderson, Nevada, and Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Raiders camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from Raiders camp 
 
 Nine takeaways from Raiders' nine training camp practices 
 Maxx Crosby's approaching Raiders training camp with intensity 
 Three-time Pro Bowl guard Andrus Peat announces retirement 
 Cousins gets nod over Mendoza to open Raiders camp 
 What's next for Crosby, WR and CB rooms? 
 

 
 

 Who is the Raiders' top performer so far at camp? 
 Malik Benson . The rookie wide receiver has had a strong camp, showing the coaching staff that he could play a meaningful role during the regular season. Whether playing with the first- or second-team offense, Benson has found ways to make plays. On top of that, he has developed a strong connection with quarterback Fernando Mendoza .

 Benson has shown solid footwork, the ability to create separation from defenders and generate yards after the catch. Benson is listed behind Jack Bech on the team's unofficial depth chart. But if he can translate his strong performance from the practice field onto the preseason games, Benson could overtake Bech as WR3.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 What does Mendoza have to do to make a serious push to be the starter? Kirk Cousins is currently in the driver's seat to be named the starting quarterback for Week 1. And even though Mendoza has been solid during training camp, Cousins has been the better quarterback. Cousins has only played with the first-team offense, while Mendoza only did so once, and that was because coach Klint Kubiak decided to hold Cousins out of practice due to his scuffle with defensive end Maxx Crosby .

 If Mendoza wants to change the narrative, he will have to play flawlessly in the preseason games, starting Thursday night against the Arizona Cardinals . By doing so, he could push the team to give him more first-team reps. Mendoza has impressed the coaching staff and remains on track in his development. But he still has a ways to go before being considered QB1.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Under the bright lights at Allegiant Stadium on Tuesday, the connection between rookies Fernando Mendoza and Malik Benson continued to thrive.

 In the team's final practice before the preseason opener against the Arizona Cardinals , Mendoza relied heavily on the sixth-round wide receiver. He connected with Benson on an out route while playing with the second-team offense. Later in practice, Mendoza zipped the ball through tight coverage to Benson on a slant route.

 Benson said he and Mendoza began developing a strong bond when they first met at the scouting combine in February -- two months before they officially became teammates. The former Oregon pass catcher said after they were both drafted by the Raiders, he wanted to make sure he could be a player who Mendoza could rely on.

 That has been the case since OTAs and mandatory minicamp.

 "I know, when it comes to Sundays, when it comes to practice, he's going to rely on me to be in that spot, and I'm going to rely on him to place the ball where it needs to be placed," Benson said.

 Overall, Mendoza was solid in what can be described as a light practice. The only blemish on his performance was a tipped pass and interception by linebacker Cody Lindenberg .

 More observations: 

 
 Second-year wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . missed his fourth straight practice. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford did not wear a red non-contact jersey and was a full participant during practice. He recorded a sack on Mendoza while playing with the second-team defense. 
 Quarterback  Aidan O'Connell  had the best throw of the evening --- a 55-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Brandon Johnson during the 7-on-7 period. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Maybe coach Klint Kubiak's decision to hold Kirk Cousins from Saturday's practice due to his scuffle with Maxx Crosby sparked a fire within the veteran quarterback. Maybe it didn't. Either way, Cousins had his best performance of training camp.

 Monday featured Cousins fitting the ball into tight windows and effectively conducting two-minute drives. He threw a touchdown pass to Brock Bowers in the corner of the end zone despite tight coverage from Taron Johnson . Both players later connected on a deep pass over the middle, positioning the offense near the goal line.

 Cousins delivered a nice pass to wide receiver Tre Tucker on a crossing route with rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses in coverage. He also connected with Malik Benson , who made a contested catch against cornerback Darien Porter .

 During the two-minute period, Cousins completed four passes, including a touchdown throw to wide receiver Jalen Nailor .

 Fernando Mendoza , on the other hand, went back to playing with the second-team offense. He didn't put together his best performance. He ran into running back Dare Ogunbowale during the handoff exchange.

 He threw his third interception of camp. Mendoza attempted a pass to wide receiver Deven Thompkins on an out route. Greedy Vance was in front of Thompkins in man coverage, and Mendoza threw the ball directly into the second-year defensive back's hands.

 His best throw -- a back-shoulder pass to Benson -- was called back because he was sacked on the play.

 Other observations: 

 
 Defensive end Kwity Paye returned to practice, but did not participate in the team period. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford practiced, but wore a red non-contact jersey. Guard Caleb Rogers , tight end Carter Runyon and wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . did not participate. 
 From a health standpoint, rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy said he feels closer to how he was in 2024. McCoy, who missed the entire 2025 college football season at Tennessee, said the Raiders' rehab plan has him feeling much better. "I'm still getting there. It's been a long time since I really played football. 
 McCoy mentioned that the biggest challenge was getting back into football shape and pre-snap stuff. McCoy felt rusty during the first day of camp, but was comfortable by Day 3. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 

 With  Kirk Cousins and Maxx Crosby  not practicing for violating team rules ,  Fernando Mendoza  played with the starters for the first time in camp.

 Mendoza had his good and bad moments. He overthrew wide receiver Jack Bech a couple of times. And he had trouble securing the ball when snapped to him by Tyler Linderbaum and Jordan Meredith .

 Mendoza, however, didn't get flustered. He had one of his best throws of camp during the red zone period. He threw a touchdown pass to Tre Tucker , in which he zipped the ball through tight coverage by cornerback Taron Johnson .

 Mendoza also threw touchdowns to tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer .

 The highlight of the day was Mendoza's efficiency during the two-minute period to close out practice. He completed five straight passes, including a throw to Tucker in tight coverage, to set up a field goal from kicker Matt Gay .

 During Mendoza's reps with the first-team, quarterback coach Mike Sullivan said the biggest things he was evaluating were the rookie's command of the offense and not panicking in the pocket. Sullivan added that the team is pleased with…

title: Rookie Caleb Douglas atop Dolphins WR depth chart for preseason opener
summary: Miami's thin wide receiver room created an opportunity for Caleb Douglas to make an early impact, which he has done so far.
full_text:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- The first name on the Miami Dolphins ' first depth chart of the year has been one of the most consistent players at the team's training camp this summer -- even though he's yet to log his first NFL snap.

 Rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas was named a starter as the team prepares for its preseason opener Friday against the Washington Commanders . The depth chart is considered unofficial at this point of the season, but is a sign that the third-round pick has exceeded expectations so far.

 

 "It's been (his) consistency over time -- he's been really consistent," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Wednesday. "He's made some flash plays and then he's made some plays where he needs to catch the ball, but he's probably been one of our most consistent guys. He showed up every day. So that's where he deserves to be at this point."

 The Dolphins took Douglas with the 75th overall pick in this year's draft, making him the 11th receiver taken -- just ahead of fellow training camp standouts Zachariah Branch and  Ja'Kobi Lane . At the time, it was considered a reach considering his college production (2,031 yards, 16 touchdowns in four seasons), struggles with drops and inconsistencies winning contested catches.

 Hafley said the latter was the "number one thing" he wanted to see from Douglas once practices began, but that the rookie has impressed him with his ability to do so.

 Douglas has used his 6-foot-4 frame to create separation from defensive backs and is starting to learn how to make defenders pay for assuming how he'll use his speed (4.39-second 40-yard dash).

 "Really just always knowing that I'm a bigger guy, they're going to always think I'm going vertical," Douglas said. "So me being able to sell my vertical so well and being able to snap it down, I have a lot of ways of going inside, outside, back down the stem."

 

 Over the past two weeks, Douglas has separated himself as quarterback Malik Willis ' most reliable target. Veterans Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington have more experience, but the rookie's upside is undeniable.

 Despite the occasional drop due to a lack of focus, Willis said Douglas has been efficient with his opportunities so far.

 "I think he's a great player. I wouldn't even say (he's) even a safety valve yet. I'm still trying to figure everybody out," Willis said. "Everybody's trying to figure me out. We're trying to figure this out together ... He's been making nice grabs in the times where he's the option, where he's the read. So I'm excited for him. I think he's doing a great job getting open. I think he's attacking the mental side of it. It's been great."

 Douglas' production carried over into Wednesday's joint practice with the Commanders, for which he drew praise as the brightest spot of an otherwise underwhelming Dolphins offense.

 

 Miami's thin wide receiver room created an opportunity for Douglas to make an early impact and offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik believes he's done so thanks to tireless work on his fundamentals since his arrival -- although there are still a few habits from college that he'll need to clean up before the season begins.

 "He's an immensely talented dude. He's got long arms. He's fast. He's got really good feet," Slowik said. "He's tall. We just need him to continue to grow in his technique and his fundamentals of what receiver play entails at the Miami Dolphins, and he's doing that. Like it flashes. It shows when he does it. And then there's still little things that you can get away with in college for all our young guys that in the NFL you no longer can do.

 "You know, the catch tuck how important that is, how fast that is. In college, you can probably catch, wait on your tuck for a good two seconds with no issues. The way our defense is going at the ball right now, if it's not instantaneous, it might come out. If our footwork isn't clean on our transitions, we're probably getting tackled. If we have clean footwork on our transitions, now we've got a chance to run through some stuff. So it's just little things like that for all our young guys, we got to continue to grow."

 Douglas' starting job is not cemented; he'll have to continue to produce in practice and in the team's three preseason games in order to keep it. But on a Dolphins offense that lacks options in the passing game, Douglas' opportunity is there for the taking.

title: 2026 Miami Dolphins training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Dolphins' training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Dolphins camp. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Dolphins' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Dolphins camp 
 
 Dolphins top pick Proctor embracing NFL learning curve 
 Miami, All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks reach 3-year, $51.3M extension 
 Dolphins, Aaron Brewer reach 3-year, $52.5 million extension 
 Why Miami's rookies can thrive 
 
 

 Who has been the Dolphins' top performer so far at camp? 
 Defensive end Chop Robinson . Now entering his third season, Robinson arrived at camp in clearly the best shape of his career, and it's shown on the practice field. He added a few pounds of muscle to his frame while keeping his speed, enabling him to win at the line of scrimmage with both speed and power.

 When right tackle Austin Jackson missed consecutive practices last week, Robinson made quick work of any lineman that was placed in front of him -- which may not be saying much considering the Dolphins' offensive line depth, but it's better than the alternative. First-year coach Jeff Hafley said Robinson will be used exclusively with his hand in the dirt this season, which should allow him to utilize his skill set more efficiently.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Where will the Dolphins get their receiving production from? Rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas has emerged as a potential top target this summer, and should get plenty of run this preseason to prove it. He played well in the team's first joint practice and Hafley & Co. will look for the third-round pick to take an additional step and produce under the lights, as well. Fellow third-round pick Chris Bell is yet to practice, but if he's able to return for at least one preseason game it could provide a glimpse of the team's future at the position.

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Monday's return to the practice field was a standout day for the Dolphins' rookies. Wide receiver Caleb Douglas started team drills with a drop due to a loss of focus but rebounded nicely with a series of contested catches. Coach Jeff Hafley said he wanted to see the third-round pick's ability to fight through contact once pads came on at practice, and so far Douglas has delivered.

 Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez 's sideline-to-sideline ability popped Monday, as did his ability to read and react to run plays. Seventh-round defensive end Max Llewellyn sacked quarterback Quinn Ewers during team drills and cornerback Chris Johnson had an impressive pass breakup in the end zone against Douglas.

 More observations: 

 
 Tight end Greg Dulcich practiced in full for the first time since last week. He'd worn the red non-contact jersey for the past few practices with an apparent hand injury. 
 Ewers threw an interception to safety Major Burns during the team's late-game drill. He stepped up in the pocket and likely would've scrambled in a real game, but appeared to try to fit the ball through a small window -- and it went directly to Burns. 
 Quarterback Malik Willis ' arm velocity was apparent throughout the practice, particularly on an off-platform throw to Douglas that got home in the blink of an eye. His speech to the Dolphins' offense about upholding the team's standard has stuck with his teammates -- several of whom have credited his growth as a leader. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 The Dolphins held Saturday's practice at Hard Rock Stadium, but a critical moment occurred before they even set foot on the field.

 Quarterback Malik Willis addressed his teammates Friday, to ensure players continued to uphold the team's standard.

 "I just wanted to talk to the offense and just have a man-to-man conversation," Willis said Saturday. "We got to understand this is a business, and we got to take what we do personally. We got to take pride in it, and we got to do it to the best of our ability -- regardless if we're calling plays to beat the defense or not.

 "We're not calling plays to beat the defense; we're calling the plays that we want to use throughout the year. We're trying to get better at those plays. Whether we win a down or not, are we doing everything that we can do to execute the playcall?"

 Rookie offensive tackle Kadyn Proctor reference Willis' speech unprompted after practice, so the message appears to have stuck.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Tahj Washington made receptions of 50 and 30 yards on balls from Cam Miller and Quinn Ewers , and rookie wide receiver  Donaven McCulley  brought down a 45-yard pass from Miller in traffic, shaking off a facemask penalty in the process. 
 Safety Tanner Wall , who signed with the Dolphins on Friday, wasted no time making his presence known in his first practice with the team. He broke up a pass in the end zone during red zone drills to save a touchdown. 
 Kicker Zane Gonzalez appeared to leave the practice field after special teams work and did not return. Riley Patterson handled all kicks during team drills at the end of practice. 
 Cornerback JuJu Brents missed practice after suffering an undisclosed injury Friday, while safety Dante Trader Jr . missed his third consecutive practice. The team hopes to get Trader back in time for next week's practice with the Commanders. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley has stressed the importance of taking the ball away to his defense, and his players have responded with gusto this summer. Miami's defense recorded four interceptions during Friday's practice, including two by second-year cornerback Miles Battle -- both off quarterback Quinn Ewers . Linebacker Jackson Woodard continued his strong week of practice with a pick-six off quarterback Mark Gronowski , and UDFA safety Louis Moore added to his big play total with an interception as well.

 The Dolphins defense has forced multiple turnovers in nearly every practice this summer. It's a direct result of the team's coaching points on and off the field.

 "One of our assistant linebacker coaches, Wendel (Davis) -- he starts every meeting with taking the ball away," linebacker Tyrel Dodson said. "So he's made excellent emphasis on those takeaway points and we've honed in on it. We've studied different techniques, punching the ball out. Jacob (Rodriguez is) good at it. So we've studied the Peanut punch and all that stuff. So it's looking good."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had an explosive play on a sideline ball from Malik Willis during team drills. The third-round pick appeared to get behind cornerback Jason Marshall Jr and picked up some yards after the catch. 
 Right tackle Austin Jackson returned to practice after missing the past two practices with an undisclosed injury. As a result, defensive end Chop Robinson didn't wreak the same level of havoc he did with Jackson sidelined, but it was a fun matchup to watch. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Pressure, pressure and more pressure was the key word for the Dolphins in Thursday's practice. The team shed its shoulder pads, looking to ease back into work following Wednesday's off day, but it didn't stop coach Jeff Hafley's defense from attacking its offensive counterparts throughout team drills.

 Linebacker Jackson Woodard was a constant presence around the ball, while defensive end Chop Robinson continued his strong camp -- albeit against a banged up right side of the Dolphins' offensive line. Thursday also marked another strong performance…

title: 2026 Minnesota Vikings training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Vikings training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Vikings' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 What Kyler Murray as QB1 means for Vikings, J.J. McCarthy 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 

 

 Who is the Vikings' top performer so far at camp? 

 Receiver Tai Felton has demonstrated remarkable improvement from his rookie year, when he struggled to catch the ball consistently in training camp and wound up with a near-exclusive special teams role during the season. He has made one-handed catches in the end zone, demonstrated soft hands at the end of deep routes and displayed his top-end speed while running quick hitters. Coach Kevin O'Connell said he has noted exceptional route running at times as well.

 Is Felton the Vikings' best player? Of course not. But no one has opened more eyes since camp began. He'll push veteran No. 3 receiver Jauan Jennings for playing time.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 The entire NFL world wants to know how quarterback Kyler Murray , who was named the starter after a two-week competition with J.J. McCarthy , will perform in the Vikings' offense. But Murray isn't likely to play nearly enough during the preseason to answer that question.

 The most important question the Vikings can realistically answer is how much of their talented draft class will truly be ready to contribute in Week 1.

 That list most notably includes defensive linemen Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange , linebacker Jake Golday , safety Jakobe Thomas , cornerback Charles Demmings and running back Demond Claiborne .

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said earlier this week that both of the quarterbacks who took part in their two-week competition for the starting job would play in Saturday's preseason opener at the New York Giants . That means Kyler Murray will start, along with most of the team's first-team offense, and J.J. McCarthy will play next.

 
The Vikings held a relatively brief practice Thursday, similar to what they would do for a Friday practice during a regular-season week. Two notable veterans did not participate -- receiver Justin Jefferson and left tackle Christian Darrisaw -- making them unlikely to play Saturday.

 
Right guard Will Fries , who had sat out the previous two days of practice, was back on the field and participating in team drills.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 While the world has been focused on the Vikings' quarterback competition, another part of their offense has been more quietly under development. 
Coaches are in the process of tweaking the team's run game to give it more variety and, they hope, more production. Once pads came on at the start of the second week of training camp, Vikings running backs have ripped through the line of scrimmage on a regular basis, especially via outside zone concepts. 
"We're running the football very, very well against a really good defense right now," coach Kevin O'Connell said this week. 
On one play Wednesday, running back Jordan Mason followed a block from right tackle Brian O'Neill to reach the sideline and sprint for a touchdown. As Mason was running, O'Neill, right guard Joe Huber and center Blake Brandel sprinted after him in celebration.

 Other observations:

 
 Right guard Will Fries again sat out practice, with Huber taking his place with the first team. 
 Rookie safety Jakobe Thomas participated in individual drills, but his absence from team drills continued. 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 After his first public practice with the Vikings this spring, Kyler Murray uttered a four-word phrase that hovered over the team's quarterback competition all summer.

 "My confidence," Murray said in May, "is unshakeable."

 That helps explain why Murray didn't sound much different Tuesday after coach Kevin O'Connell named him the team's starter as the third week of training camp began. Murray said he did not expect to be handed the job and acknowledged that not every practice this summer has gone smoothly as he split reps with J.J. McCarthy .

 "There's going to be good days," Murray said. "There's going to be bad days. We're facing adversity every single day. But I'm definitely getting more comfortable as each day goes."

 Murray had a sharp practice Tuesday while taking all of the first-team reps for the first time since Week 5 of last season when he was with the Arizona Cardinals . McCarthy said he would address the decision publicly Wednesday.

 More observations:  

 
 Right guard Will Fries did not practice Tuesday. He was replaced on the first team by second-year guard Joe Huber . 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 As the third week of training camp began in the evening, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was not ready to name a winner in the QB1 competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy .

 "Nothing has really changed from a standpoint of the timeline and things like that," O'Connell said before the Vikings took the field at TCO Stadium for their annual night practice. "So we'll see how the reps continue to go and when we feel like we're at that place, we're going to make sure we communicate that both in house and internally and obviously to you guys as soon as possible."

 The Vikings have a scheduled off day Monday to reset the competition if they desire. Murray entered training camp as the favorite for the job, and sources say they believe he still is. Asked Sunday where Murray is in the offensive system compared to where he thought he would be at this point, O'Connell said: "I think mentally he's definitely probably ahead of where I thought." O'Connell went on to say there are some parts of the offense that are new to everyone.

 
 It was a rough practice for the offense as defensive pressure made it difficult for quarterbacks Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy to get into a rhythm. Murray threw two interceptions, to cornerbacks James Pierre and Isaiah Rodgers , the latter when he was scrambling and tried to get the ball to Justin Jefferson on the sideline. McCarthy continued his theme of hitting deep out routes, including another to receiver Myles Price . McCarthy completed a deep pass to Jefferson down the right sideline but it forced Jefferson to slow down to bring it in, and he struggled later in a red zone drill. 
 Part of the protection issue was caused by the absence of left tackle Christian Darrisaw , who took a veteran's rest day. The Vikings also rested rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks , who remains on a maintenance plan to ensure full recovery from a broken left foot. 
 Defensive linemen Levi Drake Rodriguez and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins also sat out the practice, giving rookie nose tackle Domonique Orange extensive first-team action. 
 Safety Jay Ward is in the latter stages of the concussion protocol, O'Connell said. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Two members of the Vikings' draft class -- both Day 3 picks -- made splash plays during a low-key practice.

 Rookie tailback Demond Claiborne ran about 70 yards off left tackle using a nifty jump cut to get outside. Claiborne, a sixth-round pick from Wake Forest, has mostly worked with the third team behind Aaron Jones Sr . and Jordan Mason . He could also…

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Patriots' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 

 

 Who has been the Patriots' top performer at camp so far? 

 CB Christian Gonzalez . The question entering training camp was if he might be a hold-in due to ongoing talks on a contract extension. Instead, he was a full participant the first 13 practices and played a significant role in elevating the competition level for the entire team with his back-and-forth, fire-breathing 1-on-1 matchup with WR A.J. Brown -- which was arguably the top storyline of camp.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 How much is the rookie class ready to contribute? First-round pick Caleb Lomu ideally projects as the swing offensive tackle, second-round pick Gabe Jacas as a top backup OLB who creates havoc as a pass-rusher, and third-round pick Eli Raridon as the No. 2 tight end behind Hunter Henry . Their performance in games can solidify those roles, along with other rookie-based questions, such as whether seventh-round pick Behren Morton earns a roster spot as the No. 3 quarterback.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Patriots' had an official ribbon-cutting ceremony for their new 160,000-square-foot New Balance Athletics Center on Wednesday, with owner Robert Kraft and coach Mike Vrabel among those sharing remarks before VP of football operations and strategy John Streicher led a behind-the-scenes tour.

 "There's not a better place to teach and prepare our players," Vrabel said.

 The facility includes a 15,000-square-foot weight room; 11,000 square feet of dining and kitchen space; a 10,500-square-foot virtual reality room; 3,700 square feet dedicated to hydrotherapy; and a state of the art draft room.

 The 160,000 square feet is more than double the amount the team previously occupied at Gillette Stadium.

 On one notable part of the tour, Streicher stopped at QB Drake Maye 's locker and explained the thought that went in to selecting the details of each locker -- which includes two separate areas to dry shoulder pads/helmets and cleats.

 Maye's locker is directly next to WR A.J. Brown 's, and across from CB Christian Gonzalez 's, with whom he has regularly engaged in back-and-forth locker room banter in recent years.

 

 More: 

 
 The Patriots waived undrafted rookie RB Myles Montgomery with an injury designation Wednesday and signed RB Hassan Haskins , a 2022 fourth-round draft pick of the Titans. The Patriots host the Colts in the preseason opener Thursday, and with top-of-the-depth-chart RBs Rhamondre Stevenson , TreVeyon Henderson and Terrell Jennings not expected to play, Haskins could get carries right away after Lan Larison and rookie Jam Miller . 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Drake Maye isn't expected to play in Thursday's preseason opener against the Colts, coach Mike Vrabel said Tuesday.

 "That's where my mindset is right now, standing here today," Vrabel said before Tuesday's joint practice with the Colts in Foxborough. "That can always change, but I wouldn't anticipate that happening right now."

 Vrabel noted that Tuesday's practice essentially takes the place of the game for Maye & Co.

 "That's really the only reason that we do these joint practices. It will be a lot of the front-line players and whoever's available [in the practice]. Some of the guys that maybe will not get as much work will get extensive work in the game on Thursday," he said.

 The plan for practice was to have the offense take 24 full-team reps, which Vrabel pointed out was more than Maye & Co. would likely see in a preseason game.

 Maye's final rep in practice wasn't to his liking, as he threw an end zone interception to Colts safety Cam Bynum on a second-down play in the two-minute drill. Otherwise, he was pleased with the Patriots' effort, energy and execution.

 "We challenged our guys to be consistent throughout the day, and I think they responded to that," Maye said.

 More observations: 

 
 Starting CB Christian Gonzalez missed his first practice of training camp. It might have been related to his final play of Monday's practice, when he landed hard in the end zone while defending WR Romeo Doubs . Gonzalez has also been in negotiations with the team on a contract extension. 
 With Gonzalez and fellow starting CB Carlton Davis III not practicing, and top backup Charles Woods also out, any evaluation of the pass defense came with a caveat. The Colts were without two top WRs, however. 
 The Colts' first units on offense/defense won the end-of-practice two-minute drill, while the Patriots' second units were victorious -- QB Tommy DeVito connecting with WR Mack Hollins on a long TD and S John Saunders Jr . notching an INT. 
 DeVito had another deep ball earlier in practice as speedy WR Kyle Williams got behind the defense and tracked the ball well. 
 With the Patriots' first-unit offense on one field and the first-unit defense on the other, Vrabel stayed with the offense. That left assistant head coach Terrell Williams and coordinator Zak Kuhr to lead the defensive field. 
 WR A.J. Brown had an active practice, with Maye looking in his direction often. He was charted with five receptions. 
 Starting LB Christian Elliss limped off early in practice. 
 RB Rhamondre Stevenson as a reliable pass catcher in the red zone has been a theme in recent days. He had another TD catch from Maye that had the crowd buzzing. 
 Colts DT Grover Stewart powered into LG Alijah Vera-Tucker on one play and got his hands up to bat down a pass. 
 OLB Elijah Ponder had the Patriots' most decisive PBU, getting his hands up at the line to swat away a pass from QB Daniel Jones . 
 Owners Robert Kraft (Patriots) and Carly Irsay-Gordon (Colts) watched practice together at one point. 
 Former Patriots safety Devin McCourty was in attendance to sign autographs. 
 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 First-round draft pick Caleb Lomu has been a full participant in all 13 training camp practices, and he shared insight Monday on the top thing he has learned.

 "The biggest thing is really focusing on not so many things. On defense, these guys are coming off the ball, they know their assignment, and everyone on the field has to know what they're doing. If you're thinking about multiple things, and if you hesitate at all for a quick second, the guy on the other side of the line is going to beat you.

 "Coming out here, at first I was thinking a lot and that caused me to play a little slower. I realized you can't think too much. You have to trust in what you learned in the classroom and go out and play ball."

 The 28th pick, Lomu had mostly been working at right tackle until the team's 12th practice last Friday, which was an intrasquad scrimmage. He flipped more to the left side that day, and that continued Monday in a practice held in shorts and light shoulder pads, as he was the backup left tackle behind Will Campbell .

 Lomu…

title: 2026 New Orleans Saints training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Saints training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Saints reporter Katherine Terrell has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Saints camp. Kellen Moore enters his second season as head coach, and expectations are higher after  Tyler Shough  impressed while starting the final nine games of the 2025 campaign. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Falcons' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.  

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Saints news 
 
 Drew Brees' greatness, as seen through eyes of teammates, coaches 
 Saints place WR Ja'Lynn Polk, 24, on reserve/retired list 
 Saints starting DT Bryan Bresee to have season-ending ACL surgery 
 The legacy of Taysom Hill in New Orleans: 'There's only one' 
 WR Chris Olave signing four-year extension 
 
 

 

 Who was the Saints' top performer at camp? 
 Saints defensive end Chase Young estimated he had six sacks in Thursday's joint practice against the Jacksonville Jaguars ' first team. The actual number likely wasn't far off.

 That summed up a terrific camp for Young, who is coming off a career-best 10 sacks in 12 games. Young has spent the offseason making life very difficult for the Saints' young offensive tackles. Coaches told Young before camp that expectations had been raised for him this year, both as a leader and a performer. He's risen to the occasion as a performer and recently told the media that he was willing and hungry to step up as a leader in the locker room as well.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 The Saints offense stepped up in a major way against the Jaguars' first-team defense in practice on Thursday after a few weeks of up-and-down performances. The Saints starters likely won't see much preseason action due to three separate sets of joint practices, but they passed their first test. The red zone offense is one of the areas in which the Saints could use improvement, as they've often settled for field goals instead of touchdowns after driving down the field during practices this summer.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 The Saints came away from their joint practice against the Jaguars with positivity on both sides of the ball. The offense had one of their best days of camp. Some highlights include a deep touchdown by QB  Tyler Shough , who completed a deep pass to Bryce Lance working against Travis Hunter with pressure in his face. Hunter would have attempted to tackle Lance if it were game situation, but there was no live tackling to the ground in practice.

 Other highlights included a QB  Zach Wilson to Bub Means touchdown; a Shough to Chris Olave touchdown, where Olave kept his toes in bounds for a score; and a Spencer Rattler to Trey Palmer deep touchdown. Shough said he felt his personal highlight occurred during the two-minute drill where he had six straight completions to set Charlie Smyth up for a 53-yard field goal as time ran out. Defensively, Julian Blackmon kicked things off with an interception of Jags' QB  Trevor Lawrence while the defensive line was active and in position for multiple sacks. At the end of the day, Young estimated he was involved in six sacks.

 More observations:  

 
 Jonas Sanker and Hunter Dekkers both got new numbers, with Sanker switching to No. 7 and Dekkers now wearing No. 13. 
 Sanker finished the day on the sideline with what appeared to be a cut above his eye. 
 Jordyn Tyson came down hard after a reception, jogged off and did not return to practice. 
 Charlie Smyth went 5-for-5 and Tanner Brown went 4-for-5 in a kicking session, where Brown's 51-yard attempt clanked off the uprights. Both made long field goals at the end of the two-minute drill 
 Spencer Rattler will start the preseason game against the Jaguars. 
 The final period for the first-team defense against the Jags first-team offense in the two minute situation had two pressures and two sacks. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Saints took a step back in anticipation of Thursday's joint practice session against the Jacksonville Jaguars . The Saints will practice against three different teams over the course of camp, and tomorrow's practice will essentially function as their preseason game. The starters won't play in Saturday's game, but they will get extensive time against the Jaguars' first-team tomorrow. The Saints had a short, non-padded inside practice to get ready for that.

 They still ran some 11-on-11 drills with a few highlights -- Isaac Yiadom broke up a Spencer Rattler pass to Bryce Lance , continuing to work through the play until the ball came out. Some teammates rushed over to celebrate the play. In the next team session, Lance caught a touchdown from Rattler in the end zone, making the catch over Jordan Howden and Elliott Davison before spiking the ball in celebration. They'll be back in pads tomorrow against Jacksonville.

 More observations: 

 
 There were multiple bad snaps among all their units, including a high snap from Erik McCoy to Tyler Shough . That comes a day after the offense had several penalties. Moore said the team is a work in progress. "We need to play more consistent football. We have to get there and that's what this time of the year is about," Moore said. 
 The Saints ended practice with red zone work, scoring a touchdown off a handoff to  Travis Etienne Jr . up the middle. Shough's two passes in the four-play session were incomplete, including an attempt to Juwan Johnson on the run with pressure from Chase Young . 
 The Saints experimented with multiple combinations, including an offensive line shuffle ( Cesar Ruiz got a few snaps at center again) and also moving Jonas Sanker around the field, while cornerback Jayden Price got some first-team reps. Moore said Price's consistency has been impressive and he earned more opportunities because of it. 
 The Saints brought former Lions CB Terrion Arnold in for a visit and said they're still gathering information on him. Arnold was released by the Lions after he was arrested on felony charges of armed robbery and kidnapping. His case is still ongoing. 
 Devaughn Vele got a rest day while Davon Godchaux was a new absence after rolling an ankle on Tuesday.  Cameron Jordan  remained absent with a hamstring injury. 
 The Saints did not attempt field goal kicks during their practice session Wednesday. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Offense and defense went at each other in an unscripted red zone scenario to end practice. The first side to 18 points won, with four points given to the defense if they held the offense to a field goal, three points to the offense for a made field goal, and seven points for a touchdown or turnover.

 The defense went up 4-3 after Charlie Smyth kicked a field goal for the first unit. Tanner Brown kicked a field goal for the second team after after  Martin Emerson Jr . broke up a Spencer Rattler pass on third down. With the defense up 8-6, Carl Granderson almost picked off Tyler Shough and then did manage to snag the ball three plays later, before punting it in celebration. That put the defense up 13-6, and Zach Wilson took advantage of an offsides penalty to throw a touchdown to Barion Brown to tie things up.

 The first-team offense took over with a chance to win outright, but Quincy Riley picked off Shough in the end zone, giving the defense the win. Coach Kellen Moore said the idea was to create a competitive environment. "It's just play ball and defense has the opportunity to score and obviously they won the day in the red zone," he said.

 Other observations:  

 
 The Saints first-team offense had multiple…

title: 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Giants training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Giants' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Cam Skattebo admits doing 'dumb things,' will save backflips for TDs 
 Nabers 'looked good' in 1st practice since knee injury 
 Giants have spoken with Skattebo after Fanatics Fest flip 
 2026 New York Giants training camp preview 
 

 

 Who is the Giants' top performer so far at camp? 
 TE Isaiah Likely  The offseason acquisition has been the Giants' No. 1 receiver with Malik Nabers not participating in team drills. He's been quarterback  Jaxson Dart 's safety net, leading all first-team receivers in catches by a wide margin.

 "Zay's done a great job," offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said.

 The way Likely smoothly gets in and out of breaks has just looked different from incumbent starter Theo Johnson . He also seems to have the best handle on the new offense given his familiarity with coach John Harbaugh and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman from Baltimore. Given the way Dart likes to throw to his tight ends, it suggests that Likely is in for a breakout season given the chemistry they already have developed.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Can the offense put it together? There are a lot of things working against Dart early in camp. He's learning a new offense, doesn't have Nabers in live drills and the structure of practice prohibits endless freelancing, which is perhaps what he does best. So it has been a struggle.

 The offense has failed to put together many big days in practice throughout the summer. Nagy said they expected there to be "highs and lows through this process" for their young quarterback. To see Dart and the first-team offense have some success in the preseason, even if it's just flashes, would be a welcome sight and could provide a confidence boost entering the season.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 The Giants are working hard at training camp. There is no doubt about that. Even on a rare day when they weren't in pads and ran a mental-rep practice that resembled a walk-through, coach John Harbaugh had the Giants on the field for two-plus hours.

 The practice concluded with them going over pregame introductions and the new routine for warmups. Every detail is important at the difficult Camp Harbaugh, which had players in full pads at seven of the past 10 practices.

 "My toughest training camp in 10 years," said fullback Patrick Ricard , who came over from Baltimore with Harbaugh.

 In a way, this has reminded some Giants of a college camp. With fewer rules, the big school colleges are known to run much harder and longer practices than the NFL.

 "I was with another Harbaugh [Jim Harbaugh at Michigan] for five years and it seems very similar to that," guard Jon Runyan  said.

 Now the Giants will see if it leads to better results.

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Malik Nabers wore a red jersey for the first time and participated in a good chunk of the walk-through. The star receiver caught close to a handful of passes as he inches closer to live drills off a torn right ACL. "Soon," Harbaugh said earlier this week. Sometime next week would seem likely. 
 The Giants have their preseason opener on Saturday afternoon against the Minnesota Vikings . Harbaugh wouldn't say whether QB Jaxson Dart and the starters would play. It seems like they might get some work as they learn a new offense. "That is a big part of it, executing the new offense," Harbaugh said. "But also a young quarterback. You've got a young quarterback who is just in his second year and didn't play a whole season even last year. So he's just getting started." 
 Players who didn't practice Thursday: CB Paulson Adebo (worked on side), C John Michael Schmitz Jr . (concussion) and WR Jalin Hyatt (leg). 
 Players who returned to practice (limited): CB Greg Newsome II (knee) CB Dru Phillips (knee) G/C Lucas Patrick (knee) WR JuJu Smith-Schuster (knee). 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 The kicking competition continues: Ben Sauls went 5-of-6 on field goal attempts in Wednesday's practice. Rookie Dominic Zvada went 7-of-7, including a 61-yarder to end practice.

 Overall in camp, Zvada is now 48-of-51 on kicks. Sauls is 41-of-48.

 "They're both having really good camps," coach John Harbaugh said.

 Running back Cam Skattebo and tight end Isaiah Likely peer-pressured Harbaugh into having Zvada attempt the 61-yard kick after the offense repeatedly sputtered in end-of-game situations. There were 10 seconds remaining on the clock and Harbaugh had the offense out on the field ready to run a play from the 44-yard line.

 He reconsidered. Zvada drilled the kick with plenty of room to spare (it clanked off the back fence) as the offense went wild.

 At this point, it seems a fait accompli that the Giants will carry a kicker with little to no experience come Week 1.

 Other observations:  

 
 Odell Beckham Jr . caught a pair of passes in live drills after a couple of quiet days. Harbaugh said Beckham will play in Saturday's preseason opener against the Vikings. 
 Harbaugh took the high road on whether QB Jaxson Dart will play. He decided to intentionally "dodge" that question. 
 Backup cornerback Art Green had a really strong practice. He knocked down a handful of passes. It comes at a time when the Giants are looking for someone to step up at cornerback. 
 CBs Dru Phillips (knee), Greg Newsome II (knee) and Paulson Adebo worked on the side at Wednesday's practice. Harbaugh said Adebo was "day to day." 
 G Francis Mauigoa was a full participant after being limited Tuesday. 
 WRs Juju Smith-Schuster (knee) and Jalin Hyatt (leg), C John Michael Schmitz Jr. (concussion), C/G Lucas Patrick (knee) and DB DJ James did not practice. 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 It was another rough afternoon for the Giants' offense. The unit sputtered and failed to hit any downfield throws during a practice without full pads.

 During one red zone drill, quarterback Jaxson Dart threw touchdown passes to Theo Johnson and Malachi Fields on two of the first three plays. He followed with five straight incompletions, including an interception at the goal line by Arvell Reese .

 These are the learning curves with a new offense.

 "[Tuesday] was an average practice, maybe below average," offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said. "It wasn't good enough. [Dart] knows that, we know that. We'll put it on tape, but we also talk about success through struggles and ... there's going to be some struggles as we go through this now in training camp and during the season. But how do we react?"

 The season starts in just over a month. The Giants are combining the offenses of Nagy, quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman. They're putting as much as possible on tape and plan to pare it down to accommodate the talent.

 The clock is ticking.

 Other observations: 

 
 Reese's interception included a circus catch. He dropped into coverage, sprinted to the flat and put an arm in the air. The ball hit off the back of Reese's hand, and he tipped it to himself for the interception at the goal line. It was the latest highlight for the No. 5 pick. "He's been impressive," defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said.

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Jets' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 Jets CB Stiggers taken to hospital after collapsing at practice 
 No. 2 pick Bailey living up to hype, bringing 'juice' to Jets 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq to miss time after hernia setback 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 

 
 Who has been the Jets' top performer so far at camp? 
Let's go with a rookie -- edge rusher David Bailey , the No. 2 overall pick. Those who criticized the Jets for drafting Bailey over LB Arvell Reese have been quiet lately. As a pass rusher, Bailey has been dominant at times, demonstrating elite first-step quickness. In joint practices with the Bucs, he caused a lot of problems for veteran RT Luke Goedeke , a $22 million-a-year player. Bailey still has to answer questions as a run defender -- he must clean up some technique stuff -- but his speed off the edge will make him a fun watch in 2026. 
 "He looks like he's everything that was advertised -- and more," MLB Demario Davis said.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
Can Geno Smith and the passing game get off the ground? They added some weapons, drafting TE Kenyon Sadiq and WR Omar Cooper Jr . in the first round, but this has been a slow-go for Smith & Co. On some days, Smith looks fantastic. Other days, not so much. Look, no one expects immediate success, but there should be incremental progress -- which is why the preseason games are so important. All told, the starters are expected to play 25 to 30 snaps. Another player (WR Adonai Mitchell ?) needs to step up as the No. 2 option, behind Garrett Wilson . That'll make it easier for Smith.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 Baker Mayfield beat the Jets with a two-minute drill last season in Week 3, setting up a game-winning field goal for the Buccaneers as time expired, and he did it again on Wednesday in the second of two joint practices.

 The Bucs' QB burned the Jets with three straight completions, hitting Dennis Houston with a short TD pass with three seconds left in a two-minute drill.

 "Baker does a really good job in that situation, and I wanted to see exactly how our guys operated in that situation," said Jets coach Aaron Glenn, adding that he could've helped the players with better defensive calls.

 It was another uneven day for the Jets, who had some hiccups in their own two-minute drive -- a drop by RB Braelon Allen , a holding call on RT Armand Membou and a false start. QB Geno Smith completed only two of seven passes on the drive, which ended with a missed field goal (61 yards) by Jason Sanders .

 "I felt like we could've made a few more plays," Smith said.

 The same could be said of the entire two-day experience. The Bucs, a playoff team in three of Todd Bowles' four seasons as coach, proved themselves the superior team.

 Silver lining for the Jets: This was a learning experience, a not-so-subtle reminder they still have a lot of work to do. Their young players got quality work, which should benefit them in the long run.

 More observations: 

 
 CB Qwan'tez Stiggers , who passed out during Tuesday's practice and was taken to a hospital, is in concussion protocol. Glenn said Swiggers experienced "symptoms" on Tuesday, but didn't elaborate except to say "something must have happened." Before collapsing and briefly losing consciousness, he was involved in a fight with some Tampa Bay players. He lost his helmet in the skirmish (it was flung by Bucs RT Luke Goedeke ). Stiggers was released from the hospital on Tuesday night. 
 Edge rusher Joseph Ossai , removed from the PUP list, is expected to start practicing next week. Rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds (calf), who hasn't practiced at all, also could return, although that seems less certain. Ponds' hopes of landing a starting job for Week 1 are fading by the day. 
 The two teams didn't fight as much as they did on Tuesday. This time, there were only a couple of scuffles. WR Tim Patrick and LG Dylan Parham were involved in "dust ups," as Glenn likes to call them. 
 Free agent CB Terrion Arnold visited the Giants on Wednesday, but there was no meeting with the Jets, a source said. They inquired about Arnold when he was released by the Detroit Lions , but their interest -- if there was any interest beyond due diligence -- appears to have cooled. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Geno Smith and the rest of the starters will play Friday night against the Buccaneers in the preseason opener, coach Aaron Glenn announced Tuesday.

 They can use the work.

 The first-team offense struggled in Tuesday's joint practice with the Bucs, as Smith was intercepted twice (one returned for a touchdown). The offense, learning new coordinator Frank Reich's system, is trending downward after an encouraging start to camp.

 The Jets were out of sync and allowed the Bucs to control the line of scrimmage, with running back  Breece Hall saying, "They beat us up a little today." And, no, he wasn't alluding to the four fights that marred practice.

 There was a spark in a red zone period late in practice, with Smith throwing touchdowns to tight end  Mason Taylor and wide receiver  Garrett Wilson (on a deflection). But it's clear the starting unit -- hardly devoid of talent -- has a way to go. Smith finished 10-for-16 in 11 on 11 periods.

 Glenn said the starters will play about 25 to 30 snaps in the preseason, though he's not sure how that will be divided over the three games. The Jets are installing new offensive and defensive systems. That's one of the reasons why Glenn wants to play his starters.

 Another reason: While many coaches prefer to be cautious, concerned about injuries, Glenn believes the best way to prep for the regular season is to actually play in the preseason.

 "Everybody's playing," he said.

 This isn't a new philosophy. A year ago, starting QB Justin Fields played 28 snaps in the preseason.

 

 More observations: 

 
 If you had to pick a "winner" in the joint practice, it would be the Bucs, who brought more energy and physicality at the outset. The two teams will do it again Wednesday. 
 WR Isaiah Williams , one of the stars of camp, has played his way into a bigger role. Before camp, he was viewed as a return specialist and No. 4 receiver, but that isn't the case anymore. Williams, who made three receptions in the joint practice, could leapfrog first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr ., who has experienced "little pitfalls," receivers coach Shawn Jefferson said. "That's part of being a rookie." 
 Wilson made one of the best plays of the day, catching the tipped pass in the red zone and evading what seemed like half of Tampa Bay's defense to find the end zone. 
 Rookie David Bailey had another impressive day as a pass rusher, making at least one sack and multiple QB pressures. He still needs work against the run, though. 
 Dane Belton , who had a pass breakup, may have the best ball production of any safety in camp. Glenn called him a "ball magnet." He's definitely pushing Andre Cisco for the starting job opposite Minkah Fitzpatrick . 
 Remember last year, when we made a big deal out of "live" tackling in training camp because it's uncommon in the NFL? Well, there won't be live tackling this summer. Glenn said he now prefers "thud" -- when defenders wrap up ball…

title: 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Eagles training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Eagles reporter Tim McManus has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and -- of course -- the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Eagles camp. How will quarterback  Jalen Hurts fare in the reimagined offense? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Eagles news 
 
 Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Eagles' Nolan Smith apologizes for 'unacceptable' speeding arrest 
 Eagles, DT Carter agree to four-year, $152M extension 
 Eagles coach Nick Sirianni adjusting to offseason changes 
 

 

 

 Who is the Eagles' top performer so far at camp? 

 WR Darius Cooper . No one has made more of their opportunities than Cooper, the 2025 undrafted free agent out of Tarleton State. He came out of nowhere to make the team as a rookie and is making another strong push this summer, standing out in a deep group that includes Hollywood Brown , Elijah Moore and Dontayvion Wicks . Hamstring injuries have sidelined both DeVonta Smith and rookie Makai Lemon for most of camp. Cooper has stepped in and has developed good rapport with QB  Jalen Hurts while showing off strong hands and a willingness to go over the middle.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How will the offensive operation look? The starters are expected to sit out the preseason but there is still plenty to learn about how things function under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion . He has never called plays and has yet to commit to whether he'll be doing so from the booth or the sideline on game days. The team's hope is the offense is quick out of the huddle, light on penalties and looks efficient during Mannion's test-drive.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts had an up-and-down day. He was intercepted by CB Mac McWilliams on an end-zone fade to Hollywood Brown during 7-on-7s early in practice. He got into a flow as the session went on, though, hitting Elijah Moore and Dontayvion Wicks in rhythm before connecting with tight end Dallas Goedert over the middle for a touchdown. Later, Hurts and Wicks hooked up for a touchdown in the corner of the end zone over Riq Woolen , who has come back to earth some this summer following a highly-productive spring.

 Other observations:  

 
 Someone should block linebacker  Jalyx Hunt . He's come free far too many times this camp, including from the left side on Thursday to blow up the play. 
 Cooper DeJean (groin) and Quinyon Mitchell (glute) were both sidelined. They were replaced in the lineup by McWilliams and Michael Carter II , respectively. 
 Brown dropped a short pass from Hurts in the red zone. The competition feels tight further down the receiver depth chart, with Darius Cooper , Moore, Brown, Britain Covey and Johnny Wilson among those hoping to find their way onto the 53-man roster. 
 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts and receiver Elijah Moore connected for another big play on Tuesday.

 Hurts uncorked a deep shot for Moore, who sped past safety  Andre' Sam  and hauled in the pass for a touchdown. Moore celebrated by punting the ball well over the practice field gate.

 Hurts has been without DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon the past six practices because of hamstring injuries but is finding a lot of value in building chemistry with some of the other receivers.

 Moore is one of the primary players capitalizing on that opportunity, generating a number of highlight plays alongside QB1.

 Other observations: 

 
 Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell sat out of team drills after pulling up during a one-on-one rep against Hollywood Brown . Mitchell went to the sideline and had his right leg stretched out by a trainer. Mac McWilliams took over for him with the first team. 
 Reserve corner Jakorian Bennett has had a good number of pass breakups this summer. He had another one on a Hurts attempt for Moore down the right seam on Tuesday. 
 Cooper DeJean came up with an interception on a reckless downfield throw from Andy Dalton . Later, DeJean blitzed Hurts and registered the "sack." 
 Edge rusher Jalyx Hunt has been one of the more impressive players on the field during camp. He came clean on one rush and chased Hurts to the other side of the field, eventually forcing him out of bounds. 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell came up with his second interception of camp -- perhaps foreshadowing a breakout year for him in the takeaway department. Mitchell sniffed out a Jalen Hurts pass intended for Hollywood Brown over the middle and came up with the pick on the first play of a simulated two-minute drive.

 
"Just his patience, his confidence," CB Riq Woolen said on what stands out about Mitchell. "He's been in this defense ... so he has a good understanding of how he can play certain techniques and certain coverages. Being able to watch him make plays, it inspires me to make plays."

 
Mitchell, a first-team All Pro in 2025, has yet to record a regular-season interception in his two years in the league but is tied for the most career playoff interceptions (four) among active players. It feels like a matter of time before he starts posting INTs more regularly.

 Other observations: 

 
 Receivers Makai Lemon and DeVonta Smith both missed their fifth straight practice with hamstring injuries. 
 Interior lineman Willie Lampkin continues to make a push for a roster spot. Listed at 5-foot-11, 290 pounds, he doesn't have the same size as most of his counterparts but is shining despite being asked to flip-flop from center to guard midpractice. Nick Sirianni said when the coaches review these sessions, they find themselves saying, "Willie did it again." 
 Emotions flared on the ninth day of camp. Guard Tyler Steen and DT Ty Robinson appeared to be at the center of an O-line vs. D-line scrum that took a little time to defuse. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Eagles running back Saquon Barkley made his presence felt. He got animated after a short touchdown run, chirping at Cooper DeJean before giving Quinyon Mitchell a playful shove.

 The offense switched from goal line to backed up work a short time later. Barkley used a nifty jump cut to speed to daylight on one play and followed that up by shaking defensive tackle Jordan Davis on his next carry.

 Barkley believes this new system can open up some things for him that he hasn't been able to fully showcase to this point in his career.

 "That's the plan," said offensive coordinator Sean Mannion . "Saquon, he's a tremendous player, and I think everything we do offensively ultimately is about how do we put all of our players in the best position to succeed and obviously Saquon is a focal point of our offense, that goes without saying."

 Other observations:  

 
 Linebacker Zack Baun intercepted Jalen Hurts on a throw over the middle. Hurts completed a pass to Elijah Moore on the previous play, and when he tried to go back to the well on a similar concept, Baun was there to jump the route. Baun nearly came up with another pick earlier in practice, but the ball somehow made it past him and into the hands of Moore along the sideline. 
 Hurts' connection with tight end Dallas Goedert is heating up. Hurts escaped pressure by rolling to his right and threw one to the corner of the end zone for Goedert, who pulled it in with Jihaad Campbell in coverage. 
 Center Cam Jurgens left practice early with a trainer for the second straight day. Saturday's exit was at the end of the session, and Jurgens appeared to be moving fine.

title: 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Steelers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Steelers camp. How will coach Mike McCarthy shape this roster and the offense in his first year in Pittsburgh? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the TEAM's top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 Jalen Ramsey, Joey Porter Jr. placed on PUP list 
 Steelers revamp wide receiver unit 
 Rodgers reunites with family ahead of final NFL season 
 
 

 Who has been the Steelers' top performer so far at camp? 
 DB  Asante Samuel Jr . He immensely benefitted from Joey Porter Jr .'s stint on the PUP list with back soreness in the midst of extension negotiations. With his increased playing time, Samuel made play after play in Latrobe, including several PBUs in two-minute drills and against wide receiver DK Metcalf .

 Samuel, whom coach Mike McCarthy said was one of his "favorite" players since arriving in Pittsburgh, was a late add last season coming off of neck surgery, and he signed a one-year, $4 million deal to stay with the Steelers in free agency. If his camp performance is any indication, Samuel's value will be significantly higher than his cost.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How does this new-look defense operate under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham? While there's plenty of questions about how Aaron Rodgers and the offense will look with McCarthy, perhaps more important to the team's success this season is Graham's ability to bring a fresh perspective and scheme to the NFL's highest-paid defense. Of course Graham won't show all of his tricks in the preseason, but these games will give an early preview of the defensive communication and the quality of depth across the board.

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Entering his 22nd year in the NFL, quarterback Aaron Rodgers  doesn't see a real advantage to playing in preseason games.

 "It's preseason," he said after Tuesday's practice. "It's not real football. So if I do, great. If not, great.

 "... Preseason's a lot different. Teams don't run anything anymore. They just really don't. ... I think preseason football is good to see guys with the pads on, under the lights, how they react to the nerves, but it's not real regular-season football."

 Instead, Rodgers said he's anxious to see how younger quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar react to being in game-like environments for the first time.

 Coach Mike McCarthy said he'll make a decision about the quarterback rotation for Thursday in meetings on Tuesday night, but he envisions using three groups on offense. The first will play one or two series, McCarthy said, while the second will finish out the first half and the third will play the second half.

 Rodgers said if he doesn't play, he views his role as providing comic relief from the sideline.

 "I like to be on the headset and calm everybody down," Rodgers said. "Usually the first game, it's a little hectic on the headset. So I like to be the voice of reason, occasional dad joke or one-liner. Just keep everybody settled in a little bit."

 It wasn't always that way, though.

 "It was my Super Bowl, for sure," Rodgers said of playing in the preseason 20 years ago.

 "I was so locked in and dialed in, and then you get out there and you run on a field and the nerves start flooding you and you start trying to slow your breathing down just to remember what the play was that you just heard in your helmet and not have to ask him again on the sideline and say it with conviction in the huddle, and then break the huddle and try and remember what the hell's going on to play and who's got what.

 "It's a great experience the first time just to be out there and to be live."

 More observations: 

 
 The Steelers moved practice indoors for the second day in a row as inclement weather hit Latrobe during their practice window. This time, the storms came through earlier than the day before, and the Steelers opted to hold the entire practice indoors. Though it was scheduled to go from 11 to 1:20 p.m., practice ended up lasting about an hour and a half. 
 McCarthy said Tuesday's padded practice was a critical one ahead of Thursday's preseason game. "We have a full slate," McCarthy said. "We wanted to have a competitive two drills today and two minutes. ... This practice is important. And frankly, you usually don't have that big of a practice as closer to the game. I get it. But it is preseason. So we'll see how we come out of today." 
 First-round pick Max Iheanachor won't play Thursday night, and McCarthy said Iheanachor is "working his way back" from last week's upper body injury. Iheanachor did individual drills on Monday. "We use the individual drills to see what he can do," McCarthy said. "... There's a strength component that we're trying to get over and there's some things we wanted to see him do in his pads and a helmet on. And he's making progress." 
 With WRs Michael Pittman Jr . and DK Metcalf out of practice for a second day in a row, rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard said he worked with the first team offense again. Rodgers said Bernard has a "really bright future," but acknowledged the wide receiver still has a lot of learning to do. "Germie just needs to learn the offense inside and out," Rodgers said. "And when he does that, he has a lot of great physical traits. He can get his feet in the ground quickly. He's very sudden. He's got natural hands. He's a great kid." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 The Steelers went through Mike McCarthy's planned "Franco Moment" on Monday and then navigated another of the intense drills as inclement weather forced the team to move inside midway through practice.

 "We've been doing it really with the Franco Moments," quarterback Will Howard said. "Kind of just, hey, sudden change, two-minute, whether it's backed up like it was today or if something happens, and sometimes you're going to have to go into the locker room for a couple minutes and then come back out. And just dealing with different changes, different sudden adversities that obviously aren't ideal.

 "I think obviously the rain is one thing, but just kind of dealing with that change of scenery and change of pace, I think we did a really good job of it."

 The Steelers were able to practice outside for about an hour. They went through a series of individual periods before an inside run team period. Then, just before the storm hit, the "Monday Night Football" jingle played over the sound system to signal the Franco Moment. The coaches set the table for the situational period: The offense was backed up at its 1-yard line with a fresh set of downs. The offense could win by picking up a first down. The defense could win by getting a stop.

 The offense sputtered as the fans started to evacuate the field. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard  committed a false start on first down. On the second play, Aaron Rodgers hit Brandon Smith for a quick pop pass and a 6-yard gain. Then, RB  Rico Dowdle ran up the middle for a 3-yard gain. Jaylen Warren got the ball on third-and-short, but the defense stuffed him to force a punt and get the win.
