full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 
 

 Who has been the Seahawks' top performer so far at camp? 
 The offense in general has been impressive considering the transition to new coordinator Brian Fleury and the fact that it faces the league's best scoring defense from 2025 every day in practice. In terms of individuals, we'll give the nod to Jaxon Smith-Njigba . The league's leading receiver from last season and the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year has remained an almost-unstoppable force. Rashid Shaheed is the deep threat in Seattle's offense, but QB  Sam Darnold has connected with JSN on several down-field shots this summer.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Who will win the third cornerback job? After letting Riq Woolen leave in free agency, the Seahawks have Noah Igbinoghene and Nehemiah Pritchett competing to replace him. Coach Mike Macdonald demands physicality from his corners, so preseason games (and Seattle's joint practice next week against the Titans) could be the differentiator in this battle. Regardless of who emerges, the position looks like a question mark, which is why Seattle is looking into free agent corner Terrion Arnold , who was released by the Lions in June after being was arrested on felony charges of armed robbery and kidnapping.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 There was nothing noteworthy to come from the Seahawks' 16th practice of training camp, with players wearing shorts and T-shirts during a 55-minute walk-through. But there was a development with  Terrion Arnold . 
 
After working out for the Seahawks on Sunday, then visiting the New Orleans Saints on Tuesday, the third-year cornerback continued his free agent tour by meeting with the New York Giants  on Wednesday. If the Seahawks are going to truly pursue Arnold, who is facing eight felony charges in Florida in connection with a kidnapping and robbery in early February, then it sounds like they'll have competition. 
 
Coach Mike Macdonald's comments on Arnold earlier this week made it clear that Seattle's interest is much more than simply the team's usual due diligence. That was reinforced on the second episode of "Hard Knocks," which showed general manager John Schneider eagerly relaying to Macdonald what Seahawks quarterback Jalen Milroe told him about Arnold while vouching for his college teammate. 
 
In another clip, Schneider was shown asking another front office member about instances of an NFL team acquiring a player with an outstanding legal case, as if trying to gauge the potential blowback. 
 
There are other questions the Seahawks likely have to ponder: 
 
When might Arnold be available should he land on the NFL commissioner's exempt list? How might the team's soon-to-be owners feel about a controversial signing if it were to happen before they'd be in position to sign off on it? And would Arnold fit into the tight-knit culture that has been part of the reigning Super Bowl champions' secret sauce? 
 
Defensive tackle Leonard Williams was asked about the possibility of adding a player with off-the-field issues to Seattle's locker room. 
 
"We have such a culture and way about ourselves here that if you don't fall in line with the way our team is, you're just going to get steamrolled and not fit in, to be honest," Williams said. "I think guys instantly come into this building and they see that we stand out in different ways in terms of the way we practice, the way we communicate, the way we show respect and want to get better. If you're not following all of our principles and guidelines, you're going to stand out really easily. You're either just going to fall in line or not end up here."

 Other observations:

 
 The Seahawks have a full-length practice Thursday and a shorter one Friday before their preseason opener Saturday against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field. 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Good news came on the injury front on Tuesday via safety Nick Emmanwori passing his physical, a significant step in his return from July ankle surgery.

 Then came bad news, with the team announcing that second-year fullback Robbie Ouzts will go on injured reserve, ending his season because of the neck issue that kept him out of the NFC Championship Game and Super Bowl.

 It's no small thing given new coordinator Brian Fleury's stated desire to run a good chunk of his offense with two backs on the field at the same time. Fleury came from the San Francisco 49ers , who ran an NFL-high 491 plays last season out of two-back formations, according to ESPN Research. Since 2022, coach Kyle Shanahan's offense leads the league in snaps with two backs.

 "I like using two backs because it can change the formation strength after the snap as opposed to the whole defense being able to identify it before the snap," Fleury said last week. "It creates some fit problems. It's becoming less and less common across the league, so it's more difficult to prepare for. Those are the elements I like about it. I'm more of an old-school traditionalist because of my upbringing in football and so I'm always going to want to play with two backs at some point. I like the guys we have in that role right now."

 At that point, it wasn't known yet that Ouzts would have to miss the season. Brady Russell , a converted tight end, is the Seahawks' next man up at fullback. They also signed Brock Lampe last week.

 General manager John Schneider has a long history of late-summer additions, so the Seahawks could potentially find their replacement for Ouzts via a trade or waiver claim. Or, as Fleury said, they could find creative ways to get a second back on the field.

 "It doesn't have to be a traditional fullback," Fleury said last week. "We've found ways to use receivers in lead blocking roles, other tight ends, even other running backs. We'll find a way to get it done."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie RB Jadarian Price missed his fourth straight practice. Coach Mike Macdonald has described his issue as lower-body soreness and said Seattle's first-round pick should be back in a matter of days. 
 Tuesday's practice again got contentious. During an 11-on-11 period, S Ty Okada hit WR Tory Horton on a screen pass. Horton took exception, pushing Okada. G Christian Haynes came to Horton's defense and ended up going to the ground with Okada. There were no flare-ups after that, and Okada was laughing about the altercation with fellow defensive backs on the sideline moments later. 
 Okada came down with an interception when CB Josh Jobe deflected a QB  Sam Darnold pass to WR Cooper Kupp near the goal line. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 The Seahawks might have more NFL-caliber safeties than they'll be able to keep, and the players who are vying for roster spots have been making plays.

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Cowboys' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 Kyle Shanahan nears full strength, plans to coach preseason opener 
 What's next for 49ers receivers Aiyuk, Deebo and Pearsall? 
 Deebo Samuel on reunion with 49ers: 'Just matter of time' 
 WR Ricky Pearsall to have season-ending knee surgery 
 VP Paraag Marathe exits to focus on soccer clubs 
 49ers GM Lynch focused on 'players that are here,' not WR Aiyuk 
 

 

 

 Who is the 49ers' top performer so far at camp? 
 QB Brock Purdy . There are others deserving of mention here, but this has been Purdy's best and most consistent training camp despite working with a constantly changing supporting cast. No matter who has been at running back or receiver, Purdy has found ways to move the offense in nearly every practice. He has been particularly sharp when pushing the ball downfield for big plays. If healthy, he looks poised for a big year.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Where's the pass rush coming from? The Niners were last in the NFL in sacks (20) and 31st in pressures (157) in 2025. In the offseason, they traded for defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa ; they used draft picks on edge Romello Height and defensive tackle Gracen Halton . All three should help, but with defensive ends Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams not yet back from ACL surgeries, the exhibition slate will be the time for others to step forward and carve out roles.

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 More than two weeks into camp, the 49ers offense was looking forward to seeing how it would fare against another team Tuesday. The answer? Quite well.

 After a slow start for the unit, QB Brock Purdy continued his strong camp by carving through the Titans secondary for much of the joint practice session, particularly in the latter half of the session. I had Purdy at 21-of-27 on the day, including multiple touchdown passes and no interceptions.

 

 His best throws came in a move in which he dropped a perfect ball between three defenders to rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling that would have gone for a long touchdown. And then, he had another layered throw over linebacker Cody Barton for a big gain to TE Jake Tonges .

 Even Purdy's toughest critic had to give it up for him after the practice.

 "Brock's a really good player, so I expect him to have good plays," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "I notice all the bad plays ... I didn't notice many bad plays today so I think he had a hell of a day."

 More observations: 

 
 There were a handful of fights early in the practice that looked like they might have ended the day early. San Francisco's defense seemed to be doing most of the early agitating. But both sides settled in and got some good work. 
 Stribling showed that his early flashes aren't limited to producing against his teammates. Regardless of which unit he was working against, he repeatedly made big plays. 
 Veteran WR Demarcus Robinson also had another big day, catching a couple of touchdowns from Purdy and continuing to make the case to be a valuable backup at multiple spots. 
 Speaking of receivers, Mike Evans was back from his quad injury, though he didn't do much beyond individual drills. 
 DE Nick Bosa is still not practicing with soreness and what Shanahan described as tendinitis. Shanahan said the tendinitis is normal for a player coming off a torn ACL; he has no concern about Bosa's long-term status. The hope is to have him at full strength for Week 1. 
 RB Christian McCaffrey watched the practice in street clothes and, like Bosa, Shanahan indicated there's no worry about the tightness McCaffrey is battling. Shanahan said he'd be more concerned if McCaffrey tried to play through it and risked making it worse. 
 Shanahan is out of the cast on his left hand and has traded it in for a black brace. He was out there for the whole session. 
 Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. was at practice and spent some time chatting with Niners GM John Lynch before the session. 
 Didn't catch who it was, but one of the officials was on the wrong end of a collision and had to be helped off the field. 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 The Niners had only one new addition to their "did not practice" report Monday, but it was a big one: running back Christian McCaffrey .

 McCaffrey did not practice because of what the team called "tightness" after participating in every other practice during this training camp. After the session, offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak indicated McCaffrey isn't dealing with anything serious and the team is trying to be smart with him.

 "[He's] a little sore, but he's doing fine," Kubiak said. "Just kind of managing him as we go."

 Kubiak said the team will continue to keep an eye on McCaffrey's workload as it tries to get him to full speed against the Rams in Australia.

 "In terms of his rep load, we're right on track where we want to be," Kubiak said. "And he's a veteran player, so you got to monitor him and get him ready for the first week."

 More observations: 

 
 Legendary Niners receiver Jerry Rice made a cameo appearance at practice, emerging early in team drills and watching from the sideline. 
 Coach Kyle Shanahan continues to work his way back and was on the field for essentially the whole practice. 
 Rookie offensive lineman Carver Willis returned from a concussion. He was back in the mix at left guard with the second-team offense. 
 Tight end George Kittle was doing the most strenuous workout the media has seen him do in this camp on the side as he continues to come back from a ruptured Achilles. Kittle was running routes and catching passes during individual drills. 
 Most of the other injured Niners also continue to work on the side, with RB Kaelon Black and DL Keion White doing some conditioning as they come back from adductor injuries. 
 QB Brock Purdy provided the biggest plays of the day, hitting WR De'Zhaun Stribling for a huge gain on a deep corner route and later connecting with WR Demarcus Robinson on another deep ball. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 While Kyle Shanahan returned to media duty and is edging close to 100% recovered from his July 14 car accident, 49ers DE Nick Bosa remained absent from practice.

 Bosa, who is recovering from the torn right ACL he suffered in Week 3 last year, has missed the past three open sessions because of what the team is calling general soreness. Before that, Bosa had been working solely in individual drills as part of his recovery. Bosa's absence has raised questions about a potential setback, though it's also worth noting the Niners are always cautious with Bosa in training camp anyway.

 Shanahan said after practice that he expects Bosa to be fine.

 "He was doing great, and then he got sore just going through some of the individuals," Shanahan said. "You wish that didn't happen. But no, there's no concern to where something's happened that is a big setback or anything. But we'll wait until that soreness goes away and evaluating why the soreness has happened. But I still feel pretty good about that."

 More observations:  

 
 The only new addition to the non-practice list was LB Luke Gifford . It's unclear what he's dealing with, though he did some work on the side during the session. 
 CB Upton Stout had a nice day, laying out for a…

title: Joe Montana Super Bowl XXIV jersey fetches record price
summary: The jersey worn by Tom Brady in his final game had held the previous record since it was sold in November 2023
full_text:
On Thursday, the high-end alternative asset and collectibles venture Treasure Trove announced it had acquired a game-worn Joe Montana Super Bowl XXIV jersey for $1,515,000 -- a record price in the NFL's most important collectibles space.

 The jersey worn by Tom Brady in his final game had held the previous record since it was sold in November 2023  with a $1.39 million price tag.

 But even at a record price, its purchaser still sees untapped value.

 

 "When you zoom out and contextualize this jersey, but also a lot of game-worn jerseys by the GOATs, whether it be in football or basketball or whatever the sport is, you think about the trading card markets," AJ Scaramucci, CEO of Treasure Trove, told ESPN. "There are huge dislocations from an investment perspective in this market, and snagging this jersey, of which there's an unbelievably scarce number of these jerseys out there ... I would argue that game-worn sports memorabilia of this caliber is dramatically and just freakishly underpriced relative to, say, the trading card market."

 The jersey comes from Montana's final Super Bowl appearance, a decisive 55-10 win by the San Francisco 49ers over the Cincinnati Bengals in 1990. Montana was dominant, being named the game's Most Valuable Player as he threw for 297 yards and five touchdowns with a completion percentage of 75.9%.

 Montana's Super Bowl jerseys are part of a unique quirk in NFL lore: Though the Hall of Fame quarterback played in four Super Bowls, he only wore three jerseys across those games -- he wore the same threads in Super Bowl XXIII as he did in Super Bowl XIX.

 

 Scaramucci said that Montana's famously perfect record in Super Bowls helps ensure that the jersey is good value for its record cost.

 "I think Joe Montana, just in terms of the markets of collectibles, is such an underpriced person," he said. "I mean, yes, Tom Brady has more Super Bowls. But Tom Brady also lost a few Super Bowls."

 It's not the first time that a Montana jersey worn on the NFL's biggest stage has fetched a record price in the NFL collectibles space. In 2023, Montana's jersey from "The Drive" in Super Bowl XXIII -- the jersey he wore in two Super Bowls -- sold for a then-record $1.212 million.

title: 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Bucs training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Buccaneers reporter Jenna Laine has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bucs camp. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Bucs' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest new s from Bucs camp 
 
 Bucs GM Licht: 'No plans' for Vea trade, Mayfield still franchise QB 
 Mayfield felt 'disrespected' and 'undervalued' by contract offers 
 History says Vea, Mayfield will play with Bucs this season 
 Vea requests trade from Bucs after stalled talks 
 2026 Bucs training camp preview 
 
 

 Who has been the Bucs' top performer so far at camp? 
 He may not have the name recognition of 15th overall draft pick Rueben Bain Jr ., nor did he have an 11-sack season under his belt like  Al-Quadin Muhammad . But one can argue that no player did more for himself each day than outside linebacker David Walker .

 The 2025 fourth-round draft pick never even got to put on pads his rookie season last year after suffering a torn ACL in training camp. But he tallied nine would-be sacks in the first nine  practices. We didn't get to see him line up against starting All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs , who missed all of camp with a hamstring injury, which would be the ultimate test, but general manager Jason Licht told WDAE Radio of Walker, "I talked about Bain before but I'd say that the level of excitement is on an equal plane with David."

 B Licht called him a "freak about his rehab" and said he was "passionate and devoted."

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Will the Bucs have enough healthy cornerbacks? A big reason the Bucs parted ways with veteran Jamel Dean was because he could not stay healthy. Yet after missing the majority of camp with a left hamstring injury, cornerback Benjamin Morrison , the Bucs' second-round draft pick in 2025 who was expected to challenge for a starting role in 2026, just returned to practice in a limited capacity.

 He saw action in only 10 games last year due to injuries and entered the NFL draft having undergone bilateral hip surgery, raising serious concerns about his availability. Because of that,  Jacob Parrish has become a starter almost by default. Then their starter from last year, Zyon McCollum , is now dealing with a groin injury. The team waived Chase Lucas and Kemon Hall due to injuries. This puts a lot more attention on Josh Hayes ,  Damarion Williams  and Ayden Garnes . Remember that some of the team's key defensive breakdowns that kept them out of the postseason -- like the infamous fourth-and-28 against the Atlanta Falcons -- happened with backups

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 The second day of Bucs-Jets joint practices on Wednesday saw wide receiver Emeka Egbuka suffer a toe sprain after having his foot rolled up on. A source told ESPN that the injury is not serious but he will undergo further testing.

 The Bucs' wide receiver room has been quickly depleted in camp, with Jalen McMillan missing practices due to a knee injury (he is now participating in individual drills though), Tez Johnson being out with a groin injury and David Sills being out due to a knee injury. That leaves rookie third-round draft pick Ted Hurst III , Kameron Johnson , Garrett Greene , Dennis Houston , Dean Patterson IV and Eric Rivers.

 Bowles had this to say about the joint practices -- "[The] effort is outstanding on both sides. I think we got a lot of work done. The young guys got a chance to play against different guys, a different scheme, so to speak, and they got thrown in there early. There's a lot of tape to correct [and] there's a lot of things to learn from, but the effort was great. We've just got to clean up some things."

 Other observations:

 
 Bowles said quarterback Baker Mayfield won't play in this week's first preseason game. Backup Jake Browning also suffered an injury Tuesday, but Bowles wasn't ready to rule him out. He did say, however, that Connor Bazelak will start. Jalon Daniels , the only other healthy quarterback on their roster, will also play. 
 Rookie outside linebacker Rueben Bain, Jr. recorded multiple would-be sacks against Jets quarterback Geno Smith . By all accounts, it sounds like Bowles saw all he needs to from the Bucs' first-round pick. When asked if he'd play Friday, Bowles said, "Not much, if at all. 
 Cornerback Benjamin Morrison , the Bucs' second-round draft pick in 2025, did wear pads and participated in individual drills, according to reports. Morrison has missed the entirety of camp so far with a hamstring injury. 
 
 
 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst III made arguably the two biggest catches of the day -- both times were with the first-team offense and fans roared with approval. The first was an overlead leaping grab coming out of a trips formation with Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with Hurst running a deep out and cornerback Josh Hayes in coverage. Hurst fell hard onto his back and it knocked the wind out of him, making him slow to get up as he was checked out by the training staff. Then during the red zone period, he caught a beautiful fade route for a touchdown with Jacob Parrish in coverage.

 The Bucs' third-round draft pick out of Georgia State has gotten more opportunities with the first-team offense due to injuries for Jalen McMillan (knee) and Tez Johnson (groin) and said he feels like he's starting to turn the corner in terms of preparation and performance. 
 
"[I'm] just trying to be myself and exploit and show that that's my game, going up, attacking the ball," Hurst said. "Lately, I feel like I haven't been doing that much, but it kind of starts in the morning. Getting up and coming in at 6:30 a.m., getting the walk-through in before we even get outside so I can just play [as] fast as I want to, not thinking out there on the field."

 Other observations:  

 
 Second-year outside linebacker David Walker , who missed all of last season with a torn ACL, was once again a force in the backfield for the ninth consecutive day. Walker would have had a sack on Mayfield coming off the left side, as he's been getting work in with the first and second-team defense. Keep in mind though, that this was against backup Ben Chukwuma and not All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs , who remains sidelined with a hamstring injury. Outside linebacker YaYa Diaby also registered a would-be sack. 
 Veteran wide receiver Chris Godwin caught several passes from quarterback Baker Mayfield , including one in red zone for a touchdown. He's looked healthy and energized throughout practices and we've seen him show some versatility in lining up all over the formation. "I think he is healthy right now," Bowles said of Godwin. "In the past he has been hurt the last two but he is a lot healthier right now and he is into it mentally he is sharp and he is tough, he understands that he is a great mentor to the guys. He is still a playmaker for us, and he makes big plays in the passing and blocking game. He is peaking at the right time." 
 Safety Tykee Smith made an impressive stop on running back Bucky Irving during red zone work, blowing up the play for no gain which got everybody fired up on defense. 
 In the red zone, wide receiver Dennis Houston , who, like Hurst, has made the most of some opportunities due to injuries, hauled in an impressive Jake Browning touchdown coming across the back of the end zone with Scott in coverage. The coaching staff has been really excited about Houston's speed and believes he may be one of, if not the fastest on…

title: 2026 Tennessee Titans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Titans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans ' camp took place at the Vanderbilt Health Football Center, and Titans reporter Turron Davenport had the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we saw and heard at Titans camp. We were looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Titans' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Titans news: 

 
 Extension makes Peter Skoronski NFL's top-paid guard 
 Titans DT Jeffery Simmons throws punch, sent to side field 
 Will Levis: There aren't 32 QBs better than me 
 Titans WRs join Cam Ward in Miami to build chemistry 
 

 

 

 Who was team's top performer at camp? 
 There's a close race for top performer between second-year receiver Elic Ayomanor and rookie wideout Carnell Tate .

 Ayomanor reported to camp with a more-chiseled physique and an aggressive approach to playing the position. He has consistently made catches on back-shoulder throws and go routes. Ayomanor uses his big body to provide an easy middle-of-the-field target for Cam Ward and Mitchell Trubisky on both slants and digs. Ayomanor worked on body language and forward lean with his stance and throughout his routes.

 Titans coach Robert Saleh praised Ayomanor for his work ethic but challenged him to be a consistent player.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Right guard remains the biggest question mark. Veteran offensive lineman Cordell Volson seemed to have the inside track at one point. He and second-year lineman Jackson Slater shared first-team reps. But fifth-round pick Fernando Carmona has made a recent push for the starting spot after getting some first-team reps himself.

 Slater started taking snaps at center in the joint practices with the 49ers before the preseason opener. Veteran lineman Andre James had been working at center but recently saw time at right guard while Slater played center.

 "There's a lot of moving parts," Titans coach Robert Saleh said. "We're trying to find the right combination for that O-line. Feel good about the first unit, but right guard has got to get solidified."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 The Titans won't admit it, but Tuesday was a wake-up call, especially for the offense after a spicy joint practice with the 49ers. San Francisco's pass rush was consistently harassing Titans quarterback Cam Ward despite the absence of premier pass rusher Nick Bosa due to knee tendinitis.

 One of the pressures led to Ward climbing the pocket and rushing a throw across the middle that was picked off by 49ers safety  Ji'Ayir Brown . The passing game struggled overall with Ward completing mostly short passes. His longest pass was an 18-yard strike to Carnell Tate on an in-breaking route.

 "If they're going to drop all the way back, we'll check it down, and they've got to come tackle Tyjae Spears and Tony Pollard in space," Ward said. "I don't have to throw the ball 20 yards. I can throw it five yards and let Tyjae and Tony do the rest."

 Both Ward and Mitchell Trubisky made multiple deep passing attempts to Elic Ayomanor , but all four of the passes fell incomplete.

 
 Starting with the first rep of team period, there were multiple skirmishes after plays. Tate took a big hit from Renardo Green along the sideline causing some extracurricular activity. Then Austin Deculus got kicked out minutes into the team period for throwing a punch at a 49ers defensive lineman. Dan Moore Jr . was kicked out after he swung on Osa Odighizuwa after a near sack of Ward. 
 The center and right guard competition took another turn with Fernando Carmona getting early reps again. He was flagged for a false start when Ward tried to use a hard count. Carmona got to protect Ward for back-to-back practices this week. Jackson Slater got reps at center instead of right guard, snapping the ball to Will Levis . Andre James played right guard instead of center. "There's a lot of moving parts," Saleh said after practice. "That right guard's got to get solidified." 
 Saleh said he plans to play everyone in the preseason opener against the 49ers on Thursday. He didn't want to commit to a snap number but said it will be a couple of series for the starters. Ward liked the idea and said he's looking forward to getting into a rhythm in an actual game. 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 Carnell Tate continues to impress in his first NFL training camp.

 One of his standout traits is how effectively Tate is running the full route tree.

 Tate was on the receiving end of three touchdown passes from Cam Ward . The rookie wideout caught a deep pass for a score on a go route with Alontae Taylor being the closest defender. Tate made an impressive catch over Cor'Dale Flott in the corner of the end zone on another play, and he caught a quick out-breaking route for his third score.

 "Tate has an innate ability to attack the ball," Titans receivers coach Greg Lewis said after practice. "He can make contested catches. He has long speed and is really smooth. The guy can also uncover."

 More observations: 

 
 - Joshua Williams was once again in the yellow "non-contact" jersey. Williams had the jersey on in the scrimmage on Friday as well. Titans coach Robert Saleh said Williams is dealing with a pectoral injury that cost him some time during minicamp. Williams was still working in team periods. 
 The center position is still a competition, but it seems like veteran Austin Schlottmann will win the job. Left guard Peter Skoronski said Schlottmann has helped accelerate the learning process for him because of the previous time with Titans offensive coordinator when they were with the Giants. Pat Coogan continues to get early reps but has struggled at times with off-target snaps to Mitchell Trubisky during team periods. 
 Right guard is another position battle to watch. Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater have been the primary competitors, with both getting opportunities to protect Ward during team periods. Rookie Fernando Carmona also got some early reps for the first time on Sunday. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 The Titans returned to the field after not practicing Wednesday. The pace was noticeably slower to start, but it livened up during team period.

 The offensive line continues to shuffle, especially along the interior, where Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater are the top contenders for right guard while Austin Schlottmann , Pat Coogan and Andre James are battling for the starting center spot.

 All five players have gotten first-team reps in different tandems. Schlottmann has enjoyed going against Jeffery Simmons during team period because "he's one of the best, if not the best interior defenders in the league." Coach Robert Saleh said they're not close to deciding who will start at this point but expects to be closer to a decision leading into the third preseason game.

 Other observations: 

 
 WR  Elic Ayomanor continues to have a solid camp. He caught a deep pass from Cam Ward on a go route in red zone team period to even the score with Alontae Taylor who broke up a pass on the same route earlier in practice. Ward went to Ayomanor again, but the pass fell incomplete. Ayomanor collided with S  Kevin Winston Jr . as they went up for the pass in what Saleh described as a "bang, bang" play. Ayomanor got up favoring his left shoulder after being down for a bit. He went inside for further evaluation. 
 Left tackle  Dan Moore Jr . returned to practice after leaving team period and walking into the building on his own with a trainer Tuesday. Moore took part in team period and got into a small pushing match with linebacker Cody Barton after one of the plays. 
 JC Latham came out during team period towards the end of…

title: 2026 Washington Commanders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Commanders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Commanders reporter John Keim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Commanders camp. Can Washington bounce back from an injury-plagued 2025 season? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Commanders' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Commanders camp 
 
 Stefon Diggs settles in with Commanders, ups NFL best talk 
 Daniels finds voice, aims to fill leadership void 
 Commanders tab ex-All-Pro WR Wes Welker to coach tight ends 
 
 

 Who was the team's top performer at camp? 

 Quarterback Jayden Daniels has jumped out because of his comfort level in the offense. Early in camp, there were more mixed results, but lately it's been almost all good. He's throwing in rhythm, keeping his eyes downfield when he gets outside the pocket and has been smooth running play-action from under center.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 There will be questions about the offensive line with left tackle Laremy Tunsil sidelined for at least a significant period because of a torn triceps. And center Nick Allegretti , the favorite to start, has missed two weeks. It hasn't affected the pass game, but the question will be about the run game and is there enough depth?

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels ' comfort level in the new offense continues to grow -- and that was evident again vs. Miami during a joint practice on Wednesday.

 The session showed that having receiver Stefon Diggs is going to make a difference for Daniels and the unit. They connected for a touchdown in an 11-on-11 session vs. the Dolphins, with Daniels hitting him in the back of the end zone and throwing where only Diggs had a shot.

 Another time, Diggs broke open off the line and caught a quick pass from Daniels.

 In one-on-one work, Daniels threw a perfect pass to Diggs, who had been covered -- but the throw was to a spot where Diggs could stop and make the catch unobstructed.

 "It's awesome," Daniels said of having Diggs. "Just his feel for space, he's a dog. He goes out and makes plays. He brings energy, he's a leader."

 But Daniels wasn't just finding Diggs. He received good protection on a play-action pass to  Treylon Burks ; those two combined for a touchdown pass on a throw deep down the right side.

 Daniels also dropped a perfect ball over a corner to Van Jefferson . The latter hooked up on a play where Daniels extended to his right and found Jefferson sprinting across the middle towards his side.

 More observations: 

 
 Corner Mike Sainristil fooled quarterback Malik Willis with his coverage on a pick-six. Sainristil, aligned outside on the offense's right side, appeared to be dropping back into coverage. So Willis opted for a pass to the flat -- but Sainristil immediately broke on the ball and picked it for an easy score. "I told him it was about damn time," said corner Amik Robertson . "He had all those [pass break-ups] in camp." 
 Washington's defensive line had a strong day against an offense lacking much firepower. "I was telling [ K'Lavon Chaisson ] I'm just playing pass," said safety Jeremy Reaves . "I've got nothing to worry about up there, they're handling all the runs... It makes playing pass so much easier when you don't have to take false steps because they've got that covered." 
 Robertson said they practiced with a lot of energy -- a focal point throughout camp. When they play that way he said it results in "domination. To prove that we belong out there and whoever steps foot out there they shouldn't be on the same field with us." 
 Washington's main area of struggles offensively vs. Miami involved inside runs. The Commanders are still missing center Nick Allegretti , who is the favorite to start, but they do have both of last year's starting guards in Chris Paul on the left side and Sam Cosmi on the right side. The outside runs appeared to be stronger. Coach Dan Quinn has said the run game is often behind because there's less contact in camp than in past years. 
 Both of Washington's placekickers -- Jake Moody and Drew Stevens -- made all six of their field goal attempts, with the last one coming from 60 yards. Both cleared it with no problem, but Stevens had about 10 yards to spare. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 The Washington Commanders ' offensive line could get reinforcements soon with center Nick Allegretti  possibly set to return from a strained calf muscle.

 He suffered the injury on July 29 and hasn't practiced since, but coach Dan Quinn said there's a good chance he'll return next week. Washington will hold a joint practice Wednesday with Miami before playing the Dolphins in the preseason opener Friday night.

 They will conduct a walk-through Sunday when Allegretti could rejoin his teammates on the field. He and tight end John Bates (hamstring) have been working on a side field this week with the strength and conditioning coaches and athletic trainers.

 Getting Allegretti back can help start to settle the line, which lost its top player in tackle Laremy Tunsil to a torn triceps. Allegretti is considered the favorite to start at center. Bates, too, might return at this time. He's a crucial part of their run blocking.

 Washington coach Dan Quinn said the early disruption along the line is "not ideal, but it's not unusual." And he said he liked the Commanders' line depth entering camp -- pointing to Coleman, who had been competing with Chris Paul to start at left guard, and veteran Andrew Wylie , who typically fills in at both spots on the right side.

 Meanwhile, Wylie said that after his triceps surgery Tunsil told his teammates that he will undergo his treatment at the Commanders' facility rather than at home in Houston, as is customary with many players expected to miss significant time.

 Also, corner Trey Amos (ankle) will not practice Wednesday nor will he play Friday. He'll be re-evaluated Sunday.

 More observations: 

 
 A number of Commanders players did not practice Tuesday after a two-hour session in full pads Monday and the joint session Wednesday. Among the group sitting out: receivers Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs ; defensive linemen Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw and linebackers Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson . Safety Jeremy Reaves , corner Amik Robertson and tight end Ben Sinnott . 
 Tight end Colson Yankoff made multiple catches in practice Tuesday and has had a productive camp as a pass-catcher. His best catch occurred earlier this week when he made a one-handed grab. And, last week, he leapt high for a pass down the middle of the field for a catch -- and hung onto the ball despite hitting the ground hard. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Washington Commanders cornerback  Trey Amos will miss the next "day or two" after injuring his ankle during practice Saturday.

 "We'll see where he's at in the next day or so," coach Dan Quinn said.

 Amos had just returned to practice Friday after opening on the physically unable to perform list. He suffered a fractured fibula in Week 10 last season but was dealing with a soft-tissue injury prior to camp.
